title: Return to Sender
tagline: She will have he revenge.
overview: A nurse living in a small town goes on a blind date with a man who is not the person he says he is.
plot:
Return to Sender is a 2015 American psychological thriller directed by Fouad Mikati, a rape-and-revenge story starring Rosamund Pike as a small-town nurse, Shiloh Fernandez as the man who assaults her and Nick Nolte as her father. Rumer Willis, Camryn Manheim and Illeana Douglas appear in supporting roles.

Miranda Wells is a nurse in a small town who is in the process of buying a new house. A friend arranges a blind date for her with a man named Kevin, and when a stranger turns up at her door on the day of the date, Miranda assumes he is Kevin and lets him in. He is courteous at first, but his manner turns, he refuses to leave, locks the door and brutally attacks and rapes her. The real Kevin finds her and takes her to the hospital. Miranda recognises her attacker as a worker from a restaurant she visited recently, and the police arrest him: William Finn.

Life does not return to normal. Her real estate agent tells her the house has become unsellable because of what happened in it, and she is passed over for a promotion at work. Miranda begins writing to William in prison, but her letters keep being returned until one finally arrives with the words "You win" written on the envelope. She visits him, he apologises again and again, and the visits become regular, friendly and even flirtatious. Her father, Mitchell, is appalled when he learns she is still in contact with the man, and the two fall out.

After his release, William shows up at her house uninvited, and Miranda sets him to work repairing her porch. One afternoon she brings him a glass of lemonade; he soon feels unwell, asks to lie down inside and collapses. He wakes strapped to a bed in her basement, where Miranda reveals that she has been planning her revenge from the start and has poisoned him with antifreeze. Later she amputates one of his hands and then castrates him, telling him that he was right and that she has won. The film closes with Miranda visiting her father and telling him that William will not be coming around again.

The film was released in the United Kingdom in May 2015 and in limited release in the United States in August by Image Entertainment. Critics were largely negative, giving it 14% on Rotten Tomatoes and 23 on Metacritic, although Mark Kermode of The Observer gave it three stars and praised Pike's icy zeal.

title: Mr. Right
tagline: They make a killer couple.
overview: A girl falls for the "perfect" guy, who happens to have a very fatal flaw: he's a hitman on the run from the crime cartels who employ him.
plot:
Mr. Right is an American romantic action comedy of 2015 directed by Paco Cabezas from a screenplay by Max Landis. Anna Kendrick stars as Martha McKay, a relentlessly upbeat young woman who discovers that her new boyfriend is a former hitman, played by Sam Rockwell, with Tim Roth as his old partner and mentor Hopper, James Ransone and Anson Mount as the brothers Von and Richard Cartigan and RZA as the gunman Steve.

Francis Munch, a former CIA agent turned mercenary, has developed the habit of killing the people who try to hire him to kill. After one such job he survives an ambush by a team including a killer named Espinoza; Hopper backs out of the attack and merely watches. Munch then asks out Martha, and they fall for each other at once. After he dodges another attempt by Espinoza, they spend a chaste night together, and the following evening he reluctantly kills Espinoza when attacked over dinner. Over hot chocolate, Munch explains that a current runs beneath all things that can be sensed in advance, and that she shares the gift; when he throws a knife at her, she catches it by the blade without a scratch.

Von Cartigan, the sole survivor of an earlier massacre in which Munch wiped out the Pirrello heroin syndicate, plots with his partner Johnny Moon to have his brother Richard killed by Munch, knowing that Munch kills those who hire him. Munch kills the middleman sent instead in front of Martha, who asks for space. Richard sends Von, Moon and a squad of hitmen, including Steve, to Martha's apartment. Munch fights them off but is hit by Steve and captured, and Moon seizes Martha. At the Cartigan house, Martha defiantly announces that she will kill her captors if Munch doesn't. Munch arrives, shares gummy bears with Steve, shoots the bodyguards and leaves the brothers to fight over a gun; Von kills Richard. When Moon threatens her, Martha's own powers awaken, and she kills him and shoots Von with his own gun. Hopper handcuffs himself to Munch to reprogram him as a killer, but Munch frees himself and Steve shoots Hopper dead, delighted to claim a $5 million bounty. Two months later, Munch and Martha travel the world pursuing her interest in palaeontology, and when a sniper targets them, it is Martha who takes him out.

The film closed the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2015 and was released in the United States by Focus World in April 2016. Critics liked the leads' chemistry but not the tonal jumble, giving it 44% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Magnificent Seven
tagline: Justice has a number.
overview: Looking to mine for gold, greedy industrialist Bartholomew Bogue seizes control of the Old West town of Rose Creek. Chisolm recruits an eclectic group of gunslingers to take on Bogue and his ruthless henchmen. With a deadly showdown on the horizon, the seven mercenaries soon find themselves fighting for more than just money once the bullets start to fly.
plot:
The Magnificent Seven is a 2016 American Western action film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Nic Pizzolatto and Richard Wenk. A remake of the 1960 film, which was itself a remake of Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai, it stars Denzel Washington, Chris Pratt, Ethan Hawke, Vincent D'Onofrio, Lee Byung-hun, Manuel Garcia-Rulfo and Martin Sensmeier as the seven gunmen, with Peter Sarsgaard as the villain Bartholomew Bogue and Haley Bennett as Emma Cullen. It was the final film scored by James Horner, who died in 2015 after composing part of the music, which was completed by Simon Franglen. The film opened the 2016 Toronto International Film Festival and closed the Venice Film Festival.

In 1879, the ruthless industrialist Bartholomew Bogue and his army of private agents take control of the frontier town of Rose Creek, forcing its residents to work in his gold mine for a pittance. When the townspeople protest, Bogue has their church burned and several citizens shot dead in public, including the farmer Matthew Cullen. He gives the survivors three weeks to sell him their land at a fraction of its value.

Matthew's widow Emma and her friend Teddy set out to hire men who can defend the town. Their first recruit is the bounty hunter Sam Chisholm, played by Washington, who shows particular interest when he hears Bogue's name. Chisholm assembles a band of six others: the gambler and trick shooter Josh Faraday, played by Pratt; the Mexican outlaw Vasquez; the haunted Confederate sharpshooter Goodnight Robicheaux, played by Hawke; his companion, the knife-wielding assassin Billy Rocks, played by Lee; the eccentric tracker Jack Horne, played by D'Onofrio; and the Comanche warrior Red Harvest. The seven ride into Rose Creek and wipe out the agents guarding the town, sending a message to Bogue. Knowing that he will return with a much larger force, they have only days to train the frightened townspeople and fortify Rose Creek for a final battle, while Chisholm's personal reasons for confronting Bogue gradually come to light.

Fuqua's version emphasises the diversity of its heroes and stages large-scale action sequences and an extended climactic battle.

The Magnificent Seven received mixed to positive reviews, with about 64 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised the cast and action while noting the lack of originality. It was a moderate success, grossing about 162 million dollars worldwide against a budget of around 90 million.

title: Woodlawn
tagline: One Hope. One Truth. One Way (John 14:6)
overview: Love and unity in a school torn by racism and hate in the 1970s. A gifted high school football player must learn to embrace his talent and his faith as he battles racial tensions on and off the field.
plot:
Woodlawn is a 2015 American Christian sports drama directed by the Erwin Brothers, Jon and Andrew Erwin, and based on the true story of coach Tandy Gerelds and running back Tony Nathan at Woodlawn High School in Birmingham, Alabama. Caleb Castille plays Nathan and Nic Bishop plays Gerelds, with Sean Astin as the sports chaplain Hank Erwin, the directors' father, Sherri Shepherd as Nathan's mother Louise, Jon Voight as the Alabama coach Paul "Bear" Bryant, and C. Thomas Howell in a supporting role. Produced by Kevin Downes and Daryl Lefever with Crescent City Pictures and Red Sky Studios, it was released by Pure Flix Entertainment on 16 October 2015.

In 1973, Woodlawn High School is desegregated amid fierce controversy, and the gifted Black athlete Tony Nathan and several other Black students join its predominantly white football team. Coach Gerelds urges his players to channel their anger into their game, but the racial divisions of the city spill over into the team, and Black and white players clash both on and off the field. After a riot erupts at the school, Gerelds reluctantly allows Hank Erwin, a travelling sports chaplain, to address the team as a motivational speaker.

Erwin's message of faith and reconciliation has an unexpected effect: many of the players commit themselves to Christianity and begin to see each other as brothers rather than rivals. As the team's unity grows, Nathan emerges as a star, becoming one of the first Black football heroes in Alabama, and his talent attracts the attention of college recruiters. The team's success builds toward what became one of the most celebrated high school football games in the state's history, played before an enormous crowd, while Gerelds, who is initially sceptical of religion, must confront his own beliefs and his responsibility to his players during a time of racial tension.

Nathan later played for Bear Bryant at the University of Alabama and for Don Shula's Miami Dolphins, where he started in two Super Bowls, and the film's closing scenes reflect on the lasting impact of the Woodlawn team. It presents the story as an example of a spiritual revival bringing a divided community together.

Woodlawn grossed about 14.4 million dollars and received generally positive reviews, with a 79 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a rare A+ grade from CinemaScore audiences.

title: Survivor
tagline: His next target is now hunting him
overview: A Foreign Service Officer in London tries to prevent a terrorist attack set to hit New York, but is forced to go on the run when she is framed for crimes she did not commit.
plot:
Survivor is a 2015 action spy thriller directed by James McTeigue and written by Philip Shelby. Milla Jovovich stars as Kate Abbott, a Diplomatic Security Service agent, and Pierce Brosnan as a deadly assassin known as the Watchmaker, with Dylan McDermott, Robert Forster, Angela Bassett, James D'Arcy, Frances de la Tour, Genevieve O'Reilly and, in his final film role, Roger Rees. The film was released in cinemas in the United Kingdom on 5 June 2015 and direct-to-video in the United States later that month.

During a firefight in the Middle East, an American soldier, Johnny Talbot, is captured by terrorists and forced to watch the execution of a comrade. In London, Kate Abbott, who joined government service after losing friends in the September 11 attacks, works at the American Embassy screening visa applications to keep terrorists out of the United States, and introduces stricter checks. When her colleagues gather at a restaurant for the birthday of their superior, Bill Talbot, a bomb explodes, killing most of her team. Kate survives only because she stepped out to buy a last-minute present. Bill, it emerges, is Johnny's father and has been blackmailed into approving visas for terrorists under threat to his son's life.

Fleeing the bomber, Kate is attacked by Bill and kills him in self-defense, and witnesses and camera footage make her the prime suspect in the attack. Investigators find traces of chromium in the bomb, leading her superior at the embassy, Sam Parker, to conclude that the killer is the Watchmaker, one of the world's most wanted assassins, known for his precision. Hunted by the police and by the Watchmaker, who has been hired to eliminate her, Kate goes on the run through London, trying to clear her name and uncover a plot by a terrorist network and its financier to carry out a devastating attack in New York's Times Square on New Year's Eve. With few allies she can trust, she must reach New York and stop the attack before midnight, while the Watchmaker closes in.

Survivor received almost uniformly negative reviews, holding an 8 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it borrowed heavily from better films in the service of a predictable story. IGN gave it 5 out of 10. Critics found Brosnan's villainous turn one of the few highlights of an otherwise generic thriller.

title: Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie

overview: When a ghost-infecting virus known as Fire-Starter begins spreading through the system resulting in the assassination of the Japanese Prime Minister, Major Motoko Kusanagi and her elite team of special operatives are called in to track down its source.
plot:
Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie is a thought-provoking anime film that explores several complex themes. Here are some of the main themes present in the movie:

1. **Existentialism and Identity**: The film delves into the nature of existence, consciousness, and identity. The protagonist, Major Motoko Kusanagi, grapples with her own existence as a cyborg, questioning what it means to be human. This theme is further explored through the character of Batou, who struggles with his own sense of self.

2. **Artificial Intelligence and Humanity**: The movie raises questions about the ethics of creating artificial intelligence that surpasses human capabilities. The cyberpunk world of Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie highlights the blurred lines between humans and machines, making it difficult to distinguish between the two.

3. **Power and Corruption**: The film explores the corrupting influence of power, particularly in the context of government agencies and corporations. The villainous character, Aramaki, represents a powerful figure who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals, highlighting the dangers of unchecked power.

4. **Free Will and Determinism**: The movie touches on the theme of free will versus determinism, as Major Kusanagi navigates her own destiny and confronts the possibility that her actions may be predetermined by external forces.

5. **Social Commentary**: Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie offers a commentary on contemporary societal issues, such as government surveillance, corporate control, and the impact of technology on human relationships.

6. **Self-Discovery and Personal Growth**: Throughout the film, Major Kusanagi undergoes a journey of self-discovery, confronting her own limitations and biases to become a more effective and compassionate leader.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story. The movie's exploration of these ideas makes it a thought-provoking and engaging watch for audiences interested in science fiction and philosophical inquiry.

title: Criminal Activities

overview: Four young men make a risky investment together that gets them into trouble with the mob.
plot:
Criminal Activities is a 2015 American crime thriller directed by Jackie Earle Haley in his directorial debut and written by Robert Lowell. Michael Pitt, Dan Stevens, Christopher Abbott, Rob Brown, Edi Gathegi and Haley star, with John Travolta as a mobster. RLJ Entertainment and Image Entertainment released it in the United States on November 20, 2015.

Four friends, tempted by a tip based on insider information, decide to invest heavily in a company whose stock is supposedly certain to multiply in value. To raise the money they borrow from a mysterious financial backer. The scheme collapses almost immediately: the company folds under federal scrutiny, wiping out their investment, and their benefactor turns out to be Eddie, a polished and seemingly friendly mid-level gangster who expects to be repaid.

Eddie offers the young men a way out of their debt. All they have to do is kidnap a man and hold him for 24 hours before handing him over, after which their obligation will be forgiven and everyone can go their separate ways. The job quickly proves far more complicated than promised. Their captive turns out to be the nephew of a rival mob boss, who is offering a two million dollar reward to whoever returns his relative, and the friends learn that they are expected to take part in killing their hostage before they will be allowed to leave the building. Tensions erupt within the group as loyalties are tested, panic sets in and they argue over what to do with the man tied up in their makeshift hideout.

As the night unfolds, it becomes clear that things are rarely what they seem. The motivations of the various players, including Eddie, the hostage and the friends themselves, differ from what they initially appear to be, and the film builds toward a series of revelations that recasts the events that came before.

Filming took place in Cleveland, Ohio, from May 27 to June 26, 2014; the story was originally set in Detroit. Image Entertainment acquired the film for release in the United States and the United Kingdom in the fall of 2015. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reports a 50% approval rating from 20 reviews, and Metacritic assigned a score of 51 out of 100.

title: 100 Streets
tagline: Anybody can take a wrong turn.
overview: Three people, three extraordinary stories. All lived out within a hundred London streets.
plot:
100 Streets is a 2016 British ensemble drama directed by Jim O'Hanlon from a screenplay by first-time feature writer Leon F. Butler, who also produced and raised its roughly £3 million budget from private investors. Idris Elba, who also served as a producer, stars alongside Gemma Arterton, Franz Drameh, Ken Stott, Charlie Creed-Miles, Kierston Wareing, Tom Cullen and Jo Martin. The production companies included CrossDay Productions and Green Door Pictures and the music is by Paul Saunderson. The title comes from Cicely Fox Smith's poem "The Oldest Thing in London".

The film weaves together three stories unfolding at the same time within about one square mile of London, each centered on a man forced to face the consequences of his past actions as he struggles toward a better life. In wealthy Chelsea, Max (Elba), a celebrated former England rugby captain, is in a bitter trial separation from his wife Emily (Arterton), an actress who gave up her career, after his infidelity came to light. As she tries to return to the stage and drifts into a romance with her old flame Jake (Cullen), Max sinks into heavy drinking and cocaine use. On a council estate south of the river, Kingsley (Drameh), a teenager with a gift for words and performance, has slipped into drug dealing and gang violence, to the dismay of his weary single mother (Martin), until a chance encounter with the aging actor Terence (Stott) offers him a way out through the theatre. Between these two worlds, the gentle cab driver George (Creed-Miles) and his patient wife Kathy (Wareing) hope to adopt a child and start a family, but their plans are thrown into turmoil when George is involved in a fatal road accident. As the stories progress, chance meetings and coincidences increasingly connect the characters, showing how circumstance and choice shape their fates.

The film premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival in June 2016, opened in British cinemas through Vertigo on 11 November 2016, and reached American theaters and video-on-demand via Samuel Goldwyn Films on 13 January 2017. Critical reception was lukewarm, with 41% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44, the consensus finding its talented cast stranded in a well-meaning but contrived drama. Variety likened it to a gentler London version of Crash, praising Drameh's promising performance, Arterton and Blaubach's bright cinematography but calling the script banal, while The Guardian also considered it a misfire.

Captain Fantastic is a 2016 American drama film directed by Matt Ross and written by Matt Ross. The movie stars Viggo Mortensen, Frank Langella, and Kesten Halpin.

The story revolves around Ben Cash (Viggo Mortensen), a father who has chosen to raise his six children in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest, away from modern society. After their mother's death, Ben became disillusioned with the world and its values, leading him to reject the conventional norms of society. title: Cristiano Ronaldo: World at His Feet
original_title: Cristiano Ronaldo: World at His Feet
overview: Cristiano Ronaldo: The World at His Feet follows the footballer from his beginnings in Portugal, breakthrough start with Manchester United and current career at Real Madrid.
plot:
Cristiano Ronaldo: The World at His Feet is a 2014 documentary film directed by Tara Pirnia and written by Nick Silverman, profiling the Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, who was then playing for Real Madrid and captaining Portugal. Narrated by Benedict Cumberbatch, it runs just under an hour and was first released online through Vimeo in June 2014; it was later distributed on DVD by Vision Films. Ronaldo himself appears in interview, and David Beckham is among the other figures featured.

The film follows Ronaldo from his humble childhood on the island of Madeira to his status as a global sports star and celebrity. It portrays a poor upbringing and a solitary boy whose constant companion was a football. In one of the comparatively rare passages in which he speaks directly to the camera, Ronaldo explains that there was no single reason he took up the game, citing his father and brother as influences rather than claiming a lifelong dream. He joined the local club Andorinha at eight and moved to Sporting Lisbon at twelve, after scouts noticed his talent.

The documentary recounts the turning point of August 2003, when, after Sporting played Manchester United, the English club's players urged manager Sir Alex Ferguson to sign the teenager. Ferguson, presented as a father figure, gave him the famous number 7 shirt, and Ronaldo went on to become a superstar in England, regarded as a hero by some and an arrogant villain by others, before his move to Real Madrid. Combining interviews, archival and recent match footage and dramatised re-enactments, the film charts his awards, his rivalry and constant comparison with Lionel Messi, and his gradual maturing from self-absorbed playboy into a philanthropist and role model. Among the commentators is West Ham United's youth development director Anthony Carr, who explains what scouts look for in young players.

Reviews were mixed. Tom Keogh of Video Librarian gave it three out of five, calling it a brisk and exciting profile and recommending it. Charles Low of Kettle Mag found Cumberbatch's narration tasteful if puzzling and appreciated some insightful interviews, but felt the film zig-zagged between key moments, padded itself with general football commentary and pointless contributors such as an astrologer and skateboarder Tony Hawk, and relied on odd re-enactments that left it somewhere between a celebrity documentary and a sports broadcast, offering less insight into the man himself than he had hoped.

Lionsgate released the film in the United States in October 2017.

The ponies of Equestria are preparing for their first Friendship Festival, organised by Princess Twilight Sparkle in Canterlot, when the celebration is interrupted by an invading army. It is led by Tempest Shadow, a unicorn with a broken horn who serves the Storm King, a ruler who has promised to restore her horn in exchange for capturing the princesses of Equestria and using their magic to empower his staff. Tempest turns Princesses Celestia, Luna and Cadance to stone, but Twilight escapes with her friends Pinkie Pie, Rainbow Dash, Rarity, Applejack, Fluttershy and the young dragon Spike.

Following Celestia's incomplete instructions to seek the "queen of the hippos", the friends travel beyond Equestria for the first time. In the desert city of Klugetown they meet Capper, a smooth-talking cat who offers to guide them while secretly planning to sell them to a crime boss to pay off his debts. As Capper develops genuine feelings of friendship, Twilight discovers that the creatures they seek are hippogriffs. Their journey takes them aboard an airship crewed by former pirates, and eventually to a hidden underwater kingdom where the hippogriffs have transformed themselves into seaponies to escape the Storm King. Under increasing pressure, Twilight makes a desperate decision that threatens her friendships, while Tempest closes in on her.

The film celebrates friendship, trust and redemption, especially through Tempest's backstory, and it features original songs, including a number performed by Sia.

The film received mixed to negative reviews, with about 49 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but it was a box-office success, grossing more than 61 million dollars worldwide against a production budget of 6.5 million.

title: Risen

overview: Clavius, a powerful Roman military tribune, and his aide, Lucius, are tasked with solving the mystery of what happened to Jesus in the weeks following the crucifixion, in order to disprove the rumors of a risen Messiah and prevent an uprising in Jerusalem.
plot:
Risen is a 2016 biblical drama film directed by Kevin Reynolds and written by Reynolds and Paul Aiello. An American-Spanish co-production starring Joseph Fiennes, Tom Felton, Peter Firth and Cliff Curtis, it tells the story of the resurrection of Jesus through the eyes of a Roman soldier who is ordered to find his missing body. The project began in 2013 as The Resurrection of Jesus Christ, conceived as a mystery thriller and an unofficial sequel to The Passion of the Christ, and was filmed in Malta and Spain between August and November 2015.

Clavius, a Roman tribune of the Legio X Fretensis, crushes a rebellion of zealots led by Barabbas and then oversees the crucifixion of Yeshua, posting guards at the tomb. When the body vanishes, rumors spread that Yeshua's followers stole it to make it appear he had risen from the dead. Pontius Pilate, eager to prevent unrest in Jerusalem before the Emperor's visit, orders Clavius to find the corpse. With his aide Lucius, Clavius interrogates people who claim to have seen Yeshua alive, but their accounts grow ever more miraculous, and followers such as Mary Magdalene and Bartholomew answer only in riddles. As his investigation unsettles Romans and Jews alike, Pilate grows distant. Clavius forces one of the tomb's disgraced guards to abandon his cover story, and the drunken soldier describes a blinding flash, the tomb's seals disintegrating and a figure emerging. Clavius refuses to believe it until, during a raid, he comes face to face with Yeshua, alive among his apostles, the same man he watched die on the cross. Shaken, he calls off the search and soon abandons his old life and gods to follow the group, befriending the apostle Peter and talking with Yeshua as they travel, while Pilate sends Lucius and a contingent of soldiers after him. Clavius helps the disciples evade the pursuing Romans and witnesses Yeshua heal a leper and ascend to heaven, before the apostles part to spread their message and Clavius reflects on how his life has been transformed.

Columbia Pictures released Risen in the United States on February 19, 2016. It grossed $46.8 million worldwide against a $20 million budget and received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 53%, with a consensus praising its lighter tone and a terrific turn from Fiennes, and audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore.

title: Renegades
tagline: 5 Navy SEALs. $300 million in gold. 1 incredible mission.
overview: In the midst of the Balkan wars, a squad of Navy SEALs attempts to unravel a long-forgotten mystery after discovering an enormous treasure trove hidden at the bottom of a lake in Serbia.
plot:
Renegades, released in the United States as American Renegades, is a 2017 English-language action thriller directed by Steven Quale from a screenplay by Luc Besson and Richard Wenk. Produced by Besson's company EuropaCorp, it stars Sullivan Stapleton as Navy SEAL team leader Matt Barnes, J. K. Simmons as Rear Admiral Levin, Charlie Bewley as Stanton Baker and Sylvia Hoeks as Lara Simić, with Clemens Schick, Diarmaid Murtagh, Joshua Henry, Dimitri Leonidas and Ewen Bremner in supporting roles. After its release was postponed several times, it opened in Germany on 1 September 2017 and in France in August 2018.

The film begins in August 1944, when retreating German forces move looted treasure, including roughly 25 tons of gold ingots, from Paris to the small Bosnian town of Bosansko Grahovo, where it is locked in the bank vault. The Germans massacre the townspeople, and only a small boy escapes to be found by Yugoslav partisans. In revenge for the massacre, partisans later blow up a nearby dam, flooding the town and leaving the gold submerged.

In 1995, during the Bosnian War, a team of American Navy SEALs disguised as journalists captures the Bosnian Serb general Milić, a war criminal responsible for atrocities against civilians. Their escape, which involves a stolen tank and considerable damage to the city, earns them a reprimand from Admiral Levin and a three-day leave. Baker becomes romantically involved with Lara, a local waitress, and when thugs led by her brother come to threaten her, Barnes intervenes. Lara then reveals the secret of the gold lying at the bottom of the lake and explains that it could rebuild her war-torn community. Seeing an opportunity to help her people and enrich themselves, the SEALs devise an unauthorised plan to dive to the drowned town, break into the vault and raise the gold without their commanders finding out, while Milić's second-in-command Petrović and his forces close in.

The film mixes heist caper, underwater action and military adventure, with much of its spectacle derived from the sequences filmed in large water tanks. Its tone alternates between humour among the team members and violent set pieces.

title: Circle
tagline: In here…everything gets you killed.
overview: In a massive, mysterious chamber, fifty strangers awaken to find themselves trapped with no memory of how they got there.  Organized in an inward-facing circle and unable to move, they quickly learn that every two minutes, one of them must die…executed by a strange device in the center of the room.
plot:
Circle is a 2015 American science fiction psychological thriller film written and directed by Aaron Hann and Mario Miscione. Inspired by the 1957 courtroom drama 12 Angry Men, it features an ensemble cast that includes Carter Jenkins, Lawrence Kao, Allegra Masters, Michael Nardelli, Julie Benz, Mercy Malick, Lisa Pelikan and Cesar Garcia. Shot in 2014, it premiered at the Seattle International Film Festival on May 28, 2015, and was released on video on demand in October of that year.

Fifty strangers wake up in a dark room, standing on platforms arranged in two concentric circles around a black dome. Anyone who steps away from their spot or touches another person is killed by a beam from the dome, and every two minutes the device kills someone else. The captives soon work out that they are voting, through small hand gestures, on who dies next, and that refusing to vote simply leaves the choice to chance. To buy time, they agree to eliminate the oldest among them first while they try to understand where they are; several remember fleeing Los Angeles and being pulled into the sky, and one elderly man insists he saw aliens, but the group refuses to listen. As the rounds continue, the debate turns ugly. People confess to affairs and violence, accusations of racism, homophobia and hypocrisy are traded, and each prejudice becomes a reason to target someone. A few volunteers sacrifice themselves to give the others more time. Eventually the survivors realize that only one person can be left standing, and they split into factions: one wants to protect a pregnant woman and a little girl at all costs, while the other argues that no one deserves special treatment. Alliances shift, lies are exposed, and the ever-shrinking circle is forced to decide who, if anyone, deserves to survive.

The film received a mixed response. On Rotten Tomatoes, four of seven critics' reviews are positive. John DeFore of The Hollywood Reporter described it as a "Twilight Zone-y drama" that works better than expected, and Tony Kay of City Arts praised the way it engineers suspense and the puzzle-box appeal of piecing together what is going on as each execution approaches.

title: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny

overview: Finding himself in a new era, approaching retirement, Indy wrestles with fitting into a world that seems to have outgrown him. plot:
Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny is a 2023 American action-adventure directed by James Mangold, who wrote it with David Koepp, Jez Butterworth and John-Henry Butterworth. The fifth and final film in the Indiana Jones series and a sequel to Kingdom of the Crystal Skull (2008), it stars Harrison Ford, with Phoebe Waller-Bridge as his goddaughter Helena Shaw, Mads Mikkelsen as the former Nazi scientist Jürgen Voller, and Antonio Banderas, Boyd Holbrook and Toby Jones, while Karen Allen and John Rhys-Davies return.

In the final days of the Second World War, Indiana Jones and the Oxford archaeologist Basil Shaw are captured by Nazis while trying to recover the Lance of Longinus. The astrophysicist Voller discovers that the relic is fake but that he has found half of Archimedes' Dial, a device said to locate fissures in time. Jones seizes the piece aboard a train loaded with plunder and escapes with Basil.

In 1969, Jones is retiring from teaching in New York and is separated from his wife Marion after the death of their son in Vietnam. Basil's daughter Helena turns up wanting the Dial, which her father had asked Jones to destroy. Voller, now working for NASA, attacks them with CIA help; Helena, a smuggler, flees with the artefact, and Jones, framed for murder, escapes the city with the help of his old friend Sallah.

In Tangier, Jones breaks up Helena's black-market auction, but Voller steals the Dial. With Helena's young accomplice Teddy, they follow Voller to Greece, where Jones's diver friend Renaldo helps them recover a tablet from the Antikythera wreck before Voller kills him. In Sicily they find Archimedes' tomb and the second half of the device, but Voller captures Jones, assembles the Dial and flies toward a fissure, hoping to reach 1939 and change the outcome of the war.

Because of continental drift, the plane instead arrives at the Siege of Syracuse in 214 BC and is shot down, killing Voller. Jones meets Archimedes and wants to remain in the past, but Helena knocks him out and brings him home, where he reconciles with Marion.

The film grossed $384 million worldwide against a budget of nearly $300 million, making it one of the most expensive films ever made, and it holds a 71% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Glass Castle
overview: A young girl is raised in a dysfunctional family constantly on the run from the FBI. Living in poverty, she comes of age guided by her drunkard, ingenious father who distracts her with magical stories to keep her mind off the family's dire state, and her selfish, nonconformist mother who has no intention of raising a family, along with her younger brother and sister, and her other older sister. Together, they fend for each other as they mature in an unorthodox journey that is their family life.
plot:
The Glass Castle is a 2017 American biographical drama directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, who wrote the screenplay with Andrew Lanham and Marti Noxon, based on Jeannette Walls's best-selling 2005 memoir about growing up in poverty with her unconventional parents. Lionsgate acquired the rights in 2012 with Jennifer Lawrence in talks to star, but Brie Larson took over the lead in 2015. Filming began on May 20, 2016, in Welch, West Virginia, and Lionsgate released the film on August 11, 2017.

Young Jeannette grows up on the move with her painter mother, Rose Mary, her brilliant but irresponsible, hard-drinking father, Rex, and her siblings Lori, Brian and later Maureen. After she is badly burned cooking alone, Rex sneaks her out of the hospital before social workers can intervene, and enchants her with plans to build the family a dream house of glass. On the run from the law and out of money, the family settles in a ramshackle house without utilities in Welch, near the children's grandmother Erma. Rex briefly beats his drinking by tying himself to his bed, but relapses, refuses to believe that Erma has sexually abused Brian, and fights violently with Rose Mary. The children promise to look after each other and escape. Lori leaves for New York, and after one of Rex's pool hustles leaves her fending off an attempted rape and he steals her savings, Jeannette follows.

By 1989 Jeannette is a gossip columnist for New York magazine engaged to David, a financial analyst, and lies to his clients about her family while her parents are homeless and squatting in the city. After Rex punches David and Jeannette learns that her parents had owned land worth nearly $1 million all along, she disowns her father. Unhappily married, she at first refuses to visit when Rex is dying, but eventually tells the truth about her upbringing and reconciles with him before his death. Divorced and working as a freelance writer, she later spends Thanksgiving with her family, remembering him.

Larson plays Jeannette, Woody Harrelson plays Rex, Naomi Watts plays Rose Mary, Sarah Snook plays Lori and Max Greenfield plays David. Critics praised the cast, especially Larson, but found the adaptation too forgiving of the parents, giving it 52% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed $22 million in North America.

title: Heist
tagline: Never make a bet you can't afford to lose.
overview: A father is without the means to pay for his daughter's medical treatment. As a last resort, he partners with a greedy co-worker to rob a casino. When things go awry they're forced to hijack a city bus.
plot:
Heist, also released as Bus 657, is a 2015 American action thriller directed by Scott Mann and written by Stephen Cyrus Sepher and Max Adams from an original story by Sepher. It stars Jeffrey Dean Morgan as Luke Vaughn, Robert De Niro as the casino owner known as the Pope, Dave Bautista as Cox and Gina Carano as police officer Kris Bajos, with Kate Bosworth, Morris Chestnut and Sepher. The story follows a desperate father whose casino robbery turns into a hostage crisis aboard a city bus.

Luke Vaughn works at a casino in the American South run by Francis Silva, a ruthless boss nicknamed the Pope. Vaughn's young daughter is seriously ill and needs an operation costing 300,000 dollars. When he asks the Pope for a loan, he is refused, fired and beaten by Silva's enforcer, Dog. A security guard named Cox then tells Vaughn that the casino launders money for the mob and proposes a robbery. Because Vaughn knows the vault codes, he agrees to join Cox's crew, and they steal the cash.

The getaway goes wrong when Dog's men intercept the thieves, a gunfight leaves one of the crew wounded and their driver abandons them. The robbers hijack a city bus full of passengers, pursued by Officer Bajos, and soon the police set up roadblocks. Vaughn tries to keep the hostages safe and negotiates with Bajos through a pregnant passenger's phone, while the volatile Cox threatens to kill people if the police do not back off. As the bus races along the highway and runs low on fuel, Detective Marconi and a SWAT team prepare to intervene, while the Pope sends Dog to recover his money at any cost. Vaughn must keep everyone alive, outwit both the police and the mob and find a way to get the money to his daughter.

The film combines a heist story with the confined, high-speed tension of a bus hijacking, setting a father's desperation against the brutality of organized crime.

Heist was released by Lionsgate Premiere on November 13, 2015. It received negative reviews, with 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that its all-star cast was dealt a poor hand by a humorless potboiler, and a Metacritic score of 37.

title: Mulan
overview: When the Emperor of China issues a decree that one man per family must serve in the Imperial Chinese Army to defend the country from Huns, Hua Mulan, the eldest daughter of an honored warrior, steps in to take the place of her ailing father. She is spirited, determined and quick on her feet. Disguised as a man by the name of Hua Jun, she is tested every step of the way and must harness her innermost strength and embrace her true potential.
plot:
Mulan is an American fantasy action drama of 2020 produced by Walt Disney Pictures, directed by Niki Caro and written by Rick Jaffa, Amanda Silver, Lauren Hynek and Elizabeth Martin. A live-action adaptation of Disney's 1998 animated film, itself drawn from the Chinese Ballad of Mulan, it stars Liu Yifei as Hua Mulan, with Donnie Yen as Commander Tung, Gong Li as the shapeshifting witch Xianniang, Jason Scott Lee as the Rouran leader Böri Khan, Yoson An as Chen Honghui, Tzi Ma as Mulan's father Hua Zhou and Jet Li as the Emperor.

In imperial China, spirited Mulan worries her parents, who hope to see her well married, and a disastrous visit to the matchmaker shames her family. In the north, Rouran warriors led by Böri Khan overrun an imperial outpost, aided by Xianniang, who disguises herself as a surviving soldier to report the attack. The Emperor orders every family to provide one man for the army, and Mulan's father, who has no sons and an injured leg, volunteers. Knowing he would not survive, Mulan takes his armour, horse and sword and enlists in his place, posing as a man.

At the training camp of Commander Tung, an old comrade of her father, Mulan becomes a skilled soldier while keeping her secret. As the Rourans advance, the recruits are sent into battle, and Xianniang confronts Mulan, mocking her disguise. Casting off her male identity, Mulan turns the enemy's trebuchet against a snowy mountainside, burying the Rourans in an avalanche, and rescues Honghui. When she confesses the truth, Tung expels her. Xianniang, herself an outcast, then reveals that the raids were a diversion and that Böri Khan intends to kill the Emperor, who had his father put to death. Risking execution, Mulan returns to warn the army; her comrades stand by her and Tung lets her lead a unit to the capital. There, Xianniang, impersonating the Chancellor, has lured the Emperor into a trap. Disillusioned with the Khan, the witch takes the form of a hawk and dies intercepting an arrow aimed at Mulan, who defeats Böri Khan and frees the Emperor. Declining a place in his guard, she returns home, where Tung brings her a new sword and an invitation to join the army as an officer.

Shot in New Zealand and China in 2018 on a reported budget of about $200 million, it was released on Disney+ Premier Access in September 2020 after pandemic delays and flopped in cinemas. Critics praised its visuals, giving it 72% on Rotten Tomatoes, while filming in Xinjiang drew criticism.

The story follows Estella de Vil (Emma Stone), a young woman who grows up in an orphanage with her two friends, Lucy and Adrian. Their cruel and abusive caretaker, Miss Havisham, instills in them a deep-seated hatred for luxury and wealth. As they grow older, the three women become embroiled in a world of high society, where Estella catches the eye of the wealthy and influential Baroness von Hellman (Carlyle).

The Baroness takes Estella under her wing, teaching her the art of fashion and introducing her to the world of luxury. However, as Estella becomes more and more entrenched in this world, she begins to lose touch with her friends and her own sense of identity.

As Estella's obsession with fur grows, she becomes fixated on acquiring the finest pelts for her designs. Her fixation leads her down a dark path, where she will stop at nothing to get what she wants. The film takes a darker turn as Estella's transformation into the infamous Cruella de Vil begins.

Throughout the film, Emma Stone delivers a captivating performance, bringing depth and nuance to the character of Estella. The supporting cast, including Emma Thompson as Lady Danbury and Joel Fry as Jasper, add to the film's humor and charm.

title: Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle
original_title: Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle
overview: When Curious George is offered a special space mission, Ted (The Man in the Yellow Hat) can't deny his little friend this exciting journey, especially after Curious George completes the training. But when he crash-lands in Africa, a worried Ted goes searching, expecting the worst, only to have it turn out to be the best.
plot:
Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle is a 2015 American traditionally animated family adventure film directed by Phil Weinstein and written by Chuck Tately, based on the Curious George books by Margret and H. A. Rey. Produced by Imagine Entertainment, Universal 1440 Entertainment and WGBH, with music by Heitor Pereira, it is the third film in the franchise and the second to skip theaters. Frank Welker and Jeff Bennett return as the voices of George and his friend Ted, the Man with the Yellow Hat, joined by John Goodman as Hal Houston, Angela Bassett as Dr. Kulinda and Alexander Polinsky as Andrew.

After a hectic kite chase in the park, George and Ted are approached by Houston, an official of a space agency, who offers George a once-in-a-lifetime mission. As part of a project to stop the floods devastating a region of Central Africa, George is to fly into orbit, retrieve a device called the Regional Dam Synchronizer from a broken satellite, and bring it back so that it can be installed on a dam, where its antenna will coordinate the other dams in the area. Ted is reluctant at first, but agrees after George's pleading, on the condition that he complete the astronaut training, which he does.

The first part of the mission goes smoothly, and George retrieves the device, but during the return his curiosity sends the capsule's systems haywire and it plunges toward Earth. George ejects and lands somewhere in the African jungle, while the capsule disappears with the device still on board. Houston, his assistant Andrew and Ted travel to Africa, where search teams scour an area hundreds of miles wide; eventually Ted sets out on his own, cut off from contact with Houston. Back in the land of his birth, George meets Dr. Kulinda, a veterinarian who runs an animal preserve. The friends must find each other, recover the device and install it before a huge storm bearing down on the region can ravage the jungle, and in the end they complete the mission in time.

The film was released on DVD by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on 23 June 2015 and later aired on PBS Kids. It was the last film in the series to use traditional animation. Reviewers praised its fast, suspenseful yet gentle storytelling, bright visuals and lack of a conventional villain, with the storm serving as the main threat, as well as songs such as "Ordinary Superman".

title: It's Only the End of the World
tagline: It would have been a lovely family dinner. If it weren’t the last.
overview: Louis, a terminally ill writer, returns home after a long absence to tell his family that he is dying.
plot:
It's Only the End of the World is a poignant and introspective film that delves into the complexities of human relationships, love, and mortality. The movie follows Antoine, a man who has been diagnosed with terminal cancer, as he embarks on a journey to visit all his former lovers in one day.

At its core, the film explores the theme of regret and the what-ifs that haunt us throughout our lives. Antoine's decision to confront each of his past loves is motivated by a desire to understand why he never took a chance on any of them, and to make amends for the opportunities he let slip away. As he navigates these encounters, the film reveals the fragility of human connections and the ease with which they can be lost.

The movie also grapples with the concept of time and its relationship to human experience. Antoine's journey is a metaphor for the way we all try to make sense of our lives by compressing time into a single, decisive moment. The film suggests that this approach can be both liberating and suffocating, as it forces us to confront the choices we've made and the paths not taken.

Furthermore, It's Only the End of the World is a deeply empathetic portrayal of a man struggling to come to terms with his own mortality. Antoine's story is one of quiet desperation, as he tries to find meaning in a world that seems determined to deny him its beauty and joy. The film's exploration of grief, loss, and longing is both heart-wrenching and profoundly moving.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced and compassionate portrait of human vulnerability, one that acknowledges our capacity for love, regret, and self-discovery. Through Antoine's journey, we are invited to reflect on our own lives, to consider the choices we've made, and to cherish the time we have with those we love.

plot:
Bloodshot is a 2020 American science fiction action film directed by David S. Goyer and starring Vin Diesel. The movie is based on the Valiant Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with Ray Garrison (Vin Diesel), a former Special Forces operative who was severely injured during his last mission. He is recruited by the government agency known as "The Agency" to participate in an experimental program called "Operation Bloodshot." This program uses advanced technology to enhance human soldiers' abilities, allowing them to fight more effectively.

Ray's body is subjected to the technology, which enhances his strength, speed, and agility. However, the process also has a devastating side effect: it slowly kills Ray's body over time, forcing him to live in a state of limbo between life and death.

The Agency uses Ray as a test subject for their new technology, but he soon discovers that they have ulterior motives. They plan to use his enhanced abilities to carry out covert operations without being detected. Ray is horrified by this revelation and decides to take matters into his own hands.

As Ray delves deeper into the truth about Operation Bloodshot, he uncovers a conspiracy involving corrupt government officials and The Agency's true intentions. He also discovers that his wife, Kate (Vanessa Kirby), has been kidnapped by The Agency, who plan to use her as leverage to control Ray.

Ray sets out on a mission to rescue Kate and take down The Agency from the inside. Along the way, he encounters other enhanced operatives, including Wolf (Samuel L. Jackson) and Dr. Karen Fischer (Deborah Ann Woll). Together, they form an uneasy alliance to take down their common enemy.

As Ray navigates this complex web of intrigue, he must also confront his own mortality. He knows that his time is limited, and he must make the most of it before he dies. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Ray and the leader of The Agency, who will stop at nothing to achieve their goals.

Throughout the film, Vin Diesel delivers a strong performance as the titular character, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and troubled hero. The action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling, with impressive visual effects that bring the enhanced operatives to life.

Overall, Bloodshot is an action-packed sci-fi thriller that explores themes of identity, mortality, and the ethics of advanced technology. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of Vin Diesel and science fiction will likely find plenty to enjoy in this visually stunning and entertaining film.

title: Hell or High Water

overview: A divorced dad and his ex-con brother resort to a desperate scheme in order to save their family's farm in West Texas.
plot:
Hell or High Water is a 2016 American crime drama film directed by David Mackenzie and written by Taylor Sheridan. The movie stars Chris Pine, Ben Foster, Jeff Bridges, and Toni Collette.

The story begins with two brothers, Toby (Ben Foster) and Tanner (Chris Pine), who are struggling to make ends meet in rural Texas. After their father's death, the brothers are forced to take over his mortgage payments for a large sum of money. However, they soon discover that the bank is unwilling to work with them, leading them to come up with a plan to rob several banks across Texas.

The brothers' motivations for robbing the banks are complex and multifaceted. On one hand, they are desperate to save their family's farm from foreclosure. On the other hand, they are also seeking revenge against the bank that has wronged them in the past. As they embark on their heist, they begin to develop a sense of camaraderie and brotherly love.

As the brothers continue to rob banks, they attract the attention of Texas Ranger Marcus Hamilton (Jeff Bridges), who is determined to bring them to justice. However, as Hamilton delves deeper into the case, he begins to see the brothers in a different light. He becomes fascinated by their story and starts to question his own motivations for pursuing them.

Meanwhile, Toby's wife, Ali (Toni Collette), is struggling to cope with her husband's absence and the financial strain of raising their two children on her own. As the situation escalates, she begins to realize that her family's fate is inextricably linked to her husband's actions.

Throughout the film, Mackenzie uses the Texas landscape as a character in its own right, capturing the beauty and desolation of the rural landscape. The cinematography is stunning, with sweeping vistas and intimate close-ups that bring the characters and their world to life.

As the story unfolds, the brothers' actions become increasingly desperate and reckless. They are forced to confront the consequences of their choices, including the risk of imprisonment and the potential harm they may cause to innocent people.

In the end, the film builds towards a tense and emotional confrontation between the brothers and Hamilton. The outcome is far from certain, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats as they wonder what will happen next.

Ultimately, Hell or High Water is a powerful exploration of family, loyalty, and redemption. It is a story about two brothers who are driven by love and desperation to do whatever it takes to protect their family and their way of life. The film's themes of brotherly love and the complexities of human relationships are both poignant and thought-provoking.

The performances in the film are outstanding, with Ben Foster and Chris Pine delivering nuanced and compelling portrayals of the brothers. Jeff Bridges brings his signature gravitas to the role of Hamilton, while Toni Collette shines as Toby's wife, Ali.

Overall, Hell or High Water is a gripping and emotionally resonant film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of our choices.

title: Hellraiser
tagline: Unlock your fears.
overview: A young woman struggling with addiction comes into possession of an ancient puzzle box, unaware that its purpose is to summon the Cenobites, a group of sadistic supernatural beings from another dimension.
plot:
Hellraiser is a 2022 supernatural horror film directed by David Bruckner from a screenplay by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski, based on a story they wrote with David S. Goyer. The eleventh film in the franchise drawn from Clive Barker's 1986 novella The Hellbound Heart, it stars Odessa A'zion as Riley McKendry, a young woman recovering from addiction, with Jamie Clayton, Adam Faison, Drew Starkey, Brandon Flynn and Goran Višnjić.

At an orgy in his mansion, hedonistic millionaire Roland Voight gives a puzzle box to a young man, Joey, whose attempt to solve it springs a blade that cuts him and opens a portal from which chains tear him apart. Six years later, Riley lives with her brother, Matt, his boyfriend, Colin, and their roommate, Nora. She and her boyfriend, Trevor, find the box in an abandoned warehouse, and after Matt accuses her of relapsing, she storms out and solves it in a park, narrowly avoiding the blade. The Cenobites, mutilated beings from another dimension, appear and demand a sacrifice. Matt, searching for her, cuts himself on the box and vanishes.

Riley and Trevor visit Voight's former lawyer, Serena Menaker, who tries to take the box but is cut and later abducted. In Voight's empty mansion, Riley learns from his journals that each of the box's six configurations requires a victim marked by the blade, after which its holder receives a "gift" from Leviathan, the ruler of Hell. Nora is stabbed by the mutilated Voight, hidden in the walls, and is flayed by the Cenobites' leader, the Priest, who offers Riley a deal: two more sacrifices or herself. Riley marks the Cenobite known as the Chatterer, who is ripped apart. Voight reappears, stabs Colin and reveals that his own reward was a device that endlessly twists his nerves, and that Trevor has been working for him to find victims. When Voight traps the Cenobites to bargain for release, Riley marks Trevor as the final sacrifice. Voight chooses "power" and is healed, only to be impaled by Leviathan's chain and later remade as a Cenobite. Offered Matt's resurrection, Riley refuses, accepting his death, and leaves with Colin.

The film premiered at Fantastic Fest on September 28, 2022, and was released on Hulu on October 7. Reviews were generally positive, with 67% on Rotten Tomatoes and 55 on Metacritic, critics calling it a welcome revival after a string of weak sequels.

title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald
original_title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald
tagline: Fate of one. Future of all.
overview: Gellert Grindelwald has escaped imprisonment and has begun gathering followers to his cause—elevating wizards above all non-magical beings. The only one capable of putting a stop to him is the wizard he once called his closest friend, Albus Dumbledore. However, Dumbledore will need to seek help from the wizard who had thwarted Grindelwald once before, his former student Newt Scamander, who agrees to help, unaware of the dangers that lie ahead. Lines are drawn as love and loyalty are tested, even among the truest friends and family, in an increasingly divided wizarding world.
plot:
Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald is a 2018 American fantasy film directed by David Yates and the sequel to Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (2016). The movie takes place in 1927, one year after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Newt Scamander (Eddie Redmayne), a magizoologist who is on the run from the Ministry of Magic. He is being pursued by the Auror Office, led by Alastor Moody (Jude Law), who believes that Newt has stolen a powerful magical creature known as the Bowtruckle.

Meanwhile, Gellert Grindelwald (Johnny Depp) is on the loose, and his true intentions are revealed. He is a dark wizard who seeks to dominate the wizarding world and establish a new order with himself at the helm. Grindelwald's ultimate goal is to create a magical utopia where wizards and non-magical people coexist.

Newt meets Leta Lestrange (Zoe Kravitz), an old friend from his past, who has been hiding secrets of her own. She reveals that she was in love with Newt, but he rejected her due to their complicated history. This revelation sets off a chain of events as Newt and Leta become entangled in Grindelwald's plans.

As the story unfolds, we see Grindelwald's rise to power, and his manipulation of the wizarding world. He uses his charisma and magical abilities to recruit followers and gain control over various magical creatures. The movie also explores the backstory of Credence Barebone (Ezra Miller), a young man with mysterious powers who is being manipulated by Grindelwald.

The plot thickens as Newt, Leta, and Albus Dumbledore's (Jude Law) past come into play. We learn that Dumbledore was once in love with Gellert Grindelwald, but their relationship ended due to his dark ambitions. The movie also reveals the tragic fate of Grindelwald's sister, Ariana, who was killed by a group of wizards who were angry about her association with Grindelwald.

As the story reaches its climax, Newt and Leta must navigate their complicated past while trying to stop Grindelwald's plans. The movie features an epic battle between good and evil, with the fate of the wizarding world hanging in the balance.

The ending sets up a thrilling conclusion for the Fantastic Beasts series, as Newt and his allies prepare to face off against Grindelwald once again. The movie concludes on a cliffhanger, leaving audiences eager to see what happens next in the story.

Overall, Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of love, power, and redemption. With its richly detailed world-building and complex characters, this movie is sure to delight fans of the wizarding world.

plot:
Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore is a 2022 American fantasy adventure film directed by David Yates, and it is the third installment in the Fantastic Beasts series, which is set in the Harry Potter universe.

plot:
Disenchanted is a 2022 American musical fantasy comedy film directed by Kevin Lima, produced by Walt Disney Pictures, and distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures.

The movie serves as a sequel to the 2007 film Enchanted, which was also produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The story follows Giselle (played by Amy Adams), a princess from the magical kingdom of Andalasia who has been living in the real world with her husband Robert (Patrick Dempsey) and their daughter Morgan (James Marsden).

The movie begins with Giselle's life being turned upside down when she discovers that her stepson, Harry (Gabriel Macht), is getting married. Feeling left out and struggling to connect with her family, Giselle decides to take a trip back to Andalasia to reconnect with her roots and find herself.

Upon her return, Giselle finds that the kingdom has changed significantly since she left. The once-peaceful land is now plagued by darkness and evil forces led by Queen Narissa (Idina Menzel), who seeks revenge against Giselle for abandoning her throne.

As Giselle navigates this new reality, she must confront her own flaws and weaknesses, as well as the consequences of her actions in the real world. Along the way, she teams up with a group of rebels, including a charming and handsome prince named Edward (Maya Rudolph), to overthrow Queen Narissa and save Andalasia.

Throughout the movie, Giselle's character undergoes significant development as she learns to let go of her idealized notions of happily ever after and instead finds strength in her own agency and vulnerability. The film features a range of catchy musical numbers, including "Happy Working Song" and "I'm a Believer," which showcase Adams' impressive vocal talents.

Overall, Disenchanted is a heartwarming and entertaining sequel that explores themes of identity, family, and the complexities of growing up. With its lighthearted tone and engaging storyline, it's sure to delight fans of the original Enchanted film and newcomers alike.

title: Zombieland: Double Tap
overview: Columbus, Tallahassee, Wichita, and Little Rock move to the American heartland as they face off against evolved zombies, fellow survivors, and the growing pains of the snarky makeshift family.
plot:
Zombieland: Double Tap is a 2019 American zombie comedy film directed by David Leitch and written by Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, and Ike Barinholtz. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2009 film Zombieland.

The story begins with Columbus (Jesse Eisenberg), Tallahassee (Woody Harrelson), Wichita (Emma Stone), and Little Rock (Abigail Breslin) living in a post-apocalyptic world where zombies roam freely. The group has been surviving together, but they've started to feel the effects of isolation and boredom.

The movie opens with Columbus and Tallahassee on a road trip to a zombie-free amusement park called "Wonderland," which is rumored to be filled with all the fun rides and attractions that were lost in the pre-apocalyptic world. Along the way, they meet a new character, Madison (Zoey Deutch), who claims to have found a safe haven for survivors.

As they journey to Wonderland, the group faces various obstacles, including hordes of zombies, other survivors with questionable intentions, and their own personal demons. Meanwhile, Wichita is struggling to come to terms with her past and her feelings about being part of a group that's constantly on the move.

Upon arriving at Wonderland, the group discovers that it's not as zombie-free as they thought. The park has been taken over by a new threat: a group of young survivors who are determined to take down the old guard and claim the park for themselves.

As tensions rise, Columbus and Tallahassee must confront their own mortality and the reality of their situation. They also have to navigate their complicated relationships with each other and the rest of the group. Along the way, they meet a new character, Seattle (Rosie Perez), who becomes an ally in their quest for survival.

Throughout the movie, the characters face numerous challenges, including zombie hordes, treacherous terrain, and personal conflicts. However, they also experience moments of humor, heart, and connection that make the film feel like a loving tribute to the original Zombieland.

Ultimately, Columbus and Tallahassee must decide what's most important: their own survival or the future of humanity. The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between the old guard and the new generation of survivors, with the fate of Wonderland hanging in the balance.

In the end, the group emerges victorious, but not without scars. They've learned to adapt to a changing world and find new ways to survive and thrive in a post-apocalyptic landscape. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Columbus and Tallahassee riding off into the sunset, ready for their next adventure together.

Overall, Zombieland: Double Tap is a fun, action-packed sequel that expands on the characters and world of the original film. It's a loving tribute to the zombie genre and a testament to the enduring power of friendship and community in the face of adversity.

title: Tomb Raider
tagline: Her legend begins.
overview: Lara Croft, the fiercely independent daughter of a missing adventurer, must push herself beyond her limits when she finds herself on the island where her father disappeared.
plot:
Tomb Raider is a 2018 action-adventure film directed by Roar Uthaug and written by Geneva Robertson-Dworet and Alastair Siddons, based on the video game series and chiefly on the 2013 game. An American and British co-production, it reboots the film series with Alicia Vikander as Lara Croft, who travels to her father's last known destination to solve the mystery of his disappearance. Dominic West plays her father Lord Richard Croft, Walton Goggins the rival archaeologist Mathias Vogel, Daniel Wu the ship captain Lu Ren and Kristin Scott Thomas Ana Miller, an associate at Croft Holdings.

Refusing to accept that her missing father is dead, Lara works as a bicycle courier in London. After Ana bails her out of a police arrest, she warns her that Croft Manor will be sold unless she claims her inheritance. Reluctantly agreeing, Lara finds a secret chamber in her father's tomb containing a video message about his research into Himiko, the mythical Queen of Yamatai said to command power over life and death, and his instruction to destroy his work. Instead, she pawns the jade pendant he gave her and travels to Hong Kong, where she hires Lu Ren to sail his ship into the Devil's Sea in search of the island of Yamatai. The ship is wrecked in a storm, and Lara washes ashore into the hands of Mathias, who leads an expedition funded by a shadowy organization called Trinity that wants to weaponize Himiko's power. Claiming he killed her father, Mathias enslaves Lara and Lu, but Lara escapes and finds Richard alive, hiding on the island to keep Trinity away from the tomb. With help from Lu and the other slaves, she steals Mathias's satellite phone, but Richard is captured and Mathias forces Lara to open the tomb. Inside, they discover that Himiko carried a deadly infectious disease and had entombed herself to protect others. Mathias cuts off one of her fingers to take back to Trinity, and Richard, now infected, sacrifices himself by blowing up the tomb, while Lara forces Mathias to swallow the finger and kicks him into a pit before escaping with Lu by helicopter. Back in London, she accepts her inheritance, finds evidence that Croft Holdings is linked to Trinity and that Ana may be its agent, and reclaims her pendant as she prepares for her next adventure.

Released in the United Kingdom on March 14, 2018, and in the United States two days later, the film received mixed reviews, with a 52% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and grossed $275 million worldwide.

title: Georgetown
overview: Ulrich Mott  is an eccentric and versatile social climber with grandiose plans to affect United States foreign policy. Encouraged  in his attempts by his strategically chosen (and much older) wife, the well-connected journalist Elsa Brecht, Mott has a knack for making himself indispensable and impossible to ignore. The only one seemingly immune to his charms is Elsa's daughter Amanda, who might simply disapprove of her mother marrying a much younger man - or perhaps she senses something more sinister beneath the smooth-talking surface?
plot:
Georgetown is a 2019 American crime drama directed by Christoph Waltz in his feature directorial debut and written by David Auburn. It is based on Franklin Foer's 2012 New York Times Magazine article "The Worst Marriage in Georgetown", about the 2011 killing of 91-year-old socialite Viola Herms Drath by her much younger husband. Waltz stars as Ulrich Mott, with Vanessa Redgrave as Elsa Breht, Annette Bening as her daughter, Amanda.

Told out of sequence, the story follows Ulrich, a fifty-year-old conman and social climber interning for a congressman, using his boss's ID card to slip into a banquet, where he meets Elsa, a wealthy, elderly journalist and socialite living in Georgetown. Posing as a doctoral student, he arranges a lunch with her. After her husband dies, Elsa retreats from society, worrying Amanda, until Ulrich calls on the eve of 2000 and invites her to a concert. Amanda, delighted by her mother's renewed energy, announces she has been offered a tenured law professorship at Harvard and asks Elsa to move to Boston, but Elsa declines, and Ulrich tells the dismayed gathering that he and Elsa will marry.

Elsa uses her connections to advance Ulrich's one-man consulting agency, which he fills with prominent names through lies. In 2004, after Iraqi diplomats humiliatingly reject his offer to broker peace talks, he comes home drunk and nearly causes Elsa to fall down the stairs. She grows suspicious of his sexuality and, in 2006, finds him in bed with a man in a New York hotel; after he throws her out, she reports him to police for assault. Ulrich then vanishes for two years, claiming to be a freelance peace envoy in Iraq, and returns hailed as a diplomatic miracle worker. After an argument following a dinner party, he goes for a walk and later says he came home to find Elsa dead. Charged with murder, he hides key facts from his lawyers, then fires them, goes on a hunger strike and is hospitalized. An epilogue shows Ulrich being rebuffed by his former lover that night, then confronted by Elsa, who has discovered that he spent his absence as a motel desk clerk in Miami; as she calls him an idiot, he rushes up the stairs toward her.

Filmed in Toronto in 2017, Georgetown premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 27, 2019, and received a limited U.S. release from Vertical Entertainment on May 14, 2021. Reviews were mixed, at 63% on Rotten Tomatoes and 49 on Metacritic, with The New York Times calling Waltz a pleasure to watch.

Solace is a 2015 American action thriller film directed by Dennis Gansel and starring Anthony Hopkins, Colin Farrell, Abbie Cornish, and Forest Whitaker.

The movie begins with Michael "Mike" Bowen (Colin Farrell), an assassin who suffers from dissociative identity disorder (DID). He has multiple personalities, each with its own distinct personality, skills, and memories. Mike's latest target is a former CIA operative named Rachel Jenkins (Abbie Cornish) who has stolen classified information.

As Mike tries to eliminate Rachel, he begins to experience flashbacks of his past traumas, which are triggered by the presence of certain objects or people. He also starts to develop feelings for Rachel, but struggles with controlling his multiple personalities.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as "The Architect" (Anthony Hopkins) is revealed to be behind the assassinations and the theft of classified information. The Architect is a mastermind who uses advanced technology to manipulate and control people's memories, making them believe they are someone else or that their past events never occurred.

As Mike delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that his own past is shrouded in secrecy. He begins to question his own identity and the nature of his DID. With the help of Rachel, a former CIA operative turned psychologist, Dr. Kathryn "Kate" Hawkins (Abbie Cornish), Mike starts to unravel the truth about The Architect's plans.

The plot thickens as Mike and Kate work together to stop The Architect, who is using advanced technology to manipulate world events from behind the scenes. Along the way, Mike's multiple personalities begin to surface, causing chaos and confusion.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Architect has a personal connection to Mike's past, which is slowly revealed through flashbacks and conversations with Kate. The Architect's true identity is eventually exposed, and Mike must confront his own demons in order to stop him.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between Mike and The Architect, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Mike emerges victorious, but not without scars. He has finally found a sense of peace and control over his multiple personalities, thanks to Kate's help.

Throughout the film, Anthony Hopkins delivers a chilling performance as The Architect, bringing depth and complexity to the character. Colin Farrell also shines as Mike, conveying the vulnerability and intensity required for the role. Abbie Cornish provides a strong supporting performance as Kate, who helps Mike navigate his complex past.

Overall, Solace is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of identity, trauma, and redemption. With its intricate plot and strong performances, it's a gripping watch from start to finish.

title: Tremors 5: Bloodlines
overview: The giant, man-eating Graboids are back and even deadlier than before, terrorizing the inhabitants of a South African wildlife reserve as they attack from below-and above.
plot:
Tremors 5: Bloodlines is a 2015 direct-to-video monster horror film directed by Don Michael Paul and produced by Ogden Gavanski. The fifth film in the Tremors franchise and the first in eleven years, it served as Universal Pictures' relaunch of the series and was the first entry made without Stampede Entertainment, the company of series creators S. S. Wilson and Brent Maddock. Michael Gross returns as the survivalist Burt Gummer, joined by Jamie Kennedy as his cameraman Travis Welker, Pearl Thusi as Dr. Nandi Montabu, Rea Rangaka as Baruti, Brandon Auret as Johan Dreyer, Daniel Janks as Erich Van Wyk, Nolitha Zulu as Amahle and Ian Roberts as the pilot Den Bravers.

Burt, now the star of his own survivalist web series, and Travis are hired by South African wildlife agents Van Wyk and Dreyer to deal with Ass-Blasters. Burt's heavy weapons are impounded under South African gun laws, leaving him with guns he considers too small. The team bases itself at an animal refuge, where Travis befriends the young Amahle and falls for her mother Nandi, sparking a rivalry with the local man Baruti. After two paleontologists are devoured at a dig, Burt realizes the creatures are a new breed of Graboid. When a refuge worker is carried off, Burt kills an Ass-Blaster in a cave, though its falling body kills Dreyer. Discovering that the creatures have been laying Graboid eggs, Van Wyk reveals himself as a poacher, locks Burt in a cage and steals the eggs, only to be eaten by a huge Graboid with detachable tentacles that Burt dubs the "Queen Bitch". With help from Den's helicopter rockets, Burt destroys the nest, and on the way back Travis reveals that he is Burt's son, the result of a one-night stand in Florida forty years earlier. At the refuge, Nandi, Amahle and Baruti fend off further attacks and learn that Amahle has been hiding a Graboid egg, which is why the creatures keep coming. As the creature besieges the village, Nandi proposes using the daily thunderstorm: the villagers build a metal trap, and lightning destroys both the egg and the Queen Bitch. Burt accepts Travis as his son, and the two go on to co-host his show, hunting monsters around the world.

Released on October 6, 2015, the film divided critics, with some welcoming the series' revival and others calling it generic without its creators' humour. It earned about $2.7 million from domestic home video sales, and a sequel, Tremors: A Cold Day in Hell, followed in 2018.

Throughout the film, the director uses vivid imagery and cinematography to convey the harsh realities of prison life. The performances by the cast are also noteworthy, particularly Coster-Waldau's portrayal of Jacob Harford, who undergoes a remarkable transformation from a privileged businessman to a hardened inmate.

The ending of Shot Caller is intense and emotional, as Jacob faces a difficult decision that will determine his future. Overall, Shot Caller is a gripping drama that explores themes of survival, redemption, and personal growth in the harsh environment of prison. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, who delivers a powerful performance as Jacob Harford.
