tagline: She lost him, but she found herself. And somehow that was everything.

plot:
The 1989 World Tour Live is a 2015 American concert film by the singer-songwriter Taylor Swift, documenting her fourth concert tour, the 1989 World Tour, staged in support of her fifth studio album, 1989 (2014), her first record marketed as pop rather than country. Directed by Jonas Åkerlund and produced in partnership with Apple Music, the film was shot at the show of 28 November 2015 at ANZ Stadium in Sydney, Australia, and also includes behind-the-scenes footage and appearances by special guests from shows in North America and Europe. Its release marked Swift's first collaboration with Apple, coming months after she pulled her catalog from Spotify over its payment model and after Apple agreed to pay artists during the free trial period of its streaming service.

The concert opens with black-and-white projections of street scenes as Swift rises from beneath the stage to sing "Welcome to New York," followed by "New Romantics" and "Blank Space," and an industrial rock version of "I Knew You Were Trouble." The set moves through "I Wish You Would," a Singin' in the Rain-inspired staging of "How You Get the Girl" with dancers twirling neon umbrellas, and "I Know Places," in which masked dancers chase her through moving doors. Swift introduces "Clean" by sharing lessons from her personal life and performs a synth-driven "Love Story" on an elevated platform that sweeps around the stadium. Later highlights include "Style," "This Love," "Bad Blood" in a black leather suit, a rock rendition of "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together" on electric guitar, a piano mashup of "Enchanted" and "Wildest Dreams," and "Out of the Woods" beneath giant paper planes, before the show closes with "Shake It Off" on a platform above the crowd amid fireworks and confetti.

The tour began in Tokyo on 5 May 2015 and ended in Melbourne on 12 December, spanning 85 shows. It was the highest-grossing tour of 2015, selling more than 2.27 million tickets and grossing over 250 million dollars, and critics praised Swift's stage presence and connection with her audience, while her parade of celebrity guests drew wide comment. Announced on 13 December 2015, the film premiered exclusively on Apple Music on 20 December 2015 and remained on the service until 22 May 2020; footage from it was also used in the music video for "New Romantics."

title: One Piece: Adventure of Nebulandia

overview: Kōmei devises a plan where Zoro and Sanji take part in an eating contest, and the two eat a strange "good-for-nothing-only" mushroom that turns them into good-for-nothing men. plot:
One Piece: Adventure of Nebulandia is a 2015 Japanese animated television special based on the One Piece manga and anime and produced by Toei Animation. Directed by Konosuke Uda, the original series director of the One Piece anime, from a screenplay by Atsuhiro Tomioka, it was broadcast on 19 December 2015 in the Saturday Premium slot as the sixth One Piece special in that slot, following Episode of Sabo earlier that year. Unlike specials that retell manga arcs, it is an original story, and it brings back the Foxy Pirates, the crew the Straw Hats defeated in the anime's Davy Back Fight arc, with new members. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in March 2016.

Sailing in the New World, Monkey D. Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates are challenged by Captain Foxy to a Davy Back Fight rematch. The contest is a trap devised by Kōmei, a brilliant strategist who has recently joined Foxy's crew. During an eating contest, Zoro and Sanji consume a strange mushroom that saps their strength and turns them into good-for-nothings, and the pair are captured and carried away. Chasing their friends, the Straw Hats reach Nebulandia, an island shrouded in a mist formed from sea water that, like seastone, neutralises the powers of Devil Fruit users. Their arrival is exactly what Kōmei planned.

Kōmei is in fact a vice admiral of the Navy and a special operations strategist who infiltrated the Foxy Pirates by deliberately losing to them. Having lost his home town to pirates as a child, he despises them and dreams of proving that ordinary people without powers can defeat Devil Fruit users through cunning, thereby changing the Navy itself. Luffy is forced into an uneasy alliance with his old Davy Back rival Foxy for the rescue. Using the island's terrain and a series of traps, especially the pitfalls he favours, Kōmei captures Robin, Franky and Usopp, but Brook and Chopper, searching for an antidote to the mushroom, foil his attempt to seize Luffy. In the final battle, Kōmei floods his base with sea water to weaken Luffy, but Foxy's Slow-Slow Beam and a pitfall turn the tables, and Luffy defeats him with a decisive blow.

The regular voice cast returns, led by Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, Kazuya Nakai as Zoro and Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji, with Toshio Shimada as Foxy. Ichikawa Ennosuke voices Kōmei, a role he modelled on the Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang, while Hoka Kinoshita plays another new crew member who is secretly a Navy officer.

After the Storm (Japanese: 海よりもまだ深く, Umi yori mo Mada Fukaku, "Even Deeper than the Sea") is a 2016 Japanese family drama film written, directed and edited by Hirokazu Kore-eda. Hiroshi Abe stars as a failed novelist, with Kirin Kiki as his mother, Yoko Maki as his former wife and Taiyo Yoshizawa as his son. It premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2016 Cannes Film Festival and was released in Japan on May 21, 2016.

Ryota once won a minor literary prize for his only novel, and still clings to the idea that he is a serious writer. In reality, he works at a small private detective agency, where he sometimes supplements his income by blackmailing the people he is hired to investigate, and squanders his money on gambling, leaving him unable to pay child support. He turns down an offer to write for a manga series, considering it beneath him, while telling people he is researching his next book.

Since the recent death of Ryota's father, a gambler like his son, his widowed mother, Yoshiko, lives alone and seems to be moving on, taking up hobbies with other elderly women. Ryota visits her frequently. His sister, Chinatsu, suspects his motives, and he in turn suspects that she is sponging off their mother. When Ryota goes to an old hiding place where his mother used to conceal money from his father, he finds only cardboard and a teasing note from his sister.

Meanwhile, Ryota's former wife, Kyoko, has lost patience with his excuses, and threatens to stop his monthly visits with their young son, Shingo, unless he pays what he owes. Ryota, jealous of Kyoko's new boyfriend, fears that her remarriage would cost him his relationship with his son. During one of his visits with Shingo, a typhoon strikes, and Ryota, Kyoko and the boy are forced to spend the night at his mother's apartment. As the storm rages, Kyoko tells Ryota that their marriage is truly over, explaining that adults cannot live on love alone and that he never acted like a family man when it mattered. Accepting this, Ryota takes Shingo out into the storm to shelter in a playground structure, as he once did with his own father, and the two share a rare moment of connection. In the morning, the storm has passed, and they go their separate ways.

After the Storm received critical acclaim, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 96% approval and a consensus praising its timeless observations on parental responsibility, personal bonds and forgiveness.

title: Dunkirk

overview: The story of the miraculous evacuation of Allied soldiers from Belgium, Britain, Canada and France, who were cut off and surrounded by the German army from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk between May 26th and June 4th 1940 during World War II.
plot:
Dunkirk is a 2017 war drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. The film is set during World War II and tells the story of the Dunkirk evacuation, also known as the Miracle of Dunkirk.

The film begins on May 26, 1940, with a dramatic sequence showing the German army's invasion of France. The British Expeditionary Force (BEF), led by General Lord Gort, is trapped in Dunkirk, a coastal town in northern France. As the Germans close in, the BEF is surrounded and outnumbered.

The story then shifts to three main plot threads: the evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk, the rescue efforts by the Royal Air Force (RAF), and the experiences of a young British soldier named Tommy (Fionn Whitehead). The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, with each thread intersecting and overlapping at various points.

The evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk is depicted as a chaotic and desperate effort. Thousands of soldiers are stranded on the beaches of Dunkirk, with no clear way to escape. The British Navy, led by Admiral Bertram Ramsay (Kenneth Branagh), launches a massive rescue operation, with ships and boats converging on the beach to evacuate the soldiers.

Meanwhile, the RAF is engaged in a fierce dogfight with German aircraft, trying to protect the evacuation fleet from enemy attack. The film's aerial sequences are intense and suspenseful, showcasing the bravery and skill of the RAF pilots.

Tommy, who has been separated from his family during the evacuation, finds himself on the beach, struggling to survive amidst the chaos. He joins a group of other soldiers, including Mr. Dawson (Mark Rylance), a civilian who is helping to evacuate the soldiers. As they try to escape, Tommy and Mr. Dawson face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy fire, and personal losses.

As the evacuation continues, the film's narrative builds towards a dramatic climax. The British Navy launches a final push to clear the beach of German forces, while the RAF provides cover with its aircraft. The soldiers are finally able to escape, but not before many have lost their lives or been separated from their loved ones.

The film ends with Tommy, who has survived the evacuation, watching as the last of the ships depart from Dunkirk. He is reunited with his family, who had been searching for him throughout the ordeal. The final shot is of a small boat, which is revealed to be carrying Mr. Dawson's body, symbolizing the sacrifice and bravery of those who helped evacuate the soldiers.

Throughout the film, Nolan uses innovative cinematography and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and urgency. The film's score, composed by Hans Zimmer, adds to the emotional impact of the story. Overall, Dunkirk is a powerful and moving tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of those who fought in World War II.

title: Duck Duck Goose
tagline: Family can be a wild ride
overview: After he’s grounded by an injury, a high-flying bachelor is saddled with two wide-eyed orphans as they come face-to-face with the dangers and beauty of the outside world.
plot:
Duck Duck Goose (Chinese: 妈妈咪鸭) is a 2018 animated adventure comedy film directed by Chris Jenkins, who wrote the original story and co-wrote the screenplay with Rob Muir, Scott Atkinson and Tegan West. An international co-production between the United States, China and the United Kingdom, it features the voices of Jim Gaffigan as Peng, a self-absorbed swan goose, Zendaya and Lance Lim as the Mandarin duckling siblings Chi and Chao, Greg Proops as the villainous Pallas's cat Banzou, Reggie Watts as the flying squirrel Carl, and Carl Reiner as Larry, a softshell turtle, with Natasha Leggero, Stephen Fry, Craig Ferguson and Diedrich Bader.

Peng is a carefree goose whose reckless attitude irritates Bing, the leader of his flock, which departs on its migration across China while he sleeps. One of his careless stunts separates two ducklings, Chi and Chao, from their own flock as it travels to a fabled place called Pleasant Valley. Seeing Peng drive off the predatory Banzou, the ducklings shelter beside him for the night. Startled to find them, Peng flies off carelessly, crashes into a gong and breaks his wing. Unable to fly and afraid of predators, he decides to use the ducklings as cover while he makes his way back to his flock, and they reluctantly join him.

Through a string of misadventures Peng grows fond of the ducklings, but when they encounter his flock, Chi and Chao discover his selfish motives and the two parties go their separate ways. Peng is knocked out of the sky by Carl, who fits him with a makeshift wing, and he sets off to find the ducklings. They meanwhile reunite with their flock and learn that Pleasant Valley is really a restaurant that cooks ducklings. Peng rescues them, but they are separated again in the escape, and Banzou takes the ducklings hostage. Peng is badly hurt fighting him, and Chi and Chao finish off the cat by launching him into the sky on a rocket. Carrying the weakened Peng through a snowstorm toward the geese's spring, the ducklings use a honk he taught them to summon Jingjing, Peng's love interest, who rescues him. Bing welcomes the ducklings into the flock, along with a newly responsible Peng.

The film opened in China on March 9, 2018. A North American theatrical release planned by Open Road Films for April 2018 was canceled when the company closed, and Netflix released it in North America on July 20, 2018. It grossed about $15.3 million worldwide in its initial run and received negative reviews from critics.

Abigail is a clever and ambitious young woman from a lower social class, determined to rise through the ranks of society.

Abigail quickly catches the eye of the Queen, who becomes infatuated with her charming personality and wit. As Abigail's influence grows, she begins to manipulate the Queen into making decisions that benefit herself and her family. Meanwhile, Sarah Churchill's power and influence begin to wane as a result of Abigail's rise.

As tensions between the three women escalate, the palace becomes a battleground for power and loyalty. The Queen is torn between her affection for Abigail and her duty to her adviser, Sarah. Abigail, on the other hand, uses her charm and cunning to turn the Queen against Sarah, ultimately leading to her downfall.

Throughout the film, Lanthimos employs his signature deadpan humor and absurdity, often using long takes and unsettling silences to create a sense of unease. The performances by Colman, Stone, and Weisz are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

One of the most striking aspects of The Favourite is its exploration of themes such as power, ambition, and female relationships. The film raises questions about the nature of femininity and how women are perceived in society, particularly during this time period.

Ultimately, Abigail's machinations lead to a tragic confrontation between the three women. In the end, only one woman emerges victorious, but at what cost? The Favourite is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that offers a fresh perspective on a pivotal moment in history.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, with many praising its performances, direction, and screenplay. It won numerous awards, including several Academy Awards, and cemented the status of Yorgos Lanthimos as one of the most innovative filmmakers working today.

The Girl with All the Gifts is a 2016 British post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Colm McCarthy, based on the novel of the same name by M.R. Carey.

In a world devastated by a zombie-like fungal infection that turns humans into mindless, violent creatures, a young girl named Melanie (Dakota Buddie) lives in an underground bunker with a small group of survivors. The fungus, known as Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, has wiped out most of humanity and turned the remaining survivors into "Hungries," aggressive and zombie-like creatures that roam the earth.

Melanie is unique among the survivors because she appears to be immune to the infection. She is also incredibly intelligent and possesses a deep understanding of the fungus and its behavior. Melanie's existence is a mystery, even to herself, as she struggles to understand her own nature and purpose.

The story begins with Melanie being taken from the bunker by a scientist named Dr. Caldwell (Gugu Mbatha-Raw), who believes that Melanie may hold the key to finding a cure for the fungus. As they journey through the post-apocalyptic world, they encounter various groups of survivors, some of whom are hostile towards them.

Along the way, Melanie begins to exhibit strange behavior, including an intense desire to infect others with the fungus. Dr. Caldwell is unsure what to make of this behavior and is torn between his scientific curiosity and his growing concern for Melanie's well-being.

As they near their destination, a supposed safe haven called "Ark," Melanie's behavior becomes increasingly erratic. She begins to experience vivid hallucinations and visions, which seem to be connected to the fungus. It becomes clear that Melanie is not just immune to the infection, but may actually be a host for the fungus.

In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Melanie has been infected with the fungus from birth, and her unique behavior is a result of the fungus's influence on her mind. The fungus has been manipulating Melanie's thoughts and actions, using her as a vessel to spread its own kind.

As Dr. Caldwell and his team prepare to enter the Ark, they are met with resistance from the infected survivors. In a tense confrontation, Melanie is forced to confront her true nature and the reality of her existence. In a final act of self-sacrifice, Melanie deliberately infects herself with the fungus, allowing it to spread and potentially find a cure.

The film ends with Dr. Caldwell and his team entering the Ark, hopeful that they may have finally found a way to stop the fungal infection and restore humanity to its former glory. However, as they look out upon the desolate landscape, it is clear that the true extent of Melanie's sacrifice remains unknown, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of her actions.

Overall, The Girl with All the Gifts is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the nature of existence. With its unique blend of science fiction and horror elements, it has become a modern classic in the post-apocalyptic genre.

title: Robin Hood
tagline: The legend you know. The story you don't.
overview: A war-hardened Crusader and his Moorish commander mount an audacious revolt against the corrupt English crown.
plot:
Robin Hood is a 2018 American action-adventure film directed by Otto Bathurst and written by Ben Chandler and David James Kelly from Chandler's story, a modern retelling of the outlaw legend that centers on Robin's training by John. First announced in February 2015 with a Joby Harold script and Leonardo DiCaprio's Appian Way producing, the project was acquired by Lionsgate and cast Taron Egerton as Robin later that year. Eve Hewson, Jamie Foxx and Ben Mendelsohn followed, and filming ran from February to May 2017. The film was released by Lionsgate's Summit Entertainment on November 21, 2018.

Robin of Loxley, an aristocrat and skilled longbowman, lives in Nottingham with Marian until the corrupt Sheriff drafts him into the Third Crusade. Four years later, after he fails to stop his commander, Guy of Gisbourne, from executing unarmed prisoners, including a teenage boy, he is sent home accused of treason. He returns to learn from Friar Tuck that the Sheriff declared him dead and seized his estate to fund the war at the urging of Cardinal Franklin, while the townspeople have been driven into a mining settlement. Marian is now with Will Tillman, a would-be leader of the commoners. The father of the boy Robin tried to save, Yahya, who says his name translates as John, proposes that they end the war by stealing back the people's money.

After hard training in his ruined manor, Robin robs the Sheriff's coffers as a hooded thief nicknamed the Hood while posing as a frivolous lord loyal to the regime. He and Marian, who recognizes him by his voice, discover that the Church is secretly funding the Saracen army in order to topple the king and seize power. John is captured and tortured but reveals nothing. Robin reveals himself to the commoners, who embrace him, and seizes a caravan carrying the Sheriff's fortune to the Saracens while Will stages a riot. After Will, scarred during the fighting, sees Marian kiss Robin, he turns against them. Robin surrenders to end the bloodshed, but John, disguised as a guard, kills the Sheriff, and the rebels retreat as outlaws to Sherwood Forest. The Cardinal then installs a vengeful Will as sheriff, and Robin dares him to come after them.

Egerton stars with Foxx as John, Mendelsohn as the Sheriff, Hewson as Marian, Tim Minchin as Tuck and Jamie Dornan as Will. Critics panned it, with 14% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and comparisons to King Arthur: Legend of the Sword. It grossed about $85 million against a $100 million budget.

title: Then Came You
tagline: Living in the moment is hard to do alone.
overview: An American hypochondriac who is working as a baggage handler is forced to confront his fears when a British teenager with a terminal illness enlists him to help her carry out her eccentric bucket list.
plot:
Then Came You, also known as Departures, is an American romantic comedy-drama of 2018 directed by Peter Hutchings and written by Fergal Rock. Asa Butterfield plays Calvin Lewis, a young hypochondriac, and Maisie Williams plays Skye Aitken, a teenager with terminal cancer, with Nina Dobrev as the flight attendant Izzy, Tyler Hoechlin as Calvin's brother Frank, David Koechner as their father and Margot Bingham as Frank's wife Lucy.

Skye has been told that her cancer is in its final stages and that she has little time left. Calvin, an airport baggage handler, has a crush on Izzy and lives in constant fear of dying. His doctor sends him to a cancer support group for perspective. There he meets Skye, who takes an instant interest in him, and although he tries to explain that he does not actually have cancer, the two become friends and he agrees to help her complete her list of things to do before she dies. At first irritated by her bluntness and unpredictability, Calvin comes to treasure her company, and as they spend more time together his fear of death begins to fade.

Skye arranges a date between Calvin and Izzy, telling Izzy that he has cancer too, and the pair start dating. Skye admits she always knew Calvin was healthy, but he hesitates to tell Izzy, fearing she only likes him for his illness. From Lucy, Skye learns that Calvin's mother withdrew from life after his twin sister was killed at the age of eight in a car crash while their mother was driving. When Calvin finally confesses the truth, Izzy, hurt by the lie, breaks up with him, and he sinks into depression until his father persuades him to return to work. Skye, meanwhile, loses her virginity to Will, a boy she has a crush on, and finds the experience a letdown.

When Skye collapses and is taken to the hospital, Lucy goes into labor at the same time, and Frank and Lucy ask Calvin and Skye to be their baby's godparents. Calvin panics, but Frank reminds him that Skye still needs him. With help from Izzy and Skye's parents, he helps her finish her list, and he tells her that he stopped celebrating his birthday for his mother's sake after his sister's death. After Skye dies, birthday cards from her arrive in the mail to make up for the ones he missed. Overcoming his fear of heights, Calvin takes a flight, exchanging hopeful glances with Izzy.

 The film premiered at the Woodstock Film Festival in October 2018 and was released by Shout! Factory on 1 February 2019, to mixed reviews.

title: No Manches Frida
overview: After his release from prison, bank robber Zequi sets off to recover the stolen money that was buried by his dizzy accomplice. He's horrified to learn that a high school gymnasium is now standing over the site where the loot is stashed. Needing to infiltrate the building, Zequi lands a job as a substitute teacher for a group of wild and unruly students. As the ex-con tries to lay down the law, he starts to realize that life in jail may have been easier than trying to deal with rebellious teens.
plot:
No Manches Frida is a 2016 Spanish comedy film directed by Pablo Lombardo and written by Pablo Lombardo and Javier Gullón. The movie stars Karra Elejalde, Blanca Suárez, and Luis Zahera.

The story revolves around Carlos (played by Karra Elejalde), a former professional soccer player who has lost his passion for the game after a serious injury. He is now working as a coach at a local soccer school in Madrid, where he tries to teach young players the basics of the sport. However, his unorthodox coaching methods and lack of patience with his students make him unpopular among both the kids and their parents.

One day, Carlos receives an offer from a wealthy businessman named Juan (played by Luis Zahera) to coach his daughter, Frida (played by Blanca Suárez), in a series of high-stakes soccer matches. The catch is that Frida has never played soccer before, but she's determined to become the best player in Spain.

As Carlos begins working with Frida, he realizes that she's not just any ordinary student - she's a talented and feisty young woman who refuses to be told what to do. Despite their initial disagreements, Carlos starts to see potential in Frida and decides to help her develop her skills.

Throughout the movie, Carlos and Frida face numerous challenges as they prepare for the big matches. They encounter rival coaches, tough opponents, and even some personal struggles that threaten to derail their partnership. However, with each passing match, Carlos and Frida grow closer, both on and off the field.

As the stakes get higher, Carlos starts to realize that his feelings for Frida go beyond mere coaching. He begins to develop romantic feelings for her, but he's hesitant to express them, fearing it might compromise their professional relationship.

In the end, Carlos and Frida face off against their toughest opponents yet - a team of ruthless and experienced players who will stop at nothing to win. With Carlos' unorthodox tactics and Frida's determination, they manage to pull off an incredible comeback victory.

As the dust settles, Carlos finally confesses his feelings to Frida, and she reveals that she feels the same way. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment of tenderness between the two leads, as they share a kiss on the field.

Overall, No Manches Frida is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of love, friendship, and perseverance. With its lighthearted tone and engaging storyline, it's a great choice for anyone looking for a feel-good movie experience.

title: Bad Sister
tagline: How long has it been since your last confession?
overview: As a top student at St. Adeline's Catholic Boarding School, Zoe senses that something is not quite right about the school's new nun-- a sense proven to be true when it is revealed the "good' nun is an imposter with a fatal attraction to Zoe's brother.
plot:
Bad Sister is a 2015 American-Canadian thriller television film written and directed by Doug Campbell for Lifetime, produced with Johnson Production Group and Golden Oak Entertainment. It stars Alyshia Ochse as a woman posing as a nun, with Devon Werkheiser, Ryan Whitney Newman, Helen Eigenberg, Robert Leeshock, Lise Simms, Sloane Avery and James Handy. Although dated 2015, it premiered on Lifetime on 3 January 2016.

Jason Brady (Werkheiser), a teenager who posts videos of his songs online, is sent by his parents to a Catholic boarding school after wrecking his father's car; they disapprove of his musical ambitions. His studious sister Zoe (Newman) attends the same school. The new teacher, Sister Sophia (Ochse), is welcomed by the headmistress, Sister Rebecca (Eigenberg), but Zoe soon notices that she skips the morning prayer and knows little about the faith. In truth she is Laura, a disturbed woman who became obsessed with Jason through his videos, murdered the real Sister Sophia and took her identity. Under her habit she wears lingerie and makeup; she moves Jason's girlfriend Sara (Avery) away from him in class, threatens her, and lets the boy glimpse her undressing. She plants a joint that gets Sara suspended and hides whiskey in Jason's room so that he must stay at school over a weekend, seduces him and secretly films them together, then frames Zoe for cheating when the girl grows suspicious. After Sara returns, Laura kills her in the shower and stages it as an accident. At a family dinner, Zoe catches the "nun" in lie after lie, and Jason confesses the affair and the sex tape she is using against him. The siblings search her computer, discover her real name and seek out Sister Rebecca, only to find her knocked unconscious. Laura confronts them in the chapel, but Sister Rebecca intervenes and Jason stabs the impostor with a screwdriver.

Reviewers who cover Lifetime films responded warmly to its excesses. Lisa Marie Bowman of Through the Shattered Lens called it an over-the-top masterpiece of the network's style, praising Campbell for playing up the sordid melodrama without taking it too seriously and singling out Ochse's switches between the cheerful nun and the irritated Laura. Lifetime Uncorked gave it a rating of three knives, though it found the casting of a genuinely teenage-looking actor as Jason somewhat creepy.

title: The Discovery
overview: In the near future, due to a breakthrough scientific discovery by Dr. Thomas Harbor, there is now definitive proof of an afterlife. While countless people have chosen suicide to reset their existence, others try to decide what it all means. Among them is Dr. Harbor's son Will, who has arrived at his father's isolated compound with a mysterious young woman named Isla. There, they discover the strange acolytes who help Dr. Harbor with his experiments.
plot:
The Discovery is a 2017 American science fiction film directed by Charlie McDowell and written by Justin Marks. The movie stars Robert Redford, Rooney Mara, and Jason Bateman.

The main themes of The Discovery revolve around the concept of immortality through cryonic preservation and the moral implications that come with it. The story follows Dr. Norman Goodman (played by Robert Redford), a scientist who has discovered a way to preserve human consciousness after death, allowing people to be revived in the future when technology allows for it.

The film explores several themes:

1. **Immortality and its consequences**: The movie delves into the idea of immortality and what it means to live forever. As people are preserved and revived, they begin to experience a loss of connection with their loved ones who have passed away, leading to emotional turmoil.
2. **Human connection and relationships**: The Discovery highlights the importance of human connections and relationships in our lives. As people are frozen and later revived, they struggle to form new relationships or reconnect with those who have moved on without them.
3. **Free will and personal identity**: The film raises questions about free will and personal identity. If a person's consciousness is preserved, do they still retain their sense of self, or do they become something new?
4. **The ethics of cryonic preservation**: The movie touches on the moral implications of preserving human consciousness after death. Is it right to revive people who have passed away, potentially disrupting the natural order of life and death?

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a thought-provoking narrative that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of playing God with human life.

Overall, The Discovery is a complex and introspective film that explores the complexities of human existence, relationships, and what it means to be alive.

title: Miss Sloane
tagline: Make sure you surprise them.
overview: An ambitious lobbyist faces off against the powerful gun lobby in an attempt to pass gun control legislation.
plot:
Miss Sloane is a 2016 American drama film directed by John Madden, starring Jessica Chastain as Elizabeth Sloane, a ruthless and cunning lobbyist. The movie follows the story of Elizabeth Sloane, a top lobbyist who specializes in gun control legislation.

The film begins with Elizabeth Sloane (Jessica Chastain) delivering a speech at a gun lobby conference, where she is booed by the audience for her stance on stricter gun control laws. Despite this, she remains committed to her cause and decides to take on the National Rifle Association (NRA), led by Senator Richard Shelby's (Sam Elliott) aide, Jacobson (Giovanni Ribisi).

Elizabeth Sloane starts working with a group of grassroots activists, including her protégée, Shelly (Samantha Morton). Together, they develop a strategy to pass stricter gun control laws in the Senate. However, Elizabeth soon realizes that the NRA is well-funded and has significant influence over politicians.

As Elizabeth navigates the complex world of lobbying, she faces opposition from her colleagues and struggles with her own moral compass. She becomes increasingly ruthless in her tactics, using underhanded methods to manipulate politicians and sway public opinion. Her personal life also begins to suffer as she becomes more consumed by her work.

Meanwhile, Jacobson, who is initially Elizabeth's adversary, starts to question his allegiances to the NRA and develops a complicated relationship with Elizabeth. The two engage in a cat-and-mouse game of one-upmanship, each trying to outmaneuver the other.

As the story unfolds, Elizabeth faces setbacks and challenges, including a failed attempt to pass gun control legislation and a personal crisis that forces her to reevaluate her priorities. In the end, she makes a bold move that could potentially change the course of the debate on gun control.

The film culminates with Elizabeth delivering a powerful speech at a Senate hearing, where she presents a compelling argument for stricter gun control laws. The outcome is uncertain, leaving the audience wondering if Elizabeth's efforts will be successful.

Throughout the movie, Jessica Chastain delivers a tour-de-force performance as Elizabeth Sloane, bringing depth and nuance to her character. The supporting cast, including Sam Elliott and Giovanni Ribisi, add complexity to the story, exploring themes of power, morality, and the human cost of politics.

Overall, Miss Sloane is a gripping drama that explores the cutthroat world of lobbying and the personal costs of fighting for a cause. With its strong performances, timely subject matter, and thought-provoking themes, it's a movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

title: Hush
tagline: Silence can be killer
overview: A deaf woman is stalked by a psychotic killer in her secluded home.
plot:
Hush is a 2016 American thriller film directed by John R. Leonetti and written by Mike Flanagan. The movie stars Kate Siegel as Maddie Young, a deaf and mute writer who must defend herself against a masked killer.

The main themes of Hush include:

1. **Isolation and Vulnerability**: The film takes place in an isolated cabin where Maddie is forced to confront her fears and vulnerabilities. Her inability to communicate verbally due to her deafness makes her even more vulnerable to the killer.
2. **Survival and Self-Defense**: As the story unfolds, Maddie must use her wits and resourcefulness to survive against the killer. The film showcases her determination to protect herself and outsmart her attacker.
3. **Trauma and PTSD**: Throughout the movie, it is revealed that Maddie has a traumatic past, which is hinted at through flashbacks and subtle hints in the narrative. Her experiences have left emotional scars, making her more susceptible to fear and anxiety.
4. **Silence and Communication**: The film explores the theme of silence and communication, highlighting how language can be both empowering and debilitating. Maddie's inability to communicate verbally creates tension and raises questions about the importance of verbal expression in our lives.

Overall, Hush is a tense, suspenseful thriller that delves into themes of isolation, vulnerability, survival, trauma, and communication.

title: Amateur Night
tagline: Every job has pros and cons
overview: Guy Carter, an insecure expectant father unable to find work in his field, accepts a job driving hookers around Los Angeles. One long and crazy evening proves to our hero that he is, in fact, up to the task of fatherhood.
plot:
Amateur Night is a 2016 American crime sex comedy written and directed by Lisa Addario and Joe Syracuse, who drew on their own early experiences in Hollywood for the story. Jason Biggs stars alongside Jenny Mollen, Janet Montgomery, Ashley Tisdale and Bria Murphy. The film premiered in Los Angeles on July 25, 2016, and was released in American cinemas by Cinedigm in early August.

Guy Carter is an unemployed architect with a pregnant wife, Anne, and a growing pile of bills. Anne finds a Craigslist advertisement for a driver and sends him, against his wishes, to apply. Expecting to deliver pizzas, Guy discovers that he has been hired to chauffeur Nikki, a sex worker, around Los Angeles for the night. Their first stop is a regular client, a kinky doctor in Bel Air. When Nikki fails to return for hours, Guy breaks into the house, finds her tied up in what he assumes is a torture session and "rescues" her by spraying the doctor with air freshener; the man falls and hits his head, and the pair flee.

Calmed down by Nikki, Guy learns that he will receive a share of the night's takings and warms to the job. They pick up two of her colleagues, Jaxi and Fallon, and Guy is made to clean a bag of well-used sex toys before driving the women to a bachelor party at a luxury Beverly Hills hotel. There the women put Guy in charge of keeping a crowd of rowdy former fraternity brothers in line, and the evening descends into a series of increasingly explicit and humiliating episodes for him. When Anne goes into false labour, Guy steps out, only to be taken hostage by the vengeful doctor, armed with a syringe of paralysing drug, until Nikki turns the needle on him.

The party resumes until the women discover they have been robbed and hold the guests at gunpoint to retrieve their money. One of the men turns out to be an undercover police officer who tries to arrest Nikki, and Guy leads the police on a chase before crashing his car, and the group escapes by bus. As dawn breaks, Nikki hires Guy to design a house for her. Expecting police at his door, Guy finds instead that his car was repossessed before the police could trace it. The end credits play over re-enactments of incidents the filmmakers say really happened.

Critics panned the film; Rotten Tomatoes recorded no positive reviews from six critics, and it grossed only about $63,000.

title: Bad Moms
tagline: Party like a mother.
overview: When three overworked and under-appreciated moms are pushed beyond their limits, they ditch their conventional responsibilities for a jolt of long overdue freedom, fun, and comedic self-indulgence.
plot:
Bad Moms is a 2016 American comedy film directed by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore, produced by Universal Pictures.

The movie follows three suburban mothers, Amy (Mila Kunis), Kiki (Kristen Bell), and Gwendolyn (Annie Mumolo), who feel suffocated by the expectations of their perfect lives. They begin to rebel against the pressures of motherhood, friendship, and societal norms.

The main themes of Bad Moms include:

1. **Empowerment**: The film celebrates women's independence and self-discovery, encouraging them to break free from societal expectations and forge their own paths.
2. **Motherhood**: The movie pokes fun at the challenges and absurdities of motherhood, highlighting the struggles of balancing personal desires with parental responsibilities.
3. **Friendship**: The bond between the three main characters is a central theme, showcasing the importance of female friendships in navigating life's ups and downs.
4. **Self-acceptance**: As the mothers shed their perfect facades, they learn to accept themselves, flaws and all, and find happiness on their own terms.
5. **Rebellion against societal expectations**: The film playfully subverts traditional notions of motherhood, marriage, and friendship, promoting a more authentic and liberated approach to life.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges, including parenting classes, PTA meetings, and social media scrutiny. Ultimately, they find freedom and joy in embracing their individuality and rejecting the pressures that once held them back.

Overall, Bad Moms is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of female empowerment, self-discovery, and the importance of nurturing meaningful relationships.

title: The Edge of Seventeen
tagline: You're only young once… is it over yet?
overview: Two high school girls are best friends until one dates the other's older brother, who is totally his sister's nemesis.
plot:
The Edge of Seventeen is a coming-of-age comedy-drama film released in 2016, directed by Kelly Fremon Craig and produced by Lianne Halfon, Molly Smith, and Jennifer Ventimilia. The movie follows the life of Nadine Byrd (played by Hailee Steinfeld), a high school junior navigating her senior year while dealing with her complicated relationships and family dynamics.

The story begins with Nadine's mother, Mary (played by Kyra Sedgwick), who is recently divorced from her husband, Jim (played by Woody Harrelson). The tension between the two parents is palpable, and Nadine struggles to cope with the changes in her life. Her father has moved out, and she feels abandoned.

Nadine's best friend, Krista (played by Haley Lu Richardson), tries to be supportive, but their friendship is put to the test as they face various challenges together. The two girls try to navigate high school cliques, relationships, and social pressures while dealing with Nadine's emotional turmoil.

As the story unfolds, Nadine develops feelings for her classmate, Eric (played by Blake Jenner), who seems perfect on the surface but turns out to be shallow and unfaithful. Meanwhile, she also starts to develop a crush on her English teacher, Mr. Bruner (played by Tom Holland).

Throughout the film, Nadine's relationships with her family members are explored in depth. Her mother is portrayed as a complex character struggling to balance her own emotions and needs with those of her daughter. The tension between them is evident, but they also share moments of tenderness and understanding.

As the school year progresses, Nadine faces various setbacks, including a failed relationship and a disappointing college acceptance letter. However, she eventually finds solace in her friendship with Krista and begins to develop a stronger sense of self.

The film's climax revolves around Nadine's confrontation with Eric, who has been unfaithful to her. The scene is intense and emotional, showcasing Nadine's growth and resilience. In the end, Nadine comes to terms with her feelings and learns to move on from her past heartbreak.

The Edge of Seventeen received widespread critical acclaim for its authentic portrayal of teenage life, nuanced character development, and outstanding performances from the cast. The film's exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, relationships, and identity resonated with audiences worldwide.

title: High Life
tagline: Oblivion Awaits.
overview: A father and his daughter struggle to survive in deep space where they live in isolation.
plot:
High Life is a 2018 science fiction film directed by Claire Denis, based on the novel "L'Étranger dans l'univers" (The Stranger in the Universe) by Michel Faber. The movie stars Robert Pattinson, Juliette Binoche, and André 3000.

The main themes of High Life revolve around existentialism, morality, and the human condition. The story takes place on a spaceship traveling through space, where a group of prisoners are being held captive for their crimes. The crew is led by Captain Hunter (played by Robert Pattinson), who is tasked with navigating the ship to a distant planet.

As the journey progresses, the characters' pasts and motivations are slowly revealed, exposing the complexities of human nature. The film explores themes of guilt, redemption, and the search for meaning in a seemingly meaningless universe. The crew's actions are driven by their own moral compasses, which often conflict with each other, leading to a series of philosophical debates.

One of the central questions posed by High Life is: "What does it mean to be human?" The film challenges traditional notions of humanity and morality, presenting characters who are both flawed and relatable. Through its exploration of existentialism, High Life encourages viewers to confront their own values and moral principles.

The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for connection in a vast, uncaring universe. As the crew navigates the ship's cramped quarters, they must confront their own emotional vulnerabilities and find ways to cope with the existential dread that comes with being trapped in space.

Ultimately, High Life presents a bleak yet thought-provoking vision of humanity's place in the universe, leaving viewers to ponder the complexities of existence and our own moral agency.

title: Jackie
tagline: I want them to see what they have done to Jack.
overview: An account of the days of First Lady, Jacqueline Kennedy, in the immediate aftermath of John F. Kennedy's assassination in 1963.
plot:
Jackie is a 2016 biographical drama film that delves into the life of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, the former First Lady of the United States. The movie masterfully weaves together themes of grief, identity, and the complexities of female experience.

At its core, Jackie explores the emotional turmoil that Jacqueline Kennedy faced in the aftermath of her husband's assassination in 1963. The film portrays a woman struggling to come to terms with the loss of her partner, both personally and professionally. As she navigates the treacherous waters of public life, Jackie must also confront the fragility of her own identity, which is threatened by the constant scrutiny and expectation that comes with being the First Lady.

One of the most striking aspects of the film is its portrayal of the societal constraints placed on women during the 1960s. The movie highlights the limited options available to Jacqueline, who is expected to maintain a perfect facade of elegance and poise, even in the face of unimaginable tragedy. This dichotomy between public image and private pain serves as a powerful commentary on the double standards faced by women during this era.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness and isolation, as Jackie finds herself increasingly disconnected from her family and friends. Her relationships with those around her are complex and multifaceted, reflecting the nuances of human connection in times of crisis.

Ultimately, Jackie is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on the complexities of grief, identity, and the enduring power of female resilience.

title: Frantz
overview: In the aftermath of WWI, a young German who grieves the death of her fiancé in France meets a mysterious French man who visits the fiance’s grave to lay flowers.
plot:
Frantz is a 2016 German drama film directed by Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck, not X Filme Creative Pool. The movie tells the story of an anonymous letter sent to a young man named Franz, who is struggling to come to terms with the loss of his brother during World War I.

The main theme of Frantz revolves around the complexities of grief, guilt, and redemption in the aftermath of war. As Franz navigates his relationships with the family of his deceased brother's killer, he begins to confront the dark secrets of his own past and the true nature of his brother's death. The film explores the emotional toll of war on individuals and families, as well as the difficulties of rebuilding relationships and finding closure in the face of trauma.

Through Franz's journey, the film delves into the themes of identity, belonging, and the search for meaning in a world torn apart by conflict. title: Barbie: Spy Squad
overview: Barbie and her best friends Teresa and Renee transform from hard-working gymnasts to undercover secret agents. plot:
Barbie: Spy Squad is a 2016 American computer-animated action comedy film and the 32nd entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Conrad Helten from a screenplay by Marsha Griffin and Kacey Arnold, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment and music by Gabriel Mann and Rebecca Kneubuhl. It opened in Polish cinemas on 15 January 2016, had limited cinema screenings in the United Kingdom alongside its DVD release there, and was released direct to video in North America by Universal in early 2016, later airing on Nickelodeon. Barbie and her best friends Renee (Stephanie Sheh) and Teresa (Jenny Pellicer) are gymnasts preparing for a championship, though Barbie is shaken after losing focus during the team's pyramid. Renee's Aunt Zoe (Cathy Weseluck), a cat-loving knitter who never misses a meet, invites the girls to a picnic at the Hollywood sign, where a hidden door leads to the headquarters of a secret spy organisation, the International Intelligence and Innovation Agency. Zoe turns out to be its head, Agent Z. Impressed by the girls' agility and teamwork, she recruits them to stop a cat burglar stealing rare gems which, once assembled, could power a device able to shut down the agency's systems.

Trained by Agent Dunbar (Brian Dobson) and equipped by the young inventor Lazlo (Ian Hanlin) with gadgets disguised as make-up and fashion accessories, motorcycles and a robotic dog named Percy, the girls must keep their mission secret even from their sisters. Their inexperience costs them dearly: the thief, a superb gymnast, escapes with a gem at their first stakeout and again at a party where their kitchen disguises end in chaos, and they are dismissed from the agency. Applying Zoe's advice to visualise a move before making it, Barbie recognises the burglar's moves in their rival gymnast Patricia (Rebecca Husain). Following her into headquarters, the girls discover she has been working for Dunbar, who resents being passed over and plans to use the gems to cripple the agency, frame Zoe and take her place. With help from Zoe, their friends and the agency's robots, the girls foil the scheme, Barbie regains her confidence, and Patricia, realising her mistakes, makes friends with the trio.

plot:
Brothers of the Wind is an English-language Austrian coming-of-age drama directed by Gerardo Olivares and Otmar Penker, first released in December 2015. Set amid the Alps, it intertwines the life of a young golden eagle with that of a grieving boy, and stars Manuel Camacho as Lukas, Jean Reno as the forester Danzer, Tobias Moretti as Lukas's father Keller and Eva Kuen as his late mother Maria.

In the 1960s a pair of eagles hatch two chicks high in the mountains. The father is killed in a fight with another eagle, and one eaglet tumbles from the nest, abandoned by its mother, who by instinct raises only the stronger chick. Below, Lukas and Keller have moved into a new mountain home after Maria died in a fire. Consumed by grief, Keller cannot connect with his son, who retreats into the forest and to the ruins of their old house. There Lukas discovers the fallen eaglet and decides to nurse it, and Danzer, fond of the boy, teaches him how to feed and care for the bird. Reading the family Bible, Lukas comes across Cain and Abel and names the eaglet Abel, thinking of the brother still in the nest as Cain.

Danzer takes Lukas and Abel to stay with him for the summer, and the boy helps the young eagle learn to fly. Abel vanishes for days and returns, and the two friends train him to hunt despite Keller's objections, until Danzer persuades Lukas that the bird must go free; they release it blindfolded in a distant part of the mountains. After a wolf frightens Lukas into a bear trap and Danzer rescues him, the rift with his father deepens. Coming to believe that Keller started the fire that killed his mother, Lukas runs away into the mountains, where a rockslide and a lightning strike leave him unconscious. Keller finds him and apologises for his harshness. Two years later, Abel reappears and lands on Lukas's arm; the boy removes the band he once tied to its leg and lets it go for good, and Abel later awaits a new hatchling with a mate.

Common Sense Media gave the film a strong recommendation, citing its gorgeous imagery, its faithful portrayal of the laws of nature and its uplifting story of a boy growing up, while Cinemagazine was cooler, rating it 2.5.

title: DC Films Presents Dawn of the Justice League
original_title: DC Films Presents Dawn of the Justice League
overview: A documentary special taking a look at the upcoming films making up the DC Universe. Kevin Smith hosts with Geoff Johns, as they take a look at Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice, Suicide Squad, the upcoming Wonder Woman and Justice League movies.
plot:
DC Films Presents: Dawn of the Justice League is a 2016 American television documentary special produced by Warner Bros. Pictures and DC Entertainment to promote the studio's slate of films based on DC Comics characters. Hosted by filmmaker and comic book enthusiast Kevin Smith together with Geoff Johns, DC's chief creative officer, it aired on The CW on 19 January 2016, immediately following an episode of The Flash, and runs about 22 minutes. Alongside its hosts it features clips and interview material with filmmakers and cast members including Zack Snyder, David Ayer, Patty Jenkins, Henry Cavill, Jesse Eisenberg, Will Smith, Jared Leto, Joel Kinnaman and Ray Fisher.

Structured as a conversation in which Smith poses questions and Johns explains the characters and their place in the shared universe, the special works through the upcoming releases one by one. It begins with Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, then due in March 2016, reusing footage from earlier trailers while cast members recall their first encounters with DC comics and Johns outlines why the two heroes come into conflict. It then turns to Suicide Squad and premieres a new trailer for the film set to Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody", before offering the first brief glimpses of footage from Wonder Woman, starring Gal Gadot and scheduled for 2017. The final section introduces the other members of the planned Justice League, Aquaman, the Flash and Cyborg, using concept art and short summaries of their backstories; Johns acknowledges the television version of the Flash while explaining that Ezra Miller's cinematic Barry Allen will have a somewhat different origin. The special's main announcement was that Green Lantern and the Green Lantern Corps would join the film universe, with Hal Jordan and John Stewart expected to be at its center.

Reactions were mixed. Geekscape felt it achieved what it set out to do, bringing viewers up to speed on the characters, and found Smith's enthusiasm infectious, though it noted that the Batman v Superman segment offered little new and that the Wonder Woman footage left it flat. Dan Greenfield of 13th Dimension was far more critical, calling it a half-hour infomercial aimed at viewers who already knew the characters, questioning the need for Smith as a cheerleader and arguing that the studio should show rather than tell, though he preferred the new Suicide Squad trailer to the first.

As they delve deeper into the case, they discover that the victim was a woman named Eurus Holmes, who is revealed to be Sherlock's long-lost sister.

As the story reaches its climax, it is revealed that Eurus was not just any ordinary person, but rather a highly intelligent and skilled individual who had been using her abilities to manipulate those around her. In the end, Sherlock finally tracks down his sister, only to discover that she has been playing him all along, using their intellectual battles as a way to keep herself entertained.

The episode ends with Sherlock realizing that he has been outsmarted by his own sister, and that he must confront the fact that he is not as intelligent or capable as he thought. The final scene shows Sherlock sitting in his armchair, looking defeated and humbled, while Eurus watches him from afar, a hint of a smile on her face.

title: Justice League vs. Teen Titans
overview: Robin is sent by Batman to work with the Teen Titans after his volatile behavior botches up a Justice League mission. The Titans must then step up to face Trigon after he possesses the League and threatens to conquer the world.
plot:
Justice League vs. Teen Titans is a 2016 animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and DC Entertainment. The movie brings together two iconic teams from the DC Comics universe: the Justice League, led by Batman, and the Teen Titans, led by Robin.

The main themes of Justice League vs. Teen Titans can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Coming of Age**: The film explores the transition from adolescence to adulthood for the Teen Titans, particularly Robin (Dick Grayson), who is struggling to balance his responsibilities as a hero with his personal life and relationships.
2. **Leadership and Power Struggle**: Batman's leadership style clashes with the more impulsive and inexperienced approach of the Teen Titans, leading to tension and conflict between the two teams. This theme highlights the challenges of leadership and the importance of effective communication and trust-building.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: The movie delves into the themes of identity and belonging, particularly for Robin, who feels like an outsider among his peers. His struggles to find his place within the Justice League serve as a metaphor for the difficulties of growing up and finding one's purpose in life.
4. **Mentorship and Guidance**: Batman's character serves as a mentor and guide for the Teen Titans, particularly Robin. The film showcases the importance of guidance and support from experienced leaders in helping young heroes navigate their roles and responsibilities.
5. **Teamwork and Unity**: Ultimately, the movie emphasizes the value of teamwork and unity among the Justice League and the Teen Titans. Through their shared experiences and challenges, the two teams learn to put aside their differences and work together towards a common goal.

Overall, Justice League vs. Teen Titans is a coming-of-age story that explores themes of leadership, identity, mentorship, and teamwork, set against the backdrop of an epic superhero battle between two iconic teams from the DC Comics universe.

title: Flight Crew
tagline: A mid air rescue mission
overview: A story about bravery, self-sacrifice and human dignity put on trial by the merciless power of nature. A young pilot is fired from military air force after disobeying an absurd order. He gets a job as a co-pilot with a civil airline. Being brutally honest and direct, he is not on best terms with his new colleagues. During a flight to Asia his crew receives a distress message from a volcanic island and makes a decision to attempt a rescue mission. Will it be a success? Will they survive the disaster? They have a single chance to find that out: by being a team and sticking up for one another.
plot:
Flight Crew (Russian: Экипаж, Ekipazh) is a 2016 Russian disaster film directed by Nikolai Lebedev and produced by the Russia-1 channel, starring Danila Kozlovsky, Vladimir Mashkov and Agnė Grudytė. A remake of the 1979 Soviet film Air Crew, it was shot with digital 3D cameras and became the second Russian film released in IMAX, after Stalingrad.

Alexey Gushchin, a gifted young military pilot, is grounded after he jettisons a car being carried for a general from a charity flight to get through a storm. Seeking work with a passenger airline, he fails a simulator test overseen by veteran captain Leonid Zinchenko, but when Zinchenko himself fails the same scenario, he takes Alexey on as a trainee co-pilot on a Tu-204. Zinchenko is estranged from his son Valera, who has dropped out of school, while Alexey begins a relationship with fellow pilot Alexandra Kuzmina. The two pilots clash after Zinchenko refuses to let locals board an evacuation flight from an African country in revolution, and Alexey is fired after a fight with a wealthy passenger who ignores safety rules. Zinchenko, valuing his skill, brings him back for a flight to Southeast Asia, taking Valera along.

Sent to the volcanic island of Kanwoo after an eruption, the crew begins evacuating survivors when an earthquake wrecks the airport. While Alexey, Valera and attendant Andrey drive out to rescue a group of trapped people, the advancing lava forces Zinchenko and Alexandra to leave in an An-26, leaving the Tu-204 behind. The rescuers return on foot, and Alexey takes off from a shorter runway covered in burning oil and flies out through the ash cloud. Learning that the An-26 is losing fuel, the crew follows a plan devised by Alexey's father Igor, an aircraft engineer, to transfer its passengers mid-air in a cage on a cable. Alexandra is saved, but the cage's ropes snap on its third trip, killing eleven people, and Zinchenko escapes along the cable before the An-26 falls into the ocean. Defying orders, Alexey lands the crippled jet in a storm at Elizovo and everyone aboard survives. Fired for disobedience, the pilots are taken on by Aeroflot.

Filmed from September 2014 to February 2015 in Moscow and Crimea, the film premiered on April 21, 2016, through Central Partnership. Critics praised its effects and tension, and it was the highest-grossing Russian film of 2016, receiving 11 nominations at the 2017 Golden Eagle Awards.

title: mother!
tagline: Seeing is believing
overview: A couple's relationship is tested when uninvited guests arrive at their home, disrupting their tranquil existence.
plot:
Mother! is a 2017 American psychological horror film written and directed by Darren Aronofsky, starring Jennifer Lawrence and Javier Bardem as a couple living in an isolated country house, with Ed Harris, Michelle Pfeiffer and Kristen Wiig. Widely read as a biblical and environmental allegory, it gives its characters only descriptive names such as Mother and Him.

In the ruins of a burned house, a poet known as Him places a crystal object on a pedestal, and the building is transformed into a beautiful home. Mother, his young wife, wakes in bed and wonders where he is. She restores the house while Him struggles with writer's block. One night a stranger, Man, arrives, claiming to be a doctor, and Him invites him to stay. Man's wife, Woman, arrives the next day, and the guests intrude ever more boldly on Mother's privacy. When the couple shatter the treasured crystal, Him seals off his study. Their two sons then appear and fight over their father's will, and the elder fatally wounds his brother.

The dead son's mourners pour into the house, behaving rudely and destructively until Mother, enraged, drives them all out. After a bitter argument, she and Him make love, and the next morning she announces that she is pregnant. Him is inspired to write again, and his new poem becomes a sensation. As Mother prepares for the baby's arrival, admirers begin to gather at the house, and their numbers swell into a frenzied, worshipful mob. The home descends into apocalyptic chaos, with cultish rituals, executions and battles with soldiers, while Him basks in the adoration. Mother gives birth in his study and refuses to let him show the baby to the crowd, but while she sleeps, Him takes the child outside, where it is killed and devoured by the worshippers.

The mob attacks Mother, and Him begs her to forgive them. Instead, she ignites the oil tank in the basement, destroying the house and everyone inside. Him survives unharmed and, with her consent, takes her heart from her burned body. It contains a new crystal, which he places on the pedestal, restoring the house, where a new woman wakes in bed and wonders where he is.

Premiering at the Venice Film Festival, the film sharply divided critics and audiences: many praised its ambition and Lawrence's performance, while others found it pretentious, and it received a rare "F" CinemaScore. It grossed $44.5 million worldwide on a $30 million budget.

title: Hidden Figures
tagline: Meet the women you don't know, behind the mission you do.
overview: The untold story of Katherine G. Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson – brilliant African-American women working at NASA and serving as the brains behind one of the greatest operations in history – the launch of astronaut John Glenn into orbit. The visionary trio crossed all gender and race lines to inspire generations to dream big.
plot:
Hidden Figures is a biographical drama film directed by Theodore Melfi, released in 2016 by Fox 2000 Pictures. The movie tells the story of three African-American women who worked as mathematicians and engineers at NASA during the early years of the space program.

The film begins with Katherine Johnson (played by Taraji P. Henson), a young girl from West Virginia who dreams of becoming an astronaut. Despite facing racism and sexism, she earns a scholarship to study mathematics at West Virginia State College. She later transfers to Howard University, where she meets her future colleagues, Dorothy Vaughan (Octavia Spencer) and Mary Jackson (Janelle Monáe).

The story takes off when Katherine is recruited by NASA's Langley Research Center in 1957. She works under the supervision of supervisor Al Harrison (Kevin Costner), who recognizes her exceptional mathematical skills. However, she faces racism and sexism from her colleagues, including the infamous "computer" segregation policy that restricts African-American employees to menial tasks.

As Katherine navigates this challenging environment, she also meets her future husband, Edgar (played by Winston Duke). The film showcases her remarkable work ethic, intelligence, and determination as she becomes an integral part of NASA's team. She works tirelessly to calculate trajectories for the Mercury Seven astronauts, including Alan Shepard and John Glenn.

Meanwhile, Dorothy Vaughan faces similar challenges as a supervisor at NASA. Despite being passed over for promotions, she perseveres and eventually earns the respect of her colleagues. Her story is intertwined with Katherine's, highlighting the struggles faced by women in STEM fields during that era.

Mary Jackson, an aspiring engineer, also faces obstacles due to her sex and skin color. She works as a "human computer" but dreams of becoming an actual engineer. With the help of her colleague, Katherine, she eventually earns the respect of her superiors and becomes the first African-American female engineer at NASA.

The film's climax revolves around the historic launch of John Glenn into space in 1962. Katherine's calculations are crucial to the success of this mission, which marks a significant milestone for the United States' space program.

Throughout the movie, the characters face numerous challenges, including racism, sexism, and personal struggles. However, they persevere, driven by their passion for mathematics, science, and engineering. The film ultimately celebrates the triumphs of these unsung heroes who paved the way for future generations of women in STEM fields.

The ending is a heartwarming tribute to the lives and achievements of Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan, and Mary Jackson. The movie concludes with a sense of hope and determination, as the characters look towards a brighter future for themselves and their communities.

Overall, Hidden Figures is an inspiring film that sheds light on the often-overlooked contributions of African-American women in NASA's early years. It is a testament to the power of perseverance, intelligence, and determination in the face of adversity.

Split is a psychological thriller film directed by M. Night Shyamalan, released in 2016 by Universal Pictures. The movie follows the story of Kevin Wendell Crumb, a man with multiple personalities, and his obsession with a teenage girl named Casey Cooke.

The film begins with Kevin (played by James McAvoy), a man who suffers from dissociative identity disorder (DID). He has 23 distinct personalities, each with its own unique personality, appearance, and backstory. The main personalities are Dennis, Patricia, Hedwig, and Barry, among others. Kevin's lives are mundane and unfulfilling, and he feels like an outsider in society.

One day, Kevin meets Casey Cooke (played by Anya Taylor-Joy), a 16-year-old girl who is being stalked by him. Despite his unsettling behavior, Casey is drawn to Kevin and begins to visit him at his apartment. As their relationship deepens, Kevin's personalities become more prominent, and he starts to reveal his true nature to Casey.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kevin's personalities are not just random manifestations of his psyche but are actually distinct individuals with their own motivations and desires. Dennis, one of Kevin's main personalities, is a charismatic and confident individual who takes charge when Kevin is in a vulnerable state. Patricia, on the other hand, is a seductive and manipulative personality who uses her charm to get what she wants.

As Casey becomes more entrenched in Kevin's life, she begins to uncover the dark secrets behind his multiple personalities. She discovers that each personality has its own unique trauma and backstory, which are linked to Kevin's childhood experiences. Through flashbacks, we see Kevin's abusive childhood and how it led to the development of his DID.

As the plot thickens, Casey realizes that Kevin is not just a stalker but a complex individual with multiple layers. She begins to empathize with him and understand his motivations, which puts her in grave danger. The film builds up to a thrilling climax as Casey tries to escape from Kevin's apartment, pursued by his increasingly aggressive personalities.

In the end, Casey manages to outsmart Dennis and escape from Kevin's clutches. However, not before she witnesses the full extent of Kevin's trauma and the depth of his DID. The film ends with Casey reflecting on her experience and realizing that she has been changed forever by her encounter with Kevin.

Throughout the film, Shyamalan explores themes of identity, trauma, and the complexities of human psychology. The movie features a standout performance from James McAvoy, who brings to life the multiple personalities of Kevin Wendell Crumb. The film's twist ending is also noteworthy, as it subverts expectations and adds depth to the story.

Overall, Split is a gripping psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human psychology. With its intricate plot, complex characters, and stunning performances, the film is a must-watch for fans of the genre.

title: A Dog's Purpose
tagline: Every dog happens for a reason.
overview: A dog goes on quest to discover his purpose in life over the course of several lifetimes with multiple owners.
plot:
A Dog's Purpose is a heartwarming drama film released in 2017, directed by Lasse Hallström and produced by Universal Pictures and Amblin Entertainment. The movie is based on the bestselling novel of the same name by W. Bruce Cameron.

The story revolves around Bailey, a golden retriever who is reincarnated multiple times throughout his life, each time with a new purpose. The film begins with Bailey's first life as a puppy, where he is adopted by a family and grows up to be a beloved pet. However, when the family decides to rehome him due to their inability to care for him properly, Bailey finds himself in a shelter.

title: Perfect Strangers
tagline: Everyone has three lives: A public life. A private life... and a secret life.
overview: During a dinner, a group of friends decide to share whatever message or phone call they will receive during the evening, with unforeseen consequences.
plot:
Perfect Strangers (Perfetti sconosciuti) is an Italian psychological comedy-drama of 2016 directed and co-written by Paolo Genovese. The ensemble cast features Kasia Smutniak and Marco Giallini as the hosts Eva and Rocco, Alba Rohrwacher and Edoardo Leo as the newlyweds Bianca and Cosimo, Anna Foglietta and Valerio Mastandrea as Carlotta and Lele, Giuseppe Battiston as Peppe and Benedetta Porcaroli as Eva and Rocco's teenage daughter Sofia.

On the night of a total lunar eclipse, Eva, a psychotherapist, and her husband Rocco, a plastic surgeon, whose marriage is in trouble, host a dinner for old friends: Cosimo, a taxi driver, and Bianca, a veterinarian, recently married and hoping for a child; Lele and Carlotta, married for ten years and also struggling; and Peppe, a divorced, unemployed former physical education teacher whose new girlfriend Lucilla is ill and cannot come. Eva, convinced that many couples would break up if they saw each other's phones, proposes a game: everyone puts their phone on the table and shares every message and call that arrives during the evening. Rocco is the most reluctant, but all agree.

The game begins harmlessly but soon spins out of control. It emerges that Rocco has secretly been seeing an analyst and that Eva plans breast surgery with another surgeon. Lele, who receives racy photos from another woman every night, persuades Peppe to swap their identical phones, only for messages from a man named Lucio to arrive on Peppe's phone, leading everyone to believe that Lele is secretly gay. Carlotta is devastated, and Cosimo, offended that his best friend never confided in him, reacts with open homophobia. Cosimo, jealous of Bianca's ex, is exposed in turn: his lover, a taxi dispatcher, is pregnant, and a call hints that he has also been sleeping with Eva. Carlotta, caught exchanging suggestive messages with another man, confesses that years earlier she killed a pedestrian while driving drunk and Lele took the blame. Peppe admits that Lucio is his partner, whom he shields from his friends, and Bianca, heartbroken, leaves after telling Peppe he is right. When the eclipse ends, it turns out the game never happened, because Rocco refused to play.

The film won the David di Donatello for Best Film and was a major hit, opening at number one in Italy and grossing more than €16 million there. Guinness World Records later recognized it as the most remade film in history, with versions in 24 languages.

Death Note: Light Up the New World is a 2016 Japanese supernatural thriller directed by Shinsuke Sato, based on the manga Death Note by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata. It stars Masahiro Higashide as Detective Tsukuru Mishima, Sosuke Ikematsu as Ryuzaki, the successor of L, Masaki Suda as the cyber-terrorist Yuki Shien and Erika Toda as Misa Amane, with Rina Kawaei and Mina Fujii, and Shidō Nakamura voicing the Shinigami Ryuk.

Ten years after the deaths of Light Yagami, known as Kira, and his nemesis L, a world troubled by cyber-terrorism is struck by a wave of unexplained deaths suggesting that Death Notes, notebooks that kill anyone whose name is written in them, are being used again. Interpol assigns Ryuzaki, L's biological successor, to a new Death Note Task Force led by Mishima. After a killing spree in Shibuya, the team learns from a Shinigami that six Death Notes are now in the human world, the maximum allowed at once.

The race to gather all six notebooks begins. Yuki Shien, a brilliant hacker who worships Kira and believes he is carrying out Light's will, hunts down the notebooks and their owners. He restores the memories of Misa Amane, Light's former girlfriend, and asks for her help in finding where Light might be hiding. Shien then spreads a computer virus featuring Light's image and threatens a massacre unless L's successor reveals himself. As Ryuzaki and Mishima try to outmaneuver him, the Task Force is disbanded, Mishima falls under suspicion, and the mystery surrounding Light's secret successor deepens, building to a showdown in which no one can be fully trusted.

The film continues the franchise's cat-and-mouse battle of wits and its moral questions about justice and the power over life and death.

Released in Japan by Warner Bros. on October 29, 2016, Light Up the New World opened at the top of the Japanese box office, displacing Your Name, and became one of the year's highest-grossing Japanese films.

This theme is particularly relevant in exploring the Joker's own backstory and his connection to Batman.

3. **The Duality of Human Nature**: The Killing Joke explores the dualities present within human nature, with characters like the Joker embodying pure chaos, while others, such as Barbara Gordon, represent a more ordered and rational approach to life. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the complexities of human psychology.

4. **The Impact of Trauma on Heroes**: The film examines how trauma can affect heroes, particularly Batman, who is forced to confront his own vulnerabilities in order to protect others. This theme highlights the psychological toll that heroism can take on individuals and the importance of seeking help when needed.

5. **The Joker's Existential Significance**: The Joker serves as a symbol for the absurdity and randomness of life, highlighting the inherent meaninglessness of existence. His actions serve as a commentary on the human condition, forcing Batman to confront the possibility that there may be no clear moral or rational explanation for the world.

Overall, Batman: The Killing Joke presents a thought-provoking exploration of complex themes, challenging viewers to consider the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of chaos in society.
