It runs about 70 minutes.

At Monster High, Lagoona Blue, who grew up in the Great Scarrier Reef, watches her friends Frankie, Draculaura and Clawdeen struggle through dance rehearsals under Toralei's poor coaching, but refuses to join them, though she dances beautifully when she thinks she is alone. At the recital Toralei exposes her dancing behind the curtain, and Lagoona freezes, becomes tangled in the stage rigging and finds the video viral the next day. When she uninvites Toralei from her poolside party, the two quarrel, Toralei falls into the pool, and a whirlpool pulls Lagoona, Toralei, Frankie, Draculaura, Clawdeen and Gil to the bottom of the sea, where they find themselves transformed into half-fish creatures.

Posea Reef, daughter of Poseidon, tends a garden in which every plant represents a sea creature; Lagoona's is wilting, and Posea tells her that to go home she must face her greatest fear. Lagoona reveals that her stage fright dates from a childhood dance competition in which her former friend Kala, a squid ghoul, deliberately tripped her. Staying with Lagoona's father and siblings, the group learns that a feared Kraken has been sighted. Kala challenges Lagoona to a dance-off, and through the serpent sisters Peri and Pearl tricks her with a false legend that looking the Kraken in the eye cures fear. Lagoona braves its lair but faints on stage again; when her friends rally the crowd to support her, a furious Kala summons the Kraken, which follows the friends back to Monster High. Climbing onto the monster, Lagoona realises her true fear was Kala's bullying, while Kala admits she was mocked for her looks and that the Kraken is her father, whom she was ashamed of. The two reconcile, the Kraken helps repair the school, and both girls' plants return to health.

Larissa Gallagher voices Lagoona, with Kate Higgins as Frankie, Debi Derryberry as Draculaura, Salli Saffioti as Clawdeen, America Young as Toralei, Lyndsy Kail as Kala and Paula Rhodes as Posea.

overview: Leo Borlock is an average student at Mica High School. He gets decent grades, is a member of the school's marching band and has always been content flying under the radar. But all that changes when he meets Stargirl Caraway, a confident and colorful new student with a penchant for the ukulele, who stands out in a crowd. She is kind, finds magic in the mundane and touches the lives of others with the simplest of gestures. Her eccentricities and infectious personality charm Leo and the student body, and she quickly goes from being ignored and ridiculed to accepted and praised, then back again, sending Leo on a rollercoaster ride of emotions.
plot:
Stargirl is a 2020 American romantic drama film directed by Julia Leona. The movie revolves around the life of Leo Borlock, a shy and introverted high school student who falls in love with an eccentric and free-spirited girl named Stargirl Caraway.

The main theme of Stargirl is the power of individuality and self-expression. Stargirl's unique personality and style inspire those around her to be more authentic and true to themselves, while also challenging the conventional norms of their small town community. Through Leo's journey, the film explores the tension between conformity and nonconformity, highlighting the importance of embracing one's quirks and passions.

The movie also delves into themes of love, acceptance, and the complexities of relationships. Leo's relationship with Stargirl is portrayed as a beautiful and all-consuming romance that pushes him out of his comfort zone and forces him to confront his own insecurities. The film ultimately suggests that true connection and understanding can only be achieved by embracing our differences and being open to new experiences.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of small-town life and the constraints it can place on individuals. Stargirl's arrival in town serves as a catalyst for change, highlighting the limitations and expectations that come with living in a close-knit community. The film ultimately celebrates the beauty of individuality and nonconformity, suggesting that true freedom and happiness can only be achieved by breaking free from societal norms.

Overall, Stargirl is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores themes of self-expression, love, acceptance, and the power of individuality.

title: Kindergarten Cop 2
overview: Assigned to recover sensitive stolen data, a gruff FBI agent goes undercover as a kindergarten teacher, but the school's liberal, politically correct environment is more than he bargained for.
plot:
Kindergarten Cop 2 is a 2016 American comedy directed by Don Michael Paul and starring Dolph Lundgren, released on home video by Universal. A standalone sequel to the 1990 hit Kindergarten Cop, it replaces Arnold Schwarzenegger's Detective John Kimble with a new hero, FBI agent Zack Reed. Bill Bellamy plays Reed's partner, Agent Sanders, with Darla Taylor as the teacher Olivia, Sarah Strange as Miss Sinclaire and Aleks Paunovic as the villain Alexander Zogu.

Reed and Sanders are hunting Zogu, a dangerous crime boss who has learned of a copy of the FBI's witness protection database. The file was stored on a USB flash drive by a kindergarten teacher, Kevin Flaherty, who has since died. Sanders questions the dead man's pupils and the school staff, but nobody knows where the drive is, so Reed invents a résumé, applies to take over the grieving class and is hired with little difficulty.

The school prides itself on a progressive, modern approach to education, which clashes with Reed's blunt manner. His first day is chaos: one boy has a severe nut allergy, so pandemonium breaks out when Reed is caught eating peanut butter, and he loses control again after handing out chocolate cookies that send the children bouncing off the walls. Insisting he can manage without help, he resorts to an air horn to impose order and earns a strike from the principal. Chastened, he apologises and turns to Sanders, a father of five, for advice, and gradually learns to lead the class with more patience and emotional awareness. When fellow kindergarten teacher Olivia catches him searching her office for the drive, he covers by asking her out, and a romance develops.

In a game of capture the flag against Olivia's class, Reed's pupils, who complain that the other children are bigger, win for the first time thanks to a Trojan horse strategy he devises. Meanwhile Zogu seizes the FBI's surveillance van and realises that the children hold the key to the drive. Reed reveals his true identity to the principal and warns her to lock down the school. Zogu tracks down the drive while the class is on a field trip, but the children ambush him using their Trojan horse tactic, the drive is returned to the FBI, and the kids celebrate with their parents.

The film was shot over 28 days in July and August 2015 in Maple Ridge, Langley and Vancouver, British Columbia, with Kanaka Elementary serving as the school. Reviews were poor; Consequence of Sound gave it a D+.

title: Weaponized
tagline: The Future of War is Here.
overview: A damaged homicide detective (Johnny Messner) must prevent a grieving father from unleashing a "robotic virus" that he believes will destroy the terrorist cell that murdered his son, but at an unimaginable cost.
plot:
Weaponized, also released as Swap, is a 2016 American science fiction action thriller directed by Timothy Woodward Jr. from a screenplay by Sean Ryan, with cinematography by Pablo Diez and music by Sid De La Cruz. Produced by Status Media & Entertainment and Puppy Entertainment, it stars Johnny Messner, Tom Sizemore and Mickey Rourke, alongside Taylor Cole, Jon Foo, Michael Paré and Woodward himself in a small role.

The story is set in the near future. On 4 July 2017 Kyle Norris (Sizemore), a former soldier working for the military contractor Blacksun, is on the phone with his son when the young man dies in a terrorist attack on the Pentagon, the worst since 11 September 2001, which opens a new phase of the war on terror. Months later an Iraq War veteran, Jack Simon (Woodward), who had survived an attack on his patrol in the Middle East and walked unscathed out of a minefield, opens fire with an automatic rifle in a crowded hotel lobby, killing several people including a senator. Under interrogation he first insists he knows nothing of the crime, then abruptly confesses and takes his own life. Detective Walker (Messner), a troubled homicide investigator, keeps digging even after he is taken off the case, and becomes convinced that a conspiracy is behind it, particularly after he is contacted by the eccentric scientist Clarence Peterson (Rourke). The trail leads to a secret Blacksun program developing a form of remote mind control capable of replacing a person's personality and directing their actions, which Norris hopes to turn against the terrorists who killed his son. As Walker's own family is put in danger, he fights to shut down the out-of-control program, whose weapon turns out to take more than one form, including a giant humanoid robot.

Cinedigm released the film on Blu-ray in the United States on 1 March 2016, and reviews were negative. Jeffrey Kauffman of Blu-ray.com rated it 1.5 out of 5, comparing it to a mix of The Manchurian Candidate and Freaky Friday and calling it so ham-fisted that key plot points make little sense even once explained, though he found Messner an appealing presence. TheaterByte likened it to a bad made-for-television B-movie, citing its plot holes and hammy performances.

title: Deadpool 2
tagline: Prepare for the Second Coming.
overview: Wisecracking mercenary Deadpool battles the evil and powerful Cable and other bad guys to save a boy's life.
plot:
Deadpool 2 is a 2018 superhero film directed by David Leitch and written by Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick. The movie is the sequel to the 2016 film Deadpool, starring Ryan Reynolds as the titular character.

The film begins with Wade Wilson (Deadpool), who has been living in hiding after his last adventure. He is approached by Cable (Josh Brolin), a time-traveling mutant from the future, who claims that he needs Wade's help to prevent a catastrophic event that will destroy humanity. Cable explains that he was sent back in time to kill a young mutant named Russell Collins (Julian Dennison), also known as Firefist, who is destined to become a powerful villain.

Wade agrees to help Cable and joins him on a mission to stop Firefist from being killed by the villainous Ajax (Ed Skrein). Along the way, they are joined by Domino (Zazie Beetz), a mutant with the ability to control luck. The team also includes Negasonic Teenage Warhead (Brianna Hildebrand) and Russell's mother, Vanessa (Gina Carano).

As they journey through time, Wade begins to develop feelings for Vanessa, who is being pursued by Ajax. Meanwhile, Cable's true intentions are revealed: he wants to kill Firefist because he believes that the young mutant will become a threat to humanity.

The team eventually reaches the present day, where they must stop Ajax from carrying out his plan. However, things don't go as planned, and Wade is forced to confront his own demons in order to save Vanessa and prevent the catastrophic event.

In the end, Wade is able to defeat Ajax and save Vanessa, but not before she sacrifices herself to protect him. Cable's true intentions are also revealed: he wants to kill Firefist because he believes that the young mutant will become a threat to humanity. However, it is later revealed that Cable's actions were motivated by a desire to prevent a disaster that would have killed millions of people.

The film ends with Wade reflecting on his experiences and realizing that he has found a new family among the X-Force team. He also begins to develop feelings for Vanessa, who appears in a post-credits scene as a ghostly apparition.

Overall, Deadpool 2 is a action-packed and humorous film that explores themes of time travel, sacrifice, and redemption. The movie features plenty of witty banter and over-the-top action sequences, making it a must-see for fans of the superhero genre.

title: The Shadow Effect
tagline: Once you remember, you will never forget.
overview: A young man's life is turned upside down when his violent dreams begin to blend with reality.
plot:
The Shadow Effect is a 2017 American action thriller directed by Obin Olson and Amariah Olson. Cam Gigandet stars as Gabriel, with Jonathan Rhys Meyers, Michael Biehn, Brit Shaw and Michael Aaron Milligan in supporting roles. The film combines elements of science fiction and conspiracy thriller, following a man who discovers that his violent nightmares may be memories of crimes he has actually committed. It was released by Momentum Pictures on demand, on digital HD and on DVD in the United States on 2 May 2017.

The film opens with the assassination of a United States senator by a lone gunman who kills the senator's guards and then blows himself up with a grenade. Gabriel, a seemingly ordinary man who runs a small restaurant with his wife Brinn in a quiet town, wakes every morning from vivid nightmares of such killings. He and Brinn are friendly with the local sheriff, Hodge, and their life appears peaceful, but Gabe's dreams grow increasingly real, and whenever he hears a certain piece of music he suffers a seizure.

Brinn takes him to a specialist, Dr. Reese, who prescribes medication to control the episodes. The nightmares continue, each one ending with Gabe killing a target and then dying in an explosion, only for him to wake up at home. Visiting the scene of one of these apparent dreams, he finds physical evidence that suggests the events were real. When he stops taking the medication, he discovers that he can resist the music's control and remain aware while a mysterious handler gives him a new target. Pretending to follow orders, Gabe begins to investigate, uncovering a secret program that uses mind control and identity manipulation to create untraceable assassins, and he realizes that people he trusted, including the sheriff, may be part of it. Running from those who want to silence him, he must determine which of his memories are his own and whether his life with Brinn is real.

The film received little critical attention on its release. As a low-budget independent production released directly to home video and on-demand platforms, it was covered by only a handful of outlets, and the reviews that did appear were largely unfavorable.

title: Wonderstruck
tagline: It's not what you look at that matters, it's what you see.
overview: The story of a young boy in the Midwest is told simultaneously with a tale about a young girl in New York from fifty years ago as they both seek the same mysterious connection.
plot:
Wonderstruck is a 2017 American drama film directed by Todd Haynes. The story revolves around two young protagonists, Ben and Rose, who are connected through a mysterious letter that sets them on a journey to uncover the truth about their families' pasts.

The main theme of Wonderstruck is the power of storytelling and its ability to transcend time and space. Through the interconnected narratives of Ben and Rose, the film explores how stories can be passed down through generations, influencing our understanding of ourselves and our place in the world.

One of the central themes of the film is also the idea of identity and self-discovery. Both Ben and Rose are searching for answers about their families' pasts, which leads them to question their own identities and sense of belonging. As they navigate through their respective stories, they begin to uncover secrets that challenge their perceptions of themselves and their relationships with others.

Furthermore, Wonderstruck touches on the theme of love and connection across time and space. Despite being separated by decades, Ben and Rose form a deep bond through their shared experiences and the mysterious letter that brings them together. The film highlights the importance of human connections in our lives, even when we are physically far apart.

The film also explores the idea of nostalgia and its impact on our understanding of the past. Through the characters' stories, the film shows how nostalgia can be both a source of comfort and a hindrance to moving forward. As Ben and Rose navigate their respective narratives, they must confront the complexities of their families' pasts and the ways in which nostalgia can shape our perceptions of reality.

Overall, Wonderstruck is a poignant exploration of the human experience, delving into themes that are both deeply personal and universally relatable.

title: Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw
tagline: Nothing is stronger than family.
overview: Ever since US Diplomatic Security Service Agent Hobbs and lawless outcast Shaw first faced off, they just have traded smack talk and body blows. But when cyber-genetically enhanced anarchist Brixton's ruthless actions threaten the future of humanity, they join forces to defeat him.
plot:
Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw is a 2019 action spy comedy film directed by David Leitch, and it serves as a spin-off from the Fast & Furious franchise. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson as Luke Hobbs, Jason Statham as Deckard Shaw, and Vanessa Kirby as Hattie Shaw.

The story begins with a flashback of Deckard Shaw (Jason Statham) being captured by the CIA after killing his brother Owen (Alexander Skarsgård), who was working for the agency. However, Shaw is rescued by Brixton Lore (Idris Elba), a British Special Forces operative and the main antagonist of the film.

The present-day story follows Luke Hobbs (Dwayne Johnson) and Deckard Shaw as they are forced to work together to take down Brixton Lore, who has stolen a genetically enhanced strain of the Riddick virus from the CIA. This virus is capable of granting superhuman strength and agility to its host.

As Hobbs and Shaw embark on their mission, they must navigate through various obstacles, including high-speed chases, hand-to-hand combat, and espionage. Along the way, they also encounter Hattie Shaw (Vanessa Kirby), Deckard's sister, who is a skilled hacker and helps them in their quest to stop Brixton.

Throughout the film, Hobbs and Shaw engage in witty banter and comedic moments, showcasing their contrasting personalities. However, as the story progresses, they begin to develop a begrudging respect for each other, which ultimately leads to a more effective partnership.

As the stakes rise, Hobbs and Shaw discover that Brixton's plan is to use the Riddick virus to create an army of super-soldiers, which would grant him control over the world. The duo must work together to stop Brixton and his minions, leading to an action-packed showdown in London.

The film features a mix of high-octane action sequences, humor, and heart, making it a thrilling ride for audiences. While it deviates from the traditional Fast & Furious formula, Hobbs & Shaw delivers on its promise of non-stop entertainment, with impressive stunts and impressive performances from its leads.

Overall, Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw is an enjoyable spin-off that expands the Fast & Furious universe in a fresh and exciting way. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and pulse-pounding action sequences, it's a must-watch for fans of the franchise and action movies in general.

title: The Cloverfield Paradox
tagline: The future unleashed every thing
overview: Orbiting above a planet on the brink of war, scientists test a device to solve an energy crisis and end up face-to-face with a dark alternate reality.
plot:
The Cloverfield Paradox is a 2018 science fiction horror film directed by Julius Onah and written by Jeff Nichols. The movie takes place in a space station called Clovers, where scientists are conducting experiments to harness the energy of black holes.

The main themes of The Cloverfield Paradox include:

1. **The Dangers of Playing with Nature**: The film explores the consequences of tampering with forces beyond human control. The scientists on the space station, led by Dr. Catherine Halsey (Gugu Mbatha-Raw), are trying to harness the energy of black holes to create a new source of clean energy. However, their experiments go awry, and they inadvertently unleash a catastrophic event that threatens the entire space station.

2. **The Ethics of Scientific Progress**: The movie raises questions about the ethics of scientific progress and the responsibility that comes with it. The scientists on the space station are driven by a desire to make history and leave a mark on humanity, but their actions have devastating consequences.

3. **Isolation and Confinement**: The film takes place in a confined environment, where the characters are isolated from the rest of the world. This isolation creates tension and paranoia among the crew members, which ultimately contributes to the chaos that unfolds.

4. **The Unpredictability of Technology**: The movie highlights the unpredictability of technology and the dangers of relying on it too heavily. The black hole energy experiments go haywire, and the characters are forced to confront the consequences of their actions.

5. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Despite the chaos and destruction that ensues, the film ultimately focuses on the human connection between the characters. The relationships between the crew members are put to the test as they try to survive and find a way to escape the space station.

Overall, The Cloverfield Paradox is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas through a sci-fi horror lens.

title: Set It Up
tagline: Finding love takes some assistants.
overview: Two overworked and underpaid assistants come up with a plan to get their bosses off their backs by setting them up with each other.
plot:
Set It Up is an American romantic comedy of 2018 directed by Claire Scanlon and written by Katie Silberman, about two overworked New York assistants who set up their demanding bosses. Zoey Deutch plays Harper Moore and Glen Powell plays Charlie Young, with Lucy Liu as Harper's boss Kirsten Stevens, Taye Diggs as Charlie's boss Rick Otis, Joan Smalls as Charlie's girlfriend Suze, Meredith Hagner as Harper's best friend and roommate Becca and Tituss Burgess as the janitor known as Creepy Tim.

Harper works for Kirsten, a former journalist who now edits a sports media empire, and dreams of writing about sports herself; Charlie works for Rick, a high-strung venture capitalist whose connections could guarantee him a promotion. They meet one night when both bosses want dinner: Harper has food but no cash, and Charlie has cash but no food, so he pays and lets her take one of the meals. Complaining that their jobs leave them no free time, Harper suggests setting up their bosses, reasoning that two people busy with romance would have less time to overwork their assistants. Charlie agrees after Suze nearly leaves him for neglecting her.

A staged meeting in a stuck elevator, arranged with Creepy Tim's help, collapses when a panicking delivery man joins them, but at a baseball game the assistants bribe the kiss-cam operator, and after three attempts Rick and Kirsten kiss. As the relationship wobbles, Harper and Charlie keep it alive by secretly planning dates, leaving notes and gifts, and booking a weekend away, and Charlie joins Harper at Becca's engagement party. When the bosses return engaged, Charlie learns that Rick proposed partly to provoke his ex-wife Kiki, with whom he is still sleeping. Harper finds out too, is dismayed that Charlie still wants the wedding to happen, and confesses the scheme to Kirsten, who fires her. Charlie, realizing he does not love Suze, breaks up with her, rushes to the airport, quits and tells Kirsten that Rick neither loves nor knows her, and she calls off the elopement. Harper, focusing on her writing, turns down Kirsten's offer to rehire her, though Kirsten offers to edit her article. Kirsten has also summoned Charlie, now working as a temp while he works out what he wants, and Harper and Charlie realize they are being set up. They admit their feelings and kiss.

Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer was originally set to distribute the film, which Netflix released on 15 June 2018. Reviews were largely positive.

title: Hostiles
tagline: No peace without sacrifice
overview: A legendary Native American-hating Army captain nearing retirement in 1892 is given one last assignment: to escort a Cheyenne chief and his family through dangerous territory back to his Montana reservation.
plot:
Hostiles is a 2017 American Western drama film directed by Scott Cooper and written by Cooper and John Logan. The film stars Christian Bale, Rosamund Pike, and Wes Studi.

The story takes place in 1873, after the end of the Indian Wars. Captain Joseph J. Blocker (Christian Bale), a former Union Army officer, is tasked with escorting Cheyenne war chief Black Kettle's family to their new home in Montana Territory. The family consists of Black Kettle's wife, Rose (Rosamund Pike), and their two children.

Blocker is initially reluctant for the job, but eventually accepts it after being offered a significant amount of money by the U.S. government. He sets out on his journey with a small group of soldiers, including Private Christian Frye (Wes Studi) and Sergeant First Class Henry Kane (Tim McGraw).

As they travel through the vast and unforgiving terrain of the American West, Blocker begins to question the morality of the mission. He is forced to confront the harsh realities of the treatment of Native Americans by the U.S. government and the violence that has been inflicted upon them.

The group faces numerous challenges along the way, including treacherous landscapes, hostile Native American tribes, and personal conflicts within their own ranks. Blocker's relationship with Frye, in particular, is strained, as they have different views on how to handle the situation.

As they near their destination, Blocker begins to realize that the journey has changed him. He has come to understand the gravity of his mission and the impact it will have on the people he is about to meet. The film's climax features a tense confrontation between Blocker and Black Kettle, which ultimately leads to a tragic outcome.

Throughout the film, Cooper explores themes of colonialism, violence, and redemption. He also delves into the complexities of human relationships and the moral ambiguities that arise in situations where right and wrong are not clearly defined.

The film's cinematography is stunning, capturing the vast expanses of the American West and the harsh beauty of its landscapes. The score by Lorne Balfe perfectly complements the on-screen action, adding to the overall sense of tension and unease.

Overall, Hostiles is a powerful and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront their assumptions about the American West and its history. With outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Christian Bale, it is a must-see for fans of Westerns and anyone interested in exploring the complexities of human nature.

The office Christmas party is an annual tradition at Harper-Dole, where employees are encouraged to let loose and have fun.

However, things take a turn when Josh's new business partner, Todd (played by Tad Hilgenbrandt), starts to exert his influence over the company. Todd is a ruthless and cunning businessman who wants to modernize the company and make it more profitable. He sees the office Christmas party as an opportunity to boost morale and increase productivity.

Todd convinces Josh that he needs to take the party to the next level, which means hiring a professional DJ and renting out a luxurious venue. He plans to use the party as a way to impress potential investors and secure funding for his own business ventures.

As the party gets underway, Josh starts to realize that Todd is not what he seems. He tries to intervene, but it's too late. The party descends into chaos, with employees getting drunk and wild, and Todd using the opportunity to schmooze with potential investors.

Meanwhile, Carol is struggling to balance her work and personal life. She's feeling overwhelmed and stressed out, and she starts to question whether she can keep up with Josh's demanding schedule.

As the night wears on, Josh realizes that he needs to take control of the situation. He rallies his employees and together they stage a rebellion against Todd's plans. In the end, Josh emerges victorious, but not before the party has descended into complete chaos.

The movie ends with Josh and Carol reflecting on the events of the previous night. They realize that they need to find a better balance between work and personal life, and that they can't let their careers define them. The final shot is of the office Christmas party decorations being taken down, symbolizing the end of an era.

Overall, Office Christmas Party is a hilarious and entertaining movie that explores the challenges of modern worklife. With its talented cast and witty script, it's a must-see for anyone who loves comedy and satire.

Rabid is a 2019 Canadian body horror film directed by David Cronenberg. The movie explores the theme of toxic masculinity and the objectification of women, particularly in the context of a patriarchal society that perpetuates violence against female bodies.

The film's narrative revolves around a mysterious outbreak of rabies that causes its victims to become violent and aggressive, leading to a series of gruesome and disturbing events. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the physical transformation of the infected individuals but in the societal attitudes that enable and perpetuate this violence.

The main character, Justin, is a male protagonist who embodies toxic masculinity, with his aggressive behavior and lack of empathy towards women. As he navigates the outbreak, he finds himself drawn to a female victim, which serves as a catalyst for his own transformation and eventual confrontation with his own demons.

Throughout the film, Cronenberg critiques the societal norms that perpetuate violence against women, particularly in the context of a patriarchal society where men are socialized to be aggressive and dominant. The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and the blurring of boundaries between human and animal.

Ultimately, Rabid is a thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to confront their own biases and assumptions about masculinity, femininity, and the natural world.

title: Kill Command
tagline: You can't fight the future.
overview: Set in a near future, technology-reliant society that pits man against killing machines. Against this backdrop an elite army unit is helicoptered to a remote, off-the-grid island training facility. What starts out as a simple training exercise for Captain Bukes and his tight-knit unit, descends into a terrifying battle to the death, as the marines discover the island is overrun by an enemy that transcends the human concept of evil.
plot:
Kill Command, also known as Identify, is a 2016 British science fiction action horror film written and directed by Steven Gomez in his feature debut. Thure Lindhardt stars as Captain Damien Bukes, the leader of a squad of U.S. Marines, with Vanessa Kirby as Katherine Mills, a cybernetically enhanced technician, David Ajala, Tom McKay and Bentley Kalu. It was released in the United Kingdom in May 2016.

In a technologically advanced near future, Mills, who works for the Harbinger Corporation and has cybernetic implants that let her interface with machines, detects an anomaly in the programming of a military artificial-intelligence system at Harbinger I, a secret training facility on a remote island. She joins Captain Bukes and his team, Drifter, Robinson, Cutbill, Goodwin, Hackett and Loftus, who have been sent for a two-day exercise against robotic drones. On arrival, the Marines find that their global communications have been cut off, and they notice autonomous surveillance drones watching their every move.

The first engagement goes easily, as the Marines destroy the drones from a vantage point. During the battle, Mills discovers an advanced robot known as S.A.R. (Study, Analyze, Reprogram) unit 003, but she cannot access it. That night Loftus is killed by the S.A.R. unit, and the next day the soldiers find his body at the site of the first battle, while the drones, now occupying the team's original vantage point, open fire and kill Hackett. The squad realizes that the machines are learning from them, analyzing their tactics and adapting with every encounter, and that the exercise has become a real fight for survival. With the drones growing more lethal, Bukes, who distrusts Mills because she is part machine, is forced to rely on her abilities as the team tries to reach an extraction point and uncover why the system was reprogrammed to kill.

Kill Command received generally positive reviews, with a 75 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on twelve reviews. Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian called it a superior sci-fi action thriller, and Alex Billington of First Showing described it as impressive, with critics praising its visual effects, which were achieved on a modest budget, and its tense, efficient staging of the combat sequences.

plot:
Scoob! is a 2020 American mystery-comedy film directed by Joe Wizan and written by Jared Bush, Emily A. Skinner, and Matt Lieberman. The movie is based on the classic Hanna-Barbera cartoon series Scooby-Doo.

The story begins with Shaggy Rogers (voiced by Will Forte) and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Frank Welker), a pair of best friends who travel around in their psychedelic van, the Mystery Machine. They are joined by Velma Dinkley (voiced by Zoe Kravitz), Daphne Blake (voiced by Kiersey Clemons), and Fred Jones (voiced by Jason Isaacs) on various adventures.

The movie takes place during the 1970s, when the gang is still in high school. They are approached by a wealthy businessman named Mr. Jenkins (voiced by Tim Blaney), who hires them to investigate a series of paranormal occurrences at his mansion. The gang soon discovers that they are not alone, as they encounter a group of ghostly apparitions and supernatural creatures.

As the mystery unfolds, the gang learns that the ghostly entities are actually the vengeful spirits of Mr. Jenkins' former business partners, who were wronged by him in the past. The gang must work together to uncover the truth behind the haunting and put an end to it.

Throughout the movie, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo's friendship is put to the test as they face various challenges and obstacles. Velma uses her analytical skills to decipher clues and solve puzzles, while Daphne provides comedic relief with her fashion sense and resourcefulness. Fred, on the other hand, struggles with his leadership role and must learn to trust his friends.

As the mystery deepens, the gang discovers that Mr. Jenkins is not who he claims to be. He is actually a former con artist who has been using his wealth and influence to cover up his past mistakes. The gang must use all their skills and work together to expose Mr. Jenkins' true identity and bring him to justice.

In the end, the gang succeeds in solving the mystery and putting an end to the haunting. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, trust, and believing in themselves. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment of Shaggy and Scooby-Doo sharing a laugh and a Scooby Snack, as the Mystery Machine drives off into the sunset.

Overall, Scoob! is a fun and entertaining movie that pays homage to the classic Scooby-Doo cartoon series while also offering a fresh and modern take on the characters. The movie features plenty of humor, action, and heart, making it a great watch for both old and new fans of the franchise.

title: The Little Mermaid
tagline: A new twist on the classic tail
overview: A young reporter and his niece discover a beautiful and enchanting creature they believe to be the real little mermaid.
plot:
The Little Mermaid is a 2018 American live-action fantasy adventure film inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's 1837 fairy tale. Written and directed by Blake Harris and co-directed by Chris Bouchard, it stars William Moseley as reporter Cam Harrison, Poppy Drayton as the mermaid Elizabeth, Loreto Peralta as Cam's niece Elle and Armando Gutierrez as the wizard Locke, with Shirley MacLaine as Eloise, Gina Gershon and Shanna Collins.

The film is framed as a story told by a grandmother, Eloise, to her two granddaughters. After recounting a version of The Little Mermaid in which a mermaid princess is tricked by a wizard who steals her soul and forces her to live in servitude, she tells them of a girl she once knew who met a real mermaid. In this tale, Cam is a young newspaper reporter caring for his niece Elle, who suffers from an incurable illness. When his editor assigns him to investigate a traveling circus whose owner, Locke, sells water that he claims has healing powers because it comes from a mermaid, Cam hopes that it might help Elle.

Cam and Elle travel to the circus in Mississippi, where they see a mermaid displayed in a glass tank. Cam's investigation shows that the healing water is a fraud, and he assumes the mermaid must be a hoax too, until he and Elle meet her in the woods. She introduces herself as Elizabeth and explains that she can walk on land when the tide is low, but that she cannot leave because Locke holds her soul in a vial. As Cam falls for Elizabeth, Locke discovers that Elle has the heart of a mermaid and kidnaps her for his own purposes. With the help of Thora, a fortune teller with magical powers, and Ulysses, a skilled circus fighter, both of whom were also tricked into joining Locke's circus, Cam tries to rescue Elle, recover Elizabeth's soul and help her return to the sea.

The film presents a family-friendly, small-town reimagining of the fairy tale, set in the American South and centered on themes of sacrifice and belief.

The Little Mermaid was released by AMC Theatres on August 17, 2018. It received negative reviews and was a box-office bomb, grossing about 4.5 million dollars against a 5 million dollar budget; the Los Angeles Times found the script too earnest and forced to be sufficiently fun or wondrous.

title: Fast X
overview: The tenth installment in the Fast Saga.
plot:
Fast X, also known as Fast & Furious 10, is a 2023 American action film directed by Louis Leterrier from a screenplay by Dan Mazeau and Justin Lin, the sequel to F9 and the tenth main installment of the Fast & Furious franchise. Vin Diesel returns as Dominic Toretto, with Michelle Rodriguez, Tyrese Gibson, Chris "Ludacris" Bridges, John Cena, Nathalie Emmanuel, Sung Kang, Jason Statham and Charlize Theron, joined by Jason Momoa as the villain and Brie Larson. Leterrier replaced Lin as director early in production.

Dante Reyes, son of the drug lord Hernan Reyes, whom Dom's crew robbed in Rio de Janeiro years earlier, survived the heist that killed his father and has spent a decade plotting revenge. The wounded cyberterrorist Cipher arrives at Dom's door to warn that Dante is coming for his family. Dom's team has been sent on a supposed Agency mission to Rome, which turns out to be a trap set by Dante: the cargo they are stealing is a powerful bomb, which Dante sends rolling through the city. Dom manages to push it into the Tiber, limiting the destruction, but Letty is captured, and the Agency's new leader, Aimes, brands the team as terrorists and launches a manhunt.

Separated and hunted, the family scatters. Dom's brother, Jakob, takes Dom's young son, Little B, into hiding, while Tess, daughter of the missing Mr. Nobody, helps Dom track Dante. Dom confronts his enemy in a street race in Rio, while Roman, Tej, Han and Ramsey travel to London and enlist the help of their former foe Deckard Shaw. Letty, held in a secret Agency prison in Antarctica, forms an uneasy alliance with Cipher.

Dante steals the God's Eye surveillance program and abducts Little B in Portugal. Jakob sacrifices himself so that Dom can rescue his son, and Dante reveals that Aimes has been his accomplice, shooting down a plane carrying the rest of the crew. In a cliffhanger ending, Dom and Little B escape a trap by driving off a dam, only for Dante to blow it up around them, while in Antarctica, Gisele, long believed dead, arrives to rescue Letty and Cipher. A mid-credits scene shows Dante targeting Luke Hobbs.

Fast X premiered in Rome on May 12, 2023, and was released by Universal Pictures on May 19. Its budget of nearly $380 million made it one of the most expensive films ever made. Reviews were mixed, praising Momoa's flamboyant performance and the action but criticizing the writing, and it grossed $714 million worldwide, falling short of expectations.

title: Okja

plot:
Okja is a 2017 South Korean-American science fiction film directed by Bong Joon-ho, written by Bong Joon-ho and Han Jin Won, and produced by Plan B Entertainment. The film stars An Seo Hyun, Byun Hee-bong, Steven Yeun, Paul Dano, Lily Collins, and Jake Gyllenhaal.

The story begins in a small village in South Korea, where a young girl named Mija (An Seo Hyun) lives with her father, Mr. Park (Byun Hee-bong), who is a kind-hearted farmer. The family's life is disrupted when a multinational corporation called Mirae Life Science, led by Lucy Mirando (Jake Gyllenhaal), arrives in the village to harvest a genetically engineered super-pig named Okja.

Okja is a massive, intelligent, and friendly creature that has been created using advanced biotechnology. Mija forms a deep bond with Okja, and as she grows older, she becomes determined to save her beloved companion from being exploited by Mirae Life Science for their own gain.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mirae Life Science plans to use Okja's DNA to create a new breed of super-pigs, which will be used for food production. Mija and her father embark on a perilous journey across the globe to stop the corporation and rescue Okja from their clutches.

Along the way, they meet a group of animal rights activists, led by Johnny Wilcox (Steven Yeun), who are fighting against Mirae Life Science's sinister plans. The group faces numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to reach Okja before it's too late.

As Mija and her allies close in on their target, the stakes become increasingly high. The corporation will stop at nothing to achieve its goals, and Mija must use all her wit and determination to outsmart them and save Okja.

The film's climax features an epic showdown between Mija and Lucy Mirando, with the fate of Okja hanging precariously in the balance. In the end, Mija emerges victorious, but not without scars. The film concludes on a hopeful note, with Mija reflecting on the lessons she has learned about the importance of compassion, empathy, and standing up for what is right.

Throughout the film, Bong Joon-ho explores themes of corporate greed, animal rights, and the ethics of scientific experimentation. Okja is a powerful commentary on the consequences of playing God with nature and the importance of treating all living beings with kindness and respect.

Overall, Okja is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its talented cast, engaging storyline, and thought-provoking themes, it's a must-see for anyone who loves science fiction, adventure, or just great storytelling in general.

title: Early Man
tagline: Time to test their metal
overview: Dug, along with his sidekick Hognob, unite a cavemen tribe to save their hidden valley from being spoiled and, all together as a team, to face the menace of a mysterious and mighty enemy, on the turf of an ancient and sacred sport.
plot:
Early Man is a 2018 British animated comedy film directed by Nick Park and Peter Lord, produced by Aardman Animations, and distributed by Universal Pictures.

The movie takes place in the Stone Age, where a group of cavemen live. The story revolves around Dug (voiced by Tom Hiddleston), a brave and clever caveman who dreams of defeating the evil Bronze Age invaders led by Lord Nooth (voiced by Hank Azaria). 

One of the main themes of Early Man is the importance of community, friendship, and unity in the face of adversity. The film showcases the strong bonds between Dug's tribe and their determination to protect their way of life.

Another significant theme is the clash of cultures and the impact of colonialism on indigenous societies. The movie highlights the struggles faced by the cavemen as they try to adapt to the changing world brought about by the Bronze Age invaders.

The film also explores the idea of perseverance, courage, and creative problem-solving in the face of overwhelming odds. Dug's cleverness and resourcefulness play a crucial role in the tribe's survival and ultimately their victory over the invaders.

Overall, Early Man is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of community, creativity, and determination in the face of adversity.

title: Ice Age: The Great Egg-Scapade
tagline: The world’s first Easter egg hunt. It all started right here.
overview: A harried prehistoric bird mother entrusts her precious, soon-to-hatch egg to Sid. When she recommends him to her neighbours, business booms at his new egg-sitting service. However, dastardly pirate bunny, Squint, who is seeking revenge on the herd, steals, camouflages and hides all the eggs. Once again, with Squint’s twin brother assisting, Manny, Diego and the rest of the gang come to the rescue and take off on a daring mission that turns into the world’s first Easter egg hunt.
plot:
Directed by Ricardo Curtis for Blue Sky Studios, Ice Age: The Great Egg-Scapade is an animated comedy-mystery television special first broadcast in 2016. Set between Ice Age: Continental Drift and Ice Age: Collision Course, it brings back most of the franchise's voice cast, with Ray Romano as Manny, John Leguizamo as Sid, Denis Leary as Diego, Queen Latifah as Ellie, Keke Palmer as Peaches, and Seann William Scott and Josh Peck as the opossum brothers Crash and Eddie. Seth Green replaces Aziz Ansari as the pirate rabbit Squint, and the cast also includes Blake Anderson as his brother Clint, Taraji P. Henson, Gabriel Iglesias, Wendy Williams and Chris Wedge as Scrat.

As spring arrives, the herd prepares for Easter. Ellie struggles to decorate alone while Manny, Diego, Crash and Eddie lounge around watching a fight between animals, and the opossums try in vain to prank Peaches, accidentally inventing April Fools' Day. Peaches only wants to spend the holiday with her friends. Sid, meanwhile, offers to look after other animals' eggs for their parents, to the scorn of Manny and Diego.

Squint, a former member of Captain Gutt's pirate crew, has spent months hiding in his family's burrow with his mother and his lazy brother Clint. Eager for revenge on Manny and his friends for what they did to Gutt and his ship, he demands that they build him a new one, and when they refuse he steals the eggs while Sid sleeps, leaving Sid to take the blame. Clint offers the friends a map, and they recover the eggs, which Squint has painted to blend in with their surroundings, but one is still missing. Squint threatens to scramble it unless he gets his ship by the next day. Clint lures his brother into an ambush, and the last egg turns out to have been painted to look like an acorn and snatched by Scrat. After a struggle and a rescue at the edge of a cliff, Sid defeats Squint with the help of a trap and one of Crash and Eddie's pranks. The family celebrates Easter together, and Sid proposes that Clint become the Easter Bunny, painting and hiding eggs every year.

The special premiered on Fox on 20 March 2016, as a lead-in to the live special The Passion: New Orleans, and was released on DVD in March 2017.

title: While the Wolf's Away
tagline: Not all secrets are innocent
overview: A young teen and his misfit group of friends try to escape from a strict boarding school that holds dangerous secrets.
plot:
While the Wolf's Away (Spanish: Mientras el lobo no está) is a 2017 Mexican mystery drama film written and directed by Joseph Hemsani in his directing debut, from a screenplay co-written with Abe Rosenberg. Hemsani had previously produced and co-written the horror film Archivo 253. Running 123 minutes, the film was distributed by Cinépolis Distribución and released in Mexican cinemas on 24 February 2017. It stars Luis de la Rosa, Mauricio García Lozano, Mar Carrera, Miranda Kay and Richie Mestre, with Regina Reynoso and Carla Adell.

Set in 1958 in an unnamed country, the story takes place at a strict, isolated boarding school deep in a forest. Alex, a troubled boy sent there after a prank that ended in tragedy, upsets the institution's rigid discipline from the moment he arrives. He bonds with three fellow students who share a single goal, to escape, and, inspired by legends of former pupils who supposedly managed to flee, the four friends begin plotting a breakout. Alex also falls for Daniela, one of the girls boarding at the school. As the friends defy the adults' authority and abuse, their flirtations and escape attempts begin to uncover the school's dark secrets, and the friendship and loyalty among them become essential for surviving an atmosphere ruled by fear and humiliation. The title's "wolf", the predator destroying the lives of those who cross its path, ultimately proves to be the school's own director, played by García Lozano.

The film addresses abuse committed in the name of education and good behaviour, violence, freedom and the anxieties of adolescence, mixing suspense with touches of comedy and romance; its message is that the living can be more frightening than the dead. It was shot across eighteen locations that together form the boarding school, conceived almost as a character in its own right.

Critics praised the period atmosphere, art direction and cinematography but were divided on the rest. Time Out México gave it three stars out of five, describing a film with a distinct personality within contemporary Mexican cinema and noting influences ranging from Carlos Enrique Taboada's Hasta el viento tiene miedo to the Harry Potter stories. CineNT found it predictable and overlong, with stilted dialogue and uneven child performances, though it singled out García Lozano's frighteningly human headmaster, and El Blog de Yes considered it a disappointing coming-of-age thriller hampered by a flat script and tedious pacing.

title: Patriots Day
tagline: The inside story of the world's greatest manhunt.
overview: In the aftermath of an unspeakable act of terror, Police Sergeant Tommy Saunders joins courageous survivors, first responders and investigators in a race against the clock to hunt down the Boston Marathon bombers before they strike again.
plot:
Patriots Day is a 2016 American biographical drama film directed by Peter Berg, based on the book "We Were Soldiers Once... And Young" by Harold G. Schrier and the book "Boston Strong: A City's United Stand in the Face of Terror" by Casey Sherman and Dave Weddle.

The main themes of Patriots Day include:

1. **Trauma and Resilience**: The film explores the traumatic events that unfolded on April 15, 2013, when two bombs exploded near the finish line of the Boston Marathon, killing three people and injuring hundreds more. The movie delves into the emotional toll of these events on the survivors, their families, and the community as a whole.

2. **Community and Unity**: Patriots Day highlights the strong sense of community and unity that emerged in Boston during this time. The film shows how ordinary citizens came together to support each other, volunteer for search and rescue efforts, and provide aid to those affected by the bombings.

3. **Heroism and Sacrifice**: The movie celebrates the bravery and selflessness of first responders, including police officers, firefighters, and medical personnel who risked their lives to save others during the crisis. It also honors the memory of the three victims killed in the bombings: Martin Richard, Krystle Campbell, and Sean Collier.

4. **Patriotism and National Unity**: The film's title, Patriots Day, refers to the day when the Boston Marathon bombing occurred. However, it also serves as a metaphor for the resilience and patriotism of the American people in the face of terrorism. The movie shows how the city of Boston and the nation came together to support each other and reaffirm their commitment to freedom and democracy.

5. **Grief and Healing**: Patriots Day explores the emotional journey of those affected by the bombings, including survivors, first responders, and family members of the victims. The film shows how time can be a balm for wounds, but also acknowledges that healing is a long and difficult process.

Overall, Patriots Day is a powerful tribute to the strength and resilience of the human spirit in the face of tragedy and adversity.

title: The Curse of Sleeping Beauty
tagline: The fairytale was only the beginning
overview: Thomas Kaiser inherits an ancestral mansion that has been in his family for generations — only to learn that he has also inherited an ancient curse stemming back to the Crusades. Forced into his new role as “protector” — the guardian appointed to keep the evil demons in the house at bay — Thomas teams with an ambitious local realtor and paranormal cleric to unravel the mystery of the house, while struggling to awaken the beautiful Briar Rose, held captive in a terrifying netherworld seen previously in his dreams.
plot:
The Curse of Sleeping Beauty is a 2016 American fantasy horror film directed by Pearry Reginald Teo, who co-wrote the screenplay with Josh Nadler. Ethan Peck stars as Thomas Kaiser, with India Eisley as Briar Rose and Natalie Hall as Linda. The story is based on a comic book of the same name by Everette Hartsoe and on the fairy tale Little Briar Rose as told by the Brothers Grimm and Charles Perrault. The film was shot in Los Angeles and released in the United States by 2B Films on Friday 13 May 2016.

Thomas, a painter, suffers from recurring dreams in which he sees a beautiful sleeping girl whom he is unable to wake. Whenever he tries to kiss her, he is distracted by a vision of a strange building and wakes up in a state of sleep paralysis. One day a law firm contacts him about an inheritance from his estranged uncle Clive, who has killed himself, leaving Thomas a letter and a property called Kaiser Gardens. The letter warns that the family is cursed. To his astonishment, Thomas discovers that the house he has inherited is the building from his dreams.

That night at the property, he dreams of the sleeping girl again and this time succeeds in kissing and waking her. She tells him that her name is Briar Rose. He then experiences a false awakening and is attacked by a terrifying figure known as the Veiled Demon. An appraiser tells him that many people have disappeared in the house over the years without the police finding any trace of them, and Thomas finds strange mannequins and an immovable door bearing a shrine. Linda, a realtor whose brother vanished in the house, helps him investigate and tells him that he is now supernaturally bound to the property. Through his dreams, Rose insists that Thomas must free her and reveals that the house belongs to his bloodline, and Thomas must uncover the dark secret behind his family's curse and the demons hidden beneath the house before it claims him.

The film reimagines the classic fairy tale as a dark, dream-based horror story, using sleep paralysis, nightmares and Gothic architecture to blur the boundaries between dreams and reality.

The Curse of Sleeping Beauty received mostly negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a rating of about 17 percent, and Luke Thompson of Forbes panned it, saying that it fractures more than a fairy tale.

title: I, Tonya
tagline: Fitting in is overrated
overview: Competitive ice skater Tonya Harding rises amongst the ranks at the U.S. Figure Skating Championships, but her future in the sport is thrown into doubt when her ex-husband intervenes.
plot:
I, Tonya is a biographical sports comedy-drama film directed by Craig Gillespie, released in 2017 by LuckyChap Entertainment, Neon, and Summit Entertainment. The movie is based on the life of Tonya Harding, an American figure skater who rose to fame in the late 1980s.

The main themes of I, Tonya are:

1. **Trauma and Abuse**: The film explores Tonya's traumatic childhood, including her abusive relationship with her mother, LaVona Golden, and her father, Jeff Gillooly. These experiences have a lasting impact on Tonya's life and shape her future actions.
2. **Feminism and Empowerment**: I, Tonya is a feminist film that challenges traditional notions of femininity and female empowerment. The movie portrays Tonya as a strong-willed and determined individual who refuses to be defined by societal expectations.
3. **Class and Socioeconomic Status**: The film highlights the contrast between Tonya's humble beginnings and her rise to fame in the wealthy world of figure skating. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on class differences and the struggles faced by those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds.
4. **Performance and Identity**: I, Tonya explores the tension between Tonya's public persona and her private self. The film shows how she navigates the pressures of fame, while also trying to maintain her individuality and authenticity.
5. **Guilt and Redemption**: Throughout the movie, Tonya grapples with guilt over her involvement in the attack on Nancy Kerrigan, which led to a scandal that ruined her career. The film ultimately suggests that redemption is possible, but it requires self-awareness, accountability, and a willingness to confront one's past mistakes.

The film features outstanding performances from Margot Robbie as Tonya Harding, Allison Janney as LaVona Golden, and Sebastian Stan as Jeff Gillooly. I, Tonya received widespread critical acclaim for its bold storytelling, sharp direction, and nuanced performances.

title: The Do-Over
tagline: Dying was their first mistake.
overview: The life of a bank manager is turned upside down when a friend from his past manipulates him into faking his own death and taking off on an adventure.
plot:
The Do-Over is a 2016 American action comedy film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around identity, redemption, and personal growth.

At its core, the movie delves into the concept of identity crisis, where the protagonist, Charlie McMillan (played by Adam Sandler), finds himself at a crossroads in his life. After being betrayed by his business partner and facing financial ruin, Charlie embarks on a journey to reinvent himself and escape his past mistakes.

Throughout the film, Charlie's transformation serves as a metaphor for redemption and personal growth. As he navigates this new chapter in his life, he confronts his flaws and weaknesses, ultimately learning to let go of his ego and find a sense of purpose. The movie showcases Charlie's journey from a self-centered individual to someone who is more empathetic and self-aware.

The film also touches on the theme of escapism, as Charlie uses his newfound identity to escape his past and start anew. However, this escapism is not without its consequences, and the movie ultimately suggests that true growth and redemption require confronting one's demons rather than running from them.

Overall, The Do-Over is a lighthearted yet thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, redemption, and personal growth in an entertaining and humorous way.

title: The Hitman's Bodyguard
tagline: Everyone's out to get them... If they don't kill each other first.
overview: The world’s top bodyguard gets a new client, a hitman who must testify at the International Court of Justice. They must put their differences aside and work together to make it to the trial on time.
plot:
The Hitman's Bodyguard is a 2017 action comedy film directed by Patrick Hughes and starring Ryan Reynolds and Samuel L. Jackson.

The movie begins with Michael Bryce (Ryan Reynolds), a top-notch bodyguard who specializes in protecting high-profile clients from assassination attempts. He has a reputation for being the best in his field, but he's also a bit of a loner. His latest client is Darius Kincaid (Salma Hayek), a notorious dictator from a small country called Salazar.

However, things take a turn when Kincaid announces that she wants to retire and leave her country to live in the United States. She hires Michael to escort her across the border, but just as they're about to depart, Kincaid is ambushed by assassins sent by her former bodyguard, Balikov (Samuel L. Jackson).

Balikov is a ruthless and cunning hitman who has been hired by Kincaid's government to kill her. Michael and Kincaid are forced to flee for their lives, and they soon discover that they have a complicated past together. It turns out that Michael was once Kincaid's bodyguard when she was still in power, but he quit after discovering that she was involved in some shady dealings.

As they try to evade Balikov and his team, Michael and Kincaid develop an unlikely partnership. They start to work together, using their skills to take down the assassins and stay one step ahead of Balikov. Along the way, they also learn more about each other's pasts and the reasons behind their complicated relationship.

As the stakes grow higher, Michael and Kincaid find themselves in a series of intense and action-packed battles against Balikov and his team. They use everything from cars to guns to take down their enemies, and they also have some witty banter along the way.

In the end, Michael and Kincaid succeed in defeating Balikov and escaping across the border into the United States. However, as they're about to part ways, Michael realizes that he's developed feelings for Kincaid, who has also started to see him in a different light. The movie ends with a hint of romance between the two characters, setting up the possibility for a sequel.

Overall, The Hitman's Bodyguard is an action-packed comedy that features plenty of twists and turns. It's a fun and entertaining ride from start to finish, with great performances from Reynolds and Jackson.

title: Aftermath
tagline: All he had left was revenge
overview: A fatal plane crash changes the lives of Roman and Jake forever. Roman loses his wife and daughter in the accident, while Jake loses his mind—as he happens to be the air traffic controller who failed to avert the nightmare. Rage and revenge engulfs Roman and Jake finds himself swamped with guilt and regret.
plot:
Aftermath is a 2017 American thriller film directed by Eshom Nelms and Christopher Renz. The movie follows a former Army Ranger, Ronin (played by Aaron Eckhart), who returns home to find his family brutally murdered in their home. Consumed by grief and anger, Ronin sets out on a quest for revenge against the perpetrators.

The main themes of Aftermath include:

1. **Grief and Trauma**: The film explores the devastating effects of trauma and loss on individuals and families. Ronin's journey is driven by his need to cope with the unbearable pain of losing his loved ones.
2. **Revenge vs. Redemption**: As Ronin navigates the dark world of revenge, he begins to question whether his actions will bring him closure or perpetuate a cycle of violence. This internal conflict serves as a commentary on the destructive nature of revenge and the importance of seeking redemption.
3. **The Blurred Lines between Good and Evil**: The film raises questions about morality and the nature of evil. Ronin's perception of right and wrong becomes increasingly distorted as he seeks justice, highlighting the complexities of human behavior in the face of trauma.
4. **The Dangers of Unchecked Emotions**: Aftermath portrays the dangers of allowing emotions like anger and grief to consume us. Ronin's inability to control his emotions leads him down a path of destruction, serving as a cautionary tale about the importance of emotional regulation.

Throughout the film, these themes are expertly woven together to create a gripping narrative that explores the human condition in the face of unimaginable tragedy.

title: Crash Pad
tagline: He finally met the love of his life...Then he met her husband.
overview: A hopeless romantic thinks he's found true love with an older woman, only to learn that she's married and that his fling is merely an instrument of revenge against her neglectful husband.
plot:
Crash Pad is a 2017 American comedy directed by Kevin Tent, best known as Alexander Payne's longtime film editor, in his solo directing debut, from a screenplay by Jeremy Catalino. Domhnall Gleeson stars as Stensland, with Thomas Haden Church as Grady Dott, Christina Applegate as his wife Morgan and Nina Dobrev as Morgan's assistant Hannah. Payne served as an executive producer, and Rolfe Kent composed the score.

Stensland is a 29-year-old slacker and hopeless romantic whose idea of a good night is getting stoned and rewatching old episodes of Dawson's Creek. After two passionate days with Morgan, an older woman he is convinced is the love of his life, she abruptly tells him, while he stands naked in her bedroom, that she is married and that their fling was only a way of getting even with her husband, whom she believes has cheated on her. Crushed, Stensland spends a week sobbing on his couch, then storms into Morgan's office and threatens to tell her husband everything, drawing the eavesdropping Hannah into the drama. When Morgan calls his bluff, he phones Grady and describes the affair in detail, and Grady vows to find him and kill him.

When the furious husband turns up at Stensland's squalid bachelor apartment, however, he is mostly interested in frightening the young man, and the sight of the mess and a can of cheap stew reminds him of his own broke youth. Resentful of Morgan and convinced that success as a lawyer has robbed him of his manhood, Grady decides to move in with Stensland, paying his bills while turning the place into a base for a vengeful bachelor lifestyle. He drags his reluctant roommate through nights of binge drinking, bar fights and keg stands, coaching him to pick up women instead of falling in love with them, but Stensland proves incapable of becoming a boor, and Grady is less committed to the act than he pretends. Both men are eventually pushed toward recognizing their own share of the blame, and the story follows a familiar romantic-comedy path to a happy ending.

Crash Pad premiered at the Woodstock Film Festival, was released on video on demand on September 25, 2017, and opened in limited release on October 27 through Vertical Entertainment and Destination Films. Reviews were mixed, with a 54 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 46. The Hollywood Reporter called it a broadly appealing bad-behavior comedy carried by its leads' chemistry, and TheWrap found it far smarter than its high concept suggests.

title: Sand Castle
tagline: Home is a war away
overview: Set during the occupation of Iraq, a squad of U.S. soldiers try to protect a small village.
plot:
Sand Castle is a 2017 American war drama film directed by Fernando Coimbra from a screenplay by Chris Roessner, who drew on his own experience as a soldier in the Iraq War. It stars Nicholas Hoult, Logan Marshall-Green, Henry Cavill, Glen Powell, Tommy Flanagan, Beau Knapp and Neil Brown Jr., and centers on a young American soldier assigned to restore the water supply of an Iraqi village. The film was released on Netflix on April 21, 2017.

Private Matt Ocre joined the Army Reserve in 2001 to pay for college, and when the 2003 invasion of Iraq begins he is so reluctant to fight that he deliberately slams his hand in a Humvee door in the hope of being sent home. The ploy fails, and once his cast is removed he is deployed to Baghdad. After the initial fighting, his civil affairs squad, led by Staff Sergeant Harper, is sent to the dangerous village of Baqubah, where a Special Forces unit under Captain Syverson, whom Ocre comes to admire, explains the mission: the squad must fill a tanker at a damaged pump station and carry water back to the villagers every day while army engineers repair the system. The engineers warn that the work will take weeks unless local men can be hired, but nobody from the village turns up, so the soldiers are forced to do much of the labor themselves. The daily water runs expose them to ambushes, and in one firefight Sergeant Chutsky is killed. Progress finally comes when Kadeer, the administrator of the local school, agrees to help, but the cooperation comes at a terrible price, as the insurgents retaliate against anyone who works with the Americans. Each step forward is matched by fresh violence, and Ocre is left to question what the occupation is achieving and what his own part in it means.

Sand Castle received mixed reviews from critics. title: Here Alone
tagline: Those who stay die
overview: A woman struggles to survive on her own in the wake of a mysterious epidemic, which has decimated society and forced her deep into the unforgiving wild.
plot:
Here Alone is a 2016 American post-apocalyptic horror drama film directed by Rod Blackhurst and written by David Ebeltoft. Lucy Walters stars as Ann, a woman trying to survive alone in the wilderness after a devastating epidemic, with Adam David Thompson as Chris, Gina Piersanti as his teenage stepdaughter, Olivia, and Shane West as Ann's husband, Jason. The film premiered at the 2016 Tribeca Film Festival, where it won the audience award for narrative features, and was released theatrically in March 2017.

Some time after a mysterious infection has turned much of the world's population into violent, zombie-like creatures, Ann lives in a makeshift camp deep in the woods. Resources are scarce, and she survives by foraging and living off the land, venturing only cautiously into abandoned houses, which tend to attract the infected. She clings to remnants of the world she has lost, listening to a hand-cranked radio that broadcasts an emergency message in French, a language she does not understand. Through flashbacks, the film gradually reveals what happened to her husband, Jason, and their infant daughter.

Returning from a scavenging trip, Ann comes across Chris, who has been injured, and Olivia. She takes them in and nurses Chris back to health, but she struggles to trust them, having grown used to depending only on herself. When a storm arrives just as the pair are about to move on, Ann allows them to stay longer, and over time she and Chris become romantically involved, to Olivia's resentment. The flashbacks reveal that Jason was killed by the infected after leaving at night to find supplies, leaving Ann to protect their baby alone in a world where any sound could draw the creatures to them. As tensions rise among the three survivors and Ann's buried guilt over the fate of her daughter comes to the surface, the group must decide whether to remain in the woods or seek out other survivors, a choice that forces Ann to confront the painful decisions she has made to stay alive.

Here Alone was praised for its restrained, character-driven approach to the zombie genre, which emphasizes isolation, grief and survival over action and gore, and for Walters's understated central performance. Its quiet, slow-burning style placed it among a wave of low-budget independent films using the post-apocalyptic setting for intimate drama.

title: Imagining Zootopia
tagline: What did it take to bring the world of 'Zootopia' to life?
overview: Fusion spent two years with the production team of Disney's smash hit film. In 'Imagining Zootopia,' you will travel with the team to Africa to explore the animals in their natural habitat and find out how the storytellers and animators dealt with the very real themes of prejudice and bias.
plot:
Imagining Zootopia is a 2016 American documentary film about the making of Walt Disney Animation Studios' feature Zootopia, released in some territories as Zootropolis. Directed by Natalie Osma and Kristofer Rios for Fusion, the millennial-oriented digital network that was then half-owned by Disney, it runs about 47 minutes. Although not an official Disney production, it was made with extensive access: the filmmakers spent two years following the crew through production. It features directors Byron Howard and Rich Moore, co-director and screenwriter Jared Bush, head of story Josie Trinidad, production designer Dave Goetz, producer Clark Spencer and John Lasseter, then chief creative officer of Disney and Pixar Animation.

The documentary follows the creative process from character conception to animation. It accompanies the team on a research trip to Kenya, where they study animals in their natural habitats, and examines the artwork produced for the film, from sketches of its expressive animal characters to its highly detailed environments. The filmmakers explain the film's roots in their love of Disney films in which animals walk upright and wear clothes, such as the studio's 1973 version of Robin Hood. Rather than cataloguing every aspect of production, however, most of the film concentrates on the evolution of the story, which changed dramatically during development. In early versions, the con artist fox Nick Wilde was the protagonist instead of the rabbit police officer Judy Hopps, and the fragile peace between predators and prey was maintained only because the predators were forced to wear shock collars. The documentary traces in depth how the storytellers moved from that version to the finished film, and how they approached the real-world themes of prejudice and bias in what is essentially a family film.

Fusion released the documentary online in early April 2016, about a month after Zootopia opened in theaters to critical acclaim; by then the film had grossed nearly $800 million worldwide. Amid Amidi of Cartoon Brew called it well worth watching, describing it as a counterpart to The Sweatbox that highlights the positive changes Lasseter had brought to Disney's feature animation division, and praising its choice to focus on story development, which he felt offered real insight into what the filmmakers were trying to achieve.

plot:
"Phineas and Ferb: Star Wars", also titled "Episode IVa: May the Ferb Be with You", is a one-hour crossover special of the American animated series Phineas and Ferb, featuring characters from the Star Wars franchise. Part of the series' fourth season, it aired on Disney Channel on July 26, 2014, and on Disney XD on August 4, 2014. The idea arose after the Walt Disney Company acquired Lucasfilm, and the special retells the events of the 1977 film Star Wars from the perspective of the Phineas and Ferb characters, though it is not considered part of the Star Wars canon.

On the desert planet Tatooine, Phineas Flynn and Ferb Fletcher live with their parents as contented moisture farmers, unaware that the galaxy's fate is about to pass through their lives. Meanwhile, Perry the Platypus, reimagined as a Rebel agent, steals the plans for the Death Star from the Empire and delivers them to Princess Leia's ship. When Darth Vader captures Leia, she hides the plans in R2-D2, a moment observed by a trio of stormtroopers: Candace Flynn, Baljeet and Buford. Eager to prove herself to her superiors, Candace sets out with her companions to recover the stolen plans.

Marshall is a 2017 American biographical legal drama film directed by Reginald Hudlin from a screenplay by Michael Koskoff and his son Jacob Koskoff. It stars Chadwick Boseman as Thurgood Marshall, who would become the first African American justice of the US Supreme Court, and centers on one of his early cases, State of Connecticut v. Joseph Spell. Josh Gad, Kate Hudson, Dan Stevens, Sterling K. Brown and James Cromwell co-star.

In April 1941, Marshall is an NAACP lawyer traveling the country to defend Black people wrongly accused of crimes because of racial prejudice. He is sent to Bridgeport, Connecticut, to defend Joseph Spell, a chauffeur accused of rape by his white employer, Eleanor Strubing, in a case splashed across the newspapers. Sam Friedman, a reluctant local insurance lawyer, is assigned by his brother to sponsor Marshall's admission to the bar. Judge Foster, a friend of the father of prosecutor Lorin Willis, admits Marshall but forbids him to speak at trial, making Friedman lead counsel while Marshall guides him with notes, including advice to seat an assertive Southern white woman on the jury. Spell insists that he never had sexual contact with Strubing, and Marshall talks him out of a plea deal, but testimony about skin under Strubing's fingernails and a patrolman's traffic stop forces Spell to admit that he lied. On the stand, Spell testifies that Strubing's bruises came from her abusive husband, that on the night in question she wanted to have sex with him and that they did so consensually, after which she panicked about being found out and pregnant. As he drove her to a doctor, she hid from the patrolman, then ran to a bridge and jumped despite his attempt to stop her, surviving and inventing the rape story for a passing motorist. Asked why he did not tell the truth at first, Spell describes Black men being lynched in his native Louisiana for relations with white women, and the shaken judge lets the testimony stand. Marshall must leave for a case in Mississippi, but he helps Friedman prepare the closing argument, and Spell rejects a lighter plea offer. The Southern woman, now jury forewoman, delivers a verdict of not guilty, and Friedman phones Marshall with the news.

Shot in Los Angeles and in Buffalo and Niagara Falls, New York, the film premiered at Howard University on 20 September 2017 and opened in the US on 13 October. Critics were largely positive, giving it 80% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 66.
