It was formerly titled Dabka.

Fresh out of the University of Toronto, Jay Bahadur is struggling to break into journalism. Still living with his parents, he scrapes by conducting product surveys in supermarkets. His chance comes after an encounter with Tolbin, who encourages him to skip graduate school and pursue a bold assignment: travelling to Somalia to uncover the story behind the country's notorious pirates.

By reaching out to news outlets in Somalia, Jay connects with a local reporter, Mohamad Farole, whose family welcomes him and gives him a place to stay. He is assigned a minder, Abdirizak, known as Abdi, who explains that the men the outside world calls pirates see themselves as saviours of the sea, a kind of coast guard. From his window Jay watches the street leading to the market, where he notices Maryan, a woman who sells khat, the stimulant that serves as currency for interviews, and whose husband is himself one of the pirates.

Jay succeeds in interviewing two pirates, Boyah and Maryan's husband Garaad, but his reports go unpublished by his contact at CBC Radio, Avril Benoit, who tells him the network will pay only for an interview with hostages aboard a hijacked ship. Abdi tries to arrange access to the captive German freighter Victoria, anchored at Eyl, but after Jay pushes his contacts too hard the ship slips away overnight. Meanwhile, the hijacking of the Maersk Alabama and the ordeal of Captain Phillips unfold, and both Jay's father and his Somali hosts warn him that it is no longer safe for him to remain.

Back in Canada, Jay is welcomed home by his family and approached by a government agent seeking his insight into Somalia. Later, living in Kenya, he advises an official committee as his book about the pirates becomes a bestseller, arguing that Somalia needs recognition of its complex and honourable culture rather than warships off its coast.

The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 27, 2017, and was released by Echo Bridge on December 8, 2017, to mixed reviews, earning 63% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Stan & Ollie
tagline: The untold story of the world's greatest comedy act.
overview: With their golden era long behind them, comedy duo Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy embark on a variety hall tour of Britain and Ireland. Despite the pressures of a hectic schedule, and with the support of their wives Lucille and Ida – a formidable double act in their own right – the pair's love of performing, as well as for each other, endures as they secure their place in the hearts of their adoring public
plot:
Stan & Ollie is a 2018 biographical comedy-drama film that explores the complex and enduring friendship between two of the most iconic comedians of the silent era, Charlie Chaplin and Stan Laurel. The movie delves into the highs and lows of their partnership, which spanned over three decades.

At its core, the film is a poignant portrayal of the power of friendship and the sacrifices that come with it. The story follows the two comedians as they navigate the challenges of fame, personal struggles, and creative differences, all while maintaining an unbreakable bond that transcends their professional relationship.

One of the main themes of Stan & Ollie is the struggle for artistic control and the tension between commercial success and creative integrity. As Chaplin's star rises, he finds himself at odds with Laurel, who feels overshadowed by his partner's success. This conflict serves as a backdrop to explore the complexities of their relationship, revealing the deep-seated insecurities and vulnerabilities that lie beneath their on-screen personas.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and the fragility of ego. Both Chaplin and Laurel are struggling with their own identities outside of their partnership, grappling with personal demons and seeking validation in each other's company. This introspection adds a layer of depth to their relationship, highlighting the ways in which they both relied on each other for emotional support.

Furthermore, Stan & Ollie is a celebration of the enduring power of friendship and the human spirit. Despite facing numerous setbacks and disappointments, Chaplin and Laurel remain steadfast in their commitment to one another, finding solace in each other's company during times of turmoil. This unwavering loyalty serves as a testament to the transformative nature of their relationship, which continues to inspire and captivate audiences long after its conclusion.

Overall, Stan & Ollie is a heartwarming and poignant exploration of the complexities of friendship, artistic collaboration, and personal identity, offering a nuanced portrayal of two beloved comedians who left an indelible mark on the world of entertainment.

title: Sheep & Wolves
tagline: You can be whatever you want. The main thing is you remain yourself!
overview: In a magical faraway land, in a picturesque little village nestled among green meadows and rolling hills, lives a flock of carefree sheep. But their pastoral and stress-free life is interrupted when a pack of wolves sets up camp in the nearby ravine.
plot:
Sheep and Wolves (Russian: Volki i ovtsy. Be-e-e-zumnoe prevrashchenie) is a 2016 Russian 3D animated fantasy comedy directed by Andrey Galat and Maxim Volkov, their directorial debut, and produced by Wizart Animation with CTB Film Company. The studio's first original story, conceived by Volkov, draws on the fairy tale The Wolf and the Seven Young Goats and the idea of a wolf in sheep's clothing. Alexander Petrov voices the hero, Grey, and Elizaveta Boyarskaya his love interest, Bianca, in the Russian version, while Tom Felton and Ruby Rose take those roles in the English dub.

A pack of wolves settles in a ravine near a village of sheep. Its wise old leader, Magra, announces his retirement, and two candidates must fight to succeed him: the cruel, selfish Ragear and the carefree joker Grey, who is in love with Bianca. When Grey's immaturity leads Bianca to leave him, he visits a gypsy camp, where an eccentric hare named Mami gives him a potion he hopes will win her back. Instead it turns him into a ram. Knocked out while fleeing his former pack, he wakes in the sheep village in the care of Lyra, older sister of the lamb Shia, whom Grey had once spared. Grey struggles with his new form, offends the flock by biting during a tournament, but wins their friendship after protecting Lyra and Shia from two wolves.

Ragear murders Magra and seizes the pack, then learns of Grey's transformation and resolves to destroy the village. After a photograph seems to show Grey as a spy, he leaves the sheep, but Mami tells him of the coming attack and that he can become a wolf again by reaching a certain tree by noon. Grey instead returns to warn the flock and leads its defense, and the wolves are trapped in a flooding cave, from which Grey rescues them. Shia exposes Ragear as Magra's killer, and Grey challenges him. A potion brought by Mami and Bianca seems to fail, but after being buried under rocks Grey emerges as a wolf and sends Ragear over a waterfall to his death. Grey marries Bianca, wolves and sheep live together in peace, and Mami reveals that the potion was only spring water and that his change came from learning responsibility.

The film had a budget of about $3.4 million. It opened at number two in Russia on 1,892 screens and earned over 143 million rubles during a 19-week run. Russian reviews were warm, but critics elsewhere were largely negative, attacking its writing, pacing, characterization and lore while giving some praise to the animation.

title: Rememory
overview: The widow of a wise professor stumbles upon one of his inventions that's able to record and play a person's memory.
plot:
Rememory is a psychological sci-fi thriller that delves into the complexities of grief, loss, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film follows a detective who is tasked with solving a murder case involving a reclusive novelist, only to find himself entangled in a web of memories and alternate realities.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the protagonist's perception of time and memory is distorted, much like the novel's protagonist, who suffers from short-term memory loss. This distortion serves as a metaphor for the fragility of human memory and how it can be manipulated by external forces.

The film explores the theme of grief in a poignant manner, highlighting the ways in which it can consume us and alter our perception of reality. The protagonist's investigation into the murder case becomes an obsession, driven by his own personal loss and sense of guilt. Through this lens, the film sheds light on the human capacity for resilience and the ways in which we cope with trauma.

Furthermore, Rememory touches upon the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and memories. The protagonist's journey raises questions about the nature of reality and whether our perceptions are truly reflective of the world around us. This existential inquiry adds a layer of depth to the narrative, inviting viewers to ponder the complexities of human existence.

Ultimately, Rememory presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that delves into the darker corners of the mind and emerges with a nuanced understanding of the fragility and resilience that define us.

title: Hold the Dark
overview: In the grim Alaskan winter, a naturalist hunts for wolves blamed for killing a local boy, but he soon finds himself swept into a chilling mystery.
plot:
Hold the Dark is a 2018 American thriller film directed by Jeremy Saulnier, based on the novel of the same name by Matt Bell.

The main themes of Hold the Dark revolve around the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of rural America. The story takes place in a remote Alaskan town where a series of gruesome child abductions has occurred, and a former Marine turned snow tracker, Vernon Sutton (played by Alexander Skarsgård), is hired to track down the perpetrator.

Some of the main themes explored in Hold the Dark include:

1. **The darkness within human nature**: The film delves into the idea that humans are capable of great evil, and that this darkness can be lurking beneath the surface of seemingly ordinary people.
2. **Trauma and PTSD**: Vernon's past traumas and his struggles with PTSD serve as a backdrop to the story, highlighting the long-term effects of trauma on individuals and their relationships.
3. **Isolation and loneliness**: The remote Alaskan setting serves as a metaphor for the characters' emotional isolation, emphasizing the difficulties of human connection in isolated environments.
4. **The struggle between nature and humanity**: The film's use of the wilderness as a character in its own right serves to highlight the tension between humanity's desire to control and dominate nature, and the inherent power and unpredictability of the natural world.
5. **Feminism and female empowerment**: The character of Victoria (played by Riley Keough) is a strong and complex representation of femininity, challenging traditional notions of masculinity and female vulnerability.

Throughout the film, these themes are expertly woven together to create a tense and unsettling narrative that explores the darker aspects of human nature.

title: Andron
tagline: Only one survives
overview: A group of people are plunged into a dark, claustrophobic maze, where they must fight to survive, as the outside world watches.
plot:
Andron, released internationally as Andròn: The Black Labyrinth, is an Italian-made, English-language dystopian science fiction action film written and directed by Francesco Cinquemani. Leo Howard and Gale Harold head an ensemble of young contestants that also includes Michelle Ryan, Antonia Campbell-Hughes, Jon Kortajarena, Margareth Madè and the Skunk Anansie singer Skin in her first acting role, with Alec Baldwin and Danny Glover in supporting parts. It was produced by Andrea Iervolino and Monika Bacardi for Ambi Pictures and shot in Italy and Malta.

Ten young people wake up in a dark underground maze with no idea how they got there and no memory even of their own names. As fragments of their past return, they are disturbed to find that they seem to come from different periods of history. Moving walls abruptly reshape the labyrinth, separating the group, crushing some of its members and bringing the survivors into contact with new people, while packs of heavily armoured fighters hunt them and a robotic voice announces each death. The captives gradually realize that they are contestants in the Redemption Games, a deadly contest from which only one can emerge alive. The year is 2154, a quarter of a century after a "Big Catastrophe" that killed billions and allowed nine corporations to take over the world and enslave most of humanity. The games are broadcast to pacify the suffering masses outside, who bet on the contestants' survival. Overseeing the show from a vast office is Adam, a television executive and puppet master who watches the action on screens and arbitrarily intervenes to liven things up, answering to his political master, Chancellor Gordon. As their numbers shrink, the survivors, among them Alexander and Julian, must work out the puzzle of where they are and try to find a way out of the labyrinth.

The film premiered at the Trieste Science+Fiction Festival on November 8, 2015, and Momentum Pictures gave it a limited release in the United States in June 2016. It was panned by critics and holds a Metacritic score of 16 out of 100. Dennis Harvey of Variety described it as a drab and dull recycling of The Hunger Games, The Maze Runner and Cube, with Baldwin and Glover barely concealing their disinterest, though he praised Gherardo Gossi's widescreen cinematography and Riccardo Eberspacher's score. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter found it boring, incoherent and derivative.

title: Death Wish
tagline: How Far Would You Go To Protect Your Family?
overview: A mild-mannered father is transformed into a killing machine after his family is torn apart by a violent act.
plot:
Death Wish is a 2018 American vigilante action thriller film directed by Eli Roth, written by Joe Carnahan and produced by Roger Birnbaum. A remake of the 1974 film and the sixth entry in the series, it stars Bruce Willis as Paul Kersey, a Chicago trauma surgeon, with Vincent D'Onofrio as his brother Frank, Elisabeth Shue as his wife Lucy, Camila Morrone as his daughter Jordan, Dean Norris and Kimberly Elise as the detectives Kevin Raines and Leonore Jackson, and Beau Knapp as Knox.

During a family dinner at a restaurant, a valet named Miguel secretly copies the Kerseys' address after overhearing their plans. While Paul is called away to the hospital, Lucy and Jordan come home to find three armed burglars, and in the struggle Lucy is fatally shot and Jordan is left in a coma. Frustrated by the slow police investigation, Paul takes a pistol that falls from a wounded gang member at the hospital and uses it to stop a carjacking. A video goes viral and the media dub him the "Grim Reaper", and after treating a boy hurt for refusing to deal drugs, Paul shoots the dealer known as the Ice Cream Man in broad daylight. Paul recognizes a dying Miguel on his operating table wearing a watch stolen from his home. Miguel's phone leads him to a liquor store that fences stolen goods, where the gunman Fish accidentally kills the owner while trying to shoot Paul. Fish names Joe as another robber before Paul kills him, and Joe, tortured at a body shop, reveals that a third man, Knox, killed Lucy. Paul kills Joe, then exchanges fire with Knox in a nightclub restroom, and both are wounded. Knox describes Paul to the police, and Paul learns that Jordan has woken from her coma. When Knox rides the hospital elevator with them a week later, Paul realizes that he will come after the family, and he legally buys guns. As Knox's crew attacks the house, Paul sends Jordan to hide and call the police, kills the intruders and uses a hidden rifle to kill Knox. The police accept his account after he suggests that he is finished with vigilantism. Months later, dropping Jordan off at New York University, Paul sees a thief snatch a bag and points a finger gun at him.

Shot in Chicago and Montreal from September 2016, the film was released by MGM on 2 March 2018, less than three weeks after the Parkland school shooting, which several critics noted. It grossed $55.9 million on a $30 million budget but received largely negative reviews, earning a 17% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

title: Only the Brave
tagline: It’s not what stands in front of you, it’s who stands beside you

plot:
Only the Brave is a 2017 American biographical drama film directed by Joseph Kosinski and written by Ken Nolan, Andrew Niccol, and Christopher McQuarrie. The film is based on the true story of the Granite Mountain Hotshots, an elite team of firefighters from Prescott, Arizona.

The movie begins with a flashback to 2008, where we see the formation of the Granite Mountain Hotshots, led by Brendan McDonough (Josh Brolin), a young and ambitious firefighter. The team is handpicked by their leader, Eric Marsh (Anders Holm), who has a vision for a elite firefighting unit that can tackle the most challenging blazes in Arizona.

As the story unfolds, we see the team come together, consisting of 20 firefighters from different backgrounds, all united by their passion for fighting fires. The team is trained to be self-sufficient and work together seamlessly, with each member having a specific role. They are equipped with state-of-the-art gear and a customized truck that becomes their mobile command center.

The film takes us through the team's rigorous training, where they learn to navigate treacherous terrain, build complex shelters, and develop strategies for tackling massive fires. We see the camaraderie and banter among the team members, as well as their personal struggles and relationships outside of work.

As the summer of 2013 approaches, the Granite Mountain Hotshots are deployed to fight a devastating wildfire in Yarnell Canyon, Arizona. The fire is intense and unpredictable, with flames reaching up to 100 feet high. The team is tasked with creating a firebreak to contain the blaze, but they soon realize that the fire is moving faster than expected.

The film's climax is one of the most intense and emotional scenes in recent memory. As the fire closes in on the team, they make a desperate last stand, using everything at their disposal to try and escape. The scene is both heart-wrenching and awe-inspiring, as we witness the bravery and sacrifice of the Granite Mountain Hotshots.

The movie ends with a somber tone, as we reflect on the tragic loss of life that occurred during the Yarnell Canyon fire. Brendan McDonough's voiceover provides context for the events leading up to the tragedy, while also highlighting the team's unwavering dedication to their craft and each other.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the vast expanse of Arizona's desert landscapes and the intensity of the wildfires. The performances by Josh Brolin, Miles Teller, and Jeff Bridges are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to the characters.

Overall, Only the Brave is a powerful tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of the Granite Mountain Hotshots. The film is both an emotional rollercoaster and a testament to the human spirit's capacity for courage and resilience in the face of adversity.

title: Life
tagline: Be careful what you search for
overview: The six-member crew of the International Space Station is tasked with studying a sample from Mars that may be the first proof of extra-terrestrial life, which proves more intelligent than ever expected.
plot:
Life is a 2017 American science fiction horror film directed by Daniel Espinosa and written by Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick. The movie stars Jake Gyllenhaal, Rebecca Ferguson, Ryan Reynolds, and Hiroyuki Sanada.

The story begins with the crew of the International Space Station (ISS), led by Captain Oram (Hiroyuki Sanada), who are on a mission to collect samples from Mars. During the journey, they discover a new species of alien life form that has been living in the Martian soil. The creature is small and appears to be harmless at first, but it quickly becomes clear that it's highly aggressive and deadly.

As the crew tries to understand the nature of the creature, they begin to experience strange occurrences on board the ISS. Equipment malfunctions, and some crew members start to act strangely, as if they're being controlled by an unknown force. It becomes apparent that the alien life form has infected one of the crew members, Dr. David Jordan (Jake Gyllenhaal), who is initially excited about the discovery but soon becomes a threat to the rest of the crew.

The crew tries to contain the situation, but it quickly spirals out of control. The creature grows at an alarming rate, and its behavior becomes increasingly erratic and violent. As the crew fights for survival, they realize that the alien life form is not just a simple organism - it's a highly adaptable and intelligent being that can evolve and mutate rapidly.

As the situation worsens, Captain Oram makes the difficult decision to quarantine Dr. Jordan in a separate section of the ISS, hoping to contain the infection. However, this only seems to make things worse, as the creature begins to break free from its restraints and wreak havoc on the rest of the crew.

In the end, it's up to Dr. Miranda North (Rebecca Ferguson), a microbiologist who was initially skeptical of the alien life form, to find a way to stop the creature before it's too late. She discovers that the creature is vulnerable to UV light, which she uses to create a makeshift solution to destroy it.

The movie ends with a tense and suspenseful climax as Dr. North faces off against the creature in a desperate bid to save the rest of the crew. In the end, she succeeds in destroying the alien life form, but not before it has claimed several lives and left the crew of the ISS forever changed by their encounter with the unknown.

Overall, Life is a tense and thrilling sci-fi horror movie that explores the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's use of practical effects to create the alien creature is impressive, and Jake Gyllenhaal delivers a standout performance as the increasingly unhinged Dr. Jordan.

title: Stronger

The film showcases Bauman's unwavering spirit and his refusal to let his disability define him.

Another significant theme in Stronger is the power of human connection. Throughout the movie, Jeff forms strong bonds with those around him, including his family, friends, and even strangers who become like a support system for him. These connections help him navigate the challenges he faces and provide a sense of purpose and belonging.

The film also delves into the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Jeff struggles to come to terms with his new reality, he must confront questions about who he is outside of his physical appearance. He finds ways to redefine himself and discover new passions, ultimately leading him to become an advocate for survivors' rights.

Furthermore, Stronger touches on the theme of trauma and its long-lasting effects. The movie portrays the emotional scars that Jeff and others suffer as a result of the bombing, highlighting the importance of seeking help and support when needed. The film also explores the complexities of PTSD and the challenges of reintegrating into society after experiencing such traumatic events.

Overall, Stronger is a powerful exploration of the human spirit, resilience, and the importance of connection in the face of adversity.

title: Ali Wong: Baby Cobra
overview: Ali Wong might be seven-months pregnant, but there’s not a fetus in the world that can stop this acerbic and savage train of comedy from delivering a masterful hour of stand-up.
plot:
Ali Wong: Baby Cobra is a 2016 American comedy film that explores themes of motherhood, identity, and feminism through the lens of Ali Wong's personal experiences. title: Woman Walks Ahead
tagline: Defy your times
overview: Based on a true story, this riveting western follows a headstrong New York widow as she journeys west to meet Sioux chief Sitting Bull, facing off with an army officer intent on war with Native Americans.
plot:
Woman Walks Ahead is a biographical Western drama of 2017 directed by Susanna White and written by Steven Knight. Jessica Chastain plays Catherine Weldon, a character inspired by the real Caroline Weldon, a New York portrait painter who travels to the Dakotas in 1890 to paint Sitting Bull, played by Michael Greyeyes. Sam Rockwell appears as the army officer Colonel Silas Grove, Ciarán Hinds as the Indian agent James McLaughlin and Bill Camp as General Crook.

Recently widowed, Catherine writes to Sitting Bull through McLaughlin at Fort Yates, asking to make his portrait. The agent secretly destroys the letter and orders her detained. On the train the colonel advises her to go home. When she arrives, a passerby steals her trunk and art supplies, and at Fort Yates she is confined overnight; the colonel returns her stolen belongings and warns her that the recent fighting between the army and the Lakota is far from forgotten. Next morning Sitting Bull's nephew, an agency employee, takes her to him. Sitting Bull agrees to sit for $1,000, and she stays on the reservation. The colonel warns her not to raise the Lakota's hopes, since a treaty taking more of their land is about to be ratified and General Crook and the 7th Cavalry are on their way.

Sitting Bull first appears for the portrait in an ordinary suit, then changes into traditional buckskins at Catherine's request. Returning, they find the village empty: the people have seen a draft of the treaty, which would halve their rations and take their land, and suspecting Catherine of being a spy, have joined a Ghost Dance. Catherine buys all the food in town for the reservation and is beaten by townsmen for it. Recovering, she announces at a dinner with Crook that she will fight the treaty, and campaigns alongside Sitting Bull, whose arrival at the vote silences the chiefs bribed to testify falsely. The treaty is overwhelmingly rejected, but the colonel tells her this gives the army its pretext for war. Sitting Bull, foreseeing his death that winter, sees the finished portrait before the colonel warns him in Lakota of an arrest at dawn and carries Catherine off for her safety. During the arrest, a hidden sniper shoots Sitting Bull dead. Closing titles note the Wounded Knee massacre that followed and Catherine's lifelong advocacy.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017 and was released by A24 and DirecTV Cinema in 2018. Reviews were mixed, praising the two leads.

title: The Meyerowitz Stories (New and Selected)
overview: An estranged family gathers together in New York for an event celebrating the artistic work of their father.
plot:
The Meyerowitz Stories (New and Selected) is a 2017 American comedy-drama written and directed by Noah Baumbach. Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller and Elizabeth Marvel star as the adult children of a self-absorbed artist played by Dustin Hoffman, with Emma Thompson as his fourth wife and Grace Van Patten as Sandler's daughter. The film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival and was released in theaters and on Netflix in October 2017.

After separating from his wife, the unemployed musician Danny Meyerowitz moves in with his father, Harold, a retired Bard College art professor and sculptor, and Harold's fourth wife, Maureen, a pleasant but scatterbrained hippie. Danny is close to his daughter, Eliza, a freshman film student at Bard whose provocative short films embarrass the family. Danny's sister, Jean, lives a quiet, solitary life, while their younger half-brother, Matthew, is a successful financial adviser in Los Angeles.

Harold, who believes the art world has unjustly forgotten him, refuses to take part in a group faculty show at Bard. He and Danny attend a retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art for Harold's more successful contemporary, L.J. Shapiro, where Harold feels so uncomfortable that he runs off down the street, and Danny chases after him, cutting short a promising encounter with Shapiro's daughter, Loretta. In town on business, Matthew meets Harold for lunch and tries to persuade him to sell his Manhattan house and his sculptures, provoking resentment. When Harold suffers a serious health crisis and is hospitalized, the three siblings are forced to come together, confronting old grievances, their father's favoritism and the ways in which his ego has shaped their lives. Jean reveals a painful secret from her youth, Danny and Matthew finally air their rivalry, and the family prepares for the Bard exhibition honoring Harold's work.

The film received positive reviews, with a 92 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Baumbach's bittersweet view of family dynamics and the remarkable cast, and a Metacritic score of 79. Sandler's performance was especially praised as one of the best of his career. At Cannes the film also won the Palm Dog award for its canine performer.

The doll is imbued with a malevolent spirit that feeds on fear and terror, and it begins to exert its influence over the other children at the orphanage.

As the situation spirals out of control, Sister Charlotte and the other nuns are forced to confront the evil entity head-on. In a desperate bid to save the children, they perform an exorcism on Annabelle, but the ritual goes horribly wrong, and the doll is left with a piece of her soul.

Overall, Annabelle: Creation is a chilling and atmospheric horror movie that explores themes of trauma, grief, and the supernatural. While it may not be as scary as some other horror movies, it is a well-crafted and engaging film that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

The film blurs the lines between truth and fiction, leaving the audience to question what is real and what is just a product of Sam's paranoid imagination.

5. **The American Dream**: The movie critiques the idea of the American Dream, which promises success, happiness, and fulfillment to those who work hard enough. Instead, Under the Silver Lake presents a darker vision of America, where the pursuit of wealth and status can lead to disillusionment and despair.

Overall, Under the Silver Lake is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of paranoia, identity, love, perception, and the American Dream.

title: Train to Busan
tagline: Life-or-death survival begins.
overview: When a zombie virus pushes Korea into a state of emergency, those trapped on an express train to Busan must fight for their own survival.
plot:
Train to Busan is a 2016 South Korean post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Yeon Sang-ho. The movie takes place in a world where a mysterious virus has turned most of humanity into violent, zombie-like creatures.

The story begins with Seok-woo (played by Gong Yoo), a wealthy stockbroker who lives in Seoul with his wife Soo-an (played by Kim Su-an) and their young son Su-an. On the day of their daughter's birthday party, Seok-woo receives an unexpected phone call from his mother, who is bedridden with cancer, asking him to take care of her. Feeling guilty for not spending enough time with his family, Seok-woo decides to visit his mother in Busan.

As they board the KTX train to Busan, Seok-woo and Soo-an are unaware of the impending disaster that awaits them. The train is suddenly attacked by a group of zombies, who have been infected by the mysterious virus. The passengers and crew fight for survival as the train becomes a battleground.

Seok-woo's mother dies shortly after they arrive in Busan, but he continues on to find his daughter, who has gone missing. Along the way, he meets a young girl named Sung-gyeol (played by Kim Soo-an), who is also searching for her family. As they navigate through the treacherous streets of Busan, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol form an unlikely bond.

As the train's passengers are picked off one by one, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol discover that the virus has been caused by a mysterious outbreak in China. The government is trying to contain the outbreak, but it's too late, and the virus has spread globally.

The duo eventually boards a bus to escape the chaos, but they soon realize that the bus is also infested with zombies. In a desperate bid to survive, Seok-woo sacrifices himself to save Sung-gyeol by pushing her off the moving bus.

In the end, Sung-gyeol manages to find her way back to her father's office building in Seoul, where she finds him alive and well. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Sung-gyeol finally finding some sense of closure and reunion with her family.

Throughout the movie, Yeon Sang-ho explores themes of class struggle, social inequality, and the breakdown of society in the face of catastrophic disaster. The film's tense atmosphere and graphic violence make it a thrilling ride, but its thought-provoking commentary on human nature makes it more than just a mindless horror flick.

Overall, Train to Busan is a gripping and intense thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and social commentary, it's no wonder this movie has become a modern classic in the zombie genre.

title: Super Dark Times
overview: Teenagers Zach and Josh have been best friends their whole lives, but when a gruesome accident leads to a cover-up, the secret drives a wedge between them and propels them down a rabbit hole of escalating paranoia and violence.
plot:

The film masterfully captures the turmoil and uncertainty of its characters as they navigate the challenges of high school, friendships, and first loves.

The protagonist, Evan, is a sensitive and introverted teenager who struggles to form meaningful connections with his peers, while his best friend, Matt, appears to have it all together on the surface but is hiding his own vulnerabilities.

title: The Autopsy of Jane Doe
tagline: Every body has a secret.
overview: Father and son coroners receive a mysterious unidentified corpse with no apparent cause of death. As they attempt to examine the "Jane Doe," they discover increasingly bizarre clues that hold the key to her terrifying secrets.
plot:
The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by André Øvredal from a screenplay by Øvredal and Joel Bergman. The movie stars Brian Cox, Anthony Mackie, and Hailee Steinfeld.

The story begins with the death of a young woman named Jane Doe, who is found dead in her apartment. Her body is discovered by her landlord, who calls the local coroner's office to report the incident. Dr. Aaron Hunt (Brian Cox) and his son, Corbin (Anthony Mackie), are called to perform an autopsy on Jane.

As they begin the examination, they notice that Jane's body appears to be in pristine condition, with no signs of trauma or injury. However, as they delve deeper into the autopsy, they start to uncover strange and inexplicable details about her life. They find a series of cryptic symbols etched into her skin, which seem to be some sort of code.

As the autopsy progresses, Corbin becomes increasingly unsettled by the strange occurrences surrounding Jane's body. He begins to suspect that something supernatural is at play, but his father is skeptical and dismissive of these concerns.

Despite their initial reservations, the doctors soon realize that they are dealing with a malevolent entity that has taken possession of Jane's body. The entity, which appears to be some sort of ancient being, begins to exert its influence over Corbin, causing him to experience terrifying hallucinations and visions.

As the night wears on, the situation becomes increasingly dire, and Corbin's grip on reality begins to slip. His father tries to intervene, but he is powerless against the entity's malevolent forces.

In a desperate bid to save his son, Dr. Hunt turns to an ancient ritual that may be able to banish the entity from Jane's body. However, this comes at a terrible cost, and Corbin is forced to confront the dark secrets of his family's past in order to survive.

The movie builds towards a shocking climax as Corbin faces off against the entity in a desperate bid for survival. In the end, only one of them will emerge victorious, and the consequences of their confrontation will be devastating.

Throughout the movie, Øvredal uses a slow-burning tension to build suspense and unease, creating a sense of creeping dread that permeates every frame. The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a masterclass in atmospheric horror, using the setting and the characters' interactions to create a sense of unease and uncertainty.

The movie's use of symbolism and metaphor adds depth and complexity to the narrative, exploring themes of grief, trauma, and the supernatural. The performances from Cox and Mackie are outstanding, bringing a sense of gravitas and intensity to their roles.

Overall, The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a chilling and unsettling horror movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

title: Vengeance: A Love Story
tagline: Beyond good and evil is Justice
overview: When a new friend is brutally assaulted, Detective John Droomor is put by chance in charge of the investigation. plot:
Vengeance: A Love Story is a 2017 American action thriller directed by former stuntman Johnny Martin from a screenplay by John Mankiewicz, a writer-producer of House of Cards. It is based on Joyce Carol Oates's 2003 novel Rape: A Love Story. Nicolas Cage stars as John Dromoor, a Niagara Falls police detective and Gulf War veteran, with Anna Hutchison as Teena Maguire, Talitha Bateman as her 12-year-old daughter, Bethie, Deborah Kara Unger as Teena's mother, Agnes, and Don Johnson as the defense attorney Jay Kirkpatrick.

The film opens with a bust that goes badly wrong, showing Dromoor's questionable judgment, and he drinks away his troubles in a bar where he meets Teena, a flirtatious single mother who quickly catches his interest. After a Fourth of July party, Teena and Bethie take a shortcut home through the dark woods, where Teena is gang-raped, beaten and left for dead in front of her daughter by a group of four meth addicts. Bethie makes her way back to the road and flags down a passing car, which happens to be driven by Dromoor.

While Teena recovers, Agnes takes on the care of both her daughter and granddaughter. Bethie identifies the attackers and a hearing is set to decide whether the case will go to trial. The defendants' families hire Kirkpatrick, a nationally renowned criminal defense lawyer, who turns the proceedings against the traumatized victim by attacking her sobriety, her parenting and her sex life, while the judge appears all too friendly with him. When the case seems lost and the men are set free, Dromoor, a lone wolf suffering from post-traumatic stress, refuses to accept the failure of the legal system and sets out on his own campaign of vigilante justice against the attackers on Teena's behalf, eventually confronting the lawyer and offering comfort to both Bethie and her mother.

The project had first been planned for production in Michigan around 2009 with Samuel L. Jackson, Dianne Wiest and Abigail Breslin attached, but stalled. Cage joined in February 2016 and was briefly announced as director before stepping back, and filming began that April. The film was released direct to video in the United Kingdom in March 2017 and by FilmRise in the United States on September 15, 2017. Reviews were negative: Michael Rechtshaffen of the Los Angeles Times called it ham-handed and cliché-ridden and found Cage's performance detached, while Flickering Myth criticized its overwrought acting and tidy, consequence-free ending.

Overall, "Before I Fall" is a thought-provoking and emotional drama that encourages viewers to reflect on their own values, priorities, and relationships.

title: Rendel
tagline: Revenge begets revenge.
overview: Rendel, a masked superhero, becomes blinded by his desire for revenge against a sinister criminal organization.
plot:
Rendel, also known as Rendel: Dark Vengeance, is a 2017 Finnish superhero action film written, produced and directed by Jesse Haaja and based on his own original character. It stars Kris Gummerus as Rendel, with Matti Onnismaa, Rami Rusinen and Renne Korppila in the other leading roles and Alina Tomnikov, Tero Salenius, Aake Kalliala, Anu Palevaara and Kristina Karjalainen in the supporting cast.

In the city of Mikkeli, a company called VALA has developed a lucrative vaccine without proper testing. VALA is a front for a criminal organization led by Pekka Erola, whose son Jarno, known as Rotikka, is one of its most violent enforcers. The gang's operations are being disrupted by a mysterious masked vigilante dressed in black, who leaves his victims marked with the name Rendel.

Through flashbacks, the film reveals the story of Rämö, a financial director and devoted family man. After refusing to invest in a scheme proposed by one of VALA's men, he loses his job and struggles to find work, until he is hired by VALA to handle paperwork. There he discovers that the vaccine, made from a tar-like substance that bonds permanently to skin, has not been properly tested and has caused numerous deaths. Fearing that Rämö will become a whistleblower, Erola sends Rotikka and his henchman to kill him. Rämö's wife and daughter are murdered, and he is beaten and left for dead, but he survives. Covering his face with the tar to create a mask and wearing the biker jacket his family gave him, he becomes Rendel, a dark avenger whose name comes from the Hungarian word for order. As his war against the organization escalates, VALA's leaders hire a team of foreign mercenaries to destroy him, while a mysterious woman named Marla offers him help.

The film combines brutal, stylized action with a dark revenge story set in a small Finnish city, offering an independently produced take on the superhero genre.

Rendel won the Best Action Movie award at the Feratum Film Festival in Mexico. A sequel, Rendel 2: Cycle of Revenge, was filmed in the Kainuu region in 2019, and an English-language continuation featuring Gummerus was later announced.

title: The House That Jack Built
overview: Failed architect, engineer and vicious murderer Jack narrates the details of some of his most elaborately orchestrated crimes, each of them a towering piece of art that defines his life's work as a serial killer for twelve years.
plot:
The House That Jack Built is a 2018 Danish black comedy film written and directed by Lars von Trier. The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, consisting of six chapters that explore the life of Jack (played by Matt Dillon), a serial killer who documents his crimes through voiceovers.

Throughout the film, several themes emerge:

1. **The Nature of Evil**: The House That Jack Built explores the concept of evil and whether it's inherent or learned. Jack's character is complex, and his actions are both disturbing and fascinating. The film raises questions about the origins of evil and whether individuals can be born with a predisposition to violence.

2. **Mortality and the Human Condition**: The film grapples with mortality, as each chapter focuses on a different victim and explores their final moments before Jack's brutal killing. This theme is intertwined with the human condition, highlighting the fragility of life and the inevitability of death.

3. **The Objectification of Women**: The House That Jack Built critiques the way women are often objectified in society. Jack's victims are frequently portrayed as sex objects or mere commodities, which serves to underscore his twisted worldview.

4. **The Power Dynamics of Relationships**: The film examines the power dynamics between men and women, particularly in relationships where one partner holds more control than the other. This theme is reflected in Jack's interactions with his victims and his own relationships throughout the narrative.

5. **The Blurred Lines Between Reality and Fantasy**: As the story unfolds, it becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish between reality and fantasy. The film's non-linear structure and Jack's voiceovers contribute to this ambiguity, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is part of Jack's twisted imagination.

6. **The Dark Side of Human Nature**: Ultimately, The House That Jack Built presents a bleak portrayal of human nature, highlighting the darker aspects of our existence. The film serves as a commentary on the darkness that can lurk within individuals and society as a whole.

It's worth noting that Lars von Trier's intention with this film was to spark controversy and challenge societal norms, rather than to provide a straightforward or sympathetic portrayal of Jack's character.

overview: In 1980s Italy, a relationship begins between seventeen-year-old teenage Elio and the older adult man hired as his father's research assistant.

As the summer draws to a close, Elio and Oliver must confront the reality of their situation. The film's climax is marked by a poignant and emotional goodbye, as Elio and Oliver part ways, leaving the audience with a sense of longing and uncertainty.

The Irishman is a 2019 crime drama film directed by Martin Scorsese, written by Steven Zaillian, and starring Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci, and Harvey Keitel. The film is based on the 2004 book "I Heard You Paint Houses" by Charles Brandt, which tells the true story of Frank Sheeran, a hitman who claims to have been involved in the disappearance of Jimmy Hoffa.

The film begins with an elderly Frank Sheeran (Robert De Niro) recounting his life story to a reporter, David Siegel (Al Pacino). The story begins in 1957, where we meet young Frank Sheeran (Annie Parisse), who is struggling to make ends meet as a truck driver. He meets Russell Bufalino (Joe Pesci), a mob hitman and friend of Jimmy Hoffa's, who becomes his mentor.

As the story unfolds, we see Frank become embroiled in the world of organized crime, working for Bufalino and Hoffa, who is the leader of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters. The film explores the complex relationships between these characters, including the friendship between Sheeran and Hoffa, as well as the power struggles within the mob.

The plot thickens when Frank becomes involved in a series of hits, including the infamous disappearance of Jimmy Hoffa in 1975. Sheeran claims to have been part of the team that killed Hoffa, but the film leaves the audience questioning whether this is true or just a product of his imagination.

Throughout the film, Scorsese uses non-linear storytelling to weave together the different threads of Frank's life. The film jumps back and forth in time, with Sheeran's older self recounting his story to Siegel, while also showing us key moments from his younger years.

As the story reaches its climax, we see Frank's involvement in Hoffa's disappearance come to a head. However, the film ultimately leaves the question of whether Sheeran was involved in Hoffa's murder unanswered, instead focusing on the emotional toll that this event takes on him.

The Irishman is a complex and nuanced exploration of the mob world, with Scorsese using his signature style to bring the story to life. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly De Niro, Pacino, and Pesci, who all deliver memorable performances as their respective characters.

Overall, The Irishman is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and the consequences of violence. While it may not provide clear answers to some of its questions, the film's emotional resonance and masterful storytelling make it a must-see for fans of Scorsese and crime dramas alike.

title: The Commuter
tagline: Lives are on the line
overview: A businessman, on his daily commute home, gets unwittingly caught up in a criminal conspiracy that threatens not only his life but the lives of those around him.
plot:
The Commuter is a 2018 action thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra, in his fourth collaboration with Liam Neeson, and written by Byron Willinger, Philip de Blasi and Ryan Engle. Neeson stars as a former policeman drawn into a murder conspiracy on his daily train ride, alongside Vera Farmiga, Patrick Wilson, Jonathan Banks, Florence Pugh and Sam Neill.

Michael MacCauley, a former NYPD officer turned insurance salesman, rides the same Hudson Line train between Tarrytown and Grand Central every day. Suddenly laid off and afraid to tell his wife, he confides in his former partner, Murphy, who is still on the force. On the ride home, a mysterious woman named Joanna offers him a "hypothetical" deal: find a passenger known as "Prynne," who has something that does not belong to them, for $100,000, starting with $25,000 hidden in the bathroom. Michael takes the money, but when he tries to get off, he is handed his wife's wedding ring as a warning. A commuter he asks for help is pushed under a bus, and Joanna reveals that his family is being held and that he must plant a GPS tracker on Prynne.

Michael's attempts to identify Prynne go wrong: the man he tags turns out to be an FBI agent, found dead soon after. Murphy tells him that Prynne is a key witness to the supposed suicide of city official Enrique Mendez, and Michael realizes that Prynne is to be killed and that he is being framed. He forces the passengers into the last car and kills another passenger, Oliver, who had been hired to murder Prynne. Prynne turns out to be Sofia, a teenage girl holding evidence against powerful people, who was being escorted to witness protection. When Michael refuses to kill her, Joanna detonates explosives to derail the train, but Michael uncouples the final car and saves most of the passengers. Police surround the car, believing he has taken hostages, and Murphy is sent in to negotiate, inadvertently revealing that he is the corrupt cop who killed Mendez. Michael removes Murphy's identifying tag, and snipers shoot Murphy. Sofia testifies, Michael's family is rescued, and he is offered his old job back. Later, he confronts Joanna on a train and prepares to arrest her.

Released by Lionsgate in the United States on January 12, 2018, The Commuter grossed $119.9 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with critics comparing it to Non-Stop but praising Neeson's performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 55% approval and Metacritic a score of 56.

title: The Shape of Water
tagline: A Fairy Tale for Troubled Times
overview: An other-worldly story, set against the backdrop of Cold War era America circa 1962, where a mute janitor working at a lab falls in love with an amphibious man being held captive there and devises a plan to help him escape.
plot:
The Shape of Water is a 2017 American romantic fantasy film directed by Guillermo del Toro, produced by J. Miles Dale and Guillermo del Toro, and written by Vanessa Taylor.

In the early 1960s, during the Cold War era, Elisa Esposito (Sally Hawkins), a mute and isolated janitor at a government research facility in Baltimore, Maryland, discovers a mysterious amphibious creature being held captive in a tank. The creature, later revealed to be Amphibian Man (Doug Jones), is a humanoid with gills and scales, who has been captured by the US government after it was discovered in the Amazon River.

As Elisa begins to care for Amphibian Man, she forms a deep bond with him, communicating through sign language and music. She also starts to notice strange occurrences around her, including the presence of Richard Strickland (Michael Shannon), a ruthless and sadistic scientist who is determined to exploit Amphibian Man's unique abilities.

Strickland plans to use Amphibian Man as a tool for espionage, intending to extract his secrets from him. Elisa, however, becomes fiercely protective of Amphibian Man and decides to help him escape. She enlists the aid of her co-worker Zelda (Octavia Spencer) and Giles (Richard Jenkins), who is initially hesitant but eventually joins their cause.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Strickland's true intentions are far more sinister than anyone could have imagined. He plans to use Amphibian Man's abilities to spy on his enemies and gain an advantage over them. Elisa and her allies must work together to stop Strickland and save Amphibian Man from a life of captivity.

Throughout the film, del Toro weaves a rich tapestry of themes, including love, acceptance, and the struggle for identity. Elisa's relationship with Amphibian Man is at the heart of the story, as they find solace and understanding in each other's company. The film also explores the complexities of human nature, highlighting the cruelty and intolerance that can exist within society.

The Shape of Water features stunning visuals, with del Toro's signature attention to detail and craftsmanship on full display. The film's use of practical effects and makeup creates a convincing and immersive world, bringing Amphibian Man to life in a way that is both captivating and heartbreaking.

Ultimately, Elisa and her allies succeed in stopping Strickland and freeing Amphibian Man from captivity. As the creature returns to his natural habitat, Elisa finds a sense of purpose and belonging, having discovered a new family among her colleagues. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest of times, there is always the possibility for love, acceptance, and transformation.

The Shape of Water received widespread critical acclaim upon its release, earning numerous awards and nominations, including four Academy Awards. It was praised for its stunning visuals, memorable performances, and thought-provoking themes, cementing its place as one of the most beloved films of 2017.

title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
original_title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
overview: Dr. Steven Murphy is a renowned cardiovascular surgeon who presides over a spotless household with his wife and two children. Lurking at the margins of his idyllic suburban existence is Martin, a fatherless teen who insinuates himself into the doctor's life in gradually unsettling ways.
plot:
The Killing of a Sacred Deer is a 2017 absurdist psychological horror thriller directed and co-produced by Yorgos Lanthimos, who wrote the screenplay with Efthimis Filippou. Colin Farrell plays Steven Murphy, a cardiac surgeon, with Nicole Kidman as his wife Anna, Barry Keoghan as the teenager Martin, Raffey Cassidy and Sunny Suljic as the couple's children Kim and Bob, and Alicia Silverstone as Martin's mother. The title alludes to Euripides' tragedy Iphigenia in Aulis.

Steven, a Cincinnati heart surgeon, has been meeting 16-year-old Martin at a diner, whose father died a few years earlier. He introduces the boy to his family, and Martin charms them all, especially Kim. When Steven dines at Martin's home, the boy's mother makes advances at him, saying it is what her son wants, and Steven leaves. Martin's demands on his time become more frequent and insistent, and Steven grows uneasy, particularly after Martin gives Kim a ride on his motorcycle.

Then Bob suddenly loses the use of his legs. Martin explains that his father died on Steven's operating table and that, to restore the balance, Steven must kill one member of his own family; otherwise all of them will die, first becoming paralysed, then refusing food, then bleeding from the eyes before death. Soon Bob will not eat, and Kim, now infatuated with Martin, collapses at choir practice. Steven admits to Anna that he had been drinking before the fatal surgery. Martin demonstrates his hold over Kim by telling her over the phone to stand, then leaving her paralysed again. Pressed by Anna, Steven imprisons Martin in the basement, beats him and shoots him in the legs, but the boy only bites his own arm to illustrate his notion of justice. The children compete for their father's favour, Steven asks their school principal which child is better, and Anna argues that he should sacrifice one of the children rather than her. When Bob's eyes begin to bleed, Steven binds his family in a circle, covers his own face and fires a rifle blindly while spinning; the third shot kills Bob. Later, the surviving Murphys see Martin at the diner and walk out.

Shot in Cincinnati in 2016, the film competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2017 and won the prize for Best Screenplay. It was released in the United States by A24 in October 2017 and grossed $10.7 million worldwide. Reviews were positive, with 79% on Rotten Tomatoes and 73 on Metacritic.

title: Piper
overview: A mother bird tries to teach her little one how to find food by herself. In the process, she encounters a traumatic experience that she must overcome in order to survive.
plot:
Piper is a 2016 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar Animation Studios, written and directed by Alan Barillaro, a veteran Pixar animator. A story about a hungry baby sandpiper who must overcome her fear of water, it was released in theaters alongside Pixar's feature Finding Dory on June 17, 2016, and was later included on that film's Blu-ray and DVD releases. The idea came to Barillaro on the shoreline less than a mile from Pixar's studios in Emeryville, California, where he would run along the beach and watch thousands of birds darting away from the incoming water and returning between waves to feed.

A flock of sandpipers forages along a beach, searching for shellfish exposed by the retreating waves and scurrying away whenever the surf rolls back in. A mother sandpiper brings her chick, Piper, to the water's edge so that she can learn to find food for herself. Piper, however, is too slow to escape an incoming wave and is drenched by the surf, an experience that leaves her terrified of the water. Back at the nest, she refuses to venture out again and insists that her mother keep feeding her as before. Eventually hunger drives her back to the shore, where she notices a small hermit crab burrowing into the sand. As she watches it, a large wave rolls in and engulfs her. Panicking, she copies the crabs and buries herself in the sand, but this time the hermit crab encourages her to open her eyes. Underwater, Piper sees large shellfish uncovered by the wave. Thrilled, she conquers her fear, learns to catch the bounty revealed beneath the water and gathers enough to feed the entire flock.

Barillaro spent more than three years making the film with new, cutting-edge technology. To give the sandpipers and the other birds a realistic look, he and the short's animation team studied their appearance and behavior on beaches around the San Francisco Bay Area and at the Monterey Bay Aquarium, and the birds' feathers were rendered in minute detail. Critics praised the lifelike animation, with Variety calling it as simple as a haiku and yet stunning, and the short holds a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Piper won the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film at the 89th Academy Awards, the first Pixar short to win the award since For the Birds in 2001.

title: Logan Lucky
tagline: See how the other half steals.
overview: Trying to reverse a family curse, brothers Jimmy and Clyde Logan set out to execute an elaborate robbery during the legendary Coca-Cola 600 race at the Charlotte Motor Speedway.
plot:
Logan Lucky is a 2017 American heist comedy film directed by Steven Soderbergh, marking his return from a self-declared retirement from filmmaking, from a screenplay credited to Rebecca Blunt. Channing Tatum and Adam Driver star as Jimmy and Clyde Logan, brothers from West Virginia, with Riley Keough as their sister, Mellie, Daniel Craig as the safecracker Joe Bang, Katie Holmes, Seth MacFarlane, Katherine Waterston, Hilary Swank, Sebastian Stan and Dwight Yoakam. Soderbergh distributed the film independently through his company Fingerprint Releasing, in partnership with Bleecker Street.

Jimmy, a former high school football star whose career was ended by a knee injury, is fired from his construction job in the tunnels beneath the Charlotte Motor Speedway because his old injury was not disclosed. He dotes on his young daughter, Sadie, who competes in beauty pageants and lives with his ex-wife, Bobbie Jo, and her wealthy new husband, who are planning to move away. Jimmy's brother, Clyde, an Iraq War veteran who lost part of his arm, tends a local bar, and the family is said to be cursed by bad luck. After a confrontation with an obnoxious NASCAR team owner, Max Chilblain, Jimmy reveals his plan to rob the speedway by exploiting what he knows about the pneumatic tube system used to move cash to its vault.

The Logans recruit Mellie and Joe Bang, an imprisoned explosives expert, along with his dim-witted brothers, Sam and Fish. Their scheme requires breaking Joe out of prison and returning him before anyone notices, so Clyde deliberately gets himself sent to the same prison. On the day of the Coca-Cola 600, one of the busiest races of the year, the gang carries out the heist, improvising around obstacles that include a prison riot staged as a diversion. Weeks later, the FBI agent Sarah Grayson investigates the robbery, but the case appears to have been solved, and the twists of the Logans' plan gradually come to light.

Logan Lucky received positive reviews for its humor, performances and clever plotting, with critics likening it to a rural counterpart of Soderbergh's Ocean's Eleven. It grossed about $48 million worldwide. Speculation that "Rebecca Blunt" was a pseudonym, possibly for Soderbergh's wife, Jules Asner, persisted after release.

title: The Assignment
tagline: A revenger's tale.
overview: Ace assassin Frank Kitchen is double crossed by gangsters and falls into the hands of rogue surgeon known as The Doctor who turns him into a woman. The hitman, now a hitwoman, sets out for revenge, aided by a nurse named Johnnie who also has secrets.
plot:
The Assignment, also released as Tomboy and, in Australia, as Revenger, is an action crime thriller directed by Walter Hill, who co-wrote it with Denis Hamill. Michelle Rodriguez plays a professional hitman who is surgically transformed into a woman against his will, and Sigourney Weaver plays the disgraced surgeon responsible, with Tony Shalhoub, Anthony LaPaglia and Caitlin Gerard. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11, 2016.

The story moves between two timelines. In the present, Dr. Rachel Jane, a brilliant but unhinged plastic surgeon who lost her licence and went on to perform illegal experiments on vulnerable homeless patients, is confined in a psychiatric institution where Dr. Ralph Galen is assessing her mental state. In the past, she sets out to avenge her brother Sebastian, who was murdered by the contract killer Frank Kitchen.

Through the gangster Honest John, Jane has Frank betrayed and captured. Driven by revenge and by curiosity about how much physical identity shapes a person, she performs gender reassignment surgery on him. Frank wakes in a hotel room in a female body, breaks down, and finds hormones and a taped message from the doctor urging him to start a new life. He takes refuge with Johnnie, a woman he once slept with, while he recovers.

Once he learns the operation cannot be undone, Frank begins killing everyone connected with it, including Honest John's men. He discovers that Johnnie was paid to watch him, but he spares her after realising she acted out of fear and has come to care for him, and she helps him set a trap. Jane's bodyguards capture Frank instead, and she plans to amputate his arm so he can never kill again. He breaks free, kills her guards and assistant, and shoots Jane without killing her.

In the institution, Jane gives a deposition explaining her actions without remorse. The film reveals that Frank arranged the scene to blame her assistant and cut off her fingers so she can never operate again.

Saban Films released the film on video on demand in March 2017 and in limited cinemas the following month. Reviews were negative, with a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Isle of Dogs
tagline: Welcome to the Isle of Dogs.
overview: In the future, an outbreak of canine flu leads the mayor of a Japanese city to banish all dogs to an island that's a garbage dump. The outcasts must soon embark on an epic journey when a 12-year-old boy arrives on the island to find his beloved pet.
plot:
Isle of Dogs is a 2018 stop-motion animated film directed by Wes Anderson, produced by Scott Rudin Productions, and distributed by Fox Searchlight Pictures.

The main themes of Isle of Dogs include:

1. **Loyalty and Friendship**: The story revolves around the bond between a group of abandoned dogs and their human companion, Atari. The dogs' loyalty to each other and to Atari drives the plot forward.
2. **Environmentalism and Pollution**: The film is set in a dystopian future where Japan has become a polluted and decaying society. The dogs' quest to find Atari's dog, Spots, serves as a metaphor for the importance of preserving nature and the consequences of human neglect.
3. **Corporate Greed and Corruption**: The character of Chief, a corrupt politician, represents the dangers of unchecked corporate power and greed. His actions drive the plot forward and serve as a commentary on the exploitation of the environment and the people.
4. **Coming of Age and Self-Discovery**: Atari's journey is also one of self-discovery, as he learns to navigate his relationships with the dogs and confronts the harsh realities of his world.

The film features a unique blend of humor, adventure, and social commentary, making it a thought-provoking and entertaining watch.

title: Beirut
tagline: Beirut, 1982: The Paris of the Middle East Was Burning
overview: In 1980s Beirut, Mason Skiles is a former U.S. diplomat who is called back into service to save a colleague from the group that is possibly responsible for his own family's death. Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working under cover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.
plot:
Beirut, released in the United Kingdom as The Negotiator, is a 2018 American political thriller directed by Brad Anderson from a screenplay Tony Gilroy wrote in 1991 under the title High Wire Act. Set during the Lebanese Civil War, it stars Jon Hamm as a former US diplomat drawn back to Beirut to negotiate for a kidnapped colleague, with Rosamund Pike, Dean Norris, Shea Whigham, Larry Pine and Mark Pellegrino.

In 1972 Mason Skiles is a diplomat in Beirut living with his Lebanese wife Nadia and Karim, a 13-year-old Palestinian boy they have taken in. At a party, CIA officer Cal Riley tells Skiles he wants to question Karim, whose brother Rafid has been tied to the Munich massacre; Rafid's men then storm the house and seize Karim, and Nadia is killed. Ten years later Skiles is an alcoholic labour arbitrator in New England. Lured back to Beirut on the pretext of a lecture, he learns Riley has been kidnapped and that the abductors asked for him by name. The grown Karim now leads the group and demands Rafid in exchange, though the Americans insist they do not hold him. A trip to Israel proves fruitless, and Riley's wife Alice blames Skiles for her husband's plight. After a car bomb disrupts his lecture, Skiles is taken to Karim and Riley, who secretly tells him that the PLO has Rafid and that CIA officer Gaines cannot be trusted. CIA officer Sandy Crowder reveals that Gaines has been embezzling, and she steals $4 million to buy Rafid. With Rafid in hand, they force their way through a militia checkpoint to the exchange, where Skiles secures Riley's release; when Rafid lunges at Skiles, he is shot by a sniper, revealed as the fixer Bernard, who slips away with Sandrine, an Israeli agent. title: Alpha
tagline: Leaders are born from survival
overview: In the prehistoric past, Keda, a young and inexperienced hunter, struggles to return home after being separated from his tribe when bison hunting goes awry. On his way back he will find an unexpected ally.
plot:
Alpha is a 2018 American epic drama film directed by Charlie McDowell and written by Dan O'Bannon and Alexander Dinelaris Jr. The movie stars Kodi Smit-McPhee, Alia Shawkat, and Justin Kelley.

The story takes place in the late Stone Age, around 20,000 years ago, during a time of great change for early humans. The film follows the journey of Oena (Kodi Smit-McPhee), a young hunter who lives with his tribe in the wilderness. After a devastating event that kills many of his people, Oena is left alone and must navigate the harsh environment to survive.

As he travels through the forest, Oena encounters a wolf pup, which he names Kenai (also known as Wahya). The two form an unlikely bond, with Kenai becoming Oena's companion and protector. However, their relationship is put to the test when they are attacked by a pack of wolves, and Kenai is killed.

Consumed by grief and anger, Oena decides to take revenge on the wolves that killed his friend. He begins to hunt them down, but as he does, he starts to transform into a wolf-like creature himself. This transformation is not just physical, but also emotional and spiritual, as Oena struggles to come to terms with his new identity.

As Oena navigates his newfound powers, he must confront the harsh realities of his tribe's existence. He witnesses their brutal treatment of animals and their disregard for the natural world. This realization sparks a transformation within him, as he begins to see himself as part of the natural world rather than separate from it.

The film's climax features Oena facing off against a rival tribe that has been threatening his people. In a symbolic confrontation, Oena uses his newfound powers to defend his tribe and restore balance to the natural world. The movie ends with Oena standing alone in the forest, having found a new sense of purpose and belonging.

Throughout the film, McDowell explores themes of identity, community, and the human relationship with nature. The movie features stunning cinematography and a haunting score, which complements the emotional depth of the story. While Alpha received mixed reviews from critics, it has developed a loyal following among fans of epic dramas and those interested in exploring the early history of humanity.

Overall, Alpha is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that explores the complexities of human nature and our relationship with the natural world.

title: Triple Frontier

overview: Struggling to make ends meet, former special ops soldiers reunite for a high-stakes heist: stealing $75 million from a South American drug lord.

Triple Frontier is a 2019 American action-adventure film directed by J.C. Chandor and written by Mark Boal, J.C. Chandor, and Matt Boling. The movie stars Oscar Isaac, Ben Affleck, Charlie Hunnam, Garrett Hedlund, and Pedro Pascal.

The story follows three former US Special Forces operatives - Chris Mullin (Oscar Isaac), Billy Marks (Ben Affleck), and Mike Kinney (Charlie Hunnam) - who have retired from their military careers. The trio reunites for a high school friend's 40th birthday party in New York City, where they are approached by Santiago "Pope" Garcia (Gael García Bernal), a former comrade-in-arms.

Santiago reveals that his younger brother, Francisco, has been kidnapped by the notorious Bolivian cartel leader, Dina (Catalina Sandino Moreno). The kidnappers demand $75 million in exchange for Francisco's safe return. Pope asks his old friends to help him rescue his brother and retrieve the ransom money.

The team devises a plan to infiltrate Bolivia and gather intelligence on the cartel's operations. They assemble a group of local fighters, including a Bolivian woman named Ana (Natalia Beristáin), who becomes an ally in their mission.

As they prepare for the rescue operation, the team faces personal demons and conflicts that threaten to derail their mission. Chris struggles with his past mistakes, Billy grapples with feelings of guilt over his role in a previous military operation gone wrong, and Mike tries to reconcile his loyalty to his friends with his growing sense of morality.

The team launches a daring rescue mission, navigating treacherous terrain and avoiding cartel henchmen. Along the way, they encounter Ana, who becomes an integral part of their plan. The group faces numerous challenges, including treacherous mountain paths, rival factions within the cartel, and personal betrayals.

As the stakes escalate, the team's bond is tested, and they are forced to confront their own mortality. In a tense showdown, they face off against Dina's henchmen in a violent confrontation that leaves several characters gravely injured or killed.

In the aftermath of the rescue mission, the team reflects on the true cost of their actions. Chris comes to terms with his past mistakes, Billy finds redemption through his sacrifice, and Mike learns to prioritize his humanity over his loyalty to his friends.

The movie concludes with a poignant moment of closure for Pope, who finally gets to see his brother safe and sound. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of adversity, friendship and loyalty can be powerful forces for redemption and healing.

Overall, Triple Frontier is an action-packed thrill ride with a strong ensemble cast and a gripping narrative that explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and redemption.

title: Marrowbone
tagline: No one will ever separate us.
overview: A young man and his three younger siblings are plagued by a sinister presence in the sprawling manor in which they live.
plot:
Marrowbone (Spanish: El secreto de Marrowbone) is a 2017 English-language Spanish psychological horror mystery film written and directed by Sergio G. Sánchez. It stars George MacKay, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Heaton, Mia Goth and Matthew Stagg, and follows four siblings who move from England to their mother's ancestral home in Maine, where they are confronted by a sinister presence. It screened in the Special Presentations section of the 2017 Toronto International Film Festival and was released in Spain by Universal Pictures on 27 October 2017.

In 1968, Rose Fairbairn brings her four children, Jack, Jane, Billy and Sam, from England to the remote house in rural Maine where she grew up, and tells them they will now go by her maiden name, Marrowbone. The family is befriended by a local girl, Allie, but Rose's health soon fails. Before she dies she makes Jack, the eldest, promise to keep the family together and to hide her death until he can become his siblings' legal guardian. Six months later the children are still living alone in the house, where every mirror is covered and the attic is sealed off because they believe something lives up there. Jack slips into town for supplies and quietly courts Allie, now working at the library, while hiding his past from her. Tom Porter, the town lawyer handling the Marrowbone estate and Allie's unrequited admirer, needs Rose's signature to complete the transfer of the property, and the siblings are forced to forge it and to dip into a box of money left by their father. As strange noises and incidents in the house multiply, Allie learns from Tom some disturbing facts about the family's past and the father the children fled from, while Tom, under financial pressure, begins to suspect the Marrowbones are hiding more money and turns to blackmail. When Billy goes looking for the money in the house, he makes a terrifying discovery, and the secret that Jack has been protecting threatens to come out.

On Rotten Tomatoes, Marrowbone holds a 49% approval rating based on 75 reviews, with a consensus that its effective setting and strong cast cannot make up for thinly conceived characters and a story short on genuine scares, while Metacritic gave it a score of 63 out of 100.

title: Hunter Killer
tagline: Courage runs deep
overview: Captain Glass of the USS Arkansas discovers that a coup d'état is taking place in Russia, so he and his crew join an elite group working on the ground to prevent a war.
plot:
Hunter Killer is a 2018 American action thriller film directed by Donovan Marsh and written by Arne Schmidt and Jamie Moss, based on the 2012 novel Firing Point by Don Keith and George Wallace. Gerard Butler stars as Commander Joe Glass, a submarine captain whose crew joins a team of Navy SEALs to rescue the Russian president from a coup, with Gary Oldman, Toby Stephens as the SEAL leader Lieutenant Bill Beaman and Michael Nyqvist, in his penultimate film role, as the Russian captain Sergei Andropov. Common and Linda Cardellini also appear.

When the American submarine USS Tampa Bay vanishes while shadowing a Russian submarine in the Barents Sea, the newly promoted and unconventional Glass is sent to investigate aboard USS Arkansas. Meanwhile, Beaman's SEAL team, watching a Russian naval base at Polyarny, sees Defense Minister Dmitriy Durov stage a coup and seize President Nikolai Zakarin in a bid to start a war, and the team is forced to leave behind a wounded member, Martinelli. Arkansas finds the wreck of Tampa Bay with no survivors and the sunken Russian submarine Konek, apparently sabotaged from within, and is ambushed by a second Russian submarine hidden beneath an iceberg, the vessel that had sunk Tampa Bay. Arkansas fights back and rescues the Konek's survivors, including Captain Andropov. Rear Admiral John Fisk proposes that Arkansas pick up Zakarin once the SEALs free him. With the reluctant Andropov's guidance, the submarine slips through a minefield to the base undetected. The SEALs free Zakarin with the help of a wounded presidential bodyguard, Oleg, losing him and two of their own, and Beaman delivers the injured president to the submarine's rescue vehicle before returning for Martinelli. Arkansas is then attacked by Andropov's old ship, the destroyer Yevchenko but Andropov signals that Zakarin is aboard. When Durov orders missiles fired at the surfaced submarine, Glass refuses to retaliate for fear of starting the war he is trying to prevent, and Andropov's former crew defy orders, shoot down the missiles and destroy the base headquarters, killing Durov. War averted, Glass returns Zakarin and the Russian survivors and departs under Russian escort.

Summit Premiere released Hunter Killer in the United States on October 26, 2018. It flopped, grossing $31.7 million worldwide, and drew mixed reviews, with a 38% Rotten Tomatoes rating.
