The film sheds light on the struggles faced by the common people, particularly the working class, who were fighting for their rights and freedoms in a society dominated by the wealthy and powerful.

The movie also touches upon themes of protest, resistance, and the power of collective action. It highlights the bravery and determination of the ordinary people who risked everything to demand change and challenge the status quo. Through the characters' stories, the film conveys the sense of hope and optimism that defined this period in history, as well as the brutal suppression of dissent.

Furthermore, Peterloo examines the complexities of British politics during this era, revealing the contradictions and hypocrisies of a society that claimed to value liberty but often used force to maintain its power. The film's portrayal of the Peterloo Massacre itself is both haunting and thought-provoking, serving as a powerful reminder of the devastating consequences of unchecked authority and the importance of protecting individual rights.

Overall, Peterloo is a moving and thought-provoking drama that offers a nuanced exploration of one of Britain's most significant and overlooked moments in history.

Godzilla vs. Kong is a 2021 American monster film directed by Adam Wingard, produced by Legendary Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The story takes place on a remote island where the legendary creature Kong has been living for years. The island is home to a group of scientists who are studying Kong's behavior and trying to understand his origins. However, their research is disrupted when Godzilla, the King of the Monsters, arrives on the scene.

Godzilla is drawn to the island by the presence of a powerful artifact known as the "Heart of the Ocean," which has the ability to control and manipulate the emotions of those around it. The scientists believe that this artifact could be the key to understanding Kong's origins and potentially harnessing his power for human benefit.

As Godzilla begins to wreak havoc on the island, Kong emerges from the depths of the ocean to defend himself and his home. The two monsters engage in an epic battle, with Kong using his intelligence and agility to try and outsmart Godzilla.

However, as the fight rages on, it becomes clear that there is more at play than just a simple monster showdown. A group of humans, led by Dr. Ilene Andrews (Vera Farmiga), are secretly working to harness the power of the Heart of the Ocean for their own gain. They believe that this artifact could be the key to unlocking new technologies and advancing human civilization.

As the battle between Godzilla and Kong reaches its climax, it becomes clear that the true enemy is not the monsters themselves, but rather the humans who seek to exploit them for their own purposes. In the end, Kong emerges victorious, but not before Godzilla is severely injured.

The film ends with Kong standing victorious on the island, but also aware of the danger that he poses to humanity. The final shot is of Kong looking out at the ocean, hinting that he may one day be forced to confront his own destiny and the consequences of his actions.

Overall, Godzilla vs. Kong is a thrilling and action-packed film that explores themes of power, responsibility, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control.

title: Alita: Battle Angel

plot:
Alita: Battle Angel is a 2019 science fiction action film directed by Robert Rodriguez and based on the manga series "Gunnm" by Yukito Kishiro. The movie takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where humans have become extinct, and advanced technology has been left behind.

The story begins with Dr. Dyson Ido (played by Christoph Waltz), a brilliant scientist who discovers a severely damaged cyborg girl, Alita (played by Rosa Salazar), in an abandoned scrapyard. Alita is a "Gunnm," a being created from the remains of humans and advanced technology to serve as soldiers or assassins. However, Alita's creator, Dr. Ido, decides to spare her life and raise her as his own.

As Alita grows up, she begins to develop her own identity and desires, which often conflict with her programming. She becomes a skilled fighter and athlete, using her advanced technology to protect herself and those around her. Meanwhile, a powerful corporation called Iron City is seeking to exploit the remaining resources of the post-apocalyptic world.

The main antagonist, Vector (played by Mahershala Ali), is a ruthless mercenary who seeks to control Iron City and eliminate any opposition. He becomes obsessed with Alita, seeing her as a means to gain power and control over the corporation.

As Alita navigates this treacherous world, she discovers that she has a unique connection to the ancient technology of the pre-apocalyptic era. She also learns about her own past and the true nature of her existence as a Gunnm.

The plot thickens when Alita is forced to confront Vector and his allies in an epic battle. Along the way, she forms alliances with other characters, including Hugo (played by Jorge Lendeborg Jr.), a young hacker who helps her uncover the truth about her past.

Throughout the movie, Rodriguez weaves together themes of identity, humanity, and what it means to be alive. Alita's journey is a powerful exploration of self-discovery and empowerment, as she navigates a world that seeks to control and exploit her.

The film features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a strong performance from Rosa Salazar as the titular character. While some critics noted that the movie deviated slightly from the original manga series, fans of the source material generally praised the adaptation's faithfulness to Kishiro's vision.

Overall, Alita: Battle Angel is a thrilling and emotionally resonant sci-fi epic that explores complex themes and features impressive action sequences. With its stunning visuals and strong performances, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

title: Daylight's End
tagline: The Dead Rise When Daylight Ends
overview: Years after a mysterious plague has devastated the planet and turned most of humanity into blood-hungry creatures, a rogue drifter on a vengeful hunt stumbles across a band of survivors in an abandoned police station and reluctantly agrees to try to help them defend themselves and escape to the sanctuary they so desperately need.
plot:
Daylight's End is a 2016 American post-apocalyptic horror action film directed by William Kaufman and written by Chad Law. Johnny Strong stars as Thomas Rourke, a drifter who agrees to help a group of survivors, played by Lance Henriksen, Louis Mandylor, Hakeem Kae-Kazim, among others, to escape to safety. The mixed martial arts fighter Krzysztof Soszynski plays the leader of the vampire-like creatures that hunt them.

A plague has turned most of humanity into savage, vampire-like creatures that cannot survive in sunlight, and civilization has collapsed. The infected hide in dark places during the day and hunt at night. Rourke, a hardened loner traveling the empty highways of Texas in search of the creature responsible for the death of his wife, arrives in a small town where a woman named Sam and her companions are being attacked by looters. Rourke kills the attackers, and Sam tells him about a group of survivors holed up in an old police station in Dallas, which still has running water and electricity.

When they reach the station at sunset, the creatures attack, and Rourke glimpses a huge infected that appears to lead the pack. Inside, the survivors, many of them former police officers, are led by Chief Frank Hill, who distrusts the newcomer, disarms him and locks him in a cell for the night. Rourke learns that Sam's group has located a cargo plane and that the survivors plan to fly to a much larger colony in Baja California. With dawn their only window of safety, the group must make it from the station to the airfield, but a series of setbacks forces them to fight their way through hordes of infected, and Rourke's personal vendetta against the pack leader puts his own goals at odds with the survival of the others.

The film received a modest release and was well received by several genre critics. Mike Wilson of Bloody Disgusting wrote that it was neither cerebral nor original but still an enjoyable romp, Hugo Ozman of Screen Anarchy called it a solid thriller and suggested Kaufman deserved a big-budget project, and Mark L. Miller of Ain't It Cool News felt that its well-shot action made up for its debt to 1980s action films.

title: The Nightingale
tagline: Her song will not be silenced.
overview: In 1825, Clare, a 21-year-old Irish convict, chases a British soldier through the rugged Tasmanian wilderness, bent on revenge for a terrible act of violence he committed against her family. She enlists the services of an Aboriginal tracker who is also marked by trauma from his own violence-filled past.
plot:
The Nightingale is a 2018 historical drama film directed by Jennifer Kent, not South Australian Film Corporation.

The movie is set in Tasmania during World War II and follows the story of two sisters, Clare and Frances, as they navigate the harsh realities of war and survival. The main themes of the film revolve around the devastating effects of colonialism, imperialism, and the brutal treatment of Indigenous Australians by British settlers.

At its core, The Nightingale is a powerful exploration of the long-lasting impact of trauma, violence, and oppression on individuals and communities. The film delves into the complexities of female relationships, particularly between sisters, as they struggle to survive in a world that seems determined to destroy them.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, belonging, and the search for meaning in the face of unimaginable suffering. Through the characters' experiences, Kent sheds light on the dark history of Tasmania's treatment of Indigenous Australians, highlighting the systemic violence and marginalization that has had lasting effects on the community.

Ultimately, The Nightingale is a haunting and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront the harsh realities of human nature and the devastating consequences of unchecked power and prejudice.

title: Bright
overview: In an alternate present-day where magical creatures live among us, two L.A. cops become embroiled in a prophesied turf battle.
plot:
Bright is a 2017 American fantasy action film directed by David Yates and written by Max Landis. The movie takes place in a world where magic has been outlawed, and orcs have taken over the city of Portland.

The story follows two detectives, Daryl Ward (Will Smith), a human cop, and Nick Jakoby (Joel Edgerton), an orc cop, who are forced to work together to solve a murder case. The victim is a young girl named Beth Harmon (Lucy Fry), who was found dead in the woods with a magical amulet around her neck.

As Daryl and Nick delve deeper into the case, they discover that the amulet is one of five magical orbs created by the ancient elf king, King Elfhelm. The orbs are said to have the power to bring about peace between humans and orcs, but they also attract the attention of a powerful sorcerer named Berruk (Ed Skrein), who seeks to use their power for his own gain.

As the investigation unfolds, Daryl and Nick must navigate the complex web of human and orc politics in Portland, all while facing their own prejudices and biases. Along the way, they are aided by a wise old elf named Professor Stone (Michael Stuhlbarg) and a young elf named Elara Vex (Noomi Rapace).

Throughout the movie, Daryl and Nick's partnership is put to the test as they learn to trust each other and work together to solve the case. Along the way, they also discover that Beth Harmon was not just an innocent victim, but rather a key player in a larger conspiracy involving the magical orbs.

As the story reaches its climax, Daryl and Nick must face off against Berruk and his minions in a battle to control the magical orbs and bring about peace between humans and orcs. In the end, they succeed in defeating Berruk and shattering the magical orbs, but not before realizing that their partnership has changed them both forever.

Overall, Bright is a visually stunning film with a unique blend of fantasy and action elements. The movie explores themes of prejudice, trust, and redemption, and features a talented cast of characters. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the genre have praised its originality and entertainment value.

title: Resident Evil: Vendetta
original_title: バイオハザード ヴェンデッタ
overview: BSAA Chris Redfield enlists the help of government agent Leon S. Kennedy and Professor Rebecca Chambers from Alexander Institute of Biotechnology to stop a death merchant with a vengeance from spreading a deadly virus in New York.
plot:
Resident Evil: Vendetta, released in Japan as Biohazard: Vendetta, is a 2017 English-language Japanese computer-animated action horror film set in the universe of Capcom's Resident Evil video games. It was directed by Takanori Tsujimoto, produced by Marza Animation Planet with Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi, and executive produced by the horror director Takashi Shimizu. The film brings together three of the series' best-known characters, Chris Redfield, Leon S. Kennedy and Rebecca Chambers, and it was released in Japanese cinemas on 27 May 2017, with a free PlayStation VR promotional experience released a few days earlier.

In 2014, Chris Redfield, an agent of the Bioterrorism Security Assessment Alliance, is pursuing Glenn Arias, a former CIA operative turned arms dealer. Arias blames the United States government for a drone strike that killed his friends and family, including his bride, at his own wedding, and he is now developing and smuggling biological weapons into the country. Chris leads a raid on a mansion in Mexico to rescue an undercover informant, but his team is wiped out by zombies and traps, and he survives only to discover that the informant has been turned into a zombie under Arias's control.

Months later, Professor Rebecca Chambers, a former member of the S.T.A.R.S. unit, is researching a new strain called the Animality Virus, which can remain dormant in a host until it is activated by a trigger. Arias's associate Maria Gomez attacks the laboratory and releases the virus, and Rebecca survives only by developing a vaccine. Recognising similarities with the parasite Las Plagas, she and Chris seek out Leon, who is struggling with guilt after a recent outbreak, to join the investigation. When Rebecca is captured and infected with a vaccine-resistant strain, Chris and Leon uncover Arias's plan for a massive viral attack on New York City and must race to rescue her and stop the outbreak.

The film emphasises action set pieces, including gunfights, close-quarters combat and a motorcycle chase, while its villain is motivated by grief and a desire for revenge. A scene involving zombie dogs was almost cut but was kept at the director's insistence.

Resident Evil: Vendetta received mixed reviews from the small number of critics who reviewed it, with about 43 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it was praised mainly for its animation and action sequences while its story was considered thin.

title: Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation
tagline: Family vacation. It will suck the life out of you.
overview: Dracula, Mavis, Johnny and the rest of the Drac Pack take a vacation on a luxury Monster Cruise Ship, where Dracula falls in love with the ship’s captain, Ericka, who’s secretly a descendant of Abraham Van Helsing, the notorious monster slayer.
plot:
Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation is a 2018 American animated monster comedy film directed by Genndy Tartakovsky and produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie serves as the third installment in the Hotel Transylvania franchise.

The story begins with Count Dracula (Adam Sandler) preparing for his daughter Mavis's (Selena Gomez) wedding to Jonathan (Andy Samberg). However, on the eve of the ceremony, a werewolf named Wayne (Kevin James) crashes the party and steals the bride. In an attempt to rescue Mavis, Dracula sets sail on a cruise ship called the "Dreadful Child" with his friends, including Frankenstein's monster (Steve Buscemi), the Invisible Man (David Spade), and the Wolfman (Robert Smigel).

As they embark on their journey, the group faces various obstacles, including sea monsters, pirates, and a rival cruise line run by the evil Captain Cutler (Peter Criss). Along the way, Dracula begins to reconnect with his daughter and learns to let go of his overprotectiveness.

Meanwhile, Mavis is being pursued by Jonathan's werewolf friend, Wayne. As they try to outsmart each other, they develop feelings for each other, but their love is put to the test when they are forced to confront their respective pasts.

Throughout the movie, Dracula and Mavis grow closer as they face various challenges together. They also learn valuable lessons about trust, acceptance, and embracing change. The film features a range of humor, from slapstick comedy to witty one-liners, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

As the story unfolds, the group faces its greatest challenge yet: a showdown with Captain Cutler and his pirate crew. In the end, Dracula and Mavis successfully rescue their friends and find love in the process. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with the entire cast coming together to celebrate the power of friendship and acceptance.

Overall, Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation is a fun and lighthearted film that explores themes of family, love, and self-discovery. With its colorful characters, engaging storyline, and hilarious humor, it's sure to delight both kids and adults alike.

title: Wonder Park
tagline: Dream Bigger
overview: A young girl named June with a big imagination makes an incredible discovery -- the amusement park of her dreams has come to life. Filled with the world's wildest rides operated by fun-loving animals, the excitement never ends. But when trouble hits, June and her misfit team of furry friends begin an unforgettable journey to save the park.
plot:
Wonder Park is a 2019 American animated fantasy adventure comedy produced by Paramount Animation and Nickelodeon Movies, with animation by Ilion Animation Studios, from a screenplay by Josh Appelbaum and André Nemec. Brianna Denski voices the young heroine June Bailey, with Jennifer Garner and Matthew Broderick as her parents and Mila Kunis, John Oliver, Kenan Thompson, Ken Jeong, Norbert Leo Butz and Ken Hudson Campbell as the park's animals. Director Dylan Brown was dismissed by Paramount in early 2018, and the film was released without a credited director on March 15, 2019.

June is an imaginative girl who, with her mother, invents Wonderland, a magical amusement park run by talking animals: Boomer the blue bear, Greta the wild boar, the beaver brothers Gus and Cooper, the porcupine Steve, who secretly loves Greta, and the chimpanzee Peanut, who builds new rides from the ideas whispered to him by June's mother. When her mother falls ill and leaves for treatment, June abandons the game and burns her park plans. Sent off to maths camp, she fears her father cannot cope without her and escapes from the bus to head home.

Lost in the woods, she discovers a real Wonderland, now run-down and engulfed by a menacing cloud called the Darkness that is devouring the park. With the animals she tries to restart the Clockwork Swings, the machine at the heart of the park, but they are attacked by the Chimpanzombies, former plush toys that serve the Darkness. Separated from the others, June finds Peanut hiding in Zero-G Land, where he admits he is lost without the voice in his head. June realises that the Darkness grew out of her own despair over her mother's illness.

When she confesses this, the hurt animals turn their backs on her, and the Chimpanzombies seize Peanut. Discovering that she has been the source of the park's ideas all along, June repairs a ride, catches up with her friends and convinces them she wants to help. She plunges into the Darkness to rescue Peanut, promising to be his imaginative voice, and he conjures an escape slide. Realising that the Clockwork Swings are keyed to her own handwritten name, they restart the machine and clear the Darkness. June returns home to her recovered mother, and together they build a backyard Wonderland.

Wonder Park grossed about 124 million dollars worldwide against a budget estimated at 80 to 100 million dollars, and received generally negative reviews.

title: The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run
original_title: The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run
tagline: They're Not in Bikini Bottom Anymore.
overview: When his best friend Gary is suddenly snatched away, SpongeBob takes Patrick on a madcap mission far beyond Bikini Bottom to save their pink-shelled pal.
plot:
The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run is a 2020 animated adventure comedy film directed by Tim Hill, based on the characters from the Nickelodeon television series SpongeBob SquarePants. The movie follows the story of SpongeBob and his pet snail Gary as they embark on an epic journey to save their home of Bikini Bottom.

The movie begins with SpongeBob (voiced by Tom Kenny) and Patrick Star (voiced by Bill Fagerbakke) trying to adopt a baby, but their plans are foiled when the adoption is rejected. Feeling defeated, SpongeBob decides to take Gary on a road trip to the Fry Cook Hall of Fame in Atlanta, Georgia, where he hopes to find inspiration for his life.

However, things quickly go awry as they get lost and kidnapped by King Poseidon (voiced by Rob Paulsen), who intends to use Gary's DNA to create an army of super-soldier snails. SpongeBob and Patrick must navigate through the underwater city of Atlantis, avoiding various obstacles and enemies along the way.

As they journey deeper into Atlantis, SpongeBob and Patrick meet a group of rebels led by Mermaid Man (voiced by Mr. Lawrence) and Barnacle Boy (voiced by Ernest Borgnine), who are fighting against King Poseidon's tyranny. The duo joins forces with the rebels to rescue Gary and stop King Poseidon's evil plans.

Throughout their adventure, SpongeBob and Patrick encounter various familiar characters from the show, including Sandy Cheeks (voiced by Carolyn Lawrence) and Squidward Tentacles (voiced by Rodger Bumpass). They also meet new characters, such as Mindy (voiced by Katie Layden), a young mermaid who becomes SpongeBob's love interest.

As the story unfolds, SpongeBob and Patrick face numerous challenges and setbacks, but their friendship and determination ultimately lead them to success. In the end, they successfully rescue Gary and defeat King Poseidon, saving Bikini Bottom from destruction.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and a heartwarming storyline that celebrates the power of friendship and perseverance. With its colorful characters, engaging plot, and exciting action sequences, The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run is a fun and entertaining film that is sure to delight both old and new fans of the beloved Nickelodeon series.

title: Sicario: Day of the Soldado
tagline: No rules this time
overview: Agent Matt Graver teams up with operative Alejandro Gillick to prevent Mexican drug cartels from smuggling terrorists across the United States border.
plot:
Sicario: Day of the Soldado, also known as Sicario 2: Soldado, is a 2018 American action crime thriller directed by Stefano Sollima and written by Taylor Sheridan. A sequel to Sicario (2015), it sees Benicio del Toro, Josh Brolin, Jeffrey Donovan and Raoul Trujillo reprise their roles, with Isabela Merced, Manuel Garcia-Rulfo and Catherine Keener joining the cast.

After an ISIS suicide bombing kills fifteen people in a Kansas City grocery store, the government authorizes CIA officer Matt Graver to take extreme action against Mexican cartels suspected of smuggling the bombers across the border. Graver and the Department of Defense decide to ignite a war between the cartels, and he recruits operative Alejandro Gillick, using a private military contractor for deniability. Gillick assassinates a Matamoros cartel lawyer in Mexico City, while Graver's team kidnaps Isabel Reyes, daughter of rival Sonoran kingpin Carlos Reyes, in a false flag operation, then stages a DEA rescue in Texas. As they return her to Mexico, their corrupt police escort turns on them, and the Americans kill 25 Mexican police officers in the firefight. Isabel, suspecting the truth, flees into the desert, and Gillick follows her.

When investigators find that at least two of the bombers were domestic terrorists, the Secretary of Defense abandons the mission and orders Isabel and Gillick killed to hide American involvement. Gillick refuses and goes rogue to protect her, and the two pose as migrants and pay smugglers to cross into the U.S. At the border, Miguel, a young Mexican American recruited by the traffickers, recognizes Gillick from an earlier encounter, and the gang seizes them. As an initiation, Miguel is made to shoot the hooded Gillick in the head. Graver's team, having watched by satellite, wipes out the gang and, defying orders, takes Isabel to the U.S. to enter witness protection. Gillick, shot only through the cheek, survives and kills his pursuers. A year later, a heavily tattooed Miguel goes to meet his gang contact and finds Gillick waiting, ready to discuss his future as a sicario.

Sony Pictures Releasing distributed the film in North America from June 29, 2018, with Lionsgate handling most international markets; it is dedicated to the first film's composer, Jóhann Jóhannsson. It grossed $75.8 million worldwide. Critics found it less subversive than its predecessor but a stylish thriller, giving it 62% on Rotten Tomatoes and 61 on Metacritic.

title: Tully
tagline: See how the mother half lives.
overview: Marlo, a mother of three, including a newborn, is gifted a night nanny by her brother. Hesitant at first, she quickly forms a bond with the thoughtful, surprising, and sometimes challenging nanny named Tully.
plot:
Tully is a 2018 American comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of motherhood, identity, and the struggles of modern womanhood.

At its core, Tully delves into the theme of exhaustion and burnout, particularly in the context of motherhood. The protagonist, Marlo (played by Charlize Theron), is a devoted but overwhelmed mother of three young children, struggling to balance her own desires and needs with the demands of caring for her family.

As the story unfolds, Tully also examines the societal expectations placed on women, particularly in terms of their roles as caregivers and nurturers. Marlo's life is marked by a sense of disconnection and isolation, as she feels suffocated by the responsibilities of motherhood and the lack of personal fulfillment in her own life.

The film also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery, as Marlo embarks on a journey of introspection and growth. Through her experiences with a night nanny (played by Mackenzie Davis), Marlo begins to re-evaluate her priorities and redefine what it means to be a mother and a woman in today's society.

Ultimately, Tully presents a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of the challenges faced by modern women, particularly those navigating the complexities of motherhood. The film offers a powerful commentary on the societal pressures that can lead to feelings of exhaustion, disconnection, and disillusionment, while also celebrating the resilience and strength of women in the face of adversity.

title: Prey
tagline: On the loose... and he's hungry.
overview: A zoo veterinarian gets caught up in a grisly adventure as she finds herself leading the city-wide hunt for a monstrous lion terrorizing the Dutch capital of Amsterdam.
plot:
Prey (Dutch: Prooi), also known as Uncaged, is a 2016 Dutch action comedy horror film written and directed by Dick Maas about a man-eating lion loose in Amsterdam. It stars Sophie van Winden, Julian Looman and Mark Frost, with Rienus Krul, Theo Pont and Victor Löw, and was released on 13 October 2016.

When a family is found slaughtered on a farm outside Amsterdam, Chief Inspector Olaf Brinkers suspects that this is no ordinary crime and calls in Lizzy, a veterinarian at the ARTIS zoo who spent several years in Tanzania. She quickly confirms his fears: the victims were killed by a large male lion. Later that day a golfer is mauled in broad daylight, proving that the animal has moved into the city, but Police Commissioner Zaimberg refuses to accept the evidence until a delivery driver is also killed. Ignoring Lizzy's advice to hire a professional hunter, Zaimberg calls in his cousin Theo, an amateur whose experience is limited to game farms, and the hunt ends in disaster for Theo and his son. When the lion attacks passengers on a city tram, its presence can no longer be hidden, and the humiliated commissioner finally agrees to Lizzy's plan. She summons Jack Delarue, an eccentric English big game hunter who uses a wheelchair and who also happens to be her former boyfriend, a development that causes friction with her current partner Dave, a television news cameraman. Delarue immediately clashes with Zaimberg by proposing to use a victim's body as bait, while further deaths and a bungled police operation, in which armed officers mistakenly open fire on a group of army veterans conducting their own hunt, push the city toward panic. As Lizzy, Delarue and Dave pursue the lion through the streets and into the university's medical building, the hunters discover that their prey is cunning, relentless and seemingly everywhere at once.

Prey received mostly positive reviews from critics in the Netherlands. Floortje Smit of de Volkskrant called it an entertaining thriller and a fine addition to Maas's body of work, full of jabs at Dutch gossip and regulatory zeal, while Bart van der Put of Het Parool gave it a mixed review, finding it weaker than the director's earlier films. Despite the positive notices, the film was a box-office flop in the Netherlands, although it found success in China.

title: Mary Poppins Returns
tagline: Magic Always Returns.
overview: Mary Poppins returns to the Banks family and helps them evade grave dangers by taking them on magical, musical adventures.
plot:
Mary Poppins Returns is a 2018 musical fantasy film directed by Rob Marshall and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1964 original film, Mary Poppins, and continues the story of the beloved nanny.

The film takes place 25 years after the events of the original. Michael Banks (Ben Whishaw), now an adult, is struggling to cope with the loss of his father, George Banks (David Tomlinson). The family's life has become dull and grey, lacking the magic and wonder that Mary Poppins brought into their lives.

When the children begin to act out and rebel against their parents' strict rules, Michael realizes that he needs help. He turns to an old friend, Jack (Lin-Manuel Miranda), who is now a struggling artist and musician. Jack introduces Michael to his cousin, Topsy Kettering (Emily Blunt), a wealthy and eccentric woman who claims to be the long-lost sister of Mary Poppins.

Topsy reveals that she has been keeping an eye on the Banks children from afar and believes that they need Mary Poppins' unique brand of magic in their lives. Michael is skeptical at first, but eventually agrees to let Topsy find Mary Poppins for him.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Mary Poppins (Emily Blunt) returning to London after a long absence. She is still as magical and mysterious as ever, with a newfound sense of purpose and determination. With the help of her trusty umbrella, Mary Poppins sets out to bring joy and wonder back into the lives of the Banks children.

Throughout the film, Mary Poppins uses her unique brand of magic to teach the children valuable lessons about love, loss, and the importance of family. Along the way, she also helps Michael come to terms with his own grief and find a new sense of purpose in life.

As the story reaches its climax, Mary Poppins reveals that she has been searching for a special place where the magic can be shared with others. She takes the children on a fantastical journey through London, using her umbrella to transport them to different locations around the city.

In the end, Mary Poppins helps the Banks family find closure and healing, and Michael comes to terms with his own emotions. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the entire family coming together to celebrate the magic of life and the power of love and connection.

Overall, Mary Poppins Returns is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that pays tribute to the original while also introducing new characters and themes. overview: Frank, a single man raising his child prodigy niece Mary, is drawn into a custody battle with his mother.

Gifted is a 2017 American drama film directed by Marc Webb and written by Tom Flynn. The movie stars Chris Evans, Mckenna Grace, Lindsay Duncan, Octavia Spencer, and Jenny Slate.

Frank discovers that Mary's grandmother, Evelyn (Lindsay Duncan), has been keeping tabs on their lives and wants to reconnect with her granddaughter. However, it turns out that Evelyn is a brilliant mathematician who has been working on a groundbreaking theory in number theory. She believes that Mary's exceptional intelligence can help her make a significant contribution to the field.

As Frank navigates his complicated relationship with Evelyn, he must also confront the reality of being an unworthy parent and the difficulties of raising a child with extraordinary abilities. Meanwhile, Evelyn's intentions are not entirely altruistic, and she has her own motivations for wanting to reconnect with Mary.

Throughout the film, Frank and Evelyn work together to help Mary develop her talents and prepare her for college. Along the way, they face numerous challenges, including bureaucratic red tape, social stigma, and personal struggles. As the story unfolds, Frank's character evolves from a reluctant single father to a determined advocate for his daughter's future.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Evelyn's true intentions are revealed, and Mary is forced to confront the harsh realities of her situation. In the end, Frank must make an impossible choice between his love for his daughter and his own sense of identity.

Gifted received widespread critical acclaim for its nuanced portrayal of complex characters, particularly Chris Evans' performance as a single father struggling to provide for his exceptional child. The film also explores themes of identity, class, and the challenges faced by gifted children and their families.

Overall, Gifted is a heartwarming and thought-provoking drama that sheds light on the often-overlooked experiences of gifted children and their caregivers.

title: Death Race: Beyond Anarchy
overview: Black Ops specialist Connor Gibson infiltrates a maximum security prison to take down legendary driver Frankenstein in a violent and brutal car race.
plot:
Death Race: Beyond Anarchy is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Don Michael Paul. It is the fourth and final entry in the Death Race series that began with the 2008 remake of Death Race 2000, and it serves as a direct sequel to the 2008 film. Zach McGowan stars as Connor Gibson, with Danny Trejo returning as Goldberg, and Danny Glover, Frederick Koehler and Christine Marzano in supporting roles. The film was released on DVD and digital platforms on 2 October 2018.

The story takes place in the Sprawl, an enormous privately run prison that holds hundreds of thousands of inmates. Inside, the brutal Death Race competition, in which convicts drive armoured vehicles in deadly races, has been outlawed by a new warden appointed by the prison's corporate owner, Weyland International. The warden's mission is to eliminate Frankenstein, the masked Death Race champion who effectively rules the prison. When a prison SWAT team attempts to take him down, Frankenstein's loyal army of inmates massacres them, and he warns the warden that every man sent after him will meet the same fate.

A helicopter carrying new prisoners arrives, and most of the newcomers are killed by a gang known as the Cops, led by the racer Johnny Law. Two survivors fight off the entire gang: one of them is Connor, a former special forces operative who has been secretly sent into the Sprawl to assassinate Frankenstein. Inside the prison, Connor learns to navigate its lawless society, which is controlled by gangs and a black market economy, with help from veteran inmates including Goldberg and Baltimore Bob. He also grows close to Jane, the bartender at a bar run by Frankenstein, who introduces him to Baltimore Bob. To get close to his target, Connor must enter the Death Race himself, and as he competes he discovers that the authorities' motives are far from clear-cut.

The film continues the series' formula of vehicular combat, gang warfare and graphic violence, set in a more anarchic environment than the earlier prison-based instalments.

Reviews were generally negative. DVD Talk felt that it offered a mixture of old and new elements that would please fans of the series without winning over anyone who disliked the previous films, while The A.V. Club described the Death Race franchise as a younger, dumber and cheaper version of Fast & Furious.

title: Everybody Knows
tagline: Who did it?
overview: Laura, a Spanish woman living in Buenos Aires, returns to her hometown outside Madrid with her Argentinian husband and children. However, the trip is upset by unexpected events that bring secrets into the open.
plot:
Everybody Knows (Spanish: Todos lo saben) is a 2018 Spanish-language mystery drama written and directed by the Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi. Penélope Cruz plays Laura, Javier Bardem her old friend Paco and Ricardo Darín her husband Alejandro, with Bárbara Lennie as Paco's wife Bea and Inma Cuesta as Laura's younger sister Ana. It opened the 2018 Cannes Film Festival in competition.

Laura, a Spanish woman living in Buenos Aires, returns with her teenage daughter Irene and young son Diego to her hometown near Madrid for Ana's wedding. In the town square she reunites with Paco, now a vineyard owner, while Irene flirts with a local boy. After the reception Irene goes upstairs feeling unwell, and later that night Laura finds her gone. A text message demands €300,000 and warns the family not to involve the police. As the family scrambles for the money, old resentments surface: some relatives believe Paco owes them because Laura sold him the land for his vineyard cheaply, though he was the son of the family's servants. A retired police officer advises the family privately and suggests that even relatives should be suspects.

Alejandro, a recovering alcoholic facing bankruptcy, arrives from Argentina to a cold welcome. Bea reveals that she has received the same ransom messages, and Laura confesses to Paco that Irene is his biological daughter, conceived sixteen years earlier. Despite Bea's anger and suspicion, Paco sets out to raise the ransom by selling his land, while Alejandro discovers that everyone in town already knows the truth about Irene's father. The kidnapping was arranged by Laura's niece Rocío, her estranged husband Gabriel and an accomplice, and as the plan spins out of control Rocío begs them to let Irene go. Paco delivers the money and finds Irene tied up in his car. He brings her back to her parents but returns home to find that Bea has left him. As Laura's family leave for Argentina, Rocío's suspicious mother Mariana tells her husband that they need to talk.

Everybody Knows was released in Spain in September 2018 and in the United States in February 2019, distributed internationally by Focus Features. Reviews were generally positive, with a 78% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, though its consensus called it less than the sum of its parts despite an outstanding cast.

title: Fahrenheit 451
tagline: Knowledge is a dangerous thing
overview: In an oppressive future, a 'fireman' whose duty is to destroy all books begins to question his task.
plot:
Fahrenheit 451 is a dystopian drama film directed by Ramin Bahrani, based on the novel of the same name by Ray Bradbury. The movie was released in 2018 and stars Michael B. Jordan, Michael Shannon, and Sophie Nélisse.

The main themes of Fahrenheit 451 (2018) include:

1. **Censorship and Book Burning**: The film explores the dangers of censorship and the suppression of knowledge. In a future society where books are banned and critical thinking is discouraged, the protagonist Guy Montag (played by Michael B. Jordan) begins to question the authority and eventually becomes an outlaw for his love of reading and learning.
2. **Conformity and Individuality**: The movie highlights the tension between conformity and individuality in a society that values sameness above all else. Montag's journey is a quest for self-discovery and autonomy, as he rejects the societal norms that have been imposed upon him.
3. **The Power of Knowledge and Literature**: Fahrenheit 451 celebrates the importance of knowledge, literature, and critical thinking. The film shows how these values can be used to challenge authority and bring about change.
4. **Dystopian Society and Totalitarianism**: The movie depicts a dystopian society where the government exercises total control over its citizens. This theme serves as a warning about the dangers of totalitarianism and the erosion of individual freedoms.
5. **Love and Human Connection**: Throughout the film, Montag's relationships with his wife Mildred (played by Sophie Nélisse) and his new friend Clarisse McClellan (played by Emma Stone) serve as a reminder of the importance of human connection and love in a world that values technology and conformity above all else.

Overall, Fahrenheit 451 (2018) is a thought-provoking film that explores the dangers of censorship, conformity, and totalitarianism, while celebrating the power of knowledge, literature, and individuality.

title: Red Sparrow
tagline: Seduce. Deceive. Repeat.
overview: Prima ballerina, Dominika Egorova faces a bleak and uncertain future after she suffers an injury that ends her career. She soon turns to Sparrow School, a secret intelligence service that trains exceptional young people to use their minds and bodies as weapons. Dominika emerges as the most dangerous Sparrow after completing the sadistic training process. plot:
Red Sparrow is a 2018 spy thriller film directed by Francis Lawrence, based on the 2013 novel of the same name by Jason Matthews. The movie stars Jennifer Lawrence as Dominika Egorova, a Russian ballerina turned CIA operative.

The story begins with Dominika (Jennifer Lawrence) performing at the Bolshoi Ballet in Moscow. She is a talented and beautiful dancer, but her life takes a dramatic turn when she is approached by her uncle, Pavlov (Matthias Schoenaerts), who works for the Russian intelligence agency SVR. Pavlov reveals that he has been watching Dominika's performances and believes she has the potential to become a spy.

Dominika is recruited by Pavlov and undergoes rigorous training, learning how to use her charm and beauty to manipulate men and gather information. She becomes a skilled operative, using her talents to infiltrate the CIA's Moscow station and gather intelligence on their operations.

Meanwhile, Nate Nash (Joe Alwyn), a CIA officer, is tasked with recruiting Dominika as a double agent. He believes that she can provide valuable insight into Russian espionage methods and help the CIA stay one step ahead of their enemies.

As Dominika navigates her new role, she must balance her loyalty to Pavlov and the SVR with her growing feelings for Nate. However, her allegiances are tested when she is sent on a mission to infiltrate a high-stakes poker game in Macau, where she encounters a wealthy businessman named Konstantin (Tom Wlaschiha).

Dominika's mission becomes complicated when she discovers that Konstantin is involved in a plot to sell nuclear technology to the highest bidder. She must use her skills and resources to gather evidence and prevent the sale from happening.

As the story unfolds, Dominika finds herself caught between her loyalty to Pavlov and Nate, as well as her own moral code. She must make difficult choices and confront the consequences of her actions in order to protect herself and those she cares about.

The film's climax features a tense showdown between Dominika and Konstantin, with Nate and his team trying to prevent the sale from happening. In the end, Dominika emerges victorious, but not without scars. She has been forced to confront the harsh realities of her profession and make difficult choices in order to survive.

Throughout the film, Jennifer Lawrence delivers a powerful performance as Dominika, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Matthias Schoenaerts and Joe Alwyn, also deliver strong performances that add to the film's tension and suspense.

Overall, Red Sparrow is a gripping spy thriller that explores the complexities of loyalty, morality, and identity. With its talented cast and intricate plot, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: Ben 10 Generator Rex Heroes United
tagline: Two Heroes. One Epic Battle.
overview: Ben Tennyson falls through a wormhole and encounters Rex. The two heroes must unite against a foe that can absorb their powers.
plot:
Ben 10/Generator Rex: Heroes United is an animated crossover special uniting Ben 10: Ultimate Alien and Generator Rex, written by Man of Action, the creative team behind both series. Structured as a double-length episode of Generator Rex, covering the third and fourth episodes of its third season, it brings Ben Tennyson into Rex's universe and redraws him and his alien forms in that show's art style. It premiered at New York Comic Con 2011 before airing in a one-hour slot on Cartoon Network on November 25, 2011, the network's second crossover special after 2007's The Grim Adventures of the KND.

A mysterious rift opens over Manhattan, and Rex Salazar, a former agent of the peacekeeping organization Providence, arrives with Agent Six and Bobo. Something comes through: Ben, transformed into Humungousaur. Mistaking him for an EVO, a human mutated by rogue nanites, Rex fights him across the city as Ben shifts into Diamondhead, Lodestar and Rath, while a strange metallic creature that also emerged from the rift slips away. Back in human form, Ben is stunned that nobody knows him. The creature self-destructs in front of Six, leaving him in a coma, and Rex blames Ben. Doctor Holiday finds the creature was nanite-based but unlike any EVO. Ben escapes confinement as Big Chill, and he and Rex meet Caesar, who admits he created the creature, Alpha, to manufacture adaptable nanites, then banished it to another dimension after it became sentient and began seizing human bodies. Ben realizes Caesar sent it into the Null Void, the alien prison where it took a cyborg body before returning.

Alpha now aims to absorb EVOs and capture Rex's Omega Nanite, the key to its perfection. At the Bug Jar, a quarantined city of EVOs, Ben fights as XLR8, Four Arms and the new Shocksquatch, but Alpha copies the Ultimatrix and takes Rex's Omega Nanite, becoming the giant Alpha-Omega. Ben merges with Rex as Upgrade and together they compress Alpha into a dense sphere. Caesar recovers the Omega Nanite and opens a rift home for Ben, who, as Upchuck, swallows the compacted Alpha before leaving. Six recovers, Caesar restores Rex's nanite, and Alpha stirs in the Null Void, hinting at a return.

Daryl Sabara voices Rex, with Yuri Lowenthal as Ben, Wally Kurth as Six, Grey DeLisle as Holiday, John DiMaggio as Bobo, J. K. Simmons as White Knight, Michael Emerson as Alpha and Freddy Rodriguez as Caesar. Fans of both series embraced the special, which reached the iTunes top 100.

title: Denial
tagline: The whole world knows the Holocaust happened. Now she needs to prove it.
overview: Acclaimed writer and historian Deborah E. Lipstadt must battle for historical truth to prove the Holocaust actually occurred when David Irving, a renowned denier, sues her for libel.
plot:
Denial is a 2016 biographical drama film directed by Mick Jackson and written by David Hare, adapted from Deborah Lipstadt's 2005 book History on Trial: My Day in Court with a Holocaust Denier. It dramatizes Irving v Penguin Books Ltd, the libel case brought against Lipstadt by the Holocaust denier David Irving. Rachel Weisz stars as Lipstadt, with Timothy Spall as Irving, Tom Wilkinson as the barrister Richard Rampton, Andrew Scott as the solicitor Anthony Julius, Alex Jennings as Justice Charles Gray and Mark Gatiss as the historian Robert Jan van Pelt, with Jack Lowden and Caren Pistorius.

Lipstadt, an American professor of Holocaust studies, has a lecture disrupted by Irving, a British writer on Nazi Germany, who sues her and her publisher for libel in England over her description of him as a Holocaust denier. Because English libel law puts the burden of proof on the defendant, Lipstadt's team, headed by Julius and Rampton, must show that Irving deliberately lied about the Holocaust. Preparing the defense, Lipstadt and Rampton visit the site of Auschwitz, where van Pelt explains how the gas chambers operated. Lipstadt bristles at Rampton's seemingly irreverent manner, and her lawyers sideline her, believing her involvement would hurt the case, while British Jewish leaders urge her to settle. The team scores an early success by flattering Irving into accepting a trial before a judge rather than a jury he might sway. Representing himself, Irving tries to twist the evidence, and his claim that the gas chamber roofs had no holes for introducing Zyklon B ("no holes, no Holocaust") dominates the press. Lipstadt wants survivors to testify, but Julius fears Irving would humiliate them. Rampton wins her trust, then dismantles Irving in cross-examination, while historians such as Richard J. Evans expose the distortions in his work. At the close, Gray unsettles the defense by asking whether Irving can be lying if he sincerely believes his claims, but Rampton argues that Irving's antisemitism proves his falsifications were deliberate. Gray finds for the defense, and her lawyers remind her that her writing was the basis of the victory. Irving later claims on television that the trial largely went his way.

Shot in London and at the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum, Denial premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 11 September 2016. It received positive reviews, with an 82% Rotten Tomatoes rating that particularly praised Weisz's performance.

title: Hard Target 2
tagline: It's hunting season again...
overview: Forced into a deadly cat-and-mouse game, a disgraced mixed martial arts fighter is hunted through the jungles of Southeast Asia.
plot:
Hard Target 2 is a 2016 American action film directed by Roel Reiné, starring Scott Adkins with Robert Knepper, Temuera Morrison, Rhona Mitra and Ann Truong. Billed as a follow-up to the 1993 film Hard Target, in which Jean-Claude Van Damme played a drifter battling a human hunting operation in New Orleans, it has no narrative connection to the original and reworks its premise of people hunted for sport in a new setting.

Professional mixed martial arts fighter Wes Baylor faces Jonny Sutherland for a welterweight championship in Las Vegas. Angry at the judges' scoring, Baylor tries for a knockout and accidentally kills Sutherland in the ring. Consumed by guilt, he goes into self-imposed exile in Thailand. Six months later, he is still haunted by the tragedy and scraping by in underground fights when he attracts the attention of Jonah Aldrich, a wealthy man who offers him $1 million for a private bout in Myanmar.

On arrival, Baylor learns that there is no fight: he is to be the prey in a lethal hunt organized by Aldrich for a group of rich clients. He is given a water bottle and a money belt that secretly contains a GPS tracker. The hunters include Sofia, a bullfighter named Esparto, a video game designer, a sharpshooter, a Texan and his son Tobias, and Aldrich's right-hand man Madden, supported by a unit of corrupt soldiers. Baylor kills his first pursuer at a waterfall and then meets Tha, a local woman who agrees to guide him to the border. As Aldrich escalates the hunt with armed motorcycles and rocket launchers, Baylor and Tha fight back, picking off hunters one by one. They make their way through a minefield, where an explosion buys them time to hide in a cave in which Tha finds her missing brother, an earlier target of Aldrich's game who had managed to survive in hiding. Baylor then turns the tables on the remaining hunters for a final confrontation with Aldrich, finding a measure of redemption along the way.

The film was released direct to video in 2016. Reviewers frequently noted that it could not match the original, which had been made with a much larger budget by the acclaimed director John Woo, but many judged it a respectable addition to Adkins's catalogue. Critics at HighDef Digest and MMA Torch were particularly enthusiastic, praising the fight scenes, Reiné's slick visuals and the cast of villains surrounding Adkins's sympathetic hero.

title: Edge of Winter
tagline: Nothing is more dangerous than a father's love.
overview: When two brothers are stranded by a brutal winter storm with an unpredictable father they barely know, the boys begin to suspect their supposed protector may be their biggest threat.
plot:
Edge of Winter is a 2016 Canadian psychological thriller drama film directed and written by Rob Connolly and Kyle Mann. Joel Kinnaman stars as Elliot Baker, a recently divorced father whose anger gradually takes control of him while he is stranded with his two sons in the wilderness, with Tom Holland as his teenage son Bradley and Percy Hynes White as his younger son Caleb. Rossif Sutherland and Shiloh Fernandez play Luc and Richard, two hunters, and Rachelle Lefevre plays Karen. The film was produced by Kyle Mann and Jonathan Bronfman and shot in and around Sudbury, Ontario.

Elliot, who has just been fired for punching his boss, eagerly seizes a chance to spend time with his sons, Bradley and Caleb, when their mother drops them off for a visit. When the boys find his shotgun, he decides to turn the discovery into a bonding lesson in firearm safety and takes them to his old lumber yard in the snowy wilderness, but the trip is strained from the start; Elliot finds messages on Bradley's phone complaining about spending time with him and hides the phone. On the way home, with Bradley at the wheel because Elliot has been drinking, an argument between the brothers sends the car off the road, where it becomes stuck. During the night in the car, Caleb lets slip that their stepfather has been promoted and the family will soon be moving to London, and Elliot reacts with fury. Facing the risk of freezing or starving if they try to walk to the main road, they make for a hunting cabin, where Elliot rescues Bradley after he falls through the ice. Their uneasy refuge is disturbed when two hunters, Richard and Luc, arrive seeking shelter. Increasingly paranoid and desperate not to lose his sons, Elliot treats the strangers as a threat, and his behavior turns violent, leaving the boys to realize that the greatest danger they face may be their own father as they try to find a way to escape and bring help.

Edge of Winter received mixed reviews, with scores of 50% on both Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter praised Kinnaman's superb performance and the boys' quietly terrified reactions, while finding that the film ultimately succumbed to tired thriller conventions.

title: All Eyez on Me
tagline: Legends never die
overview: All Eyez on Me chronicles the life and legacy of Tupac Shakur, including his rise to superstardom as a hip-hop artist, actor, poet and activist, as well as his imprisonment and prolific, controversial time at Death Row Records. Against insurmountable odds, Tupac rose to become a cultural icon whose career and persona both continue to grow long after his passing.
plot:
All Eyez on Me is a 2017 American biographical drama film directed by Benny Boom, based on the life of rapper Tupac Shakur. The movie explores several themes that are central to Tupac's story and legacy.

One of the main themes of All Eyez on Me is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Tupac's journey from a young boy growing up in poverty-stricken East Harlem to becoming one of the most influential figures in hip-hop culture is marked by his search for purpose and meaning. The film delves into his experiences as a teenager, his involvement with the Black Panther Party, and his rise to fame, highlighting the challenges he faced in navigating his identity as a black man in America.

Another significant theme is the impact of violence and trauma on individuals and communities. Tupac's life was marked by numerous violent incidents, including the shooting that left him paralyzed from the waist down. The film portrays the emotional toll these experiences took on him, as well as the devastating effects they had on his loved ones. This theme serves as a commentary on the cyclical nature of violence in urban communities and the need for healing and redemption.

The movie also explores Tupac's passion for social justice and activism. His music often addressed issues like police brutality, racism, and poverty, inspiring a generation of young people to take action. Through his lyrics and public statements, Tupac advocated for human rights and equality, leaving a lasting legacy that continues to inspire social change.

Furthermore, All Eyez on Me touches on the theme of fame and its consequences. As Tupac's star rises, he becomes increasingly consumed by the pressures of fame, including the scrutiny of the media and the expectations of his fans. The film shows how these pressures can both elevate and destroy an individual, highlighting the tension between artistic expression and commercial success.

Lastly, the movie explores Tupac's complex relationships with those around him, particularly his family and friends. His bond with his mother, Afeni Shakur, is a central theme, as she struggles to provide for her children while also advocating for their rights. The film also portrays Tupac's friendships with Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre, and other influential figures in the hip-hop world.

Overall, All Eyez on Me offers a nuanced portrayal of Tupac Shakur's life, exploring themes that continue to resonate with audiences today.

At its core, the movie is a scathing critique of totalitarianism, exploring the themes of power, corruption, and the dangers of unchecked ambition. As the characters navigate the treacherous landscape of Stalin's death, they reveal their true selves, showcasing the depths of human depravity and the lengths to which people will go to achieve power.

The film also touches on the theme of identity, as the characters struggle to define themselves in a world where loyalty is a luxury few can afford. The movie's use of satire and absurdity serves to highlight the absurdity of the situation, making it difficult for the viewer not to laugh at the sheer audacity of these characters.

Furthermore, The Death of Stalin explores the theme of mortality, as the characters confront their own mortality and the fragility of life. This is particularly evident in the character of Nikita Khrushchev, who must navigate the treacherous waters of Stalin's death to emerge as a viable successor.

Overall, The Death of Stalin is a masterful exploration of the human condition, offering a darkly comedic commentary on the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals.

title: Ocean's Eight
tagline: The plan is priceless.
overview: Debbie Ocean, a criminal mastermind, gathers a crew of female thieves to pull off the heist of the century at New York's annual Met Gala.
plot:
Ocean's Eight is a heist comedy-drama film released in 2018, directed by Gary Ross and written by Olivia Milch. The movie serves as a spin-off to the Ocean's franchise, with Sandra Bullock taking on the lead role of Debbie Ocean, the sister of Danny Ocean (played by George Clooney in the previous films).

The story begins with Debbie Ocean, who has just been released from prison after serving time for a crime she didn't commit. She sets out to plan and execute a massive heist at the Met Gala, one of the most prestigious events in New York City's social calendar.

Debbie assembles a team of eight women, each with their unique skills and expertise: Cate Blanchett as Lou, the tough-as-nails ex-con; Anne Hathaway as Daphne, a talented thief; Mindy Kaling as Amita, an expert hacker; Sarah Paulson as Tammy, a skilled pickpocket; Awkwafina as Constance, a street-smart thief; Rihanna as Nine Ball, a charismatic and deadly thief; Helena Bonham Carter as Rose, a quirky and artistic forger; and Richard Armitage as Claude Becker, the wealthy businessman who has hired Debbie to pull off the heist.

As the team prepares for the Met Gala, they must navigate their personal demons and learn to work together in order to succeed. Along the way, they discover that Claude's true intentions are not what they seem, and that the heist is just a cover for something much more sinister.

A Hidden Life is a 2019 biographical drama film directed by Terrence Malick, starring August Diehl as Franz Jägerstätter, an Austrian conscientious objector who refused to fight for Nazi Germany during World War II.

1. **Conscience vs. State**: The film explores the conflict between individual conscience and the state's demands. Franz Jägerstätter's refusal to fight for the Nazis is a powerful statement against the ideology of the Third Reich, highlighting the tension between personal conviction and societal pressure.
2. **Faith and Spirituality**: The movie delves into Franz's Catholic faith and its role in shaping his moral compass. His spiritual beliefs serve as a source of strength and guidance throughout his struggles with the Nazi regime.
3. **Sacrifice and Martyrdom**: A Hidden Life portrays Franz's ultimate sacrifice, where he chooses to die rather than betray his principles. This act of martyrdom serves as a testament to the power of conviction and the human spirit's capacity for selflessness.
4. **The Human Cost of War**: The film sheds light on the personal costs of war, highlighting the emotional toll it takes on individuals and their families. Franz's story is a poignant reminder of the human cost of conflict and the importance of empathy in understanding the experiences of those affected by war.
5. **Redemption and Forgiveness**: Through Franz's story, the film explores the themes of redemption and forgiveness. Despite his tragic fate, Franz's actions are seen as a form of redemption, and his legacy serves as a reminder to forgive and understand those who have been wronged.

Overall, A Hidden Life is a powerful exploration of the human condition, highlighting the complexities of conscience, faith, and sacrifice in the face of adversity.

title: 1898: Our Last Men in the Philippines
tagline: There are men who want medals and men who want to come back.
overview: The Philippines, 1898. Fifty Spanish soldiers arrive in the small village of Baler to rebuild an outpost. Although the war against the Filipinos and their American allies is almost lost, as is the Spanish Empire, the garrison will endure a cruel siege for eleven months. They will be the last to surrender.
plot:
1898, Our Last Men in the Philippines (Spanish: 1898, Los últimos de Filipinas) is a 2016 Spanish war drama directed by Salvador Calvo. It dramatises the Siege of Baler of 1898 to 1899, in which a Spanish detachment held out for almost a year inside the church of San Luis Obispo de Tolosa against Filipino revolutionaries, unaware that the war had ended. The cast includes Luis Tosar, Javier Gutiérrez, Álvaro Cervantes, Karra Elejalde and Carlos Hipólito. It was released on December 2, 2016.

During the Philippine Revolution, rebels attack the Spanish garrison in the coastal town of Baler and kill most of its soldiers. A detachment of young recruits under Captain Enrique de las Morenas and Lieutenant Martín Cerezo is sent from Manila to reoccupy the town. They are welcomed by the parish priest, Brother Carmelo. Among the recruits is Carlos, a sensitive young man who dreams of studying art, and who begins to share the priest's opium.

News arrives that the United States has declared war on Spain and destroyed its fleet, cutting the garrison off from supplies. When the revolutionaries attack, the soldiers barricade themselves in the church. Months pass under siege as beriberi, caused by poor rations, kills many of them, including de las Morenas and Brother Carmelo, leaving the rigid Cerezo in command. One recruit deserts to the enemy and urges his comrades to give up a lost cause, and offers of peace, including newspapers reporting Spain's defeat, are dismissed by Cerezo as tricks.

The men grow desperate, and violence and paranoia spread. Carlos, suffering from withdrawal after his opium is discovered, is locked up. Even when a Spanish officer arrives with orders to surrender, Cerezo refuses to believe that Spain has lost its colonies. Carlos goes out to verify the news and learns from the Filipino commander that Spain has ceded the islands to the Americans, but Cerezo still holds out, and deserters are brutally punished.

Only when Cerezo reads a minor item in a newspaper about the posting of a friend, a detail no enemy could have invented, does he accept the truth. The garrison surrenders in June 1899, and the Filipino forces, impressed by their resistance, allow the survivors to leave with honour rather than as prisoners. Carlos, disillusioned, discards his drawings as the men depart.

The film was shortlisted as Spain's possible Academy Award submission. The Hollywood Reporter called it spectacular and striking, if not subtle.

title: A Street Cat Named Bob
tagline: Sometimes it takes nine lives to save one
overview: James Bowen, a homeless busker and recovering drug addict, has his life transformed when he meets a stray ginger cat.
plot:
A Street Cat Named Bob is a 2016 British biographical drama directed by Roger Spottiswoode and written by Tim John and Maria Nation, based on James Bowen's memoirs A Street Cat Named Bob and The World According to Bob. Luke Treadaway stars as Bowen, with Ruta Gedmintas, Joanne Froggatt and Anthony Head, while Bob the cat plays himself in most scenes. The title is a play on A Streetcar Named Desire. The film premiered in London on 3 November 2016 and went on general release the following day.

James Bowen is a homeless former heroin addict busking on the streets of London and struggling to survive. After a near-fatal overdose, his support worker Val finds him a council flat and puts him on a methadone programme in the hope of getting him off the streets for good. On his first night in the flat, James discovers a ginger cat raiding his food. He assumes the cat belongs to someone nearby and tries to send him home, but the cat returns, this time with an infected wound on his leg. James's neighbour Betty, an animal lover, tells him about a charity veterinary clinic where she volunteers, and gives the cat the name Bob.

James spends what little money he has on Bob's treatment and then lets him go, but Bob refuses to leave and follows him onto the bus and into central London. The sight of a busker with a cat perched on his shoulders draws crowds, and James begins to earn more money than ever before, eventually becoming a well-known figure in the area and selling The Big Issue magazine. His friendship with Betty grows, and caring for Bob gives him the motivation to stay clean. But his path to recovery is not easy: he faces hostility from other vendors, trouble with authorities, the temptation of his old life and a painful attempt to reconcile with his estranged father, and he must undergo the ordeal of withdrawal from methadone to finally free himself from addiction.

The film was a success in the United Kingdom and won Best British Film at the National Film Awards UK in 2017. Critics praised Treadaway's performance and Bob's natural screen presence, though some found it sentimental. A Christmas sequel, A Gift from Bob, was released in 2020, after the real Bob had died earlier that year.

title: Don't Kill It
overview: Demon hunter, Jebediah Huntley teams up with an FBI agent to battle a supernatural force in the southern state of Mississippi.
plot:
Don't Kill It is a 2016 American comedy horror film directed and edited by Mike Mendez from a screenplay by Dan Berk and Robert Olsen. Dolph Lundgren stars as Jebediah Woodley, an eccentric demon hunter who travels to a small Mississippi town to destroy an ancient, murderous demon. Kristina Klebe, Tony Bentley, James Chalke, Billy Slaughter and Miles Doleac appear in supporting roles. The script was originally set in Alaska, but filming was moved to Mississippi for financial reasons, and the film was made for less than $1 million, part of it raised through crowdfunding on Indiegogo.

While hunting deer in southern Mississippi, a man named Gabriel follows his dog to a small golden box, which the dog opens. The animal begins to act strangely and attacks Gabriel, who is forced to shoot it. Gabriel returns home with the same black eyes and erratic behavior, murders his family and then begins killing his neighbors until he is shot dead by a neighbor named Marcus, who immediately develops black eyes himself and carries on the slaughter. The demon, it turns out, passes into whoever kills its current host.

Days later, Jebediah Woodley, a weathered demon hunter who has spent decades tracking this particular entity, hears about the killings on the radio and comes to town. At the same time, FBI agent Evelyn Pierce, who grew up in the area, has been sent to investigate the massacres as a possible case of domestic terrorism. Pierce and the local police chief dismiss Woodley's talk of demons and have him detained, but when the killings continue, Pierce is forced to accept that he is right. Woodley explains that the demon cannot simply be killed, since its killer becomes the next host, and that it must be trapped instead. As panic spreads and the townspeople start to turn on one another, Woodley and Pierce try to stop the demon without letting anyone kill it, a task that becomes increasingly difficult as it jumps from body to body.

The film played on the genre festival circuit before its release and was generally well received by horror critics, who enjoyed its sense of humor, its gory effects and Lundgren's relaxed, self-mocking turn as the gruff hunter.

title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
original_title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
overview: Just one enchanted jewel stands between earth and an army of evil spirits led by the devious ghoul, Phears. With the help of his new girlfriend and ghost pals, Max Doyle races to find the crystal and save the world.
plot:
Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House, released as R.L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly: One Night in Doom House, is a 2016 American family fantasy horror comedy written and directed by Ron Oliver. It is the third feature film based on R. L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly book series, following Mostly Ghostly: Who Let the Ghosts Out? (2008) and Mostly Ghostly: Have You Met My Ghoulfriend? (2014), and was made by Universal 1440 Entertainment. To keep the characters at the same ages, the main roles were recast: Corey Fogelmanis plays Max Doyle, with Sophie Reynolds as Cammie, Blake Michael and Olivia Ryan Stern as the ghosts Nicky and Tara, Adam Tsekhman as Phears, Danny Trejo as Mr. Morgo and Jamie Kennedy as a television ghost hunter. Morgan Fairchild also appears.

Max is a teenage stage magician who shares his home with Nicky and Tara, two young ghosts who are counting on him to help them find their missing parents. To raise money for his girlfriend Cammie's school dance crew, he stages a public séance. The ghosts supply genuine spectral effects, but everyone assumes they are Max's tricks, and when the ghost of a French maid interrupts the show with information about Nicky and Tara's parents, the evening ends in embarrassment and Cammie breaks up with him. At the same time, his ghost friends complain that he treats them more like pets than friends.

Max turns for help to Simon Drake, the self-obsessed host of a ghost-hunting television show who is filming an episode in town, only to discover that he is a fraud. The evil ghost Phears, working with the sinister Mr. Morgo, takes possession of Drake as part of a new attempt to release an army of evil spirits on the world and plunge it into darkness. The key is a dark crystal that turns up in Max's house, which Max has tried to use to win Cammie back. Hampered by fame, family squabbles, a rich rival for Cammie's affections and an anxious dance choreographer, Max has to recover the jewel and rescue Nicky and Tara before Phears succeeds, in a showdown at a derelict mansion, the Doom House of the title.

The film was released directly on DVD, digital download and on demand on 6 September 2016. Common Sense Media described it as a low-budget, harmless fright-fest with nonstop action and over-the-top villains, enlivened by Kennedy's send-up of a reality television star, but lacking in depth.

As Elise delves deeper into the mystery, she realizes that The Key is connected to her own traumatic experiences and that it has been manipulating her sister's visions in an attempt to lure her back to the asylum. Elise must use her skills and knowledge of the spirit world to defeat The Key and free Sally from its grasp.

Throughout the movie, Elise faces numerous challenges and obstacles as she navigates the treacherous world of spirits and demons. She is aided by Specs and Tucker, who provide comedic relief and technical support throughout the investigation.

Ultimately, Elise emerges victorious, but not without scars. She realizes that her experiences have left her with emotional baggage and that she must find a way to heal and move forward. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, as Elise begins to rebuild her life and reconnect with her sister.

The movie takes a thrilling turn as Sam Bell and J.T. O'Grady embark on a perilous journey to prevent the asteroid from colliding with Earth. Along the way, they encounter numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning equipment, and personal demons.

Throughout the film, Emmerich's signature style of explosive action sequences and heart-pumping suspense is on full display. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Sam and J.T., as they work together to prevent the asteroid from destroying Earth.

While "Moonfall" received mixed reviews from critics, it has its fans who appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and thrilling plot twists. However, some viewers may find the pacing a bit uneven and the scientific explanations lacking in depth.

title: Better Watch Out
tagline: You might be home but you're not alone
overview: On a quiet suburban street tucked within a 'safe neighborhood', a babysitter must defend a twelve-year-old boy from strangers breaking into the house, only to discover that this is far from a normal home invasion.
plot:
Better Watch Out, originally titled Safe Neighborhood, is a 2016 Christmas psychological horror film directed by Chris Peckover, who co-wrote the script with Zack Kahn. It stars Olivia DeJonge as the babysitter Ashley, Levi Miller as twelve-year-old Luke Lerner, Ed Oxenbould as Luke's friend Garrett, Aleks Mikic as Ashley's boyfriend Ricky, Dacre Montgomery as her ex-boyfriend Jeremy, and Patrick Warburton and Virginia Madsen as Luke's parents, Robert and Deandra Lerner.

At Christmas, seventeen-year-old Ashley babysits Luke, a precocious boy with a crush on her, who tries and fails to seduce her as they watch a horror film. Strange noises outside unnerve her, but they seem to come from Luke's best friend Garrett, who drops by. When a brick reading "U leave and U die" smashes through an upstairs window, Garrett panics, runs out the back and appears to be shot dead. Ashley and Luke hide, first in the attic, where he saves her from a dangerous fall, and then in his closet, as a masked figure with a shotgun enters. Recognizing the mask as Luke's, Ashley demands that the intruder remove it, revealing Garrett, and she realizes that Luke staged the attack to frighten her so he could play the hero. When she scolds him, Luke knocks her out. He ties her up with duct tape and makes her play truth or dare, and Ricky, lured by a text that Luke sent from her phone, arrives and senses something wrong. With Garrett holding him at gunpoint, Ricky is subdued and tied up next to Ashley. As Ashley cuts herself free with a piece of glass, Luke kills Ricky by dropping a paint can on him. She points the gun at Luke, but it is unloaded, and as she tries to reach carolers outside, Luke knocks her out again with the brick. Luke then gets Jeremy to write Ashley an apology note and hangs him from a tree, making the letter look like a suicide note. When a remorseful Garrett starts to free Ashley, Luke kills him, then stabs Ashley in the neck and arranges the scene to frame Jeremy before going to bed to await his parents, who call the police. Ashley, however, survives, having sealed her wound with duct tape, and she gives Luke the finger from her stretcher as he watches from his window.

Shot in Sydney in early 2016 on a $3 million budget, the film premiered at Fantastic Fest on 22 September 2016 and was released in the United States on 6 October 2017. Critics responded positively, giving it an 89% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praising the young cast, though it grossed only $188,756.
