title: Our House
tagline: The dead are sending you a signal
overview: Ethan is suffering enormous guilt after his parents are killed in a car accident. He quits a promising future at MIT and work on a revolutionary experiment in order to care for his younger siblings.
plot:
Our House is a 2018 supernatural horror film directed by Anthony Scott Burns from a screenplay by Nathan Parker. A remake of Matt Osterman's 2010 film Ghost from the Machine, it stars Thomas Mann as a young inventor, with Nicola Peltz, Kate Moyer and Percy Hynes White. It was released in the United States and Canada on July 27, 2018, by IFC Midnight and Elevation Pictures.

Ethan, a gifted college student, visits his parents and younger siblings, Matt and Becca, but leaves early to work on his invention. His project, a machine designed to transmit electricity wirelessly, lacks university approval, so he sneaks into a campus lab with his girlfriend, Hannah, and a friend to test it. The experiment causes a blackout across the campus. The next morning, Ethan learns that his parents have been killed in a car accident. He returns home to care for his siblings and keeps working on the machine.

When he runs it in the house, strange phenomena begin to occur, and the siblings become convinced that the device is allowing their dead parents to reach out to them. A presence communicates that the machine is drawing on spiritual energy and that more power will let both parents appear. Ethan enlists his neighbor Tom, a grieving widower, to illegally tap into the street's power supply. Becca speaks of a new friend, Alice, who is afraid of a man named Henry, and the activity grows increasingly menacing. An elderly neighbor, Marie, tells Ethan that a girl named Alice vanished from the house years earlier and was believed to have been killed by her foster father, Henry.

Becca is lured into the basement and disappears. Realizing that the spirits are not his parents, Ethan tries to shut the machine off, but discovers that Tom has taken it to contact his late wife, and the two men fight. Meanwhile Matt and Hannah find Becca in a hidden room beneath the house, where they are attacked by hostile ghosts. Ethan persuades Tom that the spirit he hears is not his wife, and the ghost turns on Tom before Ethan smashes the machine, ending the haunting and saving his family. As the siblings move to a new home, Becca returns a doll she had left behind to keep Alice company, but the doll is later seen peering out of a packing box.

Critical reception was mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 62% approval, while Metacritic gave it a score of 45.

plot:

The film sheds light on the brutal realities faced by African Americans during this period, including forced labor, segregation, and violence. Through the characters' experiences, the movie highlights the ways in which systemic racism can destroy lives and relationships.

The film also explores themes of family, love, and loyalty, as both families grapple with their own demons and struggles. The white family's patriarch, Henry, is a complex character whose troubled past and sense of entitlement are slowly revealed throughout the story. In contrast, the black family's matriarch, Florence, is a strong and resilient woman who holds her family together despite the hardships they face.

One of the most striking aspects of Mudbound is its portrayal of the interconnectedness of these two families. Despite their differences, both families are bound together by their experiences as farmers in the rural South, and their struggles are deeply intertwined. The film shows how the actions of one family can have far-reaching consequences for another, highlighting the devastating effects of racism on individuals and communities.

Ultimately, Mudbound is a powerful exploration of the human condition, revealing the complexities and nuances of life in the American South during World War II. Through its thought-provoking themes and well-developed characters, the film offers a nuanced and empathetic portrayal of two families struggling to survive and thrive in a society marked by racism and oppression.

title: The Batman

overview: In his second year of fighting crime, Batman uncovers corruption in Gotham City that connects to his own family while facing a serial killer known as the Riddler.
plot:
The Batman is a 2022 superhero thriller film directed by Matt Reeves, starring Robert Pattinson as the titular character. The movie takes place in Gotham City, where a series of brutal murders has taken place, targeting young women.

The story begins with Bruce Wayne (Pattinson), now an older and more brooding individual, still grieving the loss of his parents. He is haunted by the trauma of his childhood and struggles to connect with others. However, when he witnesses one of the victims being attacked, he becomes determined to track down the killer.

As Bruce delves deeper into the case, he discovers that the murders are all connected to a larger conspiracy involving the Riddler (Paul Dano), a serial killer who is using his intelligence and cunning to taunt the police. The Riddler's true identity is revealed to be Edward Nashton, a former student of Bruce's at the Gotham City Academy.

As the investigation unfolds, Bruce becomes increasingly obsessed with catching the Riddler, often putting himself in harm's way. He also begins to question his own morality and whether he is truly making a difference as a vigilante. Meanwhile, Selina Kyle (Zoë Kravitz), a cat burglar, becomes entangled in Bruce's investigation, and they develop a complicated relationship.

Throughout the film, Matt Reeves explores themes of trauma, grief, and redemption, delving into Bruce's psyche to understand what drives him as a hero. The movie also features a standout performance from Jeffrey Wright as James Gordon, the Commissioner of Gotham City Police Department, who is struggling to maintain order in the city.

The Batman received widespread critical acclaim for its dark and atmospheric tone, as well as Pattinson's performance as the iconic character. The film's success has paved the way for future DC Comics adaptations, with Reeves set to direct a sequel.

Overall, The Batman is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of Bruce Wayne's psyche and his role as a hero in Gotham City.

title: Ravenous
overview: In an isolated rural community of Quebec, Canada, some inhabitants attack other people, hungry for human flesh. A few survivors gather and go deep into the forest to escape them.
plot:
Ravenous (French: Les Affamés) is a 2017 French-language Canadian horror film written and directed by Robin Aubert. The cast includes Marc-André Grondin, Monia Chokri, Brigitte Poupart, Luc Proulx, Charlotte St-Martin, Micheline Lanctôt and Marie-Ginette Guay. Set in rural Quebec, the film follows a handful of ordinary people struggling to survive after an outbreak turns most of the population into ravenous, zombie-like creatures, and it uses the genre to explore loneliness, grief and community.

Following the outbreak, the countryside has been emptied of most of its inhabitants. Bonin and his friend Vézina patrol the area with shotguns, killing infected and passing the time telling each other jokes, until Vézina is drawn into the forest and attacked. Elsewhere, Céline, a wife and mother who has lost her family, roams alone, fighting off the infected with a machete. She arrives at the farm of Thérèse and Pauline, two armed elderly women who check her for bites before taking her in.

Bonin meets Tania, a young woman bitten on the arm who insists the wound came from a dog, and he frees her and flees with her when the infected attack. Along the way they take in Zoé, a silent little girl. Bonin notices that the infected behave strangely: rather than simply hunting, they gather in fields around towers of household objects they have piled up, standing motionless as if taking part in a ritual. The survivors join up with the women at the farm, but the house lies in the path of the advancing horde, and they are forced to flee. They are joined by Réal, a retired insurance agent, and Ti-Cul, a boy armed with a rifle. As the group moves through forests and abandoned farms, they must decide whom they can trust, and the losses they suffer reveal how fragile their makeshift community is.

Ravenous received positive reviews, holding an 89 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. T'cha Dunlevy of the Montreal Gazette praised it as a successful reinvention of the zombie genre that was funny, philosophical, frightening and boldly cinematic, and Robert Everett-Green of The Globe and Mail read it as an allegory. It won the Toronto International Film Festival award for Best Canadian Film and was nominated for five Canadian Screen Awards, including Best Motion Picture, winning for Best Make-Up.

title: Operation Mekong

title: Barbie: Star Light Adventure
overview: Barbie is a cosmic princess who flies high on her hoverboard through a far-off universe with her adorable and devoted pet sidekick, Pupcorn. One day, everything changes when the twinkling stars start to dim and slow their dance in the sky. Barbie travels to a beautiful new planet to join a special rescue team on a mission to save the stars. Once there, she teams up with a group of talented new friends who work together to save the galaxy through exciting hoverboarding adventures. Barbie soon discovers that if she listens to her heart, and with the help of her friends, she might be the leader the whole universe has been waiting for!
plot:
Barbie: Star Light Adventure is a 2016 computer-animated children's adventure film directed by Andrew Tan and written by Kacey Arnold, with Kate Boutilier assisting on the script. The 33rd entry in the Barbie film series, it was the first produced under Mattel's new Mattel Creations banner and the first to open with the doll brand's message sequence. After a one-day Fathom Events screening, it was released on home video by Universal and later aired on Nickelodeon. Its voice cast includes Erica Lindbeck, Dwight Schultz and Robbie Daymond.

A prophecy foretells that one day the stars will stop their cosmic dance and go dark unless "the One" can make them shine again, and the sky is indeed growing darker. The rigid, orderly King Constantine, convinced despite repeated failures that he is the One, recruits a team of gifted young people for his latest plan. On the wildlife preserve planet of Para-Den, Barbie is an enthusiastic but impulsive hoverboarder who can communicate with animals and objects through telekinesis. Encouraged by her widowed father, she accepts the king's invitation and travels to the Capital Planet.

There she meets her teammates: Sal-Lee, a sarcastic, competitive hoverboarder with super speed; Prince Leo, a shy and awkward but brilliant pilot; and the kindly alien twins Kareena and Sheena, who share a psychic link and can make things lighter or heavier. Barbie's free-spirited ways repeatedly clash with Constantine's insistence on order, and when she persuades the team to release a Starlian creature they were meant to capture, believing he wants it for a zoo, he fires her, explaining that the creature was needed to guide them to the centre of the galaxy. Barbie apologises for misjudging him but not for following her conscience, and uses her powers to ask the Starlian for help. Under pressure from her teammates, Constantine reinstates her as leader.

Guided by the Starlian, the team reaches the galaxy's central planet, where Barbie and her friends clear a path to the core for Constantine and his machine. Ignoring Barbie's advice, he uses the device to force the stars into order, and they go out at once. Sensing that the stars have stopped dancing out of sadness and loneliness, Barbie begins a new dance with them, restoring their light and proving herself the One. Humbled, Constantine takes Barbie and her father in as his wards, and the film ends with Princess Starlight and her friends teaching the king to dance.

The movie's plot development revolves around the events of November 26-27, 2008, when a group of terrorists attacked several locations in Mumbai, including the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, where the story is set. The film follows the hotel staff as they try to evacuate guests, fend off the terrorists, and find a way to escape the hotel.

The ending of the movie is a mix of emotional and intense moments, as the characters face their fears and work together to overcome the odds. Ultimately, the hotel staff manages to save many lives, but not without great personal cost. The film ends on a hopeful note, highlighting the resilience and bravery of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

Overall, Hotel Mumbai is a powerful and emotional movie that explores themes of bravery, survival, terrorism, and human connection.

title: Godard Mon Amour
tagline: This movie is a “stupid, stupid idea.”
overview: In 1967, during the making of “La Chinoise,” film director Jean-Luc Godard falls in love with 19-year-old actress Anne Wiazemsky and marries her.
plot:
Godard Mon Amour, released in France as Le Redoutable (Redoubtable), is a 2017 French biographical comedy-drama written and directed by Michel Hazanavicius, adapted from Un an après, Anne Wiazemsky's 2015 memoir. Louis Garrel plays the filmmaker Jean-Luc Godard and Stacy Martin plays Wiazemsky, while the supporting cast includes Bérénice Bejo (Michèle Rosier), Micha Lescot (Jean-Pierre Bamberger), Grégory Gadebois (Michel Cournot) and Guido Caprino (Bernardo Bertolucci). Structured in nine chapters with an epilogue, the film playfully imitates Godard's own techniques, including black-and-white passages, voice-over, characters addressing the camera, title cards and ironic subtitles.

In Paris in 1967, Godard, the celebrated 37-year-old figurehead of the French New Wave, falls in love with the 20-year-old Anne while directing her in La Chinoise, and asks her to marry him on the day the radio reports news of the submarine Le Redoutable. His growing commitment to Maoism shapes his work, but the film is rejected by the Chinese embassy and poorly received by critics and audiences. A year later the events of May 1968 erupt. Godard joins the often violent street protests, is pestered by fans who want him to return to lighter films such as Breathless and Pierrot le Fou, is shouted down at the occupied Sorbonne and mocked in graffiti, and meets the same scorn at a conference in Rome hosted by Bertolucci. He and friends travel to the Cannes Film Festival, which they help shut down in solidarity with the strikes, and then find themselves stranded without fuel during the general strike.

Back in Paris, Godard founds the Dziga Vertov Group with Jean-Pierre Gorin to make radical political cinema, but he becomes increasingly isolated, accused by others of being incomprehensible. As Anne pursues her own acting career, their marriage deteriorates and Godard attempts suicide with an overdose. Anne falls out of love, and they separate during the collective shoot of Wind from the East, where Godard is confronted with his own contradictions.

Produced by Les Compagnons du Cinéma with Wild Bunch and France 3 Cinéma and photographed by Guillaume Schiffman, the film premiered in competition for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival. Reviews were mixed, with a Rotten Tomatoes approval rating of 54% and a Metacritic score of 55.

title: The Quake
tagline: The Wave Was Only The Beginning
overview: A geologist races against time to save his estranged wife and two children when a devastating earthquake strikes Oslo, Norway.
plot:
The Quake (Norwegian: Skjelvet) is a 2018 Norwegian disaster film directed by John Andreas Andersen and the sequel to the 2015 film The Wave. Kristoffer Joner returns as geologist Kristian Eikjord, with Ane Dahl Torp, Jonas Hoff Oftebro, Edith Haagenrud-Sande and Kathrine Thorborg Johansen in the main cast. It was released in Norwegian cinemas on 31 August 2018.

Three years after he was hailed as a hero for his actions during the Geiranger tsunami, Kristian is a broken man. He blames himself for the 250 people who died, keeps a hidden room devoted to the disaster, and has become estranged from his wife Idun, who is divorcing him, and their children Sondre and Julia, who have moved to Oslo, where Idun works at the Radisson Blu Plaza Hotel. When a fellow geologist, Konrad Lindblom, is killed in a collapse in the Oslofjord Tunnel, Kristian travels to the capital to find out why. Konrad's supervisor, Johannes Løberg, assures him that the tremors Konrad had been monitoring were nothing more than construction blasting, but Kristian, working with Konrad's daughter Marit, finds core samples, maps of alarming seismic activity and video of laboratory rats killed by gas escaping from the ground. Kristian concludes that a massive earthquake, as strong as 8.5 on the Richter scale, is about to strike Oslo. A smaller rift that damages the Oslo Opera House during Julia's ballet recital proves he is right, but no one in authority will listen. As the city goes about its business, Kristian races to warn his family, calling in a fake bomb threat to clear Sondre's university and hurrying to Idun's office high in the hotel tower. The earthquake hits while they are still inside, devastating the city and leaving Kristian, Idun, Julia and Marit fighting to survive in the collapsing skyscraper.

The Quake was well received by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an 85% approval rating based on 40 reviews, with a consensus describing it as a satisfyingly smart action thriller that delivers nail-biting tension without sacrificing character development or common sense, and on Metacritic it has a score of 70 out of 100, indicating "generally favorable reviews".

title: Barbie & Her Sisters in a Puppy Chase
original_title: Barbie & Her Sisters in a Puppy Chase
overview: Barbie and her sisters go to an island paradise for a dance competition, but they must work together as a team to find their pets after their furry friends go missing at a horse festival.
plot:
Barbie & Her Sisters in a Puppy Chase is a 2016 American computer-animated adventure film and the 34th entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Conrad Helten with Michael Goguen from a screenplay by Amy Wolfram and Kacey Arnold, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment, with music by Steven Argila and The Math Club. It was released direct to video in the United States in October 2016 and made its television debut on Nickelodeon that November. Its theme song is "Live in the Moment".

Barbie (Erica Lindbeck) and her sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea fly with their puppies Taffy, DJ, Rookie and Honey to a tropical island, where Chelsea is to compete in a dance competition against her rival, Lindsay. Chelsea wants to go straight to the hotel to rehearse, but Barbie has planned a surprise. With most rental cars taken, the sisters set off in a golf cart, send their luggage ahead and head to Banyan Tree Park for the Dancing Horse Festival, where the trainers Vivian and Marco present the nervous young horse Beauty in her debut. While the girls watch, the puppies explore a horse trailer belonging to a show dog, Archibald, and are unwittingly driven away when the trainers leave.

Trying to follow, Barbie gets the cart stuck in the arch of the great banyan tree, and with no internet signal the sisters must spend the night in the park, passing the time with imagination games and learning of a macaw constellation once used by local fishermen for navigation. The next day, finding the road washed out, they climb a mountain, take a zip-line to a village and rent a camper, only to run out of fuel near the beach campground where the trainers have stopped. Meanwhile the puppies, cared for by Vivian and Marco, enjoy their own adventure, running with the horses and learning to surf.

As her worries mount, Chelsea snaps at Barbie for being relentlessly positive, and Barbie reassures her that doing her best matters more than winning. The sisters are reunited with their pets, and when another washed-out road blocks the way, the horses carry the girls across. Barbie admits that she hid her own worries to seem dependable, and her sisters tell her she can share them. Guided north by the macaw constellation, they reach the competition. The voice cast also includes Kazumi Evans as Skipper, Claire Margaret Corlett as Stacie, Alyssya Swales as Chelsea and Mark Oliver as Archibald.

As the story unfolds, Jake finds himself torn between his feelings for Lucy and his lingering emotions for Gerry. He must confront his past heartbreak and figure out what he truly wants from life. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about love, loss, and finding one's true purpose.

Throughout the movie, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of Nashville's music scene and the charm of Lucy's bookstore. The soundtrack features a mix of original songs and classic country tunes, adding to the film's nostalgic and romantic atmosphere.

In the end, Jake must make a choice between his old life with Gerry and his new life with Lucy. Will he find happiness with the woman who has captured his heart, or will he return to his past and risk losing the love of his life? The movie's ending is bittersweet, leaving audiences to ponder the complexities of love and relationships.

Overall, Forever My Girl is a poignant and romantic drama that explores the ups and downs of love, loss, and self-discovery. Step Brothers is a comedy film released in 2008 by Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of two middle-aged men, Brennan Huff (Will Ferrell) and Dale Doback (John C. Reilly), who become stepbrothers when their parents get married.

Brennan, played by Will Ferrell, is a 39-year-old unemployed slacker who still lives with his mother, Nancy (Mary Steenburgen). He is immature, lazy, and has no direction in life. On the other hand, Dale, played by John C. Reilly, is a 40-year-old terminally unemployed man who lives with his father, Robert (Richard Jenkins).

When their parents get married, Brennan and Dale are forced to live together under one roof, leading to a series of hilarious and chaotic events. Initially, they clash and try to outdo each other in various ways, but eventually, they develop an unlikely bond.

As the story progresses, Brennan and Dale start to take on childish behaviors, such as playing video games, eating junk food, and engaging in juvenile pranks. They also start to compete with each other for attention from their parents, leading to a series of ridiculous and absurd situations.

However, when they discover that they are stepbrothers, they realize that they have more in common than they thought. They bond over their shared immaturity and laziness, and they start to support each other in their attempts to find purpose and direction in life.

As the movie reaches its climax, Brennan and Dale decide to take matters into their own hands and try to become a family unit of their own. They come up with a plan to get jobs, move out of their parents' houses, and start a new life together.

title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
original_title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
tagline: Stories taken from true urban legends
overview: Mill Valley, Pennsylvania, Halloween night, 1968. After playing a joke on a school bully, Stella and her friends decide to sneak into a supposedly haunted house that once belonged to the powerful Bellows family, unleashing dark forces that they will be unable to control.
plot:
Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark is a 2019 supernatural horror film directed by André Øvredal and based on Alvin Schwartz's children's book series. Dan and Kevin Hageman wrote the screenplay from a story by Guillermo del Toro, Patrick Melton and Marcus Dunstan, and del Toro also produced. CBS Films acquired the rights in 2013, del Toro came aboard in 2016 and Øvredal was hired in late 2017. A co-production of the United States, Canada and Mexico, it was shot in Ontario between August and November 2018 and released by Lionsgate on August 9, 2019. Del Toro explained that he avoided an anthology format because such films are only as good as their weakest segment.

On Halloween night in 1968, in the fictional town of Mill Valley, Pennsylvania, teenagers Stella, Auggie and Chuck and the newcomer Ramón explore the supposedly haunted Bellows house. They find a book of horror stories by Sarah Bellows, an outcast girl blamed for the deaths of local children who reportedly killed herself in 1898, and Stella takes it home. New stories begin writing themselves in blood, and each comes true. The bully Tommy is turned into the scarecrow Harold, and Auggie is dragged away by a corpse searching for its missing toe. Chuck's sister Ruth survives a swelling that bursts with spiders but is left traumatized.

Investigating, the friends learn that Sarah actually hanged herself in a hospital where her brother, a doctor, had subjected her to electroshock to make her confess, and that the children had really died because the family's paper mill poisoned the water with mercury. Chuck is absorbed by the Pale Lady, and after Police Chief Turner arrests Stella and Ramón, exposing Ramón as a draft dodger, the Jangly Man kills Turner. Back at the Bellows house, Stella relives Sarah's abuse and promises to tell the truth if she stops the killings, then writes the true story in her own blood, and the monsters vanish. Ramón leaves for Vietnam, while Stella searches for a way to bring Chuck and Auggie back.

The cast includes Zoe Colletti, Michael Garza, Gabriel Rush, Austin Zajur, Natalie Ganzhorn, Austin Abrams, Dean Norris, Gil Bellows and Lorraine Toussaint, with Javier Botet also joining the cast. Reviews were generally positive, with 78% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, praise for its faithful re-creations of the books' scares and some complaints about filler. It grossed $104.5 million worldwide, and a sequel is in development.

Monos is a 2019 Colombian drama film directed by Alejandro Landes. The movie follows a group of young guerrilla fighters in a remote region of Colombia, exploring their lives, struggles, and relationships.

The main theme of Monos revolves around the complexities of war, violence, and its impact on individuals, particularly children. The film delves into the moral dilemmas faced by these young fighters, who are forced to confront harsh realities and make difficult choices that shape their identities and futures.

One of the central themes is the struggle for identity and belonging within a group defined by conflict and violence. The characters' experiences are marked by a sense of disorientation and disillusionment with the war, as they grapple with the consequences of their actions and the true nature of their cause.

The film also explores the theme of innocence lost, as the young fighters confront the harsh realities of war and are forced to grow up too quickly. This is particularly evident in the character of Iban, who becomes increasingly disillusioned with the group's ideology and struggles to reconcile his own sense of morality with the brutal actions of those around him.

Furthermore, Monos examines the theme of trauma and its long-lasting effects on individuals and communities. The film portrays the devastating impact of war on the characters' lives, relationships, and psyches, highlighting the ways in which traumatic experiences can shape one's worldview and inform their decisions.

Throughout the movie, Landes masterfully weaves together these themes, creating a nuanced and thought-provoking portrayal of life in a war-torn region. The result is a powerful and haunting film that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of conflict and its human cost.

As he navigates adolescence, Jamie must confront his own desires, values, and sense of self, all while struggling to understand his father's complex and often contradictory nature.

Ultimately, Wildlife is a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that probes the intricacies of family relationships, masculinity, and the search for meaning in life. title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul
original_title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul
overview: A Heffley family road trip to attend Meemaw's 90th birthday party goes hilariously off course thanks to Greg's newest scheme to get to a video gaming convention.
plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul is a 2017 American road comedy film directed by David Bowers, who co-wrote it with the series' author Jeff Kinney. It is the fourth installment in the Diary of a Wimpy Kid film series and is based on the ninth book of the same name, with elements of the seventh, eighth and tenth books. The film recast the Heffley family, with Jason Ian Drucker as Greg, Alicia Silverstone as his mother Susan, Tom Everett Scott as his father Frank, Charlie Wright as his older brother Rodrick and Owen Asztalos as his best friend Rowley.

At a family restaurant, Susan announces that the Heffleys will take a road trip to attend Meemaw's 90th birthday party, to the dismay of Greg and Rodrick. Before they leave, Greg suffers a public humiliation when he gets stuck in the restaurant's ball pit with a dirty diaper stuck to his hand. Someone films his panic, and the clip goes viral online as the "Diaper Hands" meme, making him infamous. When Greg discovers that a video game convention, the Player Expo, is taking place near Meemaw's home in Indianapolis, and that his favorite online gamer, Mac Digby, will appear there, he decides to secretly sneak off during the trip, hoping that a video with Digby will make people forget about Diaper Hands.

Susan has declared the trip "technology-free" and confiscates everyone's phones, but Greg retrieves his and enlists Rodrick's help with his plan. Along the way the family endures a long series of disasters. At a county fair, Greg wins a piglet that the family is forced to take along, and they repeatedly cross paths with a menacing family who become convinced the Heffleys have wronged them. Their trip includes a seedy motel, a flock of seagulls, car trouble and other mishaps, as Greg's schemes to reach the Expo keep backfiring and threaten to ruin the family vacation entirely.

Released by 20th Century Fox in May 2017, the film was a critical and commercial failure, grossing about $40 million worldwide. Fans objected strongly to the recasting of the familiar characters, and critics found the humor crude and the story thin. It was the last live-action film in the franchise, which later continued with animated adaptations on Disney+.

The main character, Will, is forced to make difficult choices that put his family's survival at risk, highlighting the harsh realities of living in a post-apocalyptic world where resources are scarce and the stakes are high.

This isolation also serves as a catalyst for the characters' own personal demons, leading to a deeper exploration of their inner struggles and vulnerabilities.

Overall, It Comes at Night is a thought-provoking film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of paranoia, sacrifice, and the devastating consequences of isolation in a post-apocalyptic world.

title: Dear Dictator
tagline: She thought she was a rebel... Until she met a real one
overview: When political turmoil forces a British-Caribbean dictator to flee his island nation, he seeks refuge and hides with a rebellious teenage girl in suburban America, and ends up teaching the young teen how to start a revolution and overthrow the "mean girls" in her high school.
plot:
Dear Dictator is a 2018 American satirical comedy film written and directed by Lisa Addario and Joe Syracuse. It stars Michael Caine as Anton Vincent, the deposed dictator of a Caribbean island nation, and Odeya Rush as Tatiana Mills, the American teenager who becomes his pen pal, with Katie Holmes, Seth Green and Jason Biggs. The script appeared on the 2006 Black List of unproduced screenplays, and Alfred Molina, Robert De Niro and Anthony Hopkins were at various times attached to the title role before Caine was cast in 2016.

Sixteen-year-old Tatiana lives a chaotic life with her single mother, Darlene, who is involved with her married boss, Dr. Charles, a dentist with a foot fetish. For a letter-writing assignment from her social studies teacher, Mr. Spines, Tatiana becomes the pen pal of Anton Vincent, a notorious strongman who rules an island nation. When his people rise up against his violent, oppressive regime and overthrow him, Vincent vanishes, and Tatiana worries about his safety. A few days later he turns up unexpectedly in the United States and hides in her family's suburban garage.

There, Anton forms a grandfatherly bond with Tatiana and her struggling mother, making himself useful around the house while secretly coordinating with loyalist forces back home to plot his return to power. He also turns his attention to Tatiana's troubles at high school, where she is bullied by a clique of popular girls. Making her a dictator-in-training, he teaches her to seize power at school using the same methods that brought him to power in the Caribbean. His schemes eventually go too far, turning Tatiana against him, and the security services, having intercepted Anton's messages to his loyalists, suspect that she is involved in terrorism. The police question Tatiana and Darlene and search their home without realizing that the old man living with them is the missing dictator. No evidence is found and they are released, but Tatiana then tells the police who he is, and Anton is arrested pending extradition.

Screened at several festivals under its working title, Coup d'Etat, the film was released in North America by Cinedigm in theaters and on video on demand on March 16, 2018. Reviews were negative, although Caine's and Rush's performances were praised; Rotten Tomatoes reported 16% approval, with critics finding that it squandered its wildly silly premise and talented cast.

title: Goodbye Christopher Robin
overview: The behind the scenes story of the life of A.A. Milne and the creation of the Winnie the Pooh stories inspired by his son Christopher Robin.
plot:
Goodbye Christopher Robin is a heartwarming and poignant film that explores the complex relationship between author A.A. Milne and his beloved son, Christopher Robin Milne. The movie delves into the bittersweet nature of childhood, love, and loss.

At its core, Goodbye Christopher Robin is a story about the fragility of childhood and the inevitability of growing up. As Christopher Robin grows older, he begins to outgrow the imaginative world of Winnie-the-Pooh, which was once his escape and source of joy. This transition is not only a rite of passage but also a painful reminder that nothing lasts forever.

title: The Current War
tagline: Power changes everything
overview: Electricity titans Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse compete to create a sustainable system and market it to the American people.
plot:
The Current War is a historical drama inspired by the 19th-century rivalry between Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse over which electrical system would power the United States, known as the "war of the currents." Directed by Alfonso Gomez-Rejon from a screenplay by Michael Mitnick, with Martin Scorsese and Steven Zaillian among the executive producers, it stars Benedict Cumberbatch as Edison, Michael Shannon as Westinghouse, Nicholas Hoult as Nikola Tesla and Tom Holland as Samuel Insull, alongside Katherine Waterston, Tuppence Middleton and Matthew Macfadyen.

In the 1880s, Edison is already famous as the inventor of the practical incandescent light bulb and is racing to electrify American cities with his direct current system. The industrialist Westinghouse, convinced that alternating current is cheaper and able to carry power over far greater distances, enters the business as Edison's rival after Edison snubs him. The competition soon turns personal and ruthless. Edison, struggling to balance his ambition with his devotion to his wife Mary and their children, launches a public campaign to brand alternating current as deadly, staging electrocutions of animals to frighten the public. Meanwhile, the brilliant Serbian immigrant Tesla, who briefly works for Edison before leaving in frustration, struggles to fund his own inventions until Westinghouse acquires his designs for an alternating current motor.

The contest escalates through patent battles and secret dealings, including Edison's covert involvement in the development of the electric chair, which is used for the first time to execute a man with alternating current. The rivalry comes to a head with the competition to light the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, a showcase of the future in which the winner will define how the nation is powered.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017, but its release was derailed when The Weinstein Company collapsed amid the sexual abuse allegations against Harvey Weinstein. Lantern Entertainment acquired the film and sold US rights to 101 Studios, and Gomez-Rejon, with Scorsese's backing, carried out reshoots and trimmed the running time. This director's cut was released in the United States in October 2019. Reviewers judged it an improvement over the festival version; Metacritic gave it 55 out of 100.

title: Get Out
tagline: Just because you're invited, doesn't mean you're welcome.

plot:
Get Out is a psychological horror film written and directed by Jordan Peele, released in 2017 by Blumhouse Productions. The movie tells the story of Chris Washington, a young African American photographer who agrees to visit his white girlfriend's family estate in upstate New York.

The film begins with Chris (played by Daniel Kaluuya) and his girlfriend Rose (played by Allison Williams) discussing their relationship and the fact that she has invited him to meet her family. Despite some initial reservations, Chris decides to attend the weekend getaway, hoping it will be a chance for them to take their relationship to the next level.

Upon arrival at the Armitage estate, Chris is greeted by Rose's parents, Dean (played by Bradley Whitford) and Missy (played by Catherine Keener), as well as her brother Jeremy (played by Caleb Landry Jones). Initially, Chris feels a sense of unease due to the family's strange behavior and the fact that they seem to be hiding something from him.

As the weekend progresses, Chris begins to notice that the family is treating him with an unusual level of hospitality, almost to the point of being overly accommodating. He also discovers that the family has a fascination with black culture, which he initially attributes to their enthusiasm for his photography work. However, as the days go by, Chris starts to uncover a sinister plot involving hypnosis, mind control, and a sinister secret that the Armitage family is hiding.

The turning point in the film comes when Chris discovers that the family has been using their wealth and influence to lure black people into their home, where they are subjected to a form of psychological manipulation. The family's true intention is to harvest the bodies of these individuals for use as vessels for their own white consciousness, essentially allowing them to experience life through the eyes of a black person without actually having to live it.

As Chris tries to escape and expose the truth, he realizes that he has become trapped in the Armitage estate. The film builds up to a tense climax, where Chris must use his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart the family and break free from their clutches.

Ultimately, Chris manages to escape the estate, but not before discovering that Rose is complicit in her family's sinister activities. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Rose has been using her relationship with Chris as a way to experience black culture without actually having to live it herself.

The film ends with Chris driving away from the Armitage estate, finally free from his ordeal. However, the final shot of the film suggests that Chris may not be entirely safe, leaving the audience with a sense of unease and uncertainty about his future.

Get Out is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling film that explores themes of racism, privilege, and the fetishization of black culture. The movie's clever script, combined with its masterful direction and performances, make it a standout in contemporary horror cinema.

Midnight Sun is a 2018 American romantic fantasy film directed by Julie Yoe and written by Josh Campbell, Matt Stuecken, and Michael H. Weber. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Stephenie Meyer.

The movie takes a unique approach to telling the story, as it focuses on Bella's inner thoughts and feelings through a series of flashbacks and diary entries. This allows the audience to experience the story from Bella's perspective, making her emotions and struggles more relatable and intimate.

As Bella and Edward's relationship deepens, they face numerous challenges, including the threat of James (played by Cam Gigandet), a rogue vampire who is determined to destroy Bella. The Cullens work together to protect Bella, but their efforts are hindered by the fact that Bella is still learning about her own supernatural abilities.

Throughout the movie, the romance between Bella and Edward is portrayed as intense and all-consuming, with a deep emotional connection between the two characters. However, the film also explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the difficulties of being in love with someone who is fundamentally different from oneself.

Ultimately, the movie ends on a hopeful note, with Bella and Edward's relationship still intact despite the many obstacles they have faced. The ending sets the stage for the rest of the Twilight Saga, which follows the further adventures of Bella and Edward as they navigate their supernatural world together.

Overall, Midnight Sun offers a fresh take on the Twilight franchise, focusing on Bella's inner world and emotions rather than the action-packed plot of the original movies. With its unique storytelling approach and beautiful cinematography, the film provides a captivating and romantic viewing experience for fans of the series.

The Babysitter is a 2017 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Christian Stevens. The movie follows Cole, a teenager who has been babysitting for his family's wealthy neighbors, the Smiths, since he was eight years old.

As they spend more time together, Cole becomes increasingly smitten with Bee, but he also starts to notice that she's not like other babysitters. Cole soon realizes that he's in grave danger and must find a way to escape from Bee and her cohorts. He enlists the help of his friends, Ben (played by Owen Vaccaro) and Max (played by Hana Mae Lee), but they're not much help. In fact, they seem to be under some sort of mind control as well.

As Cole tries to outsmart Bee and her coven, he discovers that she's been using a magical artifact to control the minds of those around her. The artifact is hidden in a mysterious box that Bee keeps locked away.

In a thrilling climax, Cole manages to break into the Smiths' house and confronts Bee. He uses his knowledge of magic and some quick thinking to outwit her and destroy the artifact. However, not before Bee reveals that she's been using the coven to exact revenge on the Smiths for their wealth and privilege.

In the end, Cole emerges victorious but shaken by the experience. He realizes that he's been living in a bubble of ignorance and that there's more to life than what he thought. The movie ends with Cole reflecting on his newfound understanding of the world and his place in it.

Overall, The Babysitter is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of teenage angst, rebellion, and the struggle for identity. While it may not be the most original plot, the movie's clever twists and turns keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape
original_title: LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape
overview: The scientists of Jurassic World create a captivating and terrifying new creature that loves hot dogs. But what happens when the hot dogs run out?
plot:
LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape is a 2016 American animated comedy short produced by Universal and the LEGO Group as part of the toy line tied to the Jurassic World franchise. It first appeared in October 2016 as a five-part online series and was then released on DVD later that month as a single 24-minute film, packaged with the short LEGO Jurassic World: Employee Safety Video. Set before the events of Jurassic World (2015), it reimagines most of that film's characters as minifigures and is regarded as the first animated spin-off of the Jurassic Park franchise. The voice cast includes Bryce Dallas Howard, A.J. LoCascio, Jake Johnson, Lauren Lapkus, Zachary Levi, BD Wong, Fred Tatasciore and Sendhil Ramamurthy.

The story opens with park owner Simon Masrani flying Claire Dearing to the island and showing off with aerial stunts, until he crashes into the aviary and tumbles out of his helicopter. Owen Grady rescues him with the help of a trained Pteranodon. Before he is driven away in an ambulance, Masrani tells Claire that Jurassic World will need a new attraction. Meanwhile, the security chief Vic Hoskins goes hunting in the woods and mistakes a park employee in a dinosaur costume for the real thing, chasing him through the jungle for much of the film.

Claire resolves to create a brand-new dinosaur. Owen doubts it can be done, but Dr. Henry Wu proves otherwise by combining Velociraptor and Carnotaurus DNA, and Owen later discovers a whole collection of earlier hybrids kept in an old section of the island. Wu's newest creation, the Indominus rex, turns out to have an insatiable appetite for hot dogs. When it spots the same costumed employee, now dressed as a hot dog mascot, it breaks out of its enclosure and pursues him. Claire calls in the containment unit, rams the beast with a truck and uses a trail of hot dogs to lure it, while Owen's raptors briefly turn against the soldiers because the Indominus shares their DNA. Eventually Owen arrives with the old Tyrannosaurus and the hybrids, and together they drive the Indominus into a pit. The next day visitors enjoy the new attraction, dinosaurs kicking a gyrosphere like a ball with Hoskins still trapped inside, while in a closing scene Wu feeds a second Indominus.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Don's past, which reveal a complex and troubled relationship with Brad. We also learn more about Ryan, who is struggling to find his place in the world after serving in the military.

Throughout the film, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they navigate their differences and try to come together for Christmas. In the end, the Whitakers and Mayrons learn to put aside their differences and work together as a blended family.

One of the standout aspects of Daddy's Home 2 is its exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, masculinity, and identity. The film tackles these issues with humor and heart, making it a relatable and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Daddy's Home 2 is a fun and lighthearted holiday film that explores the ups and downs of blended families. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and heartfelt moments, it's a great addition to any Christmas movie marathon.

overview: On Halloween night, a young woman finds herself as the obsession of a sadistic murderer known as Art the Clown.
plot:
Terrifier is a 2016 American horror film written, directed, and edited by Damien Leone. The film stars David Howard Thornton as Art the Clown, a sadistic and murderous clown who terrorizes a small town on Halloween night.

As the night progresses, Art begins to stalk and murder a group of teenagers who are out trick-or-treating. The film's pacing is fast-moving and intense, with a focus on building tension and suspense through its use of long takes and close-ups.

Throughout the film, Art's backstory is slowly revealed through a series of flashbacks, which show him being abused by Reverend Henry as a child. This traumatic experience has left Art with deep emotional scars, and he seeks revenge against those who wronged him.

One of the standout aspects of Terrifier is its use of practical effects to bring Art to life. David Howard Thornton's performance as the titular character is chilling and unsettling, and his physicality and presence on screen are truly unnerving.

The film has received widespread critical acclaim for its originality and effectiveness in building tension and suspense. It has also spawned a sequel, Terrifier 2, which was released in 2022.

Overall, Terrifier is a masterclass in building tension and suspense through its use of long takes, close-ups, and practical effects. The film's unique blend of horror and dark humor makes it a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: Cage Dive
tagline: First you find the sharks. Then they find you.
overview: Three friends from California are filming an audition tape for an extreme reality game show. They document their journey to Australia where they will be doing their most dangerous activity.... Shark Cage Diving. A catastrophic turn of events leaves them in baited water full of Great White Sharks, turning their recording into a blood chilling diary of survival... and death.
plot:
Open Water 3: Cage Dive is a 2017 Australian found-footage survival horror film written and directed by Gerald Rascionato. Presented as a mockumentary about supposedly true events, it follows three American tourists recording an audition tape for an extreme reality show when their shark cage diving boat capsizes. The cast includes Joel Hogan, Megan Peta Hill and Pete Valley. Although billed as the third Open Water film, it is a standalone story linked to the earlier entries only by theme.

A news report from October 2015 describes a capsized shark diving boat off Australia and a search for three missing passengers from Laguna Beach, California. A week later a diver finds an underwater camera lodged in a reef, its memory card intact, and posts the footage online. The recordings show brothers Josh and Jeff and Jeff's girlfriend, Megan, arriving in Sydney to stay with the brothers' cousin Greg before flying to Adelaide for their dive, and reveal that Megan is secretly having an affair with Josh. During the excursion, as the three enter the cage, a rogue wave overturns the boat. They escape to the surface amid wounded passengers, and sharks soon kill several people nearby.

Drifting for hours, the trio clings to tangled life preservers while Jeff, who has a heart condition and needs regular medication, weakens. That night they find an inflatable emergency raft with supplies, and Josh rescues an unconscious, hypothermic woman from floating debris. During an argument Megan and Josh accidentally fire a flare inside the raft, which burns, killing the woman. The quarrel exposes the affair, and soon afterward a shark drags Megan under. The next morning Jeff taunts Josh about Megan's death until he loses consciousness from his heart condition, and Josh eventually lets his brother's body sink. With the camera battery nearly exhausted, Josh films a rescue helicopter in the distance, but as he waves and shouts, the camera captures a great white rising beneath him, and the footage ends as he is pulled under.

Lionsgate acquired the independent production in early 2017 and rebranded it as part of the Open Water series after the success of Open Water 2: Adrift, releasing it across multiple platforms on August 11, 2017. It bears similarities to 47 Meters Down, another 2017 film about a cage dive gone wrong. It received a 25% score on Rotten Tomatoes from eight critics, although Starburst Magazine reviewed it positively.

However, Maleficent (Angelina Jolie), who has been watching over Aurora from afar, senses that something is amiss. She discovers that the royal family's advisor, King Stefan (Harris Dickinson), plans to use dark magic to ensure his daughter's happiness and secure the throne.

Maleficent sets out to stop the wedding, knowing that it will lead to a catastrophic outcome for all of them. Along the way, she meets Morgan (Jemaine Clement), a powerful sorcerer who claims to be her long-lost brother. As they journey together, Maleficent learns more about her past and the reason behind her curse.

Meanwhile, Prince Philip's mother, Queen Grimhilde (Lesley Manville), is revealed to be the one responsible for casting the original curse on Aurora as a child. The queen's true intentions are to use Aurora's blood to gain ultimate power and control over the kingdom.

As Maleficent navigates her complicated past and confronts her enemies, she must also face her own morality and the consequences of her actions. Alongside Morgan, she forms an unlikely alliance with the fairy godmother, who helps them in their quest to stop the wedding and save Aurora from a terrible fate.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Maleficent and Queen Grimhilde, with the two powerful women engaging in a magical duel that will determine the future of the kingdom. In the end, Maleficent emerges victorious, but not without scars and a newfound understanding of her own strength and vulnerability.

Throughout the film, Angelina Jolie's performance as Maleficent is both captivating and nuanced, bringing depth to the character's complexities. The supporting cast delivers solid performances, particularly Ella Balinska as Aurora, who shines in her breakout role.

Overall, Maleficent: Mistress of Evil offers a thrilling and emotionally resonant sequel that expands on the original story while introducing new characters and themes. With its stunning visuals, engaging storyline, and strong performances, this film is sure to delight fans of fantasy and adventure movies alike.

He is struggling to find meaning in his life as a successful businessman, but feels unfulfilled and disconnected from his past.

One day, while on vacation at the Hundred Acre Wood, Christopher Robin reunites with his old friends Pooh (voiced by Jim Cummings), Piglet (voiced by Nick Mohammed), Eeyore (voiced by Brad Garrett), Tigger (voiced by Jim Cummings), Rabbit (voiced by Peter Capaldi), Owl (voiced by Toby Jones), and Kanga (voiced by Nicole Scherzinger). As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Christopher Robin's adult life is marked by stress, anxiety, and a lack of creativity. He feels like he's losing himself in the process of becoming a successful businessman. Meanwhile, Pooh and the other animals are struggling to cope with the changing world around them, including the loss of their home due to urban development.

Through his interactions with his friends, Christopher Robin begins to rediscover the joys of childhood imagination and creativity. He starts to see the world through the eyes of a child again, and finds inspiration in the simple pleasures of life. The movie features stunning animation, bringing the beloved characters to life in a way that is both nostalgic and fresh.

As the story reaches its climax, Christopher Robin must confront his own fears and doubts in order to find his true purpose in life. With the help of his friends, he learns to let go of his adult responsibilities and rediscover the magic of childhood. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Christopher Robin returning home to his family, but this time with a renewed sense of wonder and imagination.

Throughout the film, there are also flashbacks that show Christopher Robin's childhood adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, which serve as a reminder of the power of imagination and friendship. The movie features a talented voice cast, including Emily Blunt as Christopher Robin's wife, Jane, and Hayley Atwell as his mother.

Overall, Christopher Robin is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the importance of childhood imagination and creativity. It's a story about finding one's true purpose in life and rediscovering the magic of childhood through the power of friendship and imagination.

Aladdin is a 2019 American fantasy adventure film directed by Guy Ritchie and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie is a live-action remake of the 1992 animated film of the same name, which was based on the Middle Eastern folk tale "Aladdin's Wonderful Lamp".

The story begins in the bustling streets of Agrabah, where we meet our protagonist, Aladdin (played by Mena Massoud), a poor but kind-hearted street urchin who lives with his pet monkey, Abu. One day, while exploring the marketplace, Aladdin stumbles upon a mysterious cave where he finds a magic lamp containing the Genie (played by Will Smith). The Genie grants Aladdin three wishes, which he uses to become a prince to win the heart of Princess Jasmine (played by Naomi Scott), the beautiful daughter of the Sultan. Throughout the film, Ritchie's signature style is evident in the witty banter, clever wordplay, and fast-paced action sequences. The movie also features stunning visuals, with intricate sets and costumes that transport viewers to the vibrant world of Agrabah.

As the story unfolds, Aladdin must confront his own identity and the consequences of his wishes. In a thrilling climax, he faces off against Jafar in an epic battle to save the kingdom and win Jasmine's heart.

Ultimately, Aladdin emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The film concludes with Aladdin and Jasmine sharing a romantic moment, while the Genie is finally able to rest in peace. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Aladdin embracing his true identity as a street urchin who has become a hero.

Overall, the 2019 live-action remake of Aladdin is a visually stunning and action-packed adventure that stays true to the spirit of the original tale while introducing new elements to captivate modern audiences.

title: The Lion King
tagline: The King has Returned.
overview: Simba idolizes his father, King Mufasa, and takes to heart his own royal destiny. But not everyone in the kingdom celebrates the new cub's arrival. Scar, Mufasa's brother—and former heir to the throne—has plans of his own. The battle for Pride Rock is ravaged with betrayal, tragedy and drama, ultimately resulting in Simba's exile. With help from a curious pair of newfound friends, Simba will have to figure out how to grow up and take back what is rightfully his.
plot:
The Lion King is a 2019 American musical drama film and a photorealistically animated remake of Disney's traditionally animated 1994 film. Directed by Jon Favreau and written by Jeff Nathanson, it was produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Fairview Entertainment. The voice cast includes Donald Glover as Simba, Beyoncé Knowles-Carter as Nala, Chiwetel Ejiofor as Scar, Seth Rogen and Billy Eichner as Pumbaa and Timon, John Oliver as Zazu, John Kani as Rafiki and Alfre Woodard as Sarabi, with James Earl Jones reprising his role as Mufasa.

In the Pride Lands, King Mufasa and Queen Sarabi present their newborn son Simba to the gathered animals, while Mufasa's younger brother Scar resentfully covets the throne. Mufasa teaches Simba about the responsibilities of a king and the "circle of life" that connects all living things. Scar tricks the curious cub into exploring a forbidden elephant graveyard, where Simba and his best friend Nala are chased by hyenas led by Shenzi before Mufasa, alerted by the hornbill Zazu, comes to their rescue. Scar then strikes a deal with the hyenas, promising them hunting rights in exchange for their help in killing Mufasa and Simba. He lures Simba into a gorge and has the hyenas drive a stampede of wildebeest toward him; Mufasa saves his son but is thrown to his death by Scar, who convinces Simba that he was to blame and urges him to run away and never return. Scar claims the throne and lets the hyenas into the Pride Lands. Rescued in the desert by the meerkat Timon and the warthog Pumbaa, Simba grows up carefree in their oasis, living by their motto "hakuna matata". Years later he is reunited with Nala, who tells him that the kingdom has fallen into drought and ruin under Scar's rule. Still burdened by guilt, Simba refuses to return, until the wise mandrill Rafiki and a vision of his father's spirit remind him of who he is, and he heads home to confront Scar and reclaim his place in the circle of life.

The film received mixed reviews, with many critics praising its visuals but faulting its lack of originality and near-identical retelling of the original; it holds a 52% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It nevertheless grossed more than $1.6 billion worldwide and broke several box-office records, including becoming the highest-grossing animated film of all time until 2024.

title: Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers
tagline: It's not a reboot. It's a comeback.
overview: Decades since their successful television series was canceled, Chip has succumbed to a life of suburban domesticity as an insurance salesman. Dale, meanwhile, has had CGI surgery and works the nostalgia convention circuit, desperate to relive his glory days. When a former cast mate mysteriously disappears, Chip and Dale must repair their broken friendship and take on their Rescue Rangers detective personas once again to save their friend’s life.
plot:
Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers is a 2022 American live-action and animated action-adventure comedy based on Disney's chipmunk duo and serving as a follow-up to the 1989 animated series of the same name. It was directed by Akiva Schaffer from a screenplay by Dan Gregor and Doug Mand. John Mulaney voices Chip and Andy Samberg voices Dale, with KiKi Layne, Will Arnett, Eric Bana, Seth Rogen and J. K. Simmons. It premiered at the El Capitan Theatre and was released on Disney+ on May 20, 2022.

In a world where humans and cartoon characters live side by side, Chip and Dale become best friends in elementary school and later move to Hollywood, where they rise from bit parts to stardom with the hit series Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers. When Dale is offered a solo spin-off, the pair fall out bitterly and the show is cancelled. Thirty years later, Chip is a cautious, jaded insurance salesman, while Dale, who has undergone "CGI surgery" to look three-dimensional, works the fan convention circuit.

Their old co-star Monterey Jack, deep in debt to the criminal Valley Gang because of his addiction to cheese, warns them of a ring that kidnaps cartoons, alters their appearance and forces them to star in cheap bootleg films overseas. When Monty disappears, the estranged chipmunks reluctantly reunite to find him, helped by Ellie Steckler, an eager police officer and devoted fan of their show.

Their investigation leads to the gang's leader, Sweet Pete, a grown-up, embittered Peter Pan who was cast aside by the industry when he aged, and his henchmen. The chipmunks trace the operation to a warehouse containing a machine for reshaping toons, and realise that someone in the police is working with Pete. During a chase at a fan convention Chip is captured, and Ellie discovers that her captain is in league with the villain.

Dale rallies their old co-stars Gadget and Zipper, now married with a large family, and stops the machine before it can be used on Chip. In the chaos, Pete is transformed into a monstrous amalgam of cartoon parts. Using a trick from one of their old episodes, the chipmunks trap him, and the FBI, led by Ugly Sonic, arrests the gang. When Dale survives a cannon blast thanks to a keepsake Chip once gave him, the friends reconcile, free Monty and the other captive toons and go on to make a successful reboot of their show.

Critics responded warmly, with 81% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and the film later won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie.

title: The Return of Godzilla
tagline: Breaking 30 years of silence comes the anticipated-worldwide latest "Godzilla" work!
overview: After a fishing boat is attacked, the sole surviving crew member realizes it is none other than a resurrected Godzilla. However, efforts to bring the story to light are suppressed by the Japanese government amid growing political tensions between the United States and the Soviet Union, who are both willing to bomb Japan to stop the monster.
plot:
The Return of Godzilla is a 1984 Japanese science fiction kaiju film directed by Kazuki Ōmori and produced by Tomoyuki Tanaka. It is the 15th film in the Godzilla franchise.

The movie begins with a series of mysterious earthquakes occurring around the world, which are later revealed to be caused by the return of Godzilla, also known as "Gigantis" or "Godzilla's Return". The story takes place two years after the events of Godzilla vs. Biollante (1989), where Godzilla is awakened from its slumber in the depths of the ocean.

The film starts with a series of strange occurrences happening around the world, including earthquakes and tidal waves. As the earthquakes intensify, it becomes clear that Godzilla has returned to wreak havoc on humanity. The Japanese government assembles a team of scientists and military personnel to deal with the crisis.

The main character, Dr. Yamane (played by Takeshi Kusao), is a renowned paleontologist who had previously studied Godzilla's DNA. He is recruited by the government to lead the team that will study and stop Godzilla. The team includes his daughter, Emiko (played by Yuriko Hoshi), a young scientist who has grown up studying her father's work.

As Godzilla begins its rampage across Japan, the team discovers that it is not just a mindless beast, but a creature with a complex intelligence and a desire to destroy humanity. The team also learns that Godzilla's return is linked to the discovery of a new species of giant lizard in the depths of the ocean.

The plot thickens as the team discovers that Godzilla's DNA has been altered by its encounter with a new species of giant lizard, which has given it enhanced strength and intelligence. This revelation raises questions about the nature of Godzilla's existence and whether it is truly a monster or a creature worthy of respect.

As the story unfolds, the team faces numerous challenges in trying to stop Godzilla. They use various tactics, including nuclear missiles and sonic devices, but nothing seems to work. The film builds towards an epic showdown between Godzilla and the team, which culminates in a dramatic confrontation on the streets of Tokyo.

In the end, Dr. Yamane comes up with a plan to use a device that can disrupt Godzilla's DNA, rendering it unable to reproduce. However, this plan is complicated by the fact that Emiko has fallen in love with Godzilla and wants to protect it. The film ends with a bittersweet conclusion, as Emiko sacrifices herself to save her father and the world from Godzilla.

The Return of Godzilla is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of nature vs. nurture, humanity's relationship with technology, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond our control. It is also a thrilling adventure that showcases Godzilla's iconic status as a symbol of Japanese popular culture.

title: Flower
tagline: Bad decisions. Good intentions.
overview: Rebellious, quick-witted Erica Vandross is a 17-year-old firecracker living with her single mom, Laurie, and her mom's new boyfriend, Bob, in L.A.'s San Fernando Valley. When Bob's mentally unbalanced son, Luke, arrives from rehab to live with the family, Erica finds her domestic and personal life overwhelmed. With Luke and her sidekicks Kala and Claudine in tow, Erica acts out by exposing a high school teacher's dark secret.
plot:
Flower is a 2017 American romantic comedy-drama directed by Max Winkler from a screenplay he wrote with Alex McAulay and Matt Spicer. Zoey Deutch stars as Erica Vandross, a brash and sexually curious seventeen-year-old, with Kathryn Hahn as her mother Laurie, Tim Heidecker as Laurie's boyfriend Bob, Joey Morgan as Bob's troubled son Luke, and Adam Scott as a former teacher. Dylan Gelula, Maya Eshet and Eric Edelstein complete the cast. The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2017 and was later released by The Orchard.

Erica and two friends run a reckless scheme in their Los Angeles suburb: Erica seduces older men while her friends secretly film the encounter, then the trio extort money by threatening to expose the men for involvement with a minor. Erica is saving the money to pay bail for her father, who is in jail awaiting trial for attempting to rob a casino. Her mother tolerates her behaviour but is frustrated that Erica refuses to warm to her new partner, Bob.

When Bob's son Luke, an anxious and emotionally fragile eighteen-year-old, returns from rehab and moves into the household, Erica first tries to provoke him but soon develops an unexpected friendship with him. At a bowling alley, Luke suffers a panic attack upon seeing Will Jordan, a former middle-school teacher he once accused of sexual abuse, a case that was dropped because of inconsistencies in his account. Shortly afterwards, Erica stops Luke from attempting suicide. Determined to punish the man she believes hurt him, Erica decides to make Will her group's next target, and Luke reluctantly agrees to help. As she pursues the teacher, however, the plan grows more dangerous and the truth about what happened between Will and Luke turns out to be more complicated than she assumed, forcing Erica to confront the consequences of her impulsive sense of justice.

The film moves between raunchy teen comedy and darker territory involving abuse, depression and family dysfunction, with the relationship between Erica and Luke at its centre.

Reviews were mixed. On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of about 48 percent; the consensus credits Deutch with bringing even a preposterously written character vividly to life, while finding the film's tonal shifts and treatment of its serious subject matter uneven.

Mike soon realizes that Ortega is not just any ordinary terrorist but a former Secret Service agent who was thought to have been killed years ago. As Mike navigates the complex web of intrigue and deception, he must also confront his own demons and the personal costs of his past actions as a Secret Service agent.

As the story unfolds, Mike teams up with his old friend and fellow Secret Service agent, Tobin (Jai Courtney), to take down Ortega and rescue Shannon. Along the way, they encounter a range of characters, including a mysterious woman named Rachel (Pati Callahan) who may hold the key to unlocking the truth about Ortega's past.

As the plot thickens, Mike finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with Ortega, who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals. The action unfolds at breakneck speed, with Mike facing off against Ortega and his henchmen in a series of intense and suspenseful confrontations.

In the end, Mike is able to outsmart Ortega and rescue Shannon, but not before he suffers a serious injury that leaves him questioning his own mortality. As the movie concludes, Mike reflects on the personal costs of his actions as a Secret Service agent and the sacrifices he has made for his country.

Throughout the film, Gerard Butler delivers a strong performance as the rugged and charismatic Mike Banning, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Morgan Freeman provides a sense of gravitas and authority as the President, while Jai Courtney brings a youthful energy to the role of Tobin.

Overall, Angel Has Fallen is a tense and thrilling action movie that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its breakneck pace, intricate plot twists, and memorable performances, it's no wonder this film has become a fan favorite among action movie enthusiasts.

title: Mass
overview: Two couples meet for a painful and raw conversation in the aftermath of a violent tragedy.
plot:
Mass is a 2021 American drama film written and directed by Fran Kranz in his directorial debut. Reed Birney, Ann Dowd, Jason Isaacs and Martha Plimpton star as two couples who meet years after a school shooting in which the son of one couple killed the son of the other. Set almost entirely in one room, it premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 30, 2021, and was released by Bleecker Street on October 8, 2021.

Six years after a high school shooting, Jay and Gail Perry, whose son Evan was among those killed, agree to meet Richard and Linda, the parents of the teenage gunman, Hayden, who killed himself after the attack. Their meeting is arranged in a quiet back room of an Episcopal church, with a church worker nervously preparing the space. The couples have met before, during the legal proceedings that followed the shooting, when Jay and Gail spoke harshly to the other parents, and Jay has since become a public advocate for gun control.

After awkward small talk and memories of their sons as young children, the conversation turns to how the tragedy happened. Jay and Gail press for details of Hayden's upbringing beyond what the public already knows. Richard and Linda describe his growing depression after the family moved, his isolation, and the bullying he suffered, and they argue briefly over the influence of violent video games. While noting that schools and therapists failed to act on warning signs, they acknowledge their own guilt at not seeing what their son was becoming.

The talk grows heated. Jay and Gail admit they wanted Richard and Linda to suffer as much as the victims' families did. When the other couple reveal that Hayden had friends who were also bullied, one of whom had access to guns, Jay explodes, suggesting that Hayden was simply a psychopath, before breaking down as he describes how Evan died. Linda tells them about a notebook in which Hayden planned the attack, and explains that she and Richard held a funeral to mourn the boy they had loved before his crime.

When Linda asks to hear about Evan, Gail shares a happy memory of him at twelve and finally forgives Hayden and his parents, and the four hold hands in silence. As they leave, Linda returns to tell Gail how afraid she once was of Hayden. Jay is overcome by the sound of a choir rehearsing nearby. The film was acclaimed for its acting and writing, with 95% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Dowd received a BAFTA nomination for Best Supporting Actress.

Johnny Spillane's journey serves as a metaphor for the search for authenticity and truth in a world where propaganda and censorship reign supreme.

As Johnny becomes more deeply embroiled in the art world, he is forced to confront his own dark past and the traumas inflicted upon him by the regime. Johnny's journey is also a quest to find his own voice and purpose, amidst the chaos and uncertainty of the Cold War era. The film raises questions about the role of art in shaping our understanding of ourselves and the world around us.

Overall, Never Look Away is a powerful exploration of the human spirit, artistic expression, and the struggle for freedom in the face of oppression.

title: In the Fade
overview: Katja's life collapses after a senseless act impacts her. After a time of mourning and injustice, she seeks revenge.
plot:
In the Fade (German: Aus dem Nichts) is a 2017 German drama thriller written and directed by Fatih Akin. Diane Kruger stars as Katja Şekerci, a German woman whose Kurdish husband and young son are killed in a bombing carried out by neo-Nazis, with Denis Moschitto as her lawyer, Numan Acar as her husband, Johannes Krisch as the defense attorney and Ulrich Tukur. The film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival, where Kruger won the award for Best Actress, in her first major German-language role.

Nuri Şekerci, a Kurdish-German man who served time in prison for drug dealing and studied business while inside, now lives a happy life in Hamburg with his German wife, Katja, and their six-year-old son, Rocco, running a small office. One day Katja leaves Rocco with Nuri while she spends the afternoon with a friend. As she leaves, she warns a young blonde woman who has parked a new bicycle in front of the office that it might be stolen if she does not lock it. Returning that evening, Katja finds the street cordoned off: a nail bomb has exploded, killing Nuri and Rocco.

Katja tells the police about the woman with the bicycle and becomes convinced the attack was the work of neo-Nazis, but investigators focus on Nuri's past and possible links to drug traffickers. Overwhelmed by grief, Katja turns to drugs and attempts suicide, but she is stopped by news that suspects have been arrested: a young neo-Nazi couple, André and Edda Möller, whose own father reported his son to the police. The trial in the film's second part becomes a painful ordeal, as the defense attacks Katja's credibility because of her drug use and a Greek neo-Nazi provides the couple with an alibi. When the court acquits them for lack of evidence, Katja, abandoned by the justice system, follows the couple to Greece and contemplates taking justice into her own hands.

In the Fade received generally favorable reviews, with a 77 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Kruger's ability to carry the film, though some felt it did not match her remarkable work. It won the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film and was shortlisted for the Academy Award. The film was inspired in part by the murders committed by the National Socialist Underground in Germany.

plot:
