title: Rakka
overview: A story of broken humanity following the invasion of a technologically superior alien species. Bleak, harrowing, and unrelenting, the humans must find enough courage to go on fighting.
plot:
Rakka is a 2017 science fiction film directed by Travis Fimmel and written by Travis Fimmel and James Blake. The movie takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where humanity has been decimated by an alien invasion.

The main theme of Rakka revolves around the struggle for survival and the human condition in the face of catastrophic loss. The story follows a young woman named Maya, who is forced to confront her own mortality and the true meaning of life when she discovers that she may be the last human survivor on Earth.

As Maya navigates this desolate world, she must come to terms with the fact that she is no longer alone, but rather part of a larger, interconnected web of humanity. The film explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for connection in a world that has been ravaged by destruction.

Throughout the movie, the audience is taken on a journey of self-discovery, as Maya grapples with her own identity and purpose in a world that seems to have lost its way. The film's use of stunning visuals and atmospheric sound design creates a sense of immersion and tension, drawing the viewer into Maya's world and forcing them to confront their own emotions and fears.

Ultimately, Rakka is a powerful exploration of what it means to be human in the face of unimaginable loss and destruction. It is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges the audience to consider the true meaning of existence and our place in the universe.

title: Hostile

Hostile is a 2018 American science fiction thriller film directed by Johannes Roberts. The movie follows a group of astronauts on a mission to Mars who are stalked and killed one by one by an alien creature.

The main theme of Hostile revolves around the fear of the unknown and the insignificance of humanity in the vastness of space. As the crew members are picked off, they begin to realize that their own mortality is not just due to the harsh Martian environment but also to a force beyond their control. This realization sparks a sense of existential dread, as they confront the possibility that they may be nothing more than prey for an alien predator.

The film also explores the theme of isolation and confinement, as the crew members are trapped on the spaceship with no escape from the creature. This isolation heightens their paranoia and fear, making it difficult for them to distinguish between reality and their own paranoia-driven hallucinations.

Furthermore, Hostile touches upon the idea of humanity's hubris and overconfidence in the face of the unknown. The crew's initial excitement and sense of accomplishment at reaching Mars is slowly eroded as they realize that they are not alone in the universe and that their presence may be seen as a threat to an alien species.

Overall, Hostile is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and our place in the universe.

title: Palm Swings
tagline: Do you play?
overview: After moving to Palm Springs, a young married couple puts their love to the test when they discover that their neighbors are swingers.
plot:
Palm Swings is a 2017 American romantic comedy-drama directed by Sean Hoessli from a screenplay by Amanda Lockhart. Produced by Hoessli, Steve Carson and Randy Wayne for Code Blue Pictures and shot in Palm Springs, California, it stars Sugar Lyn Beard and Jackson Davis as a newly married couple, with Diane Farr, Chaka Forman, Jason Lewis, Madison McKinley, Danny Pardo, Antonimar Murphy and Gentry White, and Tia Carrere in a cameo as Ms. Cherry Bomb. Kristin Fieldhouse was the cinematographer and Alf Alpha and Alex Kovacs composed the music.

Allison Hughes (Beard), a photographer, and her husband Mark (Davis), a philosophy professor, move to the desert town of Palm Springs. They have barely unpacked when their flirtatious new neighbor Claire (Farr) introduces herself. That evening Allison notices strange goings-on next door and, peering through a window with her camera, sees Claire and her husband Jim (Forman) in a foursome, unaware that Claire has spotted her. After a shopping trip with Claire and a dinner at which Jim bluntly explains the couple's lifestyle, the newlyweds dip their toes into swinging. At a swingers' weekend built around a key exchange, it is Mark, against expectations, who gets cold feet, while Allison enthusiastically takes the plunge. She becomes infatuated with Lance (Lewis) and begins seeing him behind her husband's back, pushing for more encounters as her marriage cools. At another party, Lance's wife Rachel (McKinley) lets slip the truth about Allison and Lance, and Mark walks out. The couple separate, and Allison, still in love with her husband, is willing to give up the lifestyle to win him back.

The film had its home-video premiere in Sweden in September 2017 and was released in the United States on 3 October 2017; it later premiered on Sky Cinema in the United Kingdom in April 2018. Reviewing it for What's on TV, Jason Best found the film daring in places and surprisingly conservative in others, praising its appropriately louche, almost 1970s look and its leading ladies, Beard's squeaky-voiced innocence contrasting with her character's raunchy adventures and Farr's seductive presence, but found the male characters much less interesting and regretted the more conventional turn the story takes later on.

title: Sierra Burgess Is a Loser
tagline: Just be you.
overview: A case of mistaken identity results in unexpected romance when the most popular girl in high school and the biggest loser must come together to win over their crushes.
plot:
Sierra Burgess Is a Loser is a 2018 American romantic comedy film directed by Ian Samuels and written by Jordan Roberts. The movie stars Shannon Purser, Noah Centineo, and Ross Butler.

The main themes of Sierra Burgess Is a Loser revolve around identity, social media, and self-discovery. The story follows Sierra Burgess (Shannon Purser), a high school student who caters to her crush, Chad (Noah Centineo), by pretending to be someone she's not on social media.

As the movie progresses, Sierra navigates her relationships with her friends, family, and romantic interests while trying to maintain her online persona. The film explores themes of:

1. Identity: Sierra struggles to reconcile her true self with the image she presents online. She must confront the consequences of curating a false identity and learn to accept herself for who she is.
2. Social media: The movie critiques the superficiality of social media, highlighting how people present a curated version of themselves online. Sierra's experiences serve as a commentary on the pressure to conform to societal expectations and the dangers of comparing oneself to others.
3. Self-discovery: Through her journey, Sierra learns valuable lessons about self-acceptance, empathy, and genuine connections with others. She comes to realize that true happiness and fulfillment can only be achieved by being authentic and embracing her individuality.

The film also touches on secondary themes such as:

* Friendship: The importance of supportive relationships in navigating life's challenges.
* Family dynamics: Sierra's complicated relationship with her mother (Mary Stuart Masterson) serves as a backdrop for exploring family dynamics and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships.
* Romance: The movie explores the ups and downs of romantic relationships, highlighting the importance of communication, trust, and mutual respect.

Overall, Sierra Burgess Is a Loser is a heartwarming and relatable coming-of-age story that encourages viewers to be true to themselves and appreciate the beauty of imperfection.

title: The Stolen Princess
tagline: Love is stronger than magic
overview: This wonderful story happened in the age of valiant knights, beautiful princesses, and battling sorcerers. Ruslan, a wandering artist dreaming to become a knight, met beautiful Mila and fell in love with her; he didn’t even suspect that she is the King’s daughter. However, the lovers’ happiness wasn’t meant to last too long. Chernomor, the evil sorcerer, appeared in a magic vortex and stole Mila right before Ruslan’s eyes to transform her power of love into his own magic power. Without further ado, Ruslan sets out on a chase after the stolen princess to overcome all obstacles and to prove that real love is stronger than magic.
plot:
The Stolen Princess (Ukrainian: Vykradena pryntsesa: Ruslan i Lyudmyla) is a 2018 Ukrainian 3D animated fantasy adventure directed by Oleg Malamuzh and produced by the Kyiv studio Animagrad. It is loosely based on Alexander Pushkin's narrative poem Ruslan and Ludmila, reimagined as a light-hearted family adventure. The film premiered in Ukraine on 7 March 2018 and according to its makers it was originally produced in English and then dubbed into Ukrainian.

The story opens with a magical duel in the past between two sorcerers, Finn and Chornomor. Finn fights to save his beloved wife, Princess Nina, but is tricked and defeated, losing his magic and his youth, which pass to Chornomor. Nina is turned into a stone statue, and Chornomor draws his power from the strength of her love, which he must periodically renew by capturing a princess who is in love.

Many years later, Ruslan is a wandering actor who dreams of becoming a knight and performs in small plays written by Lester, an eccentric aspiring playwright, often playing the roles of the old sorcerers. In a nearby castle lives Mila, a spirited princess who longs for adventure and resents her overprotective father, King Vladimir, who wants her to marry. One night she sneaks out of the castle and is rescued from two thugs by Ruslan. Afraid that his humble status will disappoint her, he pretends to be a knight, and the two quickly fall in love. Soon afterwards, Mila is carried off by a tornado conjured by Chornomor, who needs the energy of her love to preserve his power. Ruslan sets out to rescue her, helped by the aged Finn and joined by Lester, facing dangers including the enormous animated head of a giant and Chornomor's dark magic, while Mila resists her captor from within his fortress.

The film blends romance, comedy and fantasy action, emphasising courage, honesty and the power of true love over magic. Its humour includes contemporary references aimed at younger audiences.

Reception was mixed. Some viewers felt that the film lacked Ukrainian character and imitated Hollywood conventions too closely, and they criticised its modern references, but reviewers praised its high standard of animation, clever jokes and its achievement as a major Ukrainian animated feature.

Overall, The Peanut Butter Falcon is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of freedom, friendship, identity, and acceptance in a heartwarming and entertaining way.

title: Shadow
tagline: The Battlefield in Ink.
overview: In a kingdom ruled by a young and unpredictable king, the military commander has a secret weapon: a shadow, a look-alike who can fool both his enemies and the King himself. Now he must use this weapon in an intricate plan that will lead his people to victory in a war that the King does not want.
plot:
Shadow (Chinese: Yǐng) is a 2018 wuxia film directed by Zhang Yimou and starring Deng Chao, Sun Li, Zheng Kai, Wang Qianyuan, Hu Jun, Wang Jingchun, Guan Xiaotong and Leo Wu. A Chinese-Hong Kong co-production, it is adapted from Zhu Sujin's play Jingzhou of the Three Kingdoms and set in a fictional historical era.

Years earlier, the Kingdom of Pei lost the strategic city of Jing to the Kingdom of Yan when its commander, Ziyu, was defeated in a duel by the Yan general Yang Cang. Pei's king, Pei Liang, is furious that Ziyu has challenged Yang Cang to a rematch without permission, and to keep the peace he arranges for his sister, Qingping, to marry Yang Cang's son, Yang Ping. The Ziyu at court, however, is a double named Jingzhou, secretly trained as a "shadow" by Ziyu's family because of his uncanny resemblance; the real Ziyu, gravely wounded in the duel, hides in secret, known only to his wife, Xiaoai, and promises Jingzhou his freedom once Jing is retaken. The king demotes "Ziyu" to commoner, and when Yan offers to take Qingping only as a concubine, he accepts, prompting General Tian Zhan to resign in protest.

Jingzhou trains with a metal umbrella against Ziyu, who imitates Yang Cang's guandao, until Xiaoai shows him a yielding, feminine technique to counter Yang's forceful style. Ziyu reveals the plan to Tian Zhan: while Jingzhou keeps Yang Cang occupied in a duel, Tian and a hundred convicts will seize Jing. On the night before, Xiaoai sleeps with Jingzhou as Ziyu watches in secret. The convicts, joined by the stowaway Qingping, attack with umbrella weapons. Qingping is mortally wounded by Yang Ping but kills him, and Jingzhou kills Yang Cang with a snapping umbrella blade. Returning home, Jingzhou finds his mother dead and is saved from assassins by the king's emissary. At the victory feast, the king reveals that he knows Jingzhou's secret and wants him to replace Ziyu entirely, but Ziyu, disguised as an assassin, stabs the king and orders Jingzhou to finish him. When Ziyu turns on him, Jingzhou mortally wounds Ziyu, kills the king and frames Ziyu for the murder, declaring himself the assassin's slayer. Tian does not object, and Xiaoai watches, torn over whether to expose him.

Shadow screened at the Venice, Toronto and London film festivals in 2018 before wider international releases in 2019. Critics acclaimed its cinematography, design and choreography, giving it 94% on Rotten Tomatoes and 81 on Metacritic.

title: Slumber
overview: A sleep doctor tries to protect a family from a demon that feeds on people in their nightmares.
plot:
Slumber is a 2017 British supernatural horror thriller directed by Jonathan Hopkins, who co-wrote the screenplay with Richard Hobley. Maggie Q stars as a sleep specialist, with Kristen Bush, Sam Troughton, Will Kemp, William Hope and Sylvester McCoy in supporting roles. It was released on 1 December 2017 by Vertical Entertainment. The film draws on the folklore of the nocturnal demon said to sit on sleepers' chests, linking it to the real medical phenomenon of sleep paralysis.

Maggie Q plays Dr. Alice Arnolds, a sleep doctor whose rational, scientific outlook masks a painful childhood memory: her younger brother died in a mysterious accident linked to sleepwalking, an event she has never fully come to terms with. As an adult she works at a sleep clinic, running overnight studies on patients with parasomnias, and she is firmly sceptical of any explanation that cannot be measured.

Alice takes on the case of the Morgan family, whose members, particularly young Daniel, suffer from violent night terrors and sleepwalking episodes. Daniel insists that a dark figure enters his room at night and sits on his chest. During observation sessions at the clinic, recordings capture disturbing behaviour that Alice cannot easily explain, and incidents involving the family grow more dangerous. Seeking answers outside medicine, she turns to Amadeus, an eccentric expert in the occult played by McCoy, who tells her that the family is being stalked by a Nocnitsa, a demon from Slavic folklore that preys on people in their sleep and feeds on them. As Alice struggles to protect the children, she discovers that the entity may be connected to her own past, and she must confront the demon in the dream world in order to save the family and herself.

The film combines a medical procedural with a classic possession and demon narrative, and much of its tension derives from the vulnerability of sleep and the inability of science to account for what Alice witnesses.

Slumber was poorly received by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of 0 percent based on eight reviews, with reviewers finding it derivative of other supernatural horror films, although Maggie Q's committed lead performance was noted.

title: Velvet Buzzsaw
tagline: All Art Is Dangerous
overview: Big money artists and mega-collectors pay a high price when art collides with commerce. After a series of paintings by an unknown artist are discovered, a supernatural force enacts revenge on those who have allowed their greed to get in the way of art.
plot:
Velvet Buzzsaw is a 2019 American satirical black comedy and supernatural horror film written and directed by Dan Gilroy. Jake Gyllenhaal, Rene Russo and Zawe Ashton lead an ensemble that includes Toni Collette, Daveed Diggs, Tom Sturridge, Natalia Dyer, Billy Magnussen and John Malkovich.

Los Angeles art critic Morf Vandewalt begins an affair with Josephina, who works for gallery owner Rhodora Haze, once a member of the punk band Velvet Buzzsaw. Josephina finds that a reclusive neighbor, Vetril Dease, has died, leaving behind a large collection of paintings, some partly destroyed. She takes them, and Rhodora shows them to great acclaim, deliberately keeping them scarce. Morf finds out that Dease had a violent childhood, killed his abusive father and was subjected to experiments in a psychiatric hospital. He later learns that Dease mixed blood into his paint.

The paintings then begin to kill the people who profit from them. Gallery worker Bryson is dragged into a painting at a deserted gas station. Rival dealer Jon Dondon is strangled with his own scarf by a hand that reaches out of the dark. Morf starts seeing figures move in the canvases. Gretchen, an art adviser who arranged a Dease show, is killed when an interactive sculpture called Sphere cuts off her arm. Each death only raises demand. Morf begs Rhodora to stop selling the work, but she rushes to sell it for tens of millions. Josephina is swallowed by a wall of graffiti. Hoboman, a robotic piece Morf once panned, comes to life and kills him. Rhodora's buzz saw tattoo starts spinning and cuts her throat. Coco, the assistant who kept finding the bodies, leaves for Michigan and passes a street vendor selling Dease paintings for five dollars each. Meanwhile, the painter Piers draws patterns in the sand at the edge of the waves.

Gilroy said he conceived the film after the cancellation of Superman Lives, a project he had worked on. He settled his frustration on a beach, which inspired the final scene. Netflix produced the film, and shooting began in Los Angeles in March 2018. Marco Beltrami and Buck Sanders scored it. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 27, 2019, and was released by Netflix on February 1. Reviews were mixed to favorable. Rotten Tomatoes rated it 61%, and RogerEbert.com called it wildly inconsistent but ambitious, with unforgettable images and an excellent ensemble.

plot:

Beginning:
The story starts with Lewis Barnavelt (Jack Black), a talented but reclusive magician who lives in a small town called New Enchantment. Lewis is an orphan who has been living with his cruel aunt, Florence (Catherine O'Hara). On the eve of his 13th birthday, Lewis receives a mysterious letter from a lawyer named Jonathan Barnavelt (Michael Caine), who claims to be his long-lost uncle.

Jonathan reveals that he was a magician and a scholar who had been studying the occult. He warns Lewis about an evil warlock named Zebulon Voldar (Patrick Warburton) who is trying to steal the magical clock in the house where Lewis lives. The clock, which has been ticking for over 100 years, holds the key to unlocking immense magical power.

Plot Development:
Lewis travels to New Enchantment with Jonathan and meets Jonah, a young boy who claims that he can see ghosts. Together, they embark on a journey to uncover the secrets of the house and the mysterious clock. Along the way, Lewis learns about his family's history and discovers that he has inherited his uncle's magical abilities.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, they realize that Zebulon Voldar is using the clock to gain control over the town. The group must work together to stop Voldar and save New Enchantment from destruction.

Ending:
In the climactic final confrontation, Lewis and Jonah face off against Zebulon Voldar in a magical showdown. With the help of his uncle's magic and his own growing powers, Lewis is able to defeat Voldar and shatter the clock, rendering it powerless.

The movie ends with Lewis and Jonah becoming friends and partners in their magical adventures. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Lewis has found a new family and a sense of belonging in New Enchantment.

Overall, The House with a Clock in Its Walls is a heartwarming and thrilling tale of magic, friendship, and self-discovery. With its blend of humor, adventure, and supernatural elements, the movie is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

title: Sweetheart
overview: Jenn has washed ashore a small tropical island and it doesn’t take her long to realize she’s completely alone. She must spend her days not only surviving the elements, but must also fend off the malevolent force that comes out each night.
plot:
Sweetheart is a 2019 American survival horror film directed by J. D. Dillard, who co-wrote it with Alex Theurer and Alex Hyner, and produced by Jason Blum among others. Kiersey Clemons stars as a castaway stranded on a tropical island where she is hunted by a sea creature, with Emory Cohen, Hanna Mangan Lawrence, Benedict Samuel and Andrew Crawford in supporting roles.

After a storm sinks their boat, Jenn Remming washes up on a small, deserted island and finds her friend Brad, who soon dies of his injuries. Exploring the island, she discovers the belongings and graves of a family who once lived there. She buries Brad in the sand, but the next morning finds the grave dug up and a trail of blood leading to the sea. While swimming to recover her luggage, she spots a mysterious dark hole in the seabed. After a failed attempt to signal a passing plane with a flare, she glimpses a huge humanoid creature that emerges from the ocean at night, and she survives the following nights by hiding. When the mutilated remains of another friend, Zack, wash ashore, she uses the body as bait to observe the monster, and later wounds it with a sharpened stick after it nearly pulls her from a makeshift hammock.

Her boyfriend Lucas and her friend Mia then arrive in a life raft. They dismiss Jenn's warnings, and tensions rise when Jenn finds Lucas's bloodied pocketknife and he hints that he had a hand in Zack's death. When Jenn tries to escape alone in the raft, the others overpower and tie her up, but the creature strikes that night, dragging Mia into the sea. Jenn frees herself and saves Lucas, and the two attempt to flee by raft, but the monster tears through it, killing Lucas. Jenn escapes its grip by stabbing it with Lucas's knife.

Alone, she records her experiences in a journal for any future castaways and prepares a final confrontation. Luring the creature into a ring of fire, she fights it with sharpened branches and bones from the family's graves. The wounded monster collapses on the shore, and Jenn beheads it before setting off in the raft with the head as proof.

Sweetheart premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 28, 2019, and was released by Universal Pictures on digital platforms and on demand that October. Critics responded favorably: Rotten Tomatoes reports 93% approval, with a consensus crediting Clemons's performance and the film's blend of social subtext and genre thrills, and Metacritic gave it 71 out of 100.

title: The Saint
overview: International master thief, Simon Templar, also known as The Saint, is asked by a desperate rich man to find his kidnapped daughter. However, in addition to evading the authorities, Simon must face a dangerous adversary from his past.
plot:
The Saint is a 2017 American action film directed by Ernie Barbarash and starring Adam Rayner as Simon Templar, the gentleman thief and adventurer created by the novelist Leslie Charteris. Eliza Dushku plays Templar's associate Patricia Holm, with James Remar among the supporting cast. Ian Ogilvy, who played Templar in the 1970s series Return of the Saint, also appears, as does Roger Moore, star of the 1960s television series The Saint. It was Moore's final screen appearance, and the film was dedicated to his memory after he died shortly before its release.

The film was shot in 2013 as a pilot for a proposed new television series. When the series was not picked up, the pilot was shelved, but it was eventually released direct to video in July 2017 as a tribute to Moore.

Templar, a master thief known as "the Saint," opens the story by thwarting a plot to trade gold for bombs, seizing most of the gold and leaving behind his trademark calling card, a stick figure with a halo. Meanwhile, a mysterious figure orders a banker, Arnie Valecross, to steal $2.5 billion in aid money intended for Nigeria. When Valecross secretly diverts the funds, his employer kidnaps his daughter to force him to cooperate. Templar, who has learned of the theft, intervenes, but Valecross is mortally wounded and with his last breath passes on a clue about someone called "the Nomad." With the help of Patricia Holm and his associate Doyle, Templar sets out to find the Nomad, rescue the banker's daughter and recover the stolen money. Pursuing him is FBI agent John Henry Fernack, while the investigation reveals that the villain behind the scheme is connected to Templar's own past.

The film's release attracted interest mainly from fans of the long-running franchise, who welcomed the chance to see Moore and Ogilvy, two former screen Saints, alongside a new actor in the role. The character had earlier been played in a 1997 feature film by Val Kilmer, and several other attempts to revive the character for television had failed to reach series.

title: Wonder Woman 1984
tagline: A new era of wonder begins.
overview: A botched store robbery places Wonder Woman in a global battle against a powerful and mysterious ancient force that puts her powers in jeopardy.
plot:
Wonder Woman 1984 is a 2020 superhero film directed by Patty Jenkins, starring Gal Gadot as Diana Prince / Wonder Woman. The movie takes place four years after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Diana (Gal Gadot) living on Themyscira, her home island, where she has been training to become a warrior and protect her people from the outside world. However, Diana's desire for human connection and experience leads her to leave the island and explore the world beyond.

In 1984, Diana meets Barbara Minerva (Kristen Wiig), an American botanist who is struggling with feelings of inadequacy and jealousy towards men. Barbara discovers a magical flower that grants eternal youth and beauty, but at a terrible cost: it slowly drains the life force from those around her, turning them into mindless, zombie-like creatures.

As Diana becomes increasingly entangled in Barbara's life, she begins to realize that the flower is not just a simple artifact, but a powerful tool created by the gods. The flower's power is so great that it can manipulate reality itself, warping the fabric of time and space.

Meanwhile, Steve Trevor (Chris Pine), Diana's love interest from the first film, has been presumed dead after his plane crashed in World War I. However, he is actually alive and has been living in a mystical realm, where he has become trapped by the gods' magic.

As Barbara's obsession with the flower grows, she becomes increasingly unstable and violent, threatening to destroy everything around her. Diana must confront her own demons and make a choice between saving humanity or protecting herself from Barbara's wrath.

Throughout the film, Jenkins explores themes of feminism, power, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The movie also delves into the complexities of female relationships, particularly the toxic bond between Barbara and Diana.

The action sequences in Wonder Woman 1984 are intense and visually stunning, with a blend of practical and CGI effects that bring the magical world to life. The film's climax features an epic battle between Diana and Barbara, with the fate of humanity hanging in the balance.

Overall, Wonder Woman 1984 is a thrilling and emotionally resonant sequel that expands on the mythology of the DC Extended Universe while introducing new characters and themes.

title: Batman vs. Two-Face
tagline: Everyone must face their demons.
overview: Former Gotham City District Attorney Harvey Dent, one side of his face scarred by acid, goes on a crime spree based on the number '2'. All of his actions are decided by the flip of a defaced, two-headed silver dollar.
plot:
Batman vs. Two-Face is a 2017 American animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and a direct sequel to Batman: Return of the Caped Crusaders (2016). Based on the 1960s Batman television series, it features Adam West, Burt Ward and Julie Newmar reprising their roles as Batman, Robin and Catwoman, with William Shatner voicing District Attorney Harvey Dent, who becomes Two-Face. It premiered at New York Comic Con in October 2017 before its digital and home-video release later that month. It was West's final performance as Batman and was released after his death in June 2017.

Batman and Robin join Gotham's district attorney, Harvey Dent, at a secret demonstration by Professor Hugo Strange and Dr. Harleen Quinzel of the "Evil Extractor," a machine designed to drain the evil from captured criminals and store it in a vat. When the vat explodes, Dent is drenched in liquefied evil, which scars half of his face and splits his personality, turning him into the coin-flipping criminal Two-Face. After a series of clashes with the Dynamic Duo, Dent undergoes reconstructive surgery that appears to erase his evil side, and he returns to fighting crime as an assistant to the district attorney.

Six months later, Batman and Robin capture King Tut and his henchmen after they steal a biplane. Commissioner Gordon and Chief O'Hara interrogate Tut's alter ego, the mild-mannered Professor William McElroy, with O'Hara repeatedly tapping him on the head to switch his personality. After the trial, Dent and Bruce Wayne share a drink before Dent leaves for a charity event for underprivileged twins at the Winning Pair casino. Soon a mysterious package arrives at Gordon's office, signaling the return of Two-Face, whose crimes revolve around duality and the number two. Batman and Robin must determine whether Dent has relapsed, and as Catwoman reappears and the threat escalates, the heroes face death traps, disguises and a scheme that endangers Gotham City itself.

Batman vs. Two-Face received positive reviews, holding a 100 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews. IGN gave it 8.4 out of 10, calling it a worthy entry in the 1966 canon and a fine send-off for West, and Nick Blackshaw of Starburst described it as a very entertaining piece of animation. Critics singled out Shatner's dual performance and the film's affectionate recreation of the series' campy humor.

Kay has always been fascinated by the supernatural and decides to investigate the cursed house where her mother died, hoping to understand the origins of the curse.

The movie takes a dark and twisted turn when Kay discovers that the curse has been awakened once again, this time targeting her own life. As she tries to uncover the truth behind the curse, she realizes that it's not just a simple vengeful spirit, but a complex web of emotions and trauma that have been passed down through generations.

Throughout the film, the audience is taken on a journey through the cursed house, where they encounter various characters who are also under the influence of the grudge. The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Kay tries to break the curse and free herself from its grasp.

The score by Roque Barral adds to the sense of unease, creating a feeling of dread that permeates throughout the movie.

The cast delivers solid performances, with Andi Matichak standing out as Kay Gushiken. Her portrayal of a strong and determined protagonist is compelling, and her chemistry with Justin Bartha is undeniable.

Overall, The Grudge is a chilling and unsettling horror film that explores themes of trauma, grief, and the supernatural. While it may not be as complex or layered as some other horror movies, its atmospheric tension and suspense make it a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: Every Day
tagline: Every day a different body. Every day a different life. Every day in love with the same girl.
overview: 16-year old Rhiannon falls in love with a mysterious spirit named “A” that inhabits a different body every day. Feeling an unmatched connection, Rhiannon and “A” work each day to find each other, not knowing what the next day will bring.
plot:
Every Day is a 2018 American romantic fantasy drama directed by Michael Sucsy and written by Jesse Andrews, based on David Levithan's 2012 novel. Angourie Rice stars as Rhiannon, a 16-year-old who falls in love with a wandering soul that wakes up each morning in a different body. Justice Smith plays her boyfriend Justin, Debby Ryan plays Jolene, Maria Bello plays Rhiannon's mother Lindsey and Owen Teague plays Alexander.

"A" is a spirit who lives each day in the body of a different teenager. One morning A wakes up as Justin, Rhiannon's neglectful boyfriend, skips school with her and falls in love as she confides about her troubled family. She tells A, whom she believes to be Justin, that their day should end on "a nice note". The next day, the real Justin is careless again and remembers nothing. A keeps finding her, at one point as Nathan at a party, telling her she deserves better than Justin. Later, as Megan, A explains the truth. As James, A reveals that the body-switching has gone on since infancy and shows Rhiannon a private Instagram account documenting every life. As Vic, a transgender teen, A persuades her that the soul matters more than the body, and she agrees to keep meeting.

One day A wakes up as Rhiannon herself and respectfully spends the day bonding with her family. Rhiannon leaves Justin and spends a weekend with A at her uncle's cabin, but A later fails to appear, having woken in a patient undergoing a lung transplant. A refuses to leave lasting marks on the lives of others, though in Kelsea's body A stays alive until the suicidal girl's father can be alerted. When A becomes Rhiannon's classmate Alexander, she asks A to stay in his body indefinitely. It works briefly, but A cannot bear to take over someone else's life. Knowing they cannot have a future together, the couple spend one last night dancing and talking, and A tells her that "this is the nice note". The next morning, A wakes up as a girl named Katie and drives off to New York, while Rhiannon meets the real Alexander at school.

It was shot in Toronto in 2017. Orion Pictures released it on February 23, 2018, after several date changes. It opened ninth and grossed $12.8 million worldwide. In the United Kingdom, four seconds showing suicide methods were cut to earn a 12A certificate. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 64% approval, with a consensus that the film wastes its metaphysical premise on shallow storytelling but is enlivened by its diverse young cast.

plot:
The Killer (Portuguese: O Matador) is a 2017 Brazilian neo-western written and directed by Marcelo Galvão. Set in the arid backlands of northeastern Brazil, it belongs to the regional genre sometimes called the "nordestern," which blends the conventions of the American western with the history and folklore of the cangaço bandits. Diogo Morgado stars as Cabeleira, known in English as Shaggy, with Étienne Chicot, Deto Montenegro, Nill Marcondes, Igor Cotrim, Maria de Medeiros and Paulo Gorgulho. Filming began in August 2016, and Netflix released the film worldwide on 10 November 2017.

The story takes place between the 1910s and the 1940s in the state of Pernambuco. As a baby, Cabeleira is found abandoned by Sete Orelhas, or Seven Ears, a local cangaceiro bandit and gunman, who raises him in the wilderness of the sertão, completely cut off from civilization. Under the outlaw's guidance the boy grows into a skilled marksman, knowing nothing of the world beyond their isolated life.

When Seven Ears mysteriously disappears, the grown Cabeleira finally ventures into town to look for him. There he finds a lawless place ruled by Monsieur Blanchard, a tyrannical Frenchman who controls the lucrative trade in precious stones and had previously employed Seven Ears as his hired killer. Drawn into Blanchard's service, Cabeleira himself becomes a feared assassin, carrying out killings for the Frenchman while searching for answers about his foster father's fate. Over the years, his violent career brings him into contact with a gallery of characters, including the local authorities represented by Lieutenant Raul Sobral, and as he discovers the truth about what happened to Seven Ears and about Blanchard's power, he is forced to confront the brutal world that shaped him.

The Killer was the first Brazilian fiction feature produced as a Netflix original and released exclusively on the platform. Brazilian critics praised its cinematography and its evocative re-creation of the sertão, but many found the screenplay overloaded with characters and subplots and criticized its heavy use of narration and its visual effects.

Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood is a 2019 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. The film is set in August 1969, on the eve of the Manson Family murders.

As the night wears on, tensions rise, and the group becomes increasingly paranoid. In the chaos, Sharon is brutally murdered, along with several other guests at the party.

The film's second half explores the aftermath of the murders, as Rick and Cliff try to come to terms with what has happened. The two men become embroiled in a police investigation into the murders, led by Lieutenant Dixon (Michael Mando).

Ultimately, the film is a meditation on the fragility of life and the power of friendship. Despite the violence and tragedy that unfolds, Rick and Cliff's bond remains strong, and they find solace in each other's company.

Overall, Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, community, and the darker side of human nature. With its talented ensemble cast and Tarantino's signature style, the film is a must-see for fans of cinema.

overview: Lara Jean's love life goes from imaginary to out of control when her secret letters to every boy she's ever fallen for are mysteriously mailed out.
plot:
To All the Boys I've Loved Before is a romantic comedy film released in 2018, produced by Susan Johnson and Matt Tyler. The movie follows the story of Lara Jean Covey, played by Lana Condor, a high school student who writes letters to all the boys she's ever had a crush on, but never intends to send them.

The story begins with Lara Jean, who lives with her single mother, Margot (Janel Parrish), and her older sister, Kitty (Anna Cathcart). After their father's death, the sisters are left to navigate high school life together. Lara Jean's life is turned upside down when she accidentally sends out the letters to all the boys on her list, including Josh Sanderson (Jordan Fisher), Peter Kavinsky (Noah Centineo), and Chris Evans (Israel Broussard).

To avoid awkwardness and potential relationships with these boys, Lara Jean tries to convince them that the letters were never meant to be sent. However, things become complicated when Josh, who is now interested in her, asks her out on a date. Meanwhile, Peter, who is also charming and popular, offers to pretend to be Josh's boyfriend in exchange for Lara Jean's help with his college applications.

As Lara Jean navigates her relationships with these two boys, she must confront her own feelings and learn to prioritize her own happiness. Along the way, she discovers that she has more in common with Peter than she initially thought, despite their initial differences. The movie takes a romantic turn as Lara Jean finds herself falling for both Josh and Peter.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including family drama, peer pressure, and self-discovery. Lara Jean's relationships with her sisters and mother are also explored, highlighting the importance of female friendships and support.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note as Lara Jean finds love and acceptance in unexpected ways. With its lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and charming performances, To All the Boys I've Loved Before has become a beloved favorite among audiences worldwide.

Overall, To All the Boys I've Loved Before is a delightful romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, relationships, and self-discovery. The film's relatable characters, engaging storyline, and sweet romance make it a must-watch for fans of the genre.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Williams' obsession with speed and power ultimately leads him down a path of destruction and chaos.

The film also explores the theme of toxic masculinity, as Williams' aggressive and dominant behavior towards women and men alike is portrayed as a symptom of his deeper psychological issues. Furthermore, Speed Kills touches on the theme of celebrity culture and the way it can both elevate and corrupt individuals. Overall, Speed Kills is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of obsession, toxic masculinity, and the corrupting influence of celebrity culture.

title: Gnome Alone
tagline: Little dudes. Big trouble.
overview: When Chloe discovers that her new home's garden gnomes are not what they seem, she must decide between the pursuit of a desired high school life and taking up the fight against the Troggs.
plot:
Gnome Alone is a 2017 computer-animated fantasy comedy directed by Peter Lepeniotis and written by Michael Schwartz and Zina Zaflow from a story by Robert Moreland. Produced by Vanguard Animation and 3QU Media, it features the voices of Becky G, Josh Peck, Olivia Holt, George Lopez, Patrick Stump, David Koechner and Tara Strong. The film follows a teenage girl who discovers that the garden gnomes around her new home are secretly guardians protecting the world from a race of ravenous monsters.

Chloe and her mother Catherine move to the small town of Tenderville, into a huge old house whose grounds are dotted with odd-looking gnomes. Exploring the house, Chloe finds a hidden room containing a glowing green gem, which she turns into a necklace. Without realizing it, she has opened a portal in the basement through which small, destructive creatures called Troggs begin to pour. At her new school, Chloe is desperate to fit in with the popular clique led by Brittany, and she gives away the necklace to win Brittany's favor.

When Catherine leaves for an extra shift at work, the gnomes reveal that they are alive. Led by Zook, and including the knowledgeable Quicksilver, they explain that the gem is the Keystone, the object that keeps the Troggs sealed away. The Troggs had long ago devoured the plant life on which the gnomes' world depended, and the gnomes' former leader Zamfeer disappeared after venturing into the Troggs' realm to stop them. The gnomes enlist Chloe to help hold back the invading creatures until the Keystone can be recovered, and Chloe recruits her awkward neighbor and classmate Liam to join the fight. As the house turns into a battlefield, Chloe must also face the consequences of trying too hard to be accepted by people who do not value her.

The film blends slapstick action with a story about friendship, self-acceptance and the difference between popularity and genuine loyalty.

Gnome Alone premiered in Greece and Cyprus in late 2017, with wider international releases following in 2018, and it was released on Netflix in the United States on October 19, 2018. It received mixed reviews, holding a score of about 45 percent on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Bring It On: Worldwide #Cheersmack
overview: When Destiny, captain of three-time national champions "The Rebels," is challenged to a global cheer showdown by an edgy new team called "The Truth," the Cheer Goddess organizes a virtual battle for squads from all around the world. It seems like the whole world wants to take down Destiny and her team, and they just might succeed, unless Destiny can rise to the challenge, set her ego aside and figure out who her real friends are.
plot:
Bring It On: Worldwide #Cheersmack, released in the United Kingdom as Bring It On: Worldwide Showdown, is a 2017 cheerleading film directed by Robert Adetuyi and the sixth installment in the Bring It On series. It was released direct-to-video on August 29, 2017.

Destiny, the bossy, victory-obsessed captain of the Rebels, an American squad with many world titles, rarely listens to anyone, including her best friend, Willow, although she idolizes Cheer Goddess, a retired five-time champion who now hosts a popular podcast. During a local competition, a mysterious masked squad called the Truth hacks the arena's audio and video feeds and vows to dethrone the Rebels. Humiliated, Destiny runs off and is mocked by a crew of street dancers. As public opinion turns against the Rebels, members quit and rival squads around the world grow bold. After failing to recruit new male members at a diner, Destiny bets the street dancers that they will join if the Rebels beat them in a dance-off, and the Rebels win.

The two groups clash in practice, though Destiny falls for Blake, the dancers' leader and a graffiti artist, while Willow devises new routines with one of the dancers and starts a romance of her own. Destiny dismisses Willow's ideas, records video diaries insulting her new teammates, and only later resolves to become a more open-minded captain. The Truth then appears on Cheer Goddess's show and proposes a worldwide competition decided by public vote. When Destiny's rants leak online, much of the squad, including the dancers, walks out. Destiny works out that Willow formed the Truth with Hannah, a seemingly dim teammate, to teach her a lesson, but that Hannah used it to try to destroy the squad. Forgiving Willow, Destiny rebuilds the Rebels with returning members, including Roxanne, and some of the dancers, and they beat the unmasked Truth in the final.

Cristine Prosperi plays Destiny, with Gia Ré as Willow, Sophie Vavasseur as Hannah, Jordan Rodrigues as Blake, Natalie Walsh as Roxanne and Vivica A. Fox as Cheer Goddess. Reviews were poor: Common Sense Media gave it one star and said it was made on the cheap and lacked flair, depth and wit, and DVD Talk found it forgettable, though it was nice to look at. Cliché Magazine disliked the plot but praised Fox and the friendships between some of the characters.

title: Unsane
tagline: Is she or isn't she?
overview: A woman is involuntarily committed to a mental institution where she is confronted by her greatest fear.
plot:
Unsane is a 2018 American psychological thriller directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by Jonathan Bernstein and James Greer. Claire Foy stars as Sawyer Valentini, with Joshua Leonard as her stalker David Strine, Jay Pharoah as fellow patient Nate Hoffman, and Juno Temple, Aimee Mullins and Amy Irving in supporting roles, while Matt Damon makes a cameo as a detective. Made on a budget of about 1.5 million dollars, the film was shot entirely on an iPhone 7 Plus. It premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival in February 2018 and was released in the United States in March 2018 by Fingerprint Releasing and Bleecker Street.

Sawyer has moved away from Boston to escape a man who has been stalking her, but she remains anxious and traumatised. She consults a counsellor at the Highland Creek Behavioral Center, and, believing she is filling out routine paperwork, signs a consent form that commits her to a locked psychiatric ward for twenty-four hours. When she calls the police, they tell her that nothing can be done because she signed voluntarily. Her panicked reaction to her confinement, including lashing out at a patient and a staff member, leads the facility to extend her stay by a week.

Another patient, Nate, explains that Highland Creek runs a scheme to profit from health insurance: it tricks people into committing themselves, keeps them for as long as their insurance pays, and then declares them cured. Sawyer's situation becomes even more nightmarish when she recognises one of the orderlies as David Strine, her stalker, working under a false name. No one believes her, and David drugs her so that she appears unstable. Her mother comes to rescue her, but is intercepted, and Nate, who has been secretly documenting the facility's abuses with a hidden phone, is also targeted. Sawyer is left to fight for her survival against a man who has obsessively pursued her, while the audience is left to wonder at first whether he is real or a product of her paranoia.

Soderbergh uses the smartphone format to create a claustrophobic, unsettling look, and the film critiques both the treatment of women who report stalking and the exploitation of patients by the private healthcare system.

Unsane received generally positive reviews, with about 80 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and particular praise for Foy's performance. It was a commercial success, grossing more than 14 million dollars worldwide.

title: In the Heights
tagline: The time has come.
overview: The story of Usnavi, a bodega owner who has mixed feelings about closing his store and retiring to the Dominican Republic or staying in Washington Heights.
plot:
In the Heights is a 2021 American musical drama directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Quiara Alegría Hudes, adapted from the 2005 stage musical she created with Lin-Manuel Miranda. Anthony Ramos stars as Usnavi, with Melissa Barrera, Corey Hawkins, Leslie Grace in her film debut, Olga Merediz, Daphne Rubin-Vega, Gregory Diaz IV and Jimmy Smits. Like the stage show, it is set in the largely Dominican neighbourhood of Washington Heights in Upper Manhattan, following residents as they chase their sueñitos, or little dreams.

Usnavi tells a group of children a story about the neighbourhood. Years earlier, he runs a bodega and dreams of returning to the Dominican Republic to revive his late father's beach bar, which has just come up for sale. Around him are Abuela Claudia, the matriarch who raised him; Kevin Rosario, owner of a taxi company, and his dispatcher Benny, Usnavi's best friend; the salon owner Daniela and her staff; Usnavi's teenage cousin Sonny; and Vanessa, an aspiring fashion designer on whom Usnavi has a crush. Kevin's daughter Nina returns from Stanford, secretly having dropped out. When the bodega sells a winning lottery ticket worth $96,000, the whole neighbourhood imagines what it would do with the money.

During a sweltering summer, rising rents force Daniela's salon to move to the Bronx. Kevin sells his business to pay Nina's tuition, but she reveals she left because of the racism she experienced, while she and Benny rekindle their romance. Usnavi learns that Sonny, an undocumented immigrant, cannot go with him to the Dominican Republic. A nervous Usnavi ruins his date with Vanessa at a salsa club, and a citywide blackout follows. In the heat, Abuela Claudia recalls her life in Cuba and her hard-won journey to New York, and dies peacefully; the neighbourhood mourns her together.

Nina decides to return to Stanford to help undocumented students, and Usnavi quietly secures a co-signer for Vanessa's apartment. Discovering that Abuela held the winning ticket and left it to him, he gives it to fund Sonny's immigration case. When Vanessa shows him a fashion line inspired by Graffiti Pete's murals, Usnavi decides to stay, and the story returns to the present, where he is telling it in the renovated bodega to his and Vanessa's daughter.

The film was acclaimed by critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 94% approval, but it underperformed at the box office, grossing about $45 million worldwide against a $55 million budget.

title: The Children Act
tagline: We all make choices. Hers make history.
overview: In the midst of a marital crisis, a High Court judge must decide if she should order a life-saving blood transfusion for a teen with cancer despite his family's refusal to accept medical treatment for religious reasons.
plot:
The Children Act is a 2017 drama directed by Richard Eyre and produced by Duncan Kenworthy, with a screenplay by Ian McEwan based on his 2014 novel. Emma Thompson stars as Fiona Maye, a High Court judge, with Stanley Tucci as her husband Jack and Fionn Whitehead as Adam Henry.

Fiona sits in the Family Division of the High Court of England and Wales. She is assigned the urgent case of Adam, a 17-year-old with leukemia whose doctors want to give him a blood transfusion so they can continue treatment. Adam and his parents are Jehovah's Witnesses and refuse on religious grounds. Fiona visits him in the hospital to find out whether the decision is truly his. Adam says he understands that refusal could leave him disabled rather than dead, and he would accept that. When he plays "Down by the Salley Gardens", Fiona sings along, and Adam, deeply drawn to her, begs her to stay. She rules under the Children Act 1989 that Adam's welfare is paramount and allows the transfusion without his or his parents' consent.

Meanwhile, Fiona's marriage is collapsing. Jack, tired of her devotion to work, openly announces an affair with a younger colleague, insisting he still loves her, and leaves. Fiona changes the locks; when Jack returns two days later, they argue bitterly. The transfusion works, and Adam, now recovering, bombards Fiona with messages, poems and letters, saying she has changed his view of the world. He follows her to Newcastle, where she attends a ceremony, and says he wants to live with her, unable to understand why his parents were willing to let him die. She sends him home, though they share a kiss. Later, just before Fiona performs at a lawyers' concert, she learns that Adam has relapsed. She plays "Down by the Salley Gardens" and rushes to see him, but he has refused another transfusion. At home, Fiona breaks down in front of Jack and falls asleep holding his hand. After Adam dies, she attends his funeral and leaves with Jack.

Filming took place in London in late 2016, with Sir Alan Ward, a judge in a conjoined twins case that had inspired the novel, serving as an adviser. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 9 September 2017. Entertainment One released it in the United Kingdom on 24 August 2018, and A24 gave it a limited U.S. release that September. Reviews were positive. Rotten Tomatoes reported 74% approval, saying Thompson's powerful performance elevates a flawed film into an affecting adult drama.

title: Revenge
tagline: Why do women always have to put up a fight?
overview: Jen's romantic getaway with her wealthy married boyfriend is disrupted when his friends arrive for an impromptu hunting trip. Tension mounts at the house until the situation culminates in an unexpected way.
plot:
Revenge is a 2017 English-language French action thriller written and directed by Coralie Fargeat in her feature debut. Matilda Lutz stars as Jen, a young woman who is assaulted and left for dead in the desert, with Kevin Janssens as her wealthy married lover Richard, and Vincent Colombe and Guillaume Bouchède as his hunting companions Stan and Dimitri. The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017 and was released in France by Rezo Films in February 2018.

Jen, a young American who dreams of moving to Los Angeles, flies by helicopter with her married boyfriend, Richard, to his isolated luxury villa in the desert for a romantic getaway. The next morning, Richard's friends Stan and Dimitri arrive a day early for their annual hunting trip, and Richard is forced to introduce Jen to them. That night the four of them party, and Jen dances flirtatiously with Stan. The following morning, while Richard is away, Stan makes advances toward her and, when she rejects him, rapes her, while Dimitri ignores what is happening.

When Richard returns, he offers Jen money and a new life in Canada in exchange for her silence. She threatens to tell his wife, and he slaps her. Jen flees into the desert, pursued by the three men, and at the edge of a cliff Richard pushes her off. She is impaled on a tree and left for dead. Regaining consciousness, she frees herself and, under the influence of peyote she took from Richard's supplies, cauterizes her wound with a heated beer can, leaving the imprint of an eagle on her skin. Transformed from victim into hunter, Jen arms herself and tracks the men across the desert as they search for her body, killing them one by one in brutal, bloody confrontations, culminating in a final showdown with Richard inside the villa.

Revenge received widespread acclaim, with critics praising Fargeat's stylish direction, Lutz's performance and the film's feminist reworking of the rape-revenge genre, which subverts the male gaze traditionally associated with such films. Its vivid colors, graphic violence and excessive bloodshed were widely noted, and the film established Fargeat, who later directed The Substance.

As he delves deeper into his research, he becomes increasingly isolated from the world around him, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition.

Ultimately, The Professor presents a cautionary tale about the risks of exploiting one's intelligence for personal gain, and the importance of maintaining balance in life to avoid losing oneself in the process.

The film's narrative is structured around key events in Tolkien's life, including:

* His time at Oxford University, where he developed his love for languages and mythology.
* His experiences during World War I, which had a profound impact on his writing.
* His romance with Edith and their marriage.
* The creation of Middle-earth and the writing of The Lord of the Rings.

title: The Starling
tagline: Hope Starts Small
overview: A woman adjusting to life after a loss contends with a feisty bird that's taken over her garden — and a husband who's struggling to find a way forward.
plot:
The Starling is a 2021 American drama film directed by Joe Wright, starring Sam Claflin and Sally Hawkins.

The main themes of The Starling revolve around loneliness, isolation, and the complexities of human relationships. The story follows William "Will" Evans (Sam Claflin), a widowed father who moves to a rural area with his young daughter, Rose (Abigail Whelan). Will's life is marked by grief and loneliness after the loss of his wife, and he struggles to connect with his daughter.

The film explores the theme of isolation through Will's character, as he navigates his new life in the countryside. He finds solace in hunting and becomes increasingly withdrawn from society. The arrival of a mysterious woman, Rose (Sally Hawkins), who is also an outsider, sets off a chain of events that challenges Will's perceptions of loneliness and human connection.

The film delves into the complexities of relationships, particularly between parents and children. Will's relationship with his daughter is strained due to his grief and emotional unavailability. However, as he forms a bond with Rose, he begins to confront his emotions and learn to connect with her on a deeper level.

Throughout the film, Wright explores the idea that loneliness can be both a source of pain and a catalyst for growth. Will's journey is marked by moments of vulnerability, self-discovery, and ultimately, healing. The Starling is a poignant exploration of the human condition, highlighting the importance of connection, empathy, and understanding in overcoming loneliness.

The film received critical acclaim for its nuanced performances, atmospheric cinematography, and Wright's sensitive direction.

title: The Insult
tagline: Words change everything.
overview: After an emotional exchange between a Lebanese Christian and a Palestinian refugee escalates, the men end up in a court case that gets national attention.
plot:
The Insult is a 2017 drama film that revolves around the complex and intricate relationship between two Lebanese men, Taki and Djoon, who engage in a heated argument over a minor insult. 

At its core, the movie explores themes of cultural identity, family dynamics, and the complexities of human relationships. The film delves into the intricacies of Lebanese culture, highlighting the nuances of tradition, honor, and social etiquette that often govern the lives of its characters.

Through Taki's character, the film sheds light on the struggles of a proud but vulnerable man who is caught between his desire to assert his dignity and his need to maintain relationships with those around him. Djoon, on the other hand, represents a more pragmatic approach to life, one that acknowledges the complexities of human emotions and the imperfections of relationships.

The Insult also touches upon themes of masculinity, highlighting the societal expectations placed on men in Lebanese culture and the consequences of not meeting these expectations. The film raises questions about what it means to be a man, how we navigate our emotions, and how we reconcile our individual desires with our responsibilities to others.

Ultimately, The Insult is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, cultural identity, and the complexities that arise when individuals from different backgrounds interact.

title: Jim & Andy: The Great Beyond
overview: Offbeat documentarian Chris Smith provides a behind-the-scenes look at how Jim Carrey adopted the persona of idiosyncratic comedian Andy Kaufman on the set of Man on the Moon.
plot:
Jim & Andy: The Great Beyond is a documentary film that delves into the complex and often tumultuous relationship between comedian Jim Carrey and his alter ego, "Andy Kaufman." At its core, the movie explores the themes of identity, performance, and the blurring of reality and fiction.

The film examines how Kaufman's innovative approach to comedy, which often involved pushing boundaries and challenging societal norms, influenced Carrey's own creative trajectory. Through their interactions, the documentary reveals a deep-seated fascination with the concept of "character" and the ways in which artists can use performance to explore and subvert identity.

The movie also touches on the theme of obsession, as Carrey becomes increasingly consumed by Kaufman's persona and the world he created. This fixation serves as a catalyst for Carrey's own creative growth, but it also raises questions about the nature of authenticity and the impact of celebrity culture on personal relationships.

Ultimately, Jim & Andy: The Great Beyond is a thought-provoking exploration of the tensions between reality and performance, identity and character. Through its nuanced portrayal of Kaufman's legacy and Carrey's enduring fascination with his alter ego, the film invites viewers to consider the ways in which art can both reflect and shape our understanding of ourselves and the world around us.

title: Nicky Larson and the Cupid's Perfume
original_title: Nicky Larson et le parfum de Cupidon
overview: Nicky Larson is tasked to recover the perfume of Cupid, a perfume that would make anyone who uses it irresistible.
plot:
Nicky Larson and the Cupid's Perfume (French: Nicky Larson et le parfum de Cupidon), also released internationally as City Hunter, is a French action comedy directed by Philippe Lacheau, who co-wrote the screenplay with Julien Arruti and Pierre Lacheau. It is a live-action adaptation of Tsukasa Hojo's Japanese manga and anime series City Hunter, which was broadcast in France under the name Nicky Larson; Hojo approved the project after reading the script. Lacheau plays the title role, with Élodie Fontan, Tarek Boudali and Julien Arruti, and Didier Bourdon, Kamel Guenfoud, Sophie Mousel and Pamela Anderson in supporting roles. The film premiered in December 2018 and was released in French cinemas on 6 February 2019.

Nicky Larson is an unconventional private detective, a skilled street fighter and an expert marksman who is hired to solve problems that nobody else can handle. Working with his partner Laura, he offers a range of services to his clients, some far more dangerous than others. For all his professionalism and fame, however, Nicky has one great weakness: an uncontrollable attraction to beautiful women, which constantly gets him into trouble and exasperates Laura, who is often left to clean up after him.

A client hires the pair to protect "Cupid's perfume," an experimental fragrance that makes anyone who wears it completely irresistible to others. During a moment of distraction on Nicky's part, a group of criminals steals the precious bottle, and he must race to recover it before it falls into the wrong hands. The chase takes him and Laura from Paris to Monaco and draws in a string of eccentric characters, as the perfume changes hands and creates comic chaos. In keeping with the original series, the film combines slapstick, crude humor and fast-paced action scenes, along with numerous nods to the anime familiar to French audiences who grew up with it on television.

The film was well received by fans and by many critics, who praised its affection for the source material and the energy of the action sequences, though some found the dialogue weak. Simon Riaux of Écran Large noted that it maintained a surprising balance between pastiche and sincerity. The film was a commercial success in France, drawing a large audience in cinemas.

title: The Cured

overview: What happens when the undead return to life? In a world ravaged for years by a virus that turns the infected into zombie-like cannibals, a cure is at last found and the wrenching process of reintegrating the survivors back into society begins.
plot:
The Cured is a 2017 Irish zombie musical horror film directed by David Freyne. The movie tells the story of a small town in Ireland that has been quarantined after a mysterious outbreak, where the infected are not the mindless undead, but rather people who have become violent and aggressive due to a mysterious illness.

The main theme of The Cured revolves around the struggle for humanity and empathy in a world that seems to have lost its way. As the story unfolds, we see how the characters grapple with their own emotions and relationships, often finding themselves torn between their desire to help others and their need to protect themselves from those who are infected.

The film also explores the idea of isolation and confinement, highlighting the psychological effects it has on individuals and communities. The quarantine serves as a metaphor for the ways in which society can become fragmented and divided, leading to a breakdown in human connection and understanding.

Furthermore, The Cured touches on themes of grief, loss, and redemption, as characters navigate their personal struggles and confront the consequences of their actions. Through its unique blend of horror and music, the film creates a sense of unease and tension, mirroring the emotional turmoil experienced by its characters.

Ultimately, The Cured presents a thought-provoking commentary on the human condition, encouraging viewers to reflect on the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding in a world that often seems to be torn apart by conflict and division.

title: Trauma
tagline: Evil requires loyalty
overview: Four friends visit a rural locality of Chile, are brutally attacked by a man and his son. After not finding help in the town, they decide to confront these men with the help of a pair of policemen. But in this way, they will discover that their attackers have in their blood the direct legacy of the darkest period of Chilean history and will have to face the most brutal enemy.
plot:
Trauma is a 2017 Chilean horror film written, directed and co-edited by Lucio A. Rojas. An extreme work of gore and exploitation cinema that doubles as a political allegory, it was produced by Trauma SpA, Border Motion Cinema and Chris Reiben Productions, with cinematography by Sebastián Ballek and music by Ignacio Redard, and was shot over six weeks on the outskirts of Santiago. The film had its world premiere at the Mórbido Film Fest in Mexico in October 2017 and went on to play festivals in Europe and the Americas, including the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival and Fantaspoa; because of its controversial content it received no commercial theatrical release in Chile.

A prologue set during the early years of Augusto Pinochet's military dictatorship shows a boy being indoctrinated and forced by his father to take part in the torture and abuse of the regime's victims. Decades later, four young women, Andrea (Catalina Martin), her sister Camila (Macarena Carrere), Julia (Ximena del Solar) and Magdalena (Dominga Bofill), travel to a remote rural village for a few days away. What first seems like paradise becomes a nightmare when they are brutally attacked and sexually assaulted by Juan (Daniel Antivilo) and his son Mario (Felipe Ríos). Juan is the boy from the prologue, who still believes the principles of the regime must live on, has been terrorising the locals for years, and is raising his son to follow in his footsteps. Finding no help in the town, the survivors join forces with a pair of police officers to confront their attackers, and their resolve hardens when Juan seizes a local girl, leading to a violent final showdown during which Juan sings an old military song.

The film provoked controversy for its scenes of torture, rape, incest, necrophilia and infanticide, and for its condemnation of the Pinochet regime and the way its brutality is handed down from fathers to sons. Rojas and the cast explained that the four leads insisted he show the violence without restraint so that the message would come through; the assault scene took three days to film.

Screen Anarchy's review of the premiere called it one of the most brutal, graphic and disturbing horror films in recent memory, comparable to A Serbian Film but more overt in its political message, praising the four actresses and singling out Antivilo's portrayal of Juan as one of the most terrible villains of the year, while finding the final act's arming of the protagonists somewhat silly.

La Maison en Petits Cubes is a poignant and visually stunning film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and the passage of time. The movie follows the story of an elderly woman who lives in a small house made up of 109 cubes, each representing a year from her life.

The main theme of the film revolves around the idea of nostalgia and how it shapes our perception of ourselves and our relationships with others. As the woman reminisces about her past, we see flashbacks of her life, filled with moments of joy, love, and heartbreak. The film masterfully interweaves these memories with the present, highlighting the ways in which our experiences shape us into who we are today.

One of the most striking aspects of La Maison en Petits Cubes is its exploration of loneliness and isolation. Despite being surrounded by loved ones, the woman feels deeply disconnected from the world around her. This sense of disconnection serves as a powerful metaphor for the human experience, where we often feel like we're just going through the motions of life without truly connecting with others.

The film also touches on the theme of love and loss, particularly in the context of relationships that have come to an end. The woman's memories are filled with moments of tenderness and intimacy, but these are also tinged with a sense of sadness and longing. This bittersweet quality is a hallmark of the film, leaving the viewer with a sense of melancholy that lingers long after the credits roll.

Ultimately, La Maison en Petits Cubes is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human emotions and relationships. Through its use of nostalgia, loneliness, love, and loss, the movie creates a poignant and thought-provoking portrait of life's fragility and beauty.
